1.28.en: I have told you all that-how I would pass my days there. O Vrikodara, in what capacity will you live in the city of Virata?

2.1.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । पौरोगवो ब्रुवाणोऽहं बल्लवो नाम भारत । उपस्थास्यामि राजानं विराटमिति मे मतिः ॥१॥
2.1.en: Bhima said O Bharata, I shall present myself before the king Virata, calling myself a cook, named Ballava. This is my intention.

2.2.sa: सूपानस्य करिष्यामि कुशलोऽस्मि महानसे । कृतपूर्वाणि यान्यस्य व्यञ्जनानि सुशिक्षितैः ॥२॥
2.2.en: I shall prepare his curries. I am expert in the business of the kitchen. I shall supercede even those experts who used to made curries for him before and I shall carry from biggest loads of wood and thus render every service; and the king, having seen that splendid work, will appoint me. O Bharata, beholding me doing these superhuman deeds the servants of the monarch will regard me as a king. Thus I shall be the lord of all sorts of food and drink.

2.3.sa: तान्यप्यभिभावष्यामि प्रीतिं सञ्जनयन्नहम् । आहरिष्यामि दारूणां निचयान् महतोऽपि च ॥३॥
2.3.en: I shall prepare his curries. I am expert in the business of the kitchen. I shall supercede even those experts who used to made curries for him before and I shall carry from biggest loads of wood and thus render every service; and the king, having seen that splendid work, will appoint me. O Bharata, beholding me doing these superhuman deeds the servants of the monarch will regard me as a king. Thus I shall be the lord of all sorts of food and drink.

2.4.sa: यत् प्रेक्ष्य विपुलं कर्म राजा संयोक्ष्यते स माम् । अमानुषाणि कुर्वाणस्तानि कर्माणि भारत ॥४॥
2.4.en: I shall prepare his curries. I am expert in the business of the kitchen. I shall supercede even those experts who used to made curries for him before and I shall carry from biggest loads of wood and thus render every service; and the king, having seen that splendid work, will appoint me. O Bharata, beholding me doing these superhuman deeds the servants of the monarch will regard me as a king. Thus I shall be the lord of all sorts of food and drink.

2.5.sa: राज्ञस्तस्य परे प्रेष्या मंस्यन्ते मां यथा नृपम् । भक्ष्यान्नरसपानानां भविष्यामि तथेश्वरः ॥५॥
2.5.en: I shall prepare his curries. I am expert in the business of the kitchen. I shall supercede even those experts who used to made curries for him before and I shall carry from biggest loads of wood and thus render every service; and the king, having seen that splendid work, will appoint me. O Bharata, beholding me doing these superhuman deeds the servants of the monarch will regard me as a king. Thus I shall be the lord of all sorts of food and drink.

2.6.sa: द्विपा वा बलिनो राजन् वृषभा वा महाबलाः । विनिग्राह्या यदि मया निग्रहीष्यामि तानपि ॥६॥
2.6.en: O king, if I am commanded to overpower the mighty elephants and powerful bulls I will do that. I will defeat those combatants who will fight against me in the lists in order to satisfy the monarch but I shall not kill those fighting heroes, but bring them down in such a way that they may not perish.

2.7.sa: ये च केचिन्नियोत्स्यन्ति समाजेषु नियोधकाः । तानहं हि नियोत्स्यामि रति तस्य विवर्धयन् ॥७॥
2.7.en: O king, if I am commanded to overpower the mighty elephants and powerful bulls I will do that. I will defeat those combatants who will fight against me in the lists in order to satisfy the monarch but I shall not kill those fighting heroes, but bring them down in such a way that they may not perish.

2.8.sa: न त्वेतान् युद्ध्यमानान् वै हनिष्यामि कथञ्चन । तथैतान् पातयिष्यामि यथा यास्यन्ति न क्षयम् ॥८॥
2.8.en: O king, if I am commanded to overpower the mighty elephants and powerful bulls I will do that. I will defeat those combatants who will fight against me in the lists in order to satisfy the monarch but I shall not kill those fighting heroes, but bring them down in such a way that they may not perish.

2.9.sa: आरालिको गोविकर्ता सूपकर्ता नियोधकः । आसं युधिष्ठिरस्याहमिति वक्ष्यामि पृच्छतः ॥९॥
2.9.en: On being asked, I shall say, “Formerly I was the cook, subduer of animals, maker of curries and wrestler of Yudhishthira. O lord of me, in whatever direction I shall went my way I shall take care of my own person. This much I promise.

2.10.sa: आत्मानमात्मना रक्षंश्चरिष्यामि विशाम्पते । इत्येतत् प्रतिजानामि विहरिष्याम्यहं यथा ॥१०॥
2.10.en: On being asked, I shall say, “Formerly I was the cook, subduer of animals, maker of curries and wrestler of Yudhishthira. O lord of me, in whatever direction I shall went my way I shall take care of my own person. This much I promise.

2.11.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । यमग्निर्ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा समागच्छन्नृणां वरम् । दिधक्षुः खाण्डवं दावं दाशार्हसहितं पुरा ॥११॥
2.11.en: Yudhishthira said What work will Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, perform, who is mighty, long armed, invincible, the foremost of men, and the joy of Kurus, and before whom formerly the fire-god, desirous of consuming the Khandava forest, appeared in the guise of a Brahmana.

2.12.sa: महाबलं महाबाहुमजितं कुरुनन्दनम् । सोऽयं किं कर्म कौन्तेयः करिष्यति धनञ्जयः ॥१२॥
2.12.en: Yudhishthira said What work will Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, perform, who is mighty, long armed, invincible, the foremost of men, and the joy of Kurus, and before whom formerly the fire-god, desirous of consuming the Khandava forest, appeared in the guise of a Brahmana.

2.13.sa: योऽयमासाद्य तं दावं तर्पयामास पावकम् । विजित्यैकरथेनेन्द्रं हत्वा पन्नगराक्षसान् ॥१३॥
2.13.en: What work will be performed by the best of dualists Arjuna, who having ascended the single chariot with Krishna, repaired to the forest and gratified the fire god after defeating and destroying the Pannagas and Rakshasas and who carried off the sister of the serpentking named Vasuki.

2.14.sa: वासुकेः सर्पराजस्य स्वसारं हृतवांश्च यः । श्रेष्ठो यः प्रतियोधानां सोऽर्जुनः किं करिष्यति ॥१४॥
2.14.en: What work will be performed by the best of dualists Arjuna, who having ascended the single chariot with Krishna, repaired to the forest and gratified the fire god after defeating and destroying the Pannagas and Rakshasas and who carried off the sister of the serpentking named Vasuki.

2.15.sa: सूर्यः प्रतपतां श्रेष्ठो द्विपदां ब्राह्मणो वरः । आशीविषश्च सर्पाणामग्निस्तेजस्विनां वरः ॥१५॥
2.15.en: The sun is the foremost of all shining bodies, the Brahmana is the foremost of all bipeds, the Ashivisha is the foremost of all serpents, the fire is the foremost of all bright substances, thunder is the foremost of all weapons, the humped bull is the foremost of its kind, the ocean is the foremost of all watery expanses, the Parjanya is the foremost of all rain clouds, Dhritarashtra is the foremost of all Nagas, Airavata is the foremost of all elephants, the son is the foremost of all beloved objects, and the wife is the foremost of all friends. O Vrikodara, as every species has its, best, so is the youthful Gudakesha the best of all archers.

2.16.sa: आयुधानां वरं वज्र ककुद्मी च गवां वरः । ह्रदानामुदधिः श्रेष्ठः पर्जन्यो वर्षतां वरः ॥१६॥
2.16.en: The sun is the foremost of all shining bodies, the Brahmana is the foremost of all bipeds, the Ashivisha is the foremost of all serpents, the fire is the foremost of all bright substances, thunder is the foremost of all weapons, the humped bull is the foremost of its kind, the ocean is the foremost of all watery expanses, the Parjanya is the foremost of all rain clouds, Dhritarashtra is the foremost of all Nagas, Airavata is the foremost of all elephants, the son is the foremost of all beloved objects, and the wife is the foremost of all friends. O Vrikodara, as every species has its, best, so is the youthful Gudakesha the best of all archers.

2.17.sa: धृतराष्ट्रश्च नागानां हस्तिष्वैरावणो वरः । पुत्रः प्रियाणामधिको भार्या च सुहृदां वरा ॥१७॥
2.17.en: The sun is the foremost of all shining bodies, the Brahmana is the foremost of all bipeds, the Ashivisha is the foremost of all serpents, the fire is the foremost of all bright substances, thunder is the foremost of all weapons, the humped bull is the foremost of its kind, the ocean is the foremost of all watery expanses, the Parjanya is the foremost of all rain clouds, Dhritarashtra is the foremost of all Nagas, Airavata is the foremost of all elephants, the son is the foremost of all beloved objects, and the wife is the foremost of all friends. O Vrikodara, as every species has its, best, so is the youthful Gudakesha the best of all archers.

2.18.sa: यथैतानि विशिष्टानि जात्यां जात्यां वृकोदर । एवं युवा गुडाकेशः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम् ॥१८॥
2.18.en: The sun is the foremost of all shining bodies, the Brahmana is the foremost of all bipeds, the Ashivisha is the foremost of all serpents, the fire is the foremost of all bright substances, thunder is the foremost of all weapons, the humped bull is the foremost of its kind, the ocean is the foremost of all watery expanses, the Parjanya is the foremost of all rain clouds, Dhritarashtra is the foremost of all Nagas, Airavata is the foremost of all elephants, the son is the foremost of all beloved objects, and the wife is the foremost of all friends. O Vrikodara, as every species has its, best, so is the youthful Gudakesha the best of all archers.

2.19.sa: सोऽयमिन्द्रादनवरो वासुदेवान्महाद्युतिः । गाण्डीवधन्वा बीभत्सुः श्वेताश्वः किं करिष्यति ॥१९॥
2.19.en: What office will be performed by Bibhatsu of great splendour, whose bow is Gandiva, and whose chariot is drawn by white horses and who is in no way inferior to Indra or Vasudeva himself?

2.20.sa: उषित्वा पञ्च वर्षाणि सहस्राक्षस्य वेश्मनि । अस्त्रयोगं समासाद्य स्ववीर्यान्मानुषाद्भुतम् । दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि चाप्तानि देवरूपेण भास्वता ॥२०॥
2.20.en: What office will be performed by Arjuna shining in celestial grace, who, having stayed for five years in the abode of the thousandeyed deity, acquired by his superhuman prowess, the art of using arms along with all the celestial weapons, and who is me-seems like the Rudra, thirteenth of the Adityas, ninth of the Vasus and the tenth of the Grahas, whose arms are symmetrical and long, having the skin rendered hard by repeated strokes of the bow string and knobs on which appear like the humps of bulls and who is the foremost of warriors as the Himavata of mountains, the sea of rivers, Shakra of the gods, Havyavahak (fire) of the Vasus, the tiger of the beasts, Garuda of the winged tribes.

2.21.sa: यं मन्ये द्वादशं रुद्रमादित्यानां त्रयोदशम् । वसूनां नवमं मन्ये ग्रहाणां दशमं तथा ॥२१॥
2.21.en: What office will be performed by Arjuna shining in celestial grace, who, having stayed for five years in the abode of the thousandeyed deity, acquired by his superhuman prowess, the art of using arms along with all the celestial weapons, and who is me-seems like the Rudra, thirteenth of the Adityas, ninth of the Vasus and the tenth of the Grahas, whose arms are symmetrical and long, having the skin rendered hard by repeated strokes of the bow string and knobs on which appear like the humps of bulls and who is the foremost of warriors as the Himavata of mountains, the sea of rivers, Shakra of the gods, Havyavahak (fire) of the Vasus, the tiger of the beasts, Garuda of the winged tribes.

2.22.sa: यस्य बाहू समौ दीर्घौ ज्याघातकठिनत्वचौ । दक्षिणे चैव सव्ये च गवामिव वहः कृतः ॥२२॥

2.23.sa: हिमवानिव शैलानां समुद्रः सरितामिव । त्रिदशानां यथा शक्रो वसूनामिव हव्यवाट् ॥२३॥
2.23.en: What office will be performed by Arjuna shining in celestial grace, who, having stayed for five years in the abode of the thousandeyed deity, acquired by his superhuman prowess, the art of using arms along with all the celestial weapons, and who is me-seems like the Rudra, thirteenth of the Adityas, ninth of the Vasus and the tenth of the Grahas, whose arms are symmetrical and long, having the skin rendered hard by repeated strokes of the bow string and knobs on which appear like the humps of bulls and who is the foremost of warriors as the Himavata of mountains, the sea of rivers, Shakra of the gods, Havyavahak (fire) of the Vasus, the tiger of the beasts, Garuda of the winged tribes.

2.24.sa: मृगाणामिव शार्दूलो गरुडः पततामिव । वरः सन्नह्यमानानां सोऽर्जुनः किं करिष्यति ॥२४॥

2.25.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । प्रतिज्ञां षण्ढकोऽस्मीति करिष्यामि महीपते । ज्याघातौ हि महान्तौ मे संवर्तुं नृप दुष्करौ ॥२५॥

2.26.sa: वलयैश्छादयिष्यामितबाहू किणकृताविमौ । कर्णयोः प्रतिमुच्याहं कुण्डले ज्वलनप्रभे ॥२६॥
2.26.en: However, I shall conceal with the bangles the marks of my arm caused by the bow-string.

2.27.sa: पिनद्धकम्बुः पाणिभ्यां तृतीयां प्रकृतिं गतः । वेणीकृतशिरा राजन् नाम्ना चैव बृहन्नला ॥२७॥
2.27.en: Having worn rings shining as fire on my ears and conch-bangles on my wrist, and dressing my hair in a bread on my head and taking the name of Brihannala I shall, O king, appear as one of the third sex, and please the king and others in the seraglio by reciting stories often and often as becomes a female.

2.28.sa: पठन्नाख्यायिकाश्चैव स्त्रीभावेन पुनः पुनः । रमयिष्ये महीपालमन्यांश्चान्तःपुरे जनान् ॥२८॥
2.28.en: Having worn rings shining as fire on my ears and conch-bangles on my wrist, and dressing my hair in a bread on my head and taking the name of Brihannala I shall, O king, appear as one of the third sex, and please the king and others in the seraglio by reciting stories often and often as becomes a female.

2.29.sa: गीतं नृत्यं विचित्रं च वादित्रं विविधं तथा । शिक्षयिष्याम्यहं राजन् विराटस्य पुरस्त्रियः ॥२९॥
2.29.en: O king, I shall instruct the ladies of Virata's house in singing, delightful dancing and also in musical performances of sundry sorts.

2.30.sa: प्रजानां समुदाचारं बहुकर्म कृतं वदन् । छाद‌यिष्यामि कौन्तेय माययाऽऽत्मानमात्मना ॥३०॥
2.30.en: And in reciting various good deeds and customs of people, I shall, O son of Kunti, conceal myself in disguise.

2.31.sa: युधिष्ठिरस्य गेहे वै द्रौपद्याः परिचारिका । उषिताऽस्मीति वक्ष्यामि पृष्टो राज्ञा च पाण्डव ॥३१॥
2.31.en: O Pandava, on being asked by the king I shall say “I lived as a waiting maid of Draupadi in the palace of Yudhishthira.

2.32.sa: एतेन विधिना छन्नः कृतकेन यथा नलः । विहरिष्यामि राजेन्द्र विराटभवने सुखम् ॥३२॥
2.32.en: O great king, hiding myself by this counterfeiting means as fire is concealed by ashes, I shall happily pass my days in the palace of Virata.

3.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । इत्येवमुक्त्वा पुरुषप्रवीरस्तथाऽर्जुनो धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः । वाक्यं तथाऽसौ विरराम भूयो नृपोऽपरं भ्रातरमाबभाषे ॥१॥
3.1.en: Vaishampayana said Having spoken thus, Arjuna, the best of men and the foremost of the virtuous, ceased, and the king again asked his another brother.

3.2.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । किं त्वं नकुल कुर्वाणस्तत्र तात चरिष्यसि । कर्म तत् त्वं समाचक्ष्व राज्ये तस्य महीपतेः । सुकुमारश्च शूरश्च दर्शनीयः सुखोचितः ॥२॥
3.2.en: Yudhishthira said O Nakula, tender, heroic, graceful and accustomed to pleasurable pursuits as you are, what work will you do in the dominion of Virata, tell me that.

3.3.sa: नकुल उवाच । अश्वबन्धो भविष्यामि विराटनृपतेरहम् । सर्वथा ज्ञानसम्पन्नः कुशलः परिरक्षणे ॥३॥
3.3.en: Nakula said I shall be the keeper of the horses of king Virata; I possess thorough knowledge of the business, and am expert in the tending of them,

3.4.sa: ग्रन्थिको नाम नाम्नाऽहं कर्मैतत् सुप्रियं मम । कुशलोऽस्म्यश्वशिक्षायां तथैवाश्वचिकित्सने । प्रियाश्च सततं मेऽश्वाः कुरुराज यथा तव ॥४॥

3.5.sa: ये मामामन्त्रयिष्यन्ति विराटनगरे जनाः । तेभ्य एवं प्रवक्ष्यामि विहरिष्याम्यहं यथा ॥५॥
3.5.en: O king of the Kurus, horses are even dear to me as they are to you. Those who will question me in the city of the Virat will be thus told by me. "Formerly I was placed by Yudhishthira in charge of his horses. O ruler of the earth, I shall thus disguised go about in the city of Virata.

3.6.sa: पाण्डवेन पुरा तात अश्वेष्वधिकृतः पुरा । विराटनगरे छन्नश्चरिष्यामि महीपते ॥६॥
3.6.en: O king of the Kurus, horses are even dear to me as they are to you. Those who will question me in the city of the Virat will be thus told by me. "Formerly I was placed by Yudhishthira in charge of his horses. O ruler of the earth, I shall thus disguised go about in the city of Virata.

3.7.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । सहदेव कथं तस्य समीपे विहरिष्यसि । किं वा त्वं कर्म कुर्वाणः प्रच्छन्नो विहरिष्यसि ॥७॥
3.7.en: Yudhishthira said O Sahadeva, how will you appear before him or what work will you do so that you may walk about undiscovered.

3.8.sa: सहदेव उवाच । गोसङ्ख्याता भविष्यामि विराटस्य महीपतेः । प्रतिषेद्धा च दोग्धा च सङ्ख्याने कुशलो गवाम् ॥८॥
3.8.en: Sahadeva said I shall be the counter of the cows of the king Virata; I am skilled in taming, milking and counting them.

3.9.sa: तन्तिपाल इति ख्यातो नाम्नाऽहं विदितस्त्वथ । निपुणं च चरिष्यामि व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः ॥९॥

3.10.sa: अहं हि सततं गोषु भवता प्रहितः पुरा । तत्र मे कौशलं सर्वमवबुद्धं विशाम्पते ॥१०॥
3.10.en: Very often was I formerly employed by you in looking after your cows. O Lord of the earth, all the arts that the business involves are known to me.

3.11.sa: लक्षणं चारतं चापि गवां यच्चापि मङ्गलम् । तत् सर्वं मे सुविदितमन्यच्चापि महीपते ॥११॥
3.11.en: 0 ruler of the earth, the nature, the characteristics and the favorable marks and other points regarding cows are well known to me.

3.12.sa: वृषभानपि जानामि राजन् पूजितलक्षणान् । येषां मूत्रमुपाघ्राय अपि वन्ध्या प्रसूयते ॥१२॥

3.13.sa: सोऽहमेवं चरिष्यामि प्रतिरत्र हि मे सदा । न च मां वेत्स्यते कश्चित् तोषयिष्ये च पार्थिवम् ॥१३॥
3.13.en: Thus shall I pass my days; there is always a delight for me in this work, and no one shall recognize me and moreover I will entertain the monarch.

3.14.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । इयं हि नः प्रिया भार्या प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी । मातेव परिपाल्या च पूज्या ज्येष्ठेव च स्वसा ॥१४॥
3.14.en: Yudhishthira said This is our beloved wife dearer even than life. Like a mother she is to be cherished and like an elder sister she is to be respected.

3.15.sa: केन स्म द्रौपदी कृष्णा कर्मणा विचरिष्यति । न हि किञ्चिद्विजानाति कर्म कर्तुं यथा स्त्रियः ॥१५॥
3.15.en: In what capacity will Krishna the daughter of Drupada, appear; like other women she does not know how to do any work.

3.16.sa: सुकुमारी च बाला च राजपुत्री यशस्विनी । पतिव्रता महाभागा कथं नु विचरिष्यति ॥१६॥
3.16.en: Tender and young is the king's daughter, endowed with eminence, devoted to her lords and highly virtuous; how will she pass her days?

3.17.sa: माल्यगन्धानलङ्कारान् वस्त्राणि विविधानि च । एतान्येवाभिजानाति यतो जाता हि भामिनी ॥१७॥
3.17.en: Since her very birth the handsome lady has only been accustomed to garlands, perfumes, ornaments and diverse kinds of robes.

3.18.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । सैरन्ध्र्यो रक्षिता लोकं भुजिष्याः सन्ति भारत । नैवमन्याः स्त्रियो यान्ति इति लोकस्य निश्चयः ॥१८॥

3.19.sa: साऽहं ब्रुवाणा सैरन्ध्री कुशला केशकर्मणि । युधिष्ठिरस्य गेहे वै द्रौपद्याः परिचारिका ॥१९॥
3.19.en: Draupadi said O Bharata, there is a class of maid-servants called Sairandhri employed in the service of others and it is the conviction of people that no (respectable) ladies will enter it.

3.20.sa: उषिताऽस्मीति वक्ष्यामि पृष्टा राज्ञा च भारत । आत्मगुप्ता चरिष्यामि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥२०॥

3.21.sa: सुदेष्णां प्रत्युपस्थास्ये राजभार्यां यशस्विनीम् । सा रक्षिष्यति मां प्राप्तां मा भूत् ते दुःखमीदृशम् ॥२१॥
3.21.en: I shall serve Shudeshna the reputed wife, of the king, and getting me, she will keep me. Let this anxiety of yours be set at rest.

3.22.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । कल्याणं भाषले कृष्णे कुले जाताऽसि भामिनि । न पापमभिजानासि साध्वी साधुव्रते स्थिता ॥२२॥
3.22.en: Yudhishthira said O Krishna, you have spoken well, O fair one, you are born in a noble family; chaste as you are and engaged in pursuit of pious vows you are a stranger to sin.

3.23.sa: यथा न दुर्हृदः पापा भवन्ति सुखिनः पुनः । कुर्यास्तत् त्वं हि कल्याणि लक्षयेयुर्न ते तथा ॥२३॥
3.23.en: O blessed one, you should behave yourself in such a way that the wicked and sinful men inay have no chance of deriving pleasure from looking at you.

4.1.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । कर्माण्युक्तानि युष्माभिर्यानि यानि करिष्यथ । मम चापि यथा बुद्धिरुचिता विधिनिश्चयात् ॥१॥
4.1.en: Yudhishthira said In consonance with the ordinance, the works which you will perform have been already described by you, and I have also said according to my discretion the office which I shall perform.

4.2.sa: पुरोहितोऽयमस्माकमग्निहोत्राणि रक्षतु । सूदपौरोगवैः सार्द्धं द्रुपदस्य निवेशने ॥२॥
4.2.en: Let this our priest go back to the house of Drupada with our charioteer and cooks, and preserve our Agnihotra fires.

4.3.sa: इन्द्रसेनमुखाश्चेमे रथानादाय केवलान् । यान्तु द्वारवतीं शीघ्रमिति मे वर्तते मतिः ॥३॥
4.3.en: Let these people with Indrasena as their head repair speedily with empty cars to the city of Amaravati. This is my wish.

4.4.sa: इमाश्च नार्यो द्रौपद्याः सर्वाश्च परिचारिकाः । पाञ्चालानेव गच्छन्तु सूदपौरोगवैः सह ॥४॥
4.4.en: Let all these attending maids of Draupadi go to the Panchalas with our charioteers and cooks.

4.5.sa: सर्वैरपि च वक्तव्यं न प्राज्ञायन्त पाण्डवाः । गता ह्यस्मानपाहाय सर्वे द्वैतवनादिति ॥५॥
4.5.en: All of them also must say this "we do not know the Pandavas, they have all departed from Dvaitavana leaving us alone here."

4.6.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवं तेऽन्योन्यमामन्त्र्य कर्माण्युक्त्वा पृथक् पृथक् । धौम्यमामन्त्रयामासुः स च तान् मन्त्रमब्रवीत्॥६॥
4.6.en: Vaishampayana said Thus having consulted one another and mentioned their own respective duties they asked the advice of Dhaumya and he also gave his advice.

4.7.sa: धौम्य उवाच । विहितं पाण्डवाः सर्वं ब्राह्मणेषु सुहृत्सु च । याने प्रहरणे चैव तथैवाग्निषु भारत ॥७॥
4.7.en: O Pandavas, you have made arrangements in regard to the Brahmanas, friends, weapons and also in regard to the fires.

4.8.sa: त्वया रक्षा विधातव्या कृष्णायाः फाल्गुनेन च । विदितं वो यथा सर्वं लोकवृत्तमिदं तव ॥८॥
4.8.en: You and Falguna (Arjuna) are to protect। Krishna. O kings, the characters of men are properly known to you all. Inspite of your knowledge, it behoves the friends to describe them out of their regard for you and that is reckoned as the everlasting virtue, pleasure and profit. Therefore I shall say something-you should attend.

4.9.sa: विदिते चापि वक्तव्यं सुहृद्भिरनुरागतः । एष धर्मश्च कामश्च अर्थश्चैव सनातनः ॥९॥
4.9.en: You and Falguna (Arjuna) are to protect। Krishna. O kings, the characters of men are properly known to you all. Inspite of your knowledge, it behoves the friends to describe them out of their regard for you and that is reckoned as the everlasting virtue, pleasure and profit. Therefore I shall say something-you should attend.

4.10.sa: अतोऽहमपि वक्ष्यामि हेतुमत्र निबोधत । हन्तेमां राजवसतिं राजपुत्रा ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥१०॥
4.10.en: You and Falguna (Arjuna) are to protect। Krishna. O kings, the characters of men are properly known to you all. Inspite of your knowledge, it behoves the friends to describe them out of their regard for you and that is reckoned as the everlasting virtue, pleasure and profit. Therefore I shall say something-you should attend.

4.11.sa: यथा राजकुलं प्राप्य सर्वान् दोषांस्तरिष्यथ । दुर्वसं चैव कौरव्य जानता राजवेश्मनि ॥११॥
4.11.en: Alas! it is woeful to stay with a king, I shall tell you. O princes, how you shall avert the calamities while residing in the royal premises. O Kauravas, whether respected or not, may you pass thus at the royal residence undiscovered by those who know you. Then in the fourteenth year you will act according to your own pleasure.

4.12.sa: अमानितेर्मानितैर्वा अज्ञातैः परिवत्सरम् । ततश्चतुर्दशे वर्षे चरिष्यथ यथासुखम् ॥१२॥
4.12.en: Alas! it is woeful to stay with a king, I shall tell you. O princes, how you shall avert the calamities while residing in the royal premises. O Kauravas, whether respected or not, may you pass thus at the royal residence undiscovered by those who know you. Then in the fourteenth year you will act according to your own pleasure.

4.13.sa: दृष्टद्वारो लभेद्द्रष्टुं राजस्वेषु न विश्वसेत् । तदेवासनमन्विच्छेद्यत्र नाभिपतेत् परः ॥१३॥
4.13.en: One ought to obtain previous permission should he want to appear before the king. As regards royal secrets one should not give credit when they are mentioned; one should rather court that seat where no one can defeat him.

4.14.sa: यो न यानं न पर्यङ्कं न पीठं न गजं रथम् । आरोहेत् सम्मतोऽस्मीति स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥१४॥
4.14.en: He alone can live in a royal residence who does not, with the confidence that he is a favorite, make use of the king's car, vehicle, or bedstead, or seat, or elephant or chariot.

4.15.sa: यत्र यत्रैनमासीनं शङ्केरन् दुष्टचारिणः । न तत्रोपविशेद्यो वै स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥१५॥
4.15.en: He alone can live in a royal house who sits on a seat the occupation of which cannot create any suspicion in the minds of the wicked.

4.16.sa: न चानुशिष्याद्राजानमपृच्छन्तं कदाचन । तूष्णीं त्वेनमुपासीत काले समभिपूजयेत् ॥१६॥
4.16.en: Unasked no one should even offer a counsel to the king; one should pay respect to never him with reticence and homage in time. Kings wish to have those who babble and hate counsellors who tell lies.

4.17.sa: असूयन्ति हि राजानो जनाननृतवादिनः । तथैव चावमन्यन्ते मन्त्रिणं वादिनं मृषा ॥१७॥
4.17.en: Unasked no one should even offer a counsel to the king; one should pay respect to never him with reticence and homage in time. Kings wish to have those who babble and hate counsellors who tell lies.

4.18.sa: नैषां दारेषु कुर्वीत मैत्रीं प्राज्ञः कदाचन । अन्तःपुरचरा ये च द्वेष्टि यानहिताश्च ये ॥१८॥
4.18.en: A wise man should contract friendship with the wife of the king nor with the other inmates of his seraglio, nor with those whom the despises and who are hostile to him.

4.19.sa: विदिते चास्य कुर्वीत कार्याणि सुलघून्यपि । एवं विचरतो राज्ञि न क्षतिर्जायते क्वचित् ॥१९॥
4.19.en: One about the king should perform the act, however greatly insignificant may be in his presence. There would be no harm to him should he behave himself towards the king in the way.

4.20.sa: गच्छन्नपि परां भूमिमपृष्टो ह्यनियोजितः । जात्यन्ध इव मन्येत मर्यादामनुचिन्तयन् ॥२०॥
4.20.en: Holding even the highest office one should, until he is asked or commanded, regard himself as born-blind in consideration of the dignity of his position).

4.21.sa: न हि पुत्रं न नप्तारं न भ्रातरमरिन्दमाः । समतिक्रान्तमर्यादं पूजयन्ति नराधिपाः ॥२१॥
4.21.en: Because the kings show no consideration even to their sons, grandsons and brothers when they are found to disregarded their dignity.

4.22.sa: यत्नाच्चोपचरेदेनमग्निवद्देववत्त्विह । अनृतेनोपचीर्णो हि हन्यादेव न संशयः ॥२२॥
4.22.en: In this world a king should be carefully served like the fire-god or any other deity; one that plays false to the king is killed by him; this admits of no doubt.

4.23.sa: यद्यद्भर्ताऽनुयुञ्जीत तत् तदेवानुवर्तयेत् । प्रमादमवलेपं च कोपं च परिवर्जयेत् ॥२३॥
4.23.en: One should follow what the master directs, and renounce carelessness, pride and anger.

4.24.sa: समर्थनासु सर्वासु हितं च प्रियमेव च । संवर्णयेत् तदेवास्य प्रियादपि हितं भवेत् ॥२४॥
4.24.en: After carefully pondering over all things one should relate to the king what is both agreeable and profitable; but one must say what is beneficial in preference to what is merely agreeable.

4.25.sa: अनुकूलो भवेच्चास्य सर्वार्थेषु कथासु च । अप्रियं चाहितं यत् स्यात्तदस्मै नानुवर्णयेत् ॥२५॥
4.25.en: In all matters and works one ought to be well-disposed towards the king and should never relate to him what is disagreeable and unprofitable.

4.26.sa: नाहमस्य प्रियोऽस्मीति मत्वा सेवेत पण्डितः । अप्रमत्तश्च सततं हितं कुर्यात् प्रियं च यत् ॥२६॥
4.26.en: Thinking that one is not his favourite, one should serve the king, always do him what is good and pleasant without neglect.

4.27.sa: नास्यानिष्टानि सेवेत नाहितैः सह संवदेत् । स्वस्थानान्न विकम्पेत स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥२७॥
4.27.en: He alone can live in a royal house who does not swerve from his place, nor does him any injury, nor associates with those who are unfriendly to him (the king).

4.28.sa: दक्षिणं वाऽथ वामं वा पार्श्वमासीत पण्डितः । रक्षिणां ह्यात्तशस्त्राणां स्थानं पश्चाद्विधीयते ॥२८॥
4.28.en: Learned men should sit either on the right or the left side of the king, because the place behind him is reverend, for the guards furnished with arms and seats in his front are always forbidden.

4.29.sa: नित्यं हि प्रतिषिद्धं तु पुरस्तादासनं महत् । न च संदर्शने किञ्चित् प्रवृत्तमपि सञ्जयेत् ॥२९॥
4.29.en: Learned men should sit either on the right or the left side of the king, because the place behind him is reverend, for the guards furnished with arms and seats in his front are always forbidden.

4.30.sa: अपि ह्येतद्दरिद्राणां व्यलीकस्थानमुत्तमम् । न मृषाऽभिहितं राज्ञां मनुष्येषु प्रकाशयेत् ॥३०॥
4.30.en: No one should give publicity to what transpires in the very presence of the king because even for those who are very favourite it is looked upon as the height of impertinence.

4.31.sa: असूयन्ति हि राजानो नराननृतवादिनः । तथैव चावमन्यन्ते नरान् पण्डितमानिनः ॥३१॥
4.31.en: One should not reveal to others any lie, that has been told by the king for he is annoyed with those who report his lies and also despise those who regard themselves as learned.

4.32.sa: शूरोऽस्मीति न दृप्तः स्याद्बुद्धिमानिति वा पुनः । प्रियमेवाचरन् राज्ञः प्रियो भवति भोगवान् ॥३२॥
4.32.en: A person that does not take pride in thinking "I am heroic and intelligent," and conducts himself agreeably to the wishes of the king is worthy of royal favour and amenities of life.

4.33.sa: ऐश्वर्यं प्राप्य दुष्प्रापं प्रियं प्राप्य च राजतः । अप्रमत्तो भवेद्राज्ञः प्रियेषु च हितेषु च ॥३३॥
4.33.en: A person, obtaining from the king wealth and other agreeable things hard to acquire, must employ himself assiduously in doing for him what is both pleasant and profitable.

4.34.sa: यस्य कोपो महाबाधः प्रसादश्च महाफलः । कस्तस्य मनसाऽपीच्छेदनर्थं प्राज्ञसंमतः ॥३४॥

4.35.sa: न चोष्ठौ न भुजौ जानू न च वाक्यं समाक्षिपेत् । सदा वातं च वाचं च ष्ठीवनं चाचरेच्छनैः ॥३५॥
4.35.en: In the presence of the king no one should move his lips, anus and thighs and one should speak gently, spit slowly and break wind softly.

4.66.sa: हास्यवस्तुषु चान्यस्य वर्तमानेषु केषुचित् । नातिगाढं प्रहृष्येत न चाप्युन्मत्तवद्धसेत् ॥६६॥
4.66.en: In the presence of the king if any laughable matter is mooted, a person should not enjoy it with the utmost reserve, nor should he laugh like a maniac.

4.67.sa: न चातिधैर्येण चरेद्गुरुतां हि व्रजेत् ततः । स्मितं तु मृदुपूर्वेण दर्शयेत प्रसादजम् ॥६७॥
4.67.en: No person should restrain himself to the reserve, for in that case he should lead him to an unnecessary gravity. But he should smile with modesty and without betraying any mistaken interest as regards real cause of the mirth. He that is always on his guard, and is neither exalted by reward nor feels wronged by disgrace, is alone worthy of residing in a royal palace.

4.68.sa: लाभे न हर्षयेद्यस्तु न व्यथेद्योऽवमानितः । असंमूढश्च यो नित्यं स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥६८॥

4.39.sa: राजानं राजपुत्रं वा संवर्णयति यः सदा । अमात्यः पण्डितो भूत्वा स चिरं तिष्ठते प्रियः ॥३९॥
4.39.en: The learned courtier who always describes the king and princes in suitable terms can stay long as a favorite in a royal residence.

4.40.sa: प्रगृहीतश्च योऽमात्यो निगृहीतस्त्वकारणैः । न निर्वदति राजानं लभते संपदं पुनः ॥४०॥
4.40.en: The favored counsel or who refrains from speaking ill of the king, if ever deprived of royal grace for some causes, regains his prosperity.

4.41.sa: प्रत्यक्षं च परोक्षं च गुणवादी विचक्षणः । उपजीवी भवेद्राज्ञो विषये योऽपि वा भवेत् ॥४१॥
4.41.en: The person, who earns his livelihood through the favour of the king or lives in his dominion, if prudent, must eulogize him both in his presence and behind him.

4.42.sa: अमात्यो हि बलाद्भोक्तुं राजानं प्रार्थयेत यः । न स तिष्ठेच्चिरं स्थानं गच्छेच्च प्राणसंशयम् ॥४२॥
4.42.en: The courtier, who desires to gain his end by using force on the king, does not hold his place long and incurs the danger of losing his life.

4.43.sa: श्रेयः सदाऽऽत्मनो दृष्ट्वा परं राज्ञा न संवदेत् । विशेषयेच्च राजानं योग्यभूमिषु सर्वदा ॥४३॥
4.43.en: No person should, for the sake of his own interest, hold communion with the king's enemies, nor should one always come forward to instruct the king on all occasions, however suitable they may be.

4.44.sa: अम्लानो बलवान् शूरश्छायेवानुगतः सदा । सत्यवादी मृदुर्दान्तः स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥४४॥
4.44.en: He, who is cheerful mighty, brave, truthful, gentle and of subdued passions, and who always follows the king like a shadow, is alone capable of living in a royal palace.

4.45.sa: अन्यस्मिन् प्रेष्यमाणे तु पुरस्ताद्यः समुत्पतेत् । अहं किं करवाणीति स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥४५॥
4.45.en: He who steps forward saying "pray, I will do it," when another is entrusted with a work, is alone worthy of living in a royal residence.

4.46.sa: आन्तरे चैव बाह्ये च राज्ञा यश्चाथ सर्वदा । आदिष्टो नैव कम्पेत स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥४६॥
4.46.en: He who never fears when commanded by the king to do work, wither in or out of his dominion, is alone fit for living in the royal premises.

4.47.sa: यो वै गृहेभ्यः प्रवसन् प्रियाणां नानुसंस्मरेत् । दुःखेन सुखमन्विच्छेत् स राजवसतिं वसेत् ॥४७॥
4.47.en: He alone, can live in a royal palace, who, although staying away from home, never remembers his beloved ones and suffers misery in the expectation of future happiness.

4.48.sa: समवेषं न कुर्वीत नोच्चैः सन्निहितो वसेत् । न मन्त्रं बहुधा कुर्यादेवं राज्ञः प्रियो भवेत् ॥४८॥
4.48.en: One should not dress like the king, should not burst out into a loud laughter in the presence of the king, nor should one divulge royal counsels; behaving in this way one may become favourite of the king.

4.49.sa: न कर्मणि नियुक्तः सन् धनं किञ्चिदपि स्पृशेत् । प्राप्नोति हि हरन् द्रव्यं बन्धनं यदि वा वधम् ॥४९॥
4.49.en: Appointed to a work one should not lay hands on money; if one does it he runs the risk of being imprisoned or put to death.

4.50.sa: यानं वस्त्रमलङ्कारं यच्चान्यत् सम्प्रयच्छति । तदेव धारयेन्नित्यमेवं प्रियतरो भवेत् ॥५०॥
4.50.en: One should always use the cars, the robes, the ornaments and other things which the king bestows; and by doing this one should win the royal favour.

4.51.sa: एवं संयम्य चित्तानि यत्नतः पाण्डुनन्दनाः । संवत्सरमिमं तात तथाशीला बुभूषत । अथ स्वविषयं प्राप्य यथाकामं करिष्यथ ॥५१॥
4.51.en: O sons of Pandu, thus controlling your minds with great efforts, spend, O children, this year, adorned with good manners. Then regaining your kingdom you may act according to your own pleasure.

4.52.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । अनुशिष्टाः स्म भद्रं ते नैतद्वक्ताऽस्ति कश्चन । कुन्तीमृते मातरं नो विदुरं वा महामतिम् ॥५२॥
4.52.en: Yudhishthira said By you we have been instructed; let good betide you. There is no one else who could say so except our mother Kunti and the highininded Vidura,

4.53.sa: यदेवानन्तरं कार्यं तद्भवान् कर्तुमर्हति । तारणायास्य दुःखस्य प्रस्थानाय जयाय च ॥५३॥

4.54.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्तस्ततो राज्ञा धौम्योऽथ द्विजसत्तमः । अकरोद्विधिवत् सर्वं प्रस्थाने यद्विधीयते ॥५४॥
4.54.en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by the king, Dhaumya, the best of the twice-born, arranged all that was necessary for their departure.

4.55.sa: तेषां समिध्य तानग्नीन् मन्त्रवच्च जुहाव सः । समृद्धिवृद्धिलाभाय पृथिवीविजयाय च ॥५५॥
4.55.en: Lighting up fires, he offered with Mantras the oblations on them that they might gain prosperity and success and spread their conquest all over the earth.

4.56.sa: अग्नीन् प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ब्राह्मणांश्च तपोधनान् । याज्ञसेनीं पुरस्कृत्य षडेवाथ प्रवव्रजुः ॥५६॥
4.56.en: Then the six, having circumbulated the fire and the Brahmanas whose only treasure is austerity, departed with Yajnseni ahead of them.

4.57.sa: गतेषु तेषु वीरेषु धौम्योऽथ जपतां वरः । अग्निहोत्राण्युपादाय पाञ्चालानभ्यगच्छत ॥५७॥
4.57.en: These heroes having departed, Dhaumya, the great among ascetics, took their Agnihotra fires and started for Panchalas.

4.58.sa: इन्द्रसेनादयश्चैव यथोक्ताः प्राप्य यादवान् । रथानश्वांश्च रक्षन्तः सुखमूषुः सुसंवृताः ॥५८॥
4.58.en: Indrasena and others as mentioned before, after having gone to the Yadavas spent their days happily and privately in looking after the horses and cars of the Pandavas.

5.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ते वीरा बद्धनिस्त्रिंशास्तथा बद्धकलापिनः । बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणाः कालिन्दीमभितो ययुः ॥१॥
5.1.en: Vaishampayana said Those heroes equipped with swords and finger-protectors made of Iguna leather and furnished with weapons and quivers proceeded in the direction of the river Kalindi.

5.2.sa: ततस्ते दक्षिणं तीरमन्वगच्छन् पदातयः । निवृत्तवनवासा हि स्वराष्ट्रं प्रेप्सवस्तदा । वसन्तो गिरिदुर्गेषु वनदुर्गेषु धन्विनः ॥२॥
5.2.en: Then they desirous of regaining their own kingdom put an end to their forest-life and walked on foot to the southern bank of the river (Kalindi).

5.3.sa: विध्यन्तो मृगजातानि महेष्वासा महाबलाः । उत्तरेण दशार्णांस्ते पञ्चालान् दक्षिणेन च ॥३॥
5.3.en: Having put an end to their forest life, those sons of Pandu, wielders of great bows, endued with great strength, equipped with swords, wearing beards and looking wan proceeded through Yakrilloma and and Shurasena, and leaving the country of Panchalas on the south and that of Dasharna on the north, dwelling (sometimes) in hill-forts and forest fastness and killing the deer (in their journey) entered Matsya's dominions giving out themselves as hunters.

5.4.sa: अन्तरेण यकृल्लोमान् शूरसेनांश्च पाण्डवाः । लुब्धा ब्रुवाणा मत्स्यस्य विषयं प्राविशन् वनात् ॥४॥
5.4.en: Having put an end to their forest life, those sons of Pandu, wielders of great bows, endued with great strength, equipped with swords, wearing beards and looking wan proceeded through Yakrilloma and and Shurasena, and leaving the country of Panchalas on the south and that of Dasharna on the north, dwelling (sometimes) in hill-forts and forest fastness and killing the deer (in their journey) entered Matsya's dominions giving out themselves as hunters.

5.5.sa: धन्विनो बद्धनिस्त्रिंशा विवर्णाः श्मश्रुधारिणः । ततो जनपदं प्राप्य कृष्णा राजानमब्रवीत् ॥५॥
5.5.en: Having put an end to their forest life, those sons of Pandu, wielders of great bows, endued with great strength, equipped with swords, wearing beards and looking wan proceeded through Yakrilloma and and Shurasena, and leaving the country of Panchalas on the south and that of Dasharna on the north, dwelling (sometimes) in hill-forts and forest fastness and killing the deer (in their journey) entered Matsya's dominions giving out themselves as hunters.

5.6.sa: पश्यैकपद्यो दृश्यन्ते क्षेत्राणि विविधानि च । व्यक्तं दूरे विराटस्य राजधानी भविष्यति । वसामेहापरां रात्रि बलवान् मे परिश्रमः ॥६॥
5.6.en: Having arrived at the country Krishna said to the king-“Look here, there are seen many foot-paths and these indicate the existence of Virata's metropolis in the distance. Spend the remaining part of the night here for great is my fatigue."

5.7.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । धनञ्जय समुद्यम्य पाञ्चालीं वह भारत । राजधान्यां निवत्स्यामो विमुक्ताश्च वनादितः ॥७॥
5.7.en: Yudhishthira said 0 Dhananjaya, o Bharata, take up Panchali and carry her. As we are come out of this forest we shall settle ourselves in the capital.

5.8.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तामादायार्जुनस्तूर्णं द्रौपदीं गजराडिव । संप्राप्य नगराभ्याशमवतारयदर्जुनः ॥८॥

5.9.sa: स राजधानीं संप्राप्य कौन्तेयोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत् । क्वायु‌धानि समासज्ज्य प्रवेक्ष्यामः पुरं वयम् ॥९॥

5.10.sa: सायुधाश्च प्रवेक्ष्यामो वयं तात पुरं यदि । समुद्वेगं जनस्यास्य करिष्यामो न संशयः ॥१०॥
5.10.en: If we enter the city with our weapons we shall undoubtedly cause terror to the citizens. Moreover your gigantic bow, the Gandiva, is known to the people of the world, therefore, if we enter the city with that weapon, the people will undoubtedly cognizant us very soon.

5.11.sa: गाण्डीवं च महद्गाढं लोके च विदितं नृणाम् । तच्चेदायुधमादाय गच्छामो नगरं वयम् । क्षिप्रमस्मान्विजानीयुर्मनुष्या नात्र संशयः ॥११॥
5.11.en: If we enter the city with our weapons we shall undoubtedly cause terror to the citizens. Moreover your gigantic bow, the Gandiva, is known to the people of the world, therefore, if we enter the city with that weapon, the people will undoubtedly cognizant us very soon.

5.12.sa: ततो द्वादश वर्षाणि प्रवेष्टव्यं वने पुनः । एकस्मिन्नपि विज्ञाते प्रतिज्ञातं हि नस्तथा ॥१२॥
5.12.en: And if any one of us be discovered we hall have to enter the forest again for another twelve years, for that has truly been our promise.

5.13.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । इयं कूटे मनुष्येन्द्र गहना महती शमी । भीमशाखा दुरारोहा श्मशानस्य समीपतः ॥१३॥

5.14.sa: न चापि विद्यते कश्चिन्मनुष्य इति मे मतिः । योऽस्मान्निदधतो द्रष्टा भवेच्छस्त्राणि पाण्डवाः ॥१४॥
5.14.en: Nor is their any human being I believe who can observe us, O Pandava, depositing our weapons.

5.15.sa: उत्पथे हि वने जाता मृगव्यालनिषेविते । समीपे च श्मशानस्य गहनस्य विशेषतः ॥१५॥
5.15.en: Remote from the road there grows the tree in the forest inhabited by beasts and snakes and it stands beside a dismal cremation ground,

5.16.sa: समाधायायुधं शम्यां गच्छामो नगरं प्रति । एवमत्र यथायोगं विहरिष्याम भारत ॥१६॥
5.16.en: Having thus deposited our weapons on the Shami tree we shall, O Bharata, go to the city and pass our days there in style befitting us.

5.17.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्त्वा स राजानं धर्मराजं युधिष्ठिरम् । प्रचक्रमे निधानाय शस्त्राणां भरतर्षभ ॥१७॥
5.17.en: Vaishampayana said Having spoken thus the king Yudhishthira, the virtuous Arjuna, O best of the Bharata race, prepared for putting aside the weapons on that tree. W to

5.18.sa: येन देवान् मनुष्यांश्च सर्वांश्चैकरथोऽजयत् । स्फीतान् जनपदांश्चान्यानजयत् कुरुपुङ्गवः ॥१८॥
5.18.en: Pritha's son, the best of the Kurus, loosened the string of the large and tremendous Gandiva, capable of producing a deeply terrific twang, of destroying the mighty hosts of enemies and by which he, on a single car, had conquered all the gods and men and many opulent countries.

5.19.sa: तदुदारं महाघोषं संपन्नबलसूदनम् । अपज्यमकरोत् पार्थो गाण्डीवं सुभयङ्करम् ॥१९॥
5.19.en: Pritha's son, the best of the Kurus, loosened the string of the large and tremendous Gandiva, capable of producing a deeply terrific twang, of destroying the mighty hosts of enemies and by which he, on a single car, had conquered all the gods and men and many opulent countries.

5.20.sa: येन वीरः कुरुक्षेत्रमभ्यरक्षत् परन्तपः । अमुञ्चद्धनुषस्तस्य ज्यामक्षय्यां युधिष्ठिरः ॥२०॥
5.20.en: The warlike Yudhishthira, the chastiser of enemies, loosened the undecaying string of bow with which he had protected the field of the Kurus (Kurukshetra).

5.21.sa: पाञ्चालान् येन सङ्ग्रामे भीमसेनोऽजयत् प्रभुः । प्रत्यषेधद्बहूनेकः सपत्नांश्चैव दिग्जये ॥२१॥
5.21.en: The mighty Bhimasena unfastened the string of the bow with which the sinless one had conquered the Panchalas in fight, defeated the lord of Sindhu, opposed many of his foes alone at the time of spreading his conquest in all directions and hearing whose twang like the splitting of a mountain, or like the roar of the thunder, the enemies had fled from the field.

5.22.sa: निशम्य यस्य विस्फारं व्यद्रवन्त रणात् परे । पर्वतस्येव दीर्णस्य विस्फोटमशनेरिव ॥२२॥
5.22.en: The mighty Bhimasena unfastened the string of the bow with which the sinless one had conquered the Panchalas in fight, defeated the lord of Sindhu, opposed many of his foes alone at the time of spreading his conquest in all directions and hearing whose twang like the splitting of a mountain, or like the roar of the thunder, the enemies had fled from the field.

5.23.sa: सैन्धवं येन राजानं पर्यामृषितवानथ । ज्यापाशं धनुषस्त्स्य भीमसेनोऽवतारयत् ॥२३॥
5.23.en: The mighty Bhimasena unfastened the string of the bow with which the sinless one had conquered the Panchalas in fight, defeated the lord of Sindhu, opposed many of his foes alone at the time of spreading his conquest in all directions and hearing whose twang like the splitting of a mountain, or like the roar of the thunder, the enemies had fled from the field.

5.24.sa: अजयत् पश्चिमामाशां धनुषा येन पाण्डवः । माद्रीपुत्रो महाबाहुस्ताम्रास्यो मितभाषिता ॥२४॥
5.24.en: The heroic son of Pandu by Madri, having large arms, copper complexion, frugal speech and immense prowess in the field of battle, known by the name Nakula by virtue of his matchless beauty in the family, took away the string of his bow with which he had conquered all the regions of the west.

5.25.sa: तस्य मोर्वीमपाकर्षच्छूरः संक्रन्दनो युधि । कुले नास्ति समो रूपे यस्येति नकुलः स्मृतः ॥२५॥

5.26.sa: दक्षिणां दक्षिणाचारो दिशं येनाजयत् प्रभुः । अपज्यमकरोद्वीरः सहदेवस्तदायुधम् ॥२६॥
5.26.en: The heroic Sahadeva of noble conduct rendered his bow stringless with which he made conquests in the southern regions.

5.27.sa: खड्गांश्च दीप्तान् दीर्घांश्च कलापांश्च महाधनान् । विपाठान् क्षुरधारांश्च धनुर्भिर्निदधुः सह ॥२७॥
5.27.en: Along with their bows they deposited their long and shining swords, quivers of great value, and arrows with edges as sharp as those of razors.

5.28.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथान्वशासन्नकुलं कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । आरुह्येमां शमीं वीर धनूंष्येतानि निक्षिप ॥२८॥
5.28.en: Vaishampayana said: Then Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, commanded Nakula-"O heroic one ascend this Shami tree and deposit those bows thereon.”

5.29.sa: तामुपारुह्य नकुलो धनूंषि निदधे स्वयम् । यानि तस्या वकाशानि दिव्यरूपाण्यमन्यत ॥२९॥
5.29.en: Having ascended the Shami tree Nakula himself placed these bows. He tied them with strong ropes with those parts of the tree which he thought to be well-formed and where the rain in an oblique lines.

5.30.sa: यत्र चापश्यत स वै तिरोवर्षाणि वर्षति । तत्र तानि दृढैः पाशैः सुगाढं पर्यबन्धत ॥३०॥
5.30.en: Having ascended the Shami tree Nakula himself placed these bows. He tied them with strong ropes with those parts of the tree which he thought to be well-formed and where the rain in an oblique lines.

5.31.sa: शरीरं च मृतस्यैकं समबध्नन्त पाण्डवाः । विवर्जयिष्यन्ति नरा दूरादेव शमीमिमाम् ॥३१॥

5.32.sa: आबद्धं शवमवेति गन्धमाघ्राय पूतिकम् । अशीतिशतवर्षेयं माता न इति वादिनः ॥३२॥
5.32.en: After having finished the fastening they gave out-"This is our mother, one hundred and eight years old. This is our ancestral custom, observed by our forefathers."

5.33.sa: कुलधर्मोऽयमस्माकं पूर्वैराचरितोऽपि वा । समासज्ज्याथ वृक्षेऽस्मिन्निति वै व्याहरन्ति ते ॥३३॥
5.33.en: After having finished the fastening they gave out-"This is our mother, one hundred and eight years old. This is our ancestral custom, observed by our forefathers."

5.34.sa: आगोपालाविपालेभ्य आचक्षाणाः परंतपाः । आजग्मुर्नगराभ्याशं पार्थाः शत्रुनिबर्हणाः ॥३४॥
5.34.en: Having said this to the cow-herds and shipherds Pritha's sons, the subduers of enemies, approached the capital.

5.35.sa: जयो जयन्तो विजयो जयत्सेनो जयद्वलः । इति गुह्यानि नामानि चक्रे तेषां युधिष्ठिरः ॥३५॥
5.35.en: (In order to live incognito) Yudhishthira selected for himself and his brothers these false names-Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Jayatsena and Jayadbala.

5.36.sa: ततो यथाप्रतिज्ञाभिः प्राविशन्नगरं महत् । अज्ञातचर्यां वत्स्यन्तो राष्ट्रे वर्षं त्रयोदशम् ॥३६॥

6.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । विराटनगरं रम्यं गच्छमानो युधिष्ठिरः । अस्तुवन्मनसा देवीं दुर्गां त्रिभुवनेश्वरीम् ॥१॥

6.2.sa: यशोदागर्भसंभूतां नारायणवरप्रियाम् । नन्द‌गोपकुले जातां मङ्गल्यां कुलवर्धिनीम् ॥२॥

6.3.en: Vaishampayana said While Yudhishthira was about to enter the beautiful city of Virata, he mentally hymned the divine Durga, the goddess of the three worlds, born of the womb of Yashoda, very dear to Narayana, born in the family of Nandagopa, bestower of prosperity capable of enhancing a family, the terror of Kansa, slayer of Asuras, the goddess who ascended the welkin when dashed on a stone slate. Vasudeva's sister, adorned with celestial garlands, attired in celestial apparel and holding sword and scimitar capable of rescuing worshippers, like a cow in the mire, who for the purpose of getting themselves released of the burden, invoke the aid of that giver of eternal blessing.

6.4.sa: वासुदेवस्य भगिनीं दिव्यमाल्यविभूषिताम् । दिव्याम्बरधरां देवीं खड्गखेटकधारिणीम् ॥४॥
6.4.en: Vaishampayana said While Yudhishthira was about to enter the beautiful city of Virata, he mentally hymned the divine Durga, the goddess of the three worlds, born of the womb of Yashoda, very dear to Narayana, born in the family of Nandagopa, bestower of prosperity capable of enhancing a family, the terror of Kansa, slayer of Asuras, the goddess who ascended the welkin when dashed on a stone slate. Vasudeva's sister, adorned with celestial garlands, attired in celestial apparel and holding sword and scimitar capable of rescuing worshippers, like a cow in the mire, who for the purpose of getting themselves released of the burden, invoke the aid of that giver of eternal blessing.

6.5.sa: भारावतरणे पुण्ये ये स्मरन्ति सदाशिवाम् । तान् वै तारयते पापात् पङ्के गामिव दुर्बलाम् ॥५॥
6.5.en: Vaishampayana said While Yudhishthira was about to enter the beautiful city of Virata, he mentally hymned the divine Durga, the goddess of the three worlds, born of the womb of Yashoda, very dear to Narayana, born in the family of Nandagopa, bestower of prosperity capable of enhancing a family, the terror of Kansa, slayer of Asuras, the goddess who ascended the welkin when dashed on a stone slate. Vasudeva's sister, adorned with celestial garlands, attired in celestial apparel and holding sword and scimitar capable of rescuing worshippers, like a cow in the mire, who for the purpose of getting themselves released of the burden, invoke the aid of that giver of eternal blessing.

6.6.sa: स्तोतुं प्रचक्रमे भूयो विविधैः स्तोत्रसंभवैः । आमन्त्र्य दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी राजा देवीं सहानुजः ॥६॥

6.7.sa: नमोऽस्तु वरदे कृष्णे कुमारि ब्रह्मचारिणि । बालार्कसदृशाकारे पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानने ॥७॥
6.7.en: I salute you, O bestower of boons, O you that are the same as Krishna, O maiden ( your Chaya, O your that have a form bright as the newly risen sun, and a face as beautiful as the full moon itself.

6.8.sa: चतुर्भुजे चतुर्वक्त्रे पीनश्रोणिपयोधरे । मयूरपिच्छवलये केयूराङ्गदधारिणि । भासि देवि यथा पद्मा नारायणपरिग्रहः ॥८॥
6.8.en: I salute you, O you of four hands and four faces, O you that have large hips and a very high-boom, O you that wears bangles and bears arınlets.

6.9.sa: स्वरूपं ब्रह्मचर्यं च विशदं तत्र खेचरि । कृष्णच्छविसमा कृष्णा संकर्षणसमानना ॥९॥
6.9.en: O goddess you appear like Padma the consort of Narayana, O you ranger in the sky, your Brahmacharya and the real forms are both without a spot.

6.10.sa: बिभ्रती विपुलौ बाहू शक्रध्वजसमुच्छ्रयौ । पात्री च पङ्कजी घण्टी स्त्रीविशुद्धा च या भुवि ॥१०॥
6.10.en: O goddess, you appear with a countenance that vies with the moon, vith a pair of well shaped ears decorated with excellent rings, having a pair of large arms like Indra's pole; you are the only female in the world endowed with the attributes of piety, purity-you are the one holding a vessel a lotus, a bell, a noose, a bow and a large discus and various other weapons.

6.11.sa: पाशं धनुर्महाचक्रं विविधान्यायुधानि च । कुण्डलाभ्यां सुपूर्णाभ्यां कर्णाभ्यां च विभूषिता ॥११॥
6.11.en: O goddess, you appear with a countenance that vies with the moon, vith a pair of well shaped ears decorated with excellent rings, having a pair of large arms like Indra's pole; you are the only female in the world endowed with the attributes of piety, purity-you are the one holding a vessel a lotus, a bell, a noose, a bow and a large discus and various other weapons.

6.12.sa: चन्द्रविस्पर्द्धिना देवि मुखेन त्वं विराजसे । मुकुटेन विचित्रेण केशबन्धेन शोभिना ॥१२॥
6.12.en: O goddess, you appear with a countenance that vies with the moon, vith a pair of well shaped ears decorated with excellent rings, having a pair of large arms like Indra's pole; you are the only female in the world endowed with the attributes of piety, purity-you are the one holding a vessel a lotus, a bell, a noose, a bow and a large discus and various other weapons.

6.13.sa: भुजङ्गाभोगवासेन श्रोणिसूत्रेण राजता । विभ्राजसे चाबद्धेन भोगेनेवेह मन्दरः ॥१३॥
6.13.en: With a beautiful crown and graceful tresses, with dresses made of the hoods of serpents and an ornament fascinating your hip, you appear to be like the mount Mandara girded with serpents; also you shine with peacock-plumes standing high on your crest.

6.14.sa: ध्वजेन शिखिपिच्छानामुच्छ्रितेन विराजसे । कौमारं व्रतमास्थाय त्रिदिवं पावितं त्वया॥१४॥
6.14.en: With a beautiful crown and graceful tresses, with dresses made of the hoods of serpents and an ornament fascinating your hip, you appear to be like the mount Mandara girded with serpents; also you shine with peacock-plumes standing high on your crest.

6.15.sa: तेन त्वं स्तूयसे देवि त्रिदशैः पूज्यसेऽपि च । त्रैलोक्यरक्षणार्थाय महिषासुरनाशिनि । प्रसन्ना मे सुरश्रेष्ठे दयां कुरु शिवा भव॥१५॥
6.15.en: For the protection of the three worlds, you have slain the demon Mahisha (buffalo); O foremost of deities, be propitious to me; give me your grace and be the cause of my wellbeing.

6.16.sa: जया त्वं विजया चैव सङ्ग्रामे च जयप्रदा । ममापि विजयं देहि वरदा त्वं च साम्प्रतम् ॥१६॥
6.16.en: You are Jaya and Vijaya and capable of giving victory in battle, as you are also capable of granting boons, now be pleased to grant me victory.

6.17.sa: विन्ध्ये चैव नगश्रेष्ठे तव स्थानं हि शाश्वतम् । कालि कालि महाकालि सीधुमांसपशुप्रिये ॥१७॥

6.18.sa: कृतानुयात्रा भूतैस्त्वं वरदा कामचारिणि । भारावतारे ये च त्वां संस्मरिष्यन्ति मानवाः ॥१८॥
6.18.en: O giver of boon, capable of ranging every where at will, you are followed by celestials beings (in your journey). Persons who, for the purpose of shaking off their burdens, bow down to, or call upon, you in the morning on earth, attain all either in respect of children or riches. O Durga, as you rescue people from danger, you are called by them Durga.

6.19.sa: प्रणमन्ति च ये त्वां हि प्रभाते तु नरा भुवि । न तेषां दुर्लभं किञ्चित् पुत्रतो धनतोऽपि वा ॥१९॥
6.19.en: O giver of boon, capable of ranging every where at will, you are followed by celestials beings (in your journey). Persons who, for the purpose of shaking off their burdens, bow down to, or call upon, you in the morning on earth, attain all either in respect of children or riches. O Durga, as you rescue people from danger, you are called by them Durga.

6.20.sa: दुर्गात् तारयसे दुर्गे तत् त्वं दुर्गा स्मृता जनैः । कान्तारेष्ववसन्नानां मग्नानां च महार्णवे ॥२०॥
6.20.en: O giver of boon, capable of ranging every where at will, you are followed by celestials beings (in your journey). Persons who, for the purpose of shaking off their burdens, bow down to, or call upon, you in the morning on earth, attain all either in respect of children or riches. O Durga, as you rescue people from danger, you are called by them Durga.

6.21.sa: दस्युभिर्वा निरुद्धानां त्वं गतिः परमा नृणाम् । जलप्रतरणे चैव कान्तारेष्वटवीषु च ॥२१॥
6.21.en: You are the greatest refuge of people who are groping in the wilderness, getting drowned in the great ocean, and are taken captives by high-way-men.

6.22.sa: ये स्मरन्ति महादेवि न च सीदन्ति ते नराः । त्वं कीर्तिः श्रीर्धृतिः सिद्धिर्ह्रीर्विद्या सन्ततिर्मतिः ॥२२॥
6.22.en: 0 great goddess, the persons who remember you in the crossing of waters and in the forest and wilderness are never afflicted with calamity.

6.23.sa: सन्ध्या रात्रिः प्रभा निद्रा ज्योत्स्ना कान्तिः क्षमा दया । नृणां च बन्धनं मोहं पुत्रनाशं धनञ्जयम् ॥२३॥
6.23.en: O great fame, and prosperity, you are fortitude and success, you are modesty and knowledge, you are offspring and intellect, you are evening and night, you are light and sleep, you are lunar beam and beauty, and you are forgiveness and mercy.

6.24.sa: व्याधिं मृत्युं भयं चैव पूजिता नाशयिष्यसि । सोऽहं राज्यात् परिभ्रष्टः शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नवान्॥२४॥
6.24.en: When worshipped, you remove men's fetters ignorance, loss of sons, loss of wealth and disease, death and dread.

6.25.sa: प्रणतश्च यथा मूर्ध्ना तव देवि सुरेश्वरि । त्राहि मां पद्मपत्राक्षि सत्ये सत्या भवस्व नः ॥२५॥
6.25.en: I have been deprived of my kingdom and seek your refuge. O supreme goddess, I make obeisance to you with bended head.

6.26.sa: शरणं भव मे दुर्गे शरण्ये भक्तवत्सले । एवं स्तुता हि सा देवी दर्शयामास पाण्डवम् ॥२६॥
6.26.en: O possessor of eyes like the petals of lotuses, be truth to us who are seeking after truth. O Durga, O refuge of all, O affectionate to devotees, be pleased to grant me protection.

6.27.sa: उपगम्य तु राजानमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् । देव्युवाच । शृणु राजन् महाबाहो मदीयं वचनं प्रभो ॥२७॥
6.27.en: Thus praised the goddess showed herself to the Pandavas and having addressed him thus said.

6.28.sa: भविष्यत्यचिरादेव संग्रामे विजयस्तव । मम प्रसादान्निर्जित्य हत्वा कौरववाहिनीम् ॥२८॥
6.28.en: O Lord endowed with massive arms, listen to my words; shortly you shall get victory in battle.

6.29.sa: राज्यं निष्कण्टकं कृत्वा भोक्ष्यसे मेदिनीं पुनः । भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन् प्रीतिं प्राप्स्यसि पुष्कलाम् ॥२९॥
6.29.en: Having defeated and slaughtered the Kaurava forces through my benediction and rendered the kingdom destitute of thorns you shall enjoy the earth again.

6.30.sa: मत्प्रसादाच्च ते सौख्यमारोग्यं च भविष्यति । ये च संकीर्तयिष्यन्ति लोके विगतकल्मषाः ॥३०॥
6.30.en: O king, you shall with your brothers again enjoy an abundance through my grace, health and happiness.

6.31.sa: तेषां तुष्टा प्रदास्यामि राज्यमायुर्वपुः सुतम् । प्रवासे नगरे चापि सङ्ग्रामे शत्रुसङ्कटे ॥३१॥
6.31.en: I propitiated, will confer, kingdom longevity, goodly form and offspring on those stainless persons who will chant my attributes aloud to the world,

6.32.sa: अटव्यां दुर्गकान्तारे सागरे गहने गिरौ । ये स्मरिष्यन्ति मां राजन् यथाऽहं भवता स्मृता ॥३२॥
6.32.en: To persons who will remember me, as you have done, in exile, in the town in battle, in danger by foes, in forest, in unapproachable deserts, in seas or in mountains, there will be nothing unattainable in this world.

6.33.sa: न तेषां दुर्लभं किञ्चिदस्मिँल्लोके भविष्यति । इदं स्तोत्रवरं भक्त्या शृणुयाद्वा पठेत वा ॥३३॥
6.33.en: To persons who will remember me, as you have done, in exile, in the town in battle, in danger by foes, in forest, in unapproachable deserts, in seas or in mountains, there will be nothing unattainable in this world.

6.34.sa: तस्य सर्वाणि कार्याणि सिद्धिं यास्यन्ति पाण्डवाः । मत्प्रसादाच्च वः सर्वान् विराटनगरे स्थितान् ॥३४॥
6.34.en: O sons of Pandu, he who will listen to, or recite with faith this excellent hymn, shall attain success in all his undertakings.

6.35.sa: न प्रज्ञास्यन्ति कुरवो नरा वा तन्निवासिनः । इत्युक्त्वा वरदा देवी युधिष्ठिरमरिन्दमम् । रक्षां कृत्वा च पाण्डूनां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥३५॥
6.35.en: Through my grace neither the Kurus nor the people inhabiting the city of Virata, will be able to recognize you all during your stay in that city.

7.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततो विराटं प्रथमं युधिष्ठिरो राजा सभायामुपविष्टमाव्रजत् । वैदूर्यरूपान् प्रतिमुच्य काञ्चनानक्षान् स कक्षे परिगृह्य वाससा ॥१॥

7.2.sa: नराधिपो राष्ट्रपतिं यशस्विनं महायशाः कौरववंशवर्धनः । महानुभावो नरराजसत्कृतो दुरासदस्तीक्ष्णविषो यथोरगः ॥२॥

7.3.sa: बलेन रूपेण नरर्षभो महानपूर्वरूपेण यथामरस्तथा । महाभ्रजालैरिव संवृतो रविर्यथाऽनलो भस्मवृतश्च वीर्यवान् ॥३॥

7.4.sa: तमापतन्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य पाण्डवं विराटराडिन्दुमिवाभ्रसंवृतम् । समागतं पूर्णशशिप्रभाननं महानुभावं नचिरेण दृष्टवान् ॥४॥
7.4.en: The king Virata first saw the Pandava coming like the moon covered with clouds and then in a moment found him arrived at the court, with a countenance like the full moon and possessed of a great splendour.

7.5.sa: मन्त्रिद्विजान् सूतमुखान्विशस्तथा ये चापि केचित् परितः समासते । पप्रच्छ कोऽयं प्रथमं समेयिवान् नृपोपमोऽयं समवेक्षते सभाम् ॥५॥
7.5.en: The king Virata asked his counsellors, the Brahmanas, the charioteers, the Vaishyas and all others who took their seats about him, "who might be the man that has come first, and just like a king appears in my court.

7.6.sa: स तु द्विजोऽयं भविता नरोत्तमः पतिः पृथिव्या इति मे मनोगतम् । न चास्य दासो न रथो न कुञ्जरः समीपतो भ्राजति चायमिन्द्रवत् ॥६॥
7.6.en: This best of men can not be a Brahmin; me-thinks he is a lord of earth, though he has neither a slave, nor a car, nor an elephant with him, yet he shines just like Indra.

7.7.sa: शरीरलिङ्गैरुपसूचितो ह्ययं मूर्द्धाभिषिक्त इति मे मनोगतम् । समीपमायाति च मे गतव्यथो यथा गजस्तामरसीं मदोत्कटः ॥७॥
7.7.en: By the marks on his person it is indicated that he is no other than one whose head has gone through the ceremony of coronal baths, and that is my belief. He approaches me as fearless as an elephant in a ruttish frenzy approaches a lotus.”

7.8.sa: वितर्कयन्तं तु नरर्षभस्तथा युधिष्ठिरोऽभ्येत्य विराटमब्रवीत् । सम्राड्विजानात्विह जीवनार्थिनं विनष्टसर्वस्वमुपागतं द्विजम् ॥८॥
7.8.en: Yudhishthira, the best of men, having come near the king Virata while he was thus indulging in thoughts, addressed him saying "O great king, know me to be a Brahmin, who having lost all, have come to you, solicitous for his livelihood.

7.9.sa: इहाहमिच्छामि तवानघान्तिके वस्तुं यथा कामचरस्तथा विभो । तमब्रवीत् स्वागतमित्यनन्तरं राजा प्रहृष्टः प्रतिसंगृहाण च ॥९॥
7.9.en: O sinless one, I wish to reside with you just like one obeying the voice of his master 0 Lord!" After having accorded him a due welcome the king well pleased said “accept the post you seek for."

7.10.sa: तं राजसिंहं प्रतिगृह्य राजा प्रीत्याऽऽत्मना चैनमिदं बभाषे । कामेन ताताभिवदाम्यहं त्वां कस्यासि राज्ञो विषयादिहागतः ॥१०॥
7.10.en: Having appointed him the best of kings, O king, glad at heart addressed him saying “O worshipful one I bow down to you" from the dominions of what king you are come here? Please tell me truly what your name is and what family you belong to and whether you have knowledge of any art.

7.11.sa: गोत्रं च नामापि च शंस तत्त्वतः । किं चापि शिल्पं तव विद्यते कृतम् ॥११॥
7.11.en: Having appointed him the best of kings, O king, glad at heart addressed him saying “O worshipful one I bow down to you" from the dominions of what king you are come here? Please tell me truly what your name is and what family you belong to and whether you have knowledge of any art.

7.12.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । युधिष्ठिरस्यासमहं पुरा सखा वैयाघ्रपद्यः पुनरस्मि विप्रः । अक्षान् प्रयोक्तुं कुशलोऽस्मि देविनां कङ्केति नाम्नाऽस्मि विराट विश्रुतः॥१२॥
7.12.en: Yudhishthira said I was formerly a friend of Yudhishthira, I am a Brahmin belonging to the family named Vaiayghara, I am expert in casting dice. O Virata, I am known by the name of Kanka.

7.13.sa: विराट उवाच । ददामि ते हन्त वरं यमिच्छसि प्रशाधि मत्स्यान् वशगो ह्यहं तव । प्रियाश्च धूर्ता मम देविनः सदा भवांश्च देवोपम राज्यमर्हति ॥१३॥
7.13.en: Virata said I grant you the boon which you may desire. Rule over the Matsyas. Know me to be your obedient. Even the cunning gamblers are always beloved of me, you, like a king, deserve a kingdom.

7.14.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । प्राप्तो विवादः प्रथमं विशाम्पते न विद्यते कंचन मत्स्य हीनतः । न मे जितः कश्चन धारयेद्धनं वरो ममैषोऽस्तु तव प्रसादजः ॥१४॥
7.14.en: Yudhishthira said O Matsya, O lord of people, I shall never pick a quarrel, from the play at dice, with low people, nor shall any person be defeated by me. Let this boon be granted to me through your grace.

7.15.sa: विराट उवाच । हन्यामवश्यं यदि तेऽप्रियं चरेत् प्रव्राजयेयं विषयाद्द्विजांस्तथा । शृण्वन्तु मे जानपदाः समागताः कङ्को ययाऽहं विषये प्रभुस्तथा ॥१५॥
7.15.en: Virata said Surely shall I kill him who may do wrong to you. Should he be a Brahmin I shall banish him from my kingdom. Let my assembled subjects hear, Kanka, is as much lord of this my dominion as I myself.

7.16.sa: समानयानो भविताऽसि मे सखा प्रभूतवस्त्रो बहुपानभोजनः । पश्येस्त्वमन्तश्च बहिश्च सर्वदा कृतं च ते द्वारमपावृतं मया ॥१६॥
7.16.en: You (Kanka) shall be my friend, your vehicle shall be the same as mine, you shall have plenty of clothes and sundry sorts of drinks and dishes. You shall look into both ins and outs of my affair, I shall always keep my doors open for you.

7.17.sa: ये त्वाऽनुवादेऽयुरवृत्तिकर्शिता ब्रूयाश्च तेषां वचनेन मां सदा । दास्यामि सर्वं तदहं न संशयो न ते भयं विद्यति सन्निधौ मम ॥१७॥
7.17.en: When the people pressed by the want of employment, will apply to you, you shall at all hours tell me all their words. I shall undoubtedly give them all that they will ask for, before iny presence there will be no fear to you.

7.18.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवं स लब्ध्वा तु वरं समागमं विराटराजेन नरर्षभस्तदा । उवास धीरः परमार्चितः सुखी न चापि कश्चिच्चरितं बुबोध तत् ॥१८॥

8.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथापरो भीमबलः श्रिया ज्वलन्नुपाययौ सिंहविलासविक्रमः । खजां च दर्वीं च करेण धारयन्नसिं च कालाङ्गमकोशमव्रणम् ॥१॥

8.2.sa: स सूदरूपः परमेण वर्चसा रविर्यथा लोकमिमं प्रकाशयन् । स कृष्णवासा गिरिराजसारवांस्तं मत्स्यराजं समुपेत्य तस्थिवान् ॥२॥
8.2.en: Although in the guise of a cook he endued with the strength of the lord of mountains, and attired in dark garments, reached the king of the Matsya's and stood before him illuming, with his great splendour, all around him like the sun revealing the world.

8.3.sa: तं प्रेक्ष्य राजा रमयन्नुपागतं ततोऽब्रवीज्जानपदान् समागतान् । सिंहोन्नतांसोऽयमतीव रूपवान् प्रदृश्यते को नु वरर्षभो युवा ॥३॥
8.3.en: Beholding hiin like a king present before him Virata asked the people assembled there "who is this young man seen, the best of men, exceedingly beautiful, and having shoulders as high as those of a lion.

8.4.sa: अदृष्टपूर्वः पुरुषो रविर्यथा वितर्कयन्नास्य लभामि निश्चयम् । तथाऽस्य चित्तं ह्यपि संवितर्कयन्नरर्षभस्यास्य न यामि तत्त्वतः ॥४॥
8.4.en: This man, not seen before, is like one seen; thinking and thinking over I cannot come to a definite conclusion (who he may be); nor do I, with a serious deliberation, understand the intention of that best of men.

8.5.sa: दृष्ट्वैव चैनं तु विचारयाम्यहं गन्धर्वराजो यदि वा पुरन्दरः । जानीत कोऽयं मम दर्शने स्थितो यदीप्सितं तल्लभतां च माचिरम् ॥५॥
8.5.en: Beholding him I do not deem it worth while to discuss whether he is the king of the Gandharvas or Purandara himself; ascertain who it is standing before my eyes, let him have in no time what he desires.

8.6.sa: विराटवाक्येन च तेन चोदिता नरा विराटस्य सुशीघ्रगामिनः । उपेत्य कौन्तेयमथाब्रुवंस्तदा यथा स राजाऽवदताच्युतानुजम् ॥६॥
8.6.en: Thus commissioned by the words of Virata, his quick-paced messengers went to the son of Kunti and told that younger brother of Yudhishthira all that the king had said.

8.7.sa: ततो विराटं समुपेत्य पाण्डवस्त्वदीनरूपं वचनं महामनाः । उवाच सूदोऽस्मि नरेन्द्र बल्लवो भजस्व मां व्यञ्जनकारमुत्तमम् ॥७॥

8.8.sa: विराट उवाच । न सूदतां बल्लव श्रद्दधामि ते सहस्रनेत्रप्रतिमो विराजते । श्रिया च रूपेण च विक्रमेण च प्रभाससे त्वं नृवरो नरेष्विव ॥८॥
8.8.en: Virata said I do not believe that cooking is your business, you shine like a thousand-eyed deity amongst men; you seem to be the best in grace, beauty and prowess.

8.9.sa: भीम उवाच । नरेन्द्र सूदः परिचारकोऽस्मि ते जानामि सूपान् प्रथमं च केवलान् । आस्वादिता ये नृपते पुराऽभवन् युधिष्ठिरेणापि नृपेण सर्वशः ॥९॥
8.9.en: Bhima said O king, I am your cook and servant; it is not so that I have only the knowledge of curries, although O king, they were always tasted, in days gone by, by the king Yudhishthira.

8.10.sa: बलेन तुल्यश्च न विद्यते मया नियुद्धशीलश्च सदैव पार्थिव । गजैश्च सिंहैश्च समेयिवानहं सदा करिष्यामि तवानघ प्रियम् ॥१०॥

8.11.sa: विराट उवाच । ददामि ते हन्त वरान् महानसे तथा च कुर्याः कुशल प्रभाषसे । न चैव मन्ये तव कर्म यत् समं समुद्रनेमिं पृथिवीं त्वमर्हसि ॥११॥
8.11.en: Virata said I grant you the boons; you will take possession of the kitchen in which you say you are skilled. I do not think this office is worthy of you. You deserve the whole earth having seas for its walls, (girt by the seas).

8.12.sa: यथा हि कामो भवतस्तथा कृतं महानसे त्वं भव मे पुरस्कृतः । नराश्च ये तत्र समाहिताः पुरा भवांश्च तेषामधिपो मया कृतः ॥१२॥
8.12.en: I have done what you desire, you are appointed in my kitchen. I place you at the head of those who have been appointed there before by me.

8.13.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तथा स भीमो विहितो महानसे विराटराज्ञो दयितोऽभवद्दृढम् । उवास राज्ये न च तं पृथग्जनो बुबोध तत्रानुचराश्च केचन ॥१३॥
8.13.en: Thus appointed in the kitchen Bhima became a great favorite of the king Virata. O king, he began to live there, but neither the servants of Virata nor other people recognized him.

9.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततः केशान् समुत्क्षिप्य वेल्लिताग्राननिन्दितान् । कृष्णान् सूक्ष्मान् मृदून्दीर्घान्समुद्ग्रथ्यशुचिस्मिता ॥१॥
9.1.en: Vaishampayana said Then Draupadi, of pleasant smile and of dark eyes, bending her black; glossy, soft, long and fine tresses of crispy ends into a twisted braid, threw it on her right side and kept it concealed (under her cloth).

9.2.sa: जुगूहे दक्षिणे पार्श्वे मृदूनसितलोचना । वासश्च परिधायैकं कृष्णा सुमलिनं महत् ॥२॥
9.2.en: Having put on a very big dirty piece of cloth and dressed herself as a Sairandhri, Krishna began to ramble hither and thither like one in a miserable plight. All males and females came running to her wandering about.

9.3.sa: कृत्वा वेषं च सैरन्ध्र्यास्ततो व्यचरदार्तवत् । तां नराः परिधावन्तीं स्त्रियश्च समुपाद्रवन् ॥३॥
9.3.en: Having put on a very big dirty piece of cloth and dressed herself as a Sairandhri, Krishna began to ramble hither and thither like one in a miserable plight. All males and females came running to her wandering about.

9.4.sa: अपृच्छंश्चैव तां दृष्ट्वा का त्वं किं च चिकीर्षसि । सा तानुवाच राजेन्द्र सैरन्ध्र्यहमिहागता ॥४॥
9.4.en: Beholding her they asked "who are you and what you want to do”? O king, she said to them "I am a Sairandhri; here have I come to do his work who will maintain me."

9.5.sa: कर्म चेच्छामि वै कर्तुं तस्य यो मां युयुक्षति । तस्या रूपेण वेषेण श्लक्ष्णया च तथा गिरा । न श्रद्दधत तां दासीमन्नहेतोरुपस्थिताम् ॥५॥
9.5.en: The people, seeing her beauty and dress, hearing her voice so sweet, could not believe her to be in a position of a maid servant come in quest of livelihood.

9.6.sa: विराटस्य तु कैकेयी भार्या परमसम्मता । आलोकयन्ती ददृशे प्रासादाद्द्द्रुपदात्मजाम् ॥६॥
9.6.en: While going abroad from the root of the palace Virata's beloved wife, the daughter of Kaikeyi, beheld the daughter of Drupada.

9.7.sa: सा समीक्ष्य तथारूपामनाथमिकवाससम् । समाहूयाब्रवीद्भद्रे का त्वं किं च चिकीर्षसि ॥७॥
9.7.en: Beholding her thus plighted, unprotected and clad in a single piece of cloth, she (Virata's wife) addressed her saying “O gentle one, who are you and what you desire to do.”

9.8.sa: सा तामुवाच राजेन्द्रसैरन्ध्र्यहमुपागता । कर्म चेच्छाम्यहं कर्तुं तस्य यो मां युयुक्षति ॥८॥
9.8.en: O king, she said to her “I am a Sairandhri, I desire to do his work who will maintain me.'

9.9.sa: सुदेष्णोवाच । नैवंरूपा भवन्त्येव यथा वदसि भामिनि । प्रेषयन्तीव वै दासीर्दासांश्च विविधान् बहून् ॥९॥
9.9.en: Sudeshna said It cannot be so as you say, O beautiful one, (but on the contrary) it seems you can appoint numerous servants both male and female.

9.10.sa: नोच्चगुल्फा संहतोरुस्त्रिगम्भीरा षडुन्नता । रक्ता पञ्चसु रक्तेषु हंसगद्गदभाषिणी ॥१०॥
9.10.en: You are such a one as your heels are not high, thighs touch each other, deep are your intelligence, voice and navel, highly developed are your soles, palms, tongue, upper and neither lips and your voice is as sweet as that of a swan.

9.11.sa: सुकेशी सुस्तनी श्यामा पीनश्रोणिपयोधरा । तेन तेनैव सम्पन्ना काश्मीरीव तुरङ्गमी ॥११॥
9.11.en: You are one of beautiful tresses, good breasts and possessed of high graces; and plump are your buttock and breasts. Being furnished with all these beautiful signs, you appear like a Kashmirean woman.

9.12.sa: अरालपक्ष्मनयना बिम्बोष्ठी तनुमध्यमा । कम्बुग्रीवा गूढशिरा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानना ॥१२॥
9.12.en: You are one with eyes having its line of hairs gracefully bent, lips scarlet as Bimba, waist slender, neck having the lines like those on the conch, veins scarcely visible and countenance like the full moon.

9.13.sa: शारदोत्पलपत्राक्ष्या शारदोत्पलगन्धया । शारदोत्पलसेविन्या रूपेण सदृशी श्रिया ॥१३॥
9.13.en: In beauty you are Sri (goddess of beauty) herself with eyes resembling the petals of the autumnal lotus, with a person fragrant as the autumnal lotus chief, and seated on the autumnal lotus.

9.14.sa: का त्वं ब्रूहि यथा भद्रे नासि दासी कथञ्चन । यक्षी वा यदि वा देवी गन्धर्वी यदि वाऽप्सराः ॥१४॥
9.14.en: O gentle one, tell me who you are; you cannot be a maid-servant; are you a Yakshi or a goddess, a Gandharvi or an Apsara (nymph)? are you the daughter of a celestials or female Naga? is a presiding deity of the city? Are you a Vidyadhari or a Kinnari or Rohini herself? Are you Alambusha or Mishrakeshi Pundarika or Malini or the queen of Indra or Varuna, or are you the wife of Vishvakarma or of the Prajapati himself? These goddesses are renowned in the regions of celestials; of these who are you, O beautiful one?

9.15.sa: देवकन्या भुजङ्गी वा नगरस्याथ देवता । विद्याधरी किन्नरी वा यदि वा रोहिणी स्वयम् ॥१५॥
9.15.en: O gentle one, tell me who you are; you cannot be a maid-servant; are you a Yakshi or a goddess, a Gandharvi or an Apsara (nymph)? are you the daughter of a celestials or female Naga? is a presiding deity of the city? Are you a Vidyadhari or a Kinnari or Rohini herself? Are you Alambusha or Mishrakeshi Pundarika or Malini or the queen of Indra or Varuna, or are you the wife of Vishvakarma or of the Prajapati himself? These goddesses are renowned in the regions of celestials; of these who are you, O beautiful one?

9.16.sa: अलम्बुषा मिश्रकेशी पुण्डरीकाऽथ मालिनी । इन्द्राणी वारुणी वा त्वं त्वष्टुर्धातुः प्रजापतेः । देव्यो देवेषु विख्यातास्तासां त्वं कतमा शुभे ॥१६॥
9.16.en: O gentle one, tell me who you are; you cannot be a maid-servant; are you a Yakshi or a goddess, a Gandharvi or an Apsara (nymph)? are you the daughter of a celestials or female Naga? is a presiding deity of the city? Are you a Vidyadhari or a Kinnari or Rohini herself? Are you Alambusha or Mishrakeshi Pundarika or Malini or the queen of Indra or Varuna, or are you the wife of Vishvakarma or of the Prajapati himself? These goddesses are renowned in the regions of celestials; of these who are you, O beautiful one?

9.17.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । नास्मि देवी न गन्धर्वी नासुरी न च राक्षसी । सैरन्ध्री तु भुजिष्याऽस्मि सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ॥१७॥

9.18.sa: केशान् जानाम्यहं कर्तुं पिंषे साधु विलेपनम् । मल्लिकोत्पलपद्मानां चम्पकानां तथा शुभे ॥१८॥
9.18.en: I know how to dress the hair, pound (fragrant staff) to make unguents. O auspicious lady, I know also how to make beautiful and variegated garlands of Jasamines, lotuses, lilies and Champakas. Formerly served Satyabhama, the beloved queen of Krishna, and also Krishna the wife of the Pandavas, and the only beauty of the Kuru race. I serve in those places where I may get good food and clothes; as long as I get them I continue to serve.

9.19.sa: ग्रथयिष्ये विचित्राश्च स्रजः परमशोभनाः । आराधयं सत्यभामां कृष्णस्य महिषीं प्रियाम् ॥१९॥
9.19.en: I know how to dress the hair, pound (fragrant staff) to make unguents. O auspicious lady, I know also how to make beautiful and variegated garlands of Jasamines, lotuses, lilies and Champakas. Formerly served Satyabhama, the beloved queen of Krishna, and also Krishna the wife of the Pandavas, and the only beauty of the Kuru race. I serve in those places where I may get good food and clothes; as long as I get them I continue to serve.

9.20.sa: कृष्णां च भार्यां पाण्डूनां कुरूणामेकसुन्दरीम् । तत्र तत्र चराम्येवं लभमाना सुभोजनम् ॥२०॥
9.20.en: I know how to dress the hair, pound (fragrant staff) to make unguents. O auspicious lady, I know also how to make beautiful and variegated garlands of Jasamines, lotuses, lilies and Champakas. Formerly served Satyabhama, the beloved queen of Krishna, and also Krishna the wife of the Pandavas, and the only beauty of the Kuru race. I serve in those places where I may get good food and clothes; as long as I get them I continue to serve.

9.21.sa: वासांसि यावन्ति लभे तावत्तावद्रमे तथा । मालिनीत्येव मे नाम स्वयं देवी चकार सा । साऽहमद्यागता देवि सुदेष्णे त्वन्निवेशनम् ॥२१॥
9.21.en: Draupadi herself called me by name Malini, O lady Sudeshna, I, her serving maid, have come to your house today.

9.22.sa: सुदेष्णोवाच । मूर्ध्नि त्वां वासयेयं वै संशयो मे न विद्यते । न चेदिच्छति राजा त्वां गच्छेत् सर्वेण चेतसा ॥२२॥
9.22.en: Sudeshna said I can place you on my head, and there is no doubt in that, provided that the king does not desire you and be not captivated with his whole heart.

9.23.sa: स्त्रियो राजकुले याश्च याश्चेमा मम वेश्मनि । प्रसक्तास्त्वां निरीक्षन्ते पुमांसं कं न मोहयेः ॥२३॥
9.23.en: Charmed by your beauty even the females of the royal house hold and as well as those in my own seraglio are gazing at you. What male person is there whom you will not captivate?

9.24.sa: वृक्षांश्चावस्थितान् पश्य य इमे मम वेश्मनि । तेऽपि त्वां सन्नमन्तीव पुमासं कं न मोहयेः ॥२४॥
9.24.en: Look again, even the very trees that stand in my palace seem to bend low as if by way of paying homage to you, what male person is there that will not be attracted by you?

9.25.sa: राजा विराटः सुश्रोणि दृष्ट्वा वपुरमानुषम् । विहाय मां वरारोहे गच्छेत् सर्वेण चेतसा ॥२५॥
9.25.en: O you of well-shaped hips; o you girl of surpassing beauty, beholding your superhuman form, king Virata, will surely forsake me and will turn to you with his whole heart.

9.26.sa: यं हि त्वमनवद्याङ्गि तरलायतलोचने । प्रसक्तमभिवीक्षेथाः स कामवशगो भवेत् ॥२६॥
9.26.en: O you of expanded eyes, of nimble glances, the person, on whom you endued with faultless limbs, will cast a look with desire, will surely fall a victim to the God of Love.

9.27.sa: यश्च त्वां सततं पश्येत् पुरुषश्चारुहासिनि । एवं सर्वानवद्याङ्गि स चानङ्गवशो भवेत् ॥२७॥
9.27.en: 0 you of sweet smiles, O you of perfectly faultless form, the man who will behold you often and often will surely be subject to that formless deity.

9.28.sa: अध्यारोहेद्यथा वृक्षान् वधायैवात्मनो नरः । राजवेश्मनि ते सुभ्रु गृहे तु स्यात् तथा मम ॥२८॥
9.28.en: As a person climbs up a tree for his own destruction, so, O you of graceful eyebrows, your stay in this royal house-hold will bring out the same result to me.

9.29.sa: यथा च कर्कटी गर्भमाधत्ते मृत्युमात्मनः । तथाविधमहं मन्ये वासं तव शुचिस्मिते ॥२९॥
9.29.en: As a crab conceives for her own death so. O you of pleasant smiles, my desire for your stay here will surely be ruinous to me.

9.30.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । नास्मि लभ्या विराटेन न चान्येन कदाचन । गन्धर्वाः पतयो मह्यं युवानः पञ्च भामिनि ॥३०॥
9.30.en: Draupadi said Neither by Virata nor by any other man I am to be won, O fair lady, for I have five youthful husbands who are all Gandharvas.

9.31.sa: पुत्रा गन्धर्वराजस्य महासत्त्वस्य कस्यचित् । रक्षन्ति ते च मां नित्यं दुःखाचारा तथा ह्यहम् ॥३१॥
9.31.en: They are the sons of certain Gandharva king of extra-ordinary strength; they always protect me. Also my mode of living is very hard.

9.32.sa: यो मे न दद्यादुच्छिष्टं न च पादौ प्रधावयेत् । प्रीणेरंस्तेन वासेन गन्धर्वाः पतयो मम ॥३२॥

9.33.sa: यो हि मां पुरुषो गृद्ध्येद्यथाऽन्याः प्राकृताः स्त्रियः । तामेव निवसेद्रात्रिं प्रविश्य च परां तनुम् ॥३३॥
9.33.en: The person who will desire me like any other woman, will surely encounter destruction that very night.

9.34.sa: न चाप्यहं चालयितुं शक्या केनचिदङ्गने । दुःखशीला हि गन्धर्वास्ते च मे बलवत्प्रियाः ॥३४॥
9.34.en: O lady of sweet smiles, no one is able to decay me from the paths of rectitude; those beloved Gandharvas of exceeding prowess always protect me secretly.

9.35.sa: प्रच्छन्नाश्चापि रक्षन्ति ते मां नित्यं शुचिस्मिते। सुदेष्णोवाच । एवं त्वां वासयिष्यामि यथा त्वं नन्दिनीच्छसि ॥३५॥
9.35.en: Sudeshna said O charming one, it being so, I will allow you a residence in my palace) according to your desire. You will never have to touch food partaken of by another nor even to wash another's feet.

9.36.sa: न च पादौ न चोच्छिष्टं स्प्रक्ष्यसि त्वं कथञ्चन । वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवं कृष्णा विराटस्य भार्यया परिसान्त्विता ॥३६॥
9.36.en: Sudeshna said O charming one, it being so, I will allow you a residence in my palace) according to your desire. You will never have to touch food partaken of by another nor even to wash another's feet.

9.37.sa: उवास नगरे तस्मिन् पतिधर्मवती सती । न चैनां वेद तत्रान्यस्तत्त्वेन जनमेजय ॥३७॥
9.37.en: Vaishampayana said Thus assured by the wife of Virata the chaste Krishna, devoted to her lords, began to live in that city. O Janamejaya, no one of that place could know who she really was.

10.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । सहदेवोऽपि गोपानां कृत्वा वेषमनुत्तमम् । भाषां चैषां समास्थाय विराटमुपयादथ ॥१॥
10.1.en: Vaishampayana said Wearing an excellent dress of a cowherd and learning the dialect of the same, Saladeva also arrived at the city of the king Virata.

10.2.sa: गोष्ठमासाद्य तिष्ठन्तं भवनस्य समीपतः । राजाऽथ दृष्ट्वा पुरुषान् प्राहिणोज्जातविस्मयः ॥२॥
10.2.en: Then the king, seeing him standing in the cow pasture in the vicinity of the royal palace, became amazed and sent for him.

10.3.sa: तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य भ्राजमानं नरर्षभम् । समुपस्थाय वै राजा पप्रच्छ कुरुनन्दनम् ॥३॥
10.3.en: The king, seeing that best of men shining in splendour, coming, asked the son of Kuru.
