10.4.sa: कस्य वा त्वं कुतो वा त्वं किं वा त्वं तु चिकीर्षसि । न हि मे दृष्टपूर्वस्त्वं तत्त्वं ब्रूहि नरर्षभ ॥४॥
10.4.en: To whom do you belong? Whence are you come and what do you seek? You were not seen by me before, tell me in sooth all about you, O best of men.

10.5.sa: संप्राप्य राजानममित्रतापनं ततोऽब्रवीन्मेघमहौघनिःस्वनः । वैश्योऽस्मि नाम्नाऽहमरिष्टनेमिर्गोसङ्ख्य आसं कुरुपुङ्गवानाम् ॥५॥
10.5.en: Having come to the king, the repressor of foes Sahadeva said with a voice deep as the roar of the clouds, "I am a Vaishya known by the name Arishtanemi, I served as an enumerator of the cows of those best of the Kuru race.

10.6.sa: वस्तुं त्वयीच्छामि विशां वरिष्ठ तान् राजसिंहान् न हि वेद्मि पार्थान् । न शक्यते जीवितुमप्यकर्मणा न च त्वदन्यो मम रोचते नृपः ॥६॥
10.6.en: O foremost of men, I do no know where the sons, of Pritha the foremost among men, are; I want to live with you. I can not keep myself without service. I do not like to serve any other king except you.

10.7.sa: विराट उवाच । त्वं ब्राह्मणो यदि वा क्षत्रियोऽसि समुद्रनेमीश्वररूपवानसि । आचक्ष्व मे तत्त्वममित्रकर्शन न वैश्यकर्म त्वयि विद्यते क्षमम् ॥७॥
10.7.en: Virata said You must either be a Brahmana or a Kshatriya, you are as graceful as the lord of the entire earth girt by the sea. Tell me truly, O afflicter of enemies, the offlice of a Vaishya does not become you.

10.8.sa: कस्यासि राज्ञो विषयादिहागतः किं वाऽपि शिल्पं तव विद्यते कृतम् । कथं त्वमस्मासु निवत्स्यसे सदा वदस्व किं चापि तवेह वेतनम् ॥८॥
10.8.en: Tell me from the dominion, of what king you are come here, what knowledge of art you are versed with, in what capacity you will remain with us and what your pay will be.

10.9.sa: सहदेव उवाच । पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणां ज्येष्ठो भ्राता युधिष्ठिरः । तस्याष्टशतसाहस्रा गवां वर्गाः शतं शतम् ॥९॥
10.9.en: Sahadeva said Of the five sons of Pandu Yudhishthira is the eldest. He had one division of kine the number where of amounts to eight hundred and ten thousand and another ten thousand, and another twenty thousand and so forth. I was employed as an enumerator of cows under them; people used to call me Tantipala.

10.10.sa: अपरे शतसाहस्त्रा द्विस्तावन्तस्तथा परे । तेषां गोसङ्ख्य आसं वै तन्तिपालेति मां विदुः॥१०॥

10.11.sa: भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च यच्च सङ्ख्यागतं गवाम् । न मेऽस्त्यविदितं किञ्चित् समन्ताद्दशयोजनम् ॥११॥
10.11.en: Nothing is unknown to me about the cows that live within ten Yojanas and whose tale has been taken in reference to their present past and future.

10.12.sa: गुणाः सुविदिता ह्यासन् मम तस्य महात्मनः । आसीच्च स मया दृष्टः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः ॥१२॥

10.13.sa: क्षिप्रं च गावो बहुला भवन्ति न तासु रोगो भवतीह कश्चन । तैस्तैरुपायैर्विदितं ममैतदेतानि शिल्पानि मयि स्थितानि ॥१३॥
10.13.en: I am perfectly aware of the arts by means of which the kine may increase in number within a short time and no disease may come upon them.

10.14.sa: ऋषभांश्चापि जानामि राजन् पूजितलक्षणान् । येषां मूत्रमुपाघ्राय अपि वन्ध्या प्रसूयते ॥१४॥
10.14.en: O king, I also know the bulls having marks for which they are adored by people and by smelling whose urine even the barren may be fruitful.

10.15.sa: विराट उवाच । शतं सहस्राणि समाहितानि सवर्णवर्णस्य विमिश्रितान् गुणैः । पशून् सपालान् भवते ददाम्यहम् त्वदाश्रया मे पशवो भवन्त्विह ॥१५॥
10.15.en: Virata said I have a hundred thousand kine of various classes the merits of which have not yet been brought to light. I give you the charge of these beasts with their keepers. Let my beasts be henceforth in your keep.

10.16.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तथा स राज्ञो विदितो विशाम्पतेरुवास तत्रैव सुखं नरोत्तमः । न चैनमन्येऽपि विदुः कथञ्चन प्रादाच्च तस्मै भरणं यथेप्सितम् ॥१६॥
10.16.en: Vaishampayana said The best of men began to live there happily without being recognized by the king, the lord of men, nor did any one else know him; the king also allowed him a stipend as much as he desired. A

11.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथापरोऽदृश्यत रूपसम्पदा स्त्रीणामलङ्कारधरो बृहत्पुमान् । प्राकारवप्रे प्रतिमुच्य कुण्डले दीर्घे च कम्बूपरि हाटके शुभे ॥१॥
11.1.en: Vaishampayana said Then there was seen at the gate of the ramparts another person of colossal form, rich in the wealth of beauty, adorned with the ornaments of woman, and putting on large earrings and fine conch bracelets set with gold.

11.2.sa: बाहू च दीर्घान् प्रविकीर्य मूर्धजान् महाभुजो वारणतुल्यविक्रमः । गतेन भूमिं प्रतिकम्पयंस्तदा विराटमासाद्य सभासमीपतः ॥२॥
11.2.en: That long armed one, having the gait like that of an elephant, with long and abundant tissues hanging about, came to Virata shaking the earth with his tread and stood in his court.

11.3.sa: तं प्रेक्ष्य राजोपगतं सभातले व्याजात् प्रतिच्छन्नमरिप्रमाथिनम् । विराजमानं परमेण वर्चसा सुतं महेन्द्रस्य गजेन्द्रविक्रमम् ॥३॥

11.4.sa: सर्वानपृच्छच्च सभानुचारिणः कुतोऽयमायाति पुरा न मे श्रुतः । न चैनमूचुर्विदितं तदा नराः सविस्मयं वाक्यमिदं नृपोऽब्रवीत् ॥४॥
11.4.en: Beholding him, the son of the great Indra, resembling an elephant in gait, him capable of crushing foes, having his real form hidden in disguise, entering the court chamber and stepping forward to the king, he (Virata) asked all his courtiers "whence does this man come; I have never heard of him before.” The people thereof said of the person as one unknown to them. Thereupon the king said wonderingly.

11.5.sa: सत्त्वोपपन्नः पुरुषोऽमरोपमः श्यामो युवा वारणयूथपोपमः । आमुच्य कम्बूपरि हाटके शुभे विमुच्य वेणीमपिनह्य कुण्डले ॥५॥
11.5.en: Endowed with might you appear like a celestials; you are are young and of dark complexion and resemble the leader of a herd of elephants. Although you have worn fine conch-bracelets beset with gold ear-rings and loosened your braid, yet you shine as one decked with garlands and fine hairs and equipped with bow, bow, mail and arrows; ascending the car you wander at your pleasure. Be you like my son or like myself.

11.6.sa: स्रग्वी सुकेशः परिधाय चान्यथा शुशोभ धन्वी कवची शरी यथा । आरुह्य यानं परिधावतां भवान् सुतैः समो मे भव वा मया समः ॥६॥
11.6.en: Endowed with might you appear like a celestials; you are are young and of dark complexion and resemble the leader of a herd of elephants. Although you have worn fine conch-bracelets beset with gold ear-rings and loosened your braid, yet you shine as one decked with garlands and fine hairs and equipped with bow, bow, mail and arrows; ascending the car you wander at your pleasure. Be you like my son or like myself.

11.7.sa: वृद्धो ह्यहं वै परिहारकामः सर्वान् मत्स्यांस्तरसा पालयस्व । नैवंविधाः क्लीबरूपा भवन्ति कथञ्चनेति प्रतिभाति मे मनः ॥७॥

11.8.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । गायामि नृत्याम्यथ वाद्यामि भद्रोऽस्मि नृत्ये कुशलोऽस्मि गीते । त्वमुत्तरायै प्रदिशस्व मां स्वयं भवामि देव्या नरदेव नर्तकः ॥८॥
11.8.en: Arjuna said I sing, dance and play on instruments. I am skilled in dancing and expert in singing. O god among men, assign me to Uttara. I shall be the dancing-master to the princess.

11.9.sa: इदं तु रूपं मम येन किं तव प्रकीर्तयित्वा भृशशोकवर्धनम् । बृहन्नलां मां नरदेव विद्धि सुतं सुतां वा पितृमातृवर्जिताम् ॥९॥
11.9.en: It will be of no avail to describe how I have come by this form. It will merely augment my pain, O lord of men; know me to be Brihannala, a son or daughter without parents.

11.10.sa: विराट उवाच । ददामि ते हन्त वरं बृहन्नले सुतां च मे नर्तय याश्च तादृशीः । इदं तु ते कर्म समं न मे मतं समुद्रनेमिं पृथिवीं त्वमर्हसि ॥१०॥

11.11.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । बृहन्नलां तामभिवीक्ष्य मत्स्यराट् कलासु नृत्येषु तथैव वादिते । संमन्त्र्य राजा विविधैः स्वमन्त्रिभिः परीक्ष्य चैनं प्रमदाभिराशु वै ॥११॥
11.11.en: Vaishampayana said The king of the Matsya's, having tested Brihannala in dancing, in playing on instruments also in other fine arts, sent him to the quarters of the maidens, after consulting with his different ministers having him examined by women and being assured of his impotency of a permanent type. There the mighty Dhananjaya began to teach singing and playing on instruments to the daughter of Virata, and her friends and serving maids. The Pandava soon became their favorite.

11.12.sa: अपुंस्त्वमप्यस्य निशम्य च स्थिरं ततः कुमारीपुरमुत्ससर्ज तम् । स शिक्षयामास च गीतवादितं सुतां विराटस्य धनञ्जयः प्रभुः ॥१२॥
11.12.en: Vaishampayana said The king of the Matsya's, having tested Brihannala in dancing, in playing on instruments also in other fine arts, sent him to the quarters of the maidens, after consulting with his different ministers having him examined by women and being assured of his impotency of a permanent type. There the mighty Dhananjaya began to teach singing and playing on instruments to the daughter of Virata, and her friends and serving maids. The Pandava soon became their favorite.

11.13.sa: सखीश्च तस्याः परिचारिकास्तथा। प्रियश्च तासां स बभूव पाण्डवः ॥१३॥
11.13.en: Vaishampayana said The king of the Matsya's, having tested Brihannala in dancing, in playing on instruments also in other fine arts, sent him to the quarters of the maidens, after consulting with his different ministers having him examined by women and being assured of his impotency of a permanent type. There the mighty Dhananjaya began to teach singing and playing on instruments to the daughter of Virata, and her friends and serving maids. The Pandava soon became their favorite.

11.14.sa: तथा स सत्रेण धनञ्जयो वसन् प्रियाणि कुर्वन् सह ताभिरात्मवान् । तथा च तं तत्र न जज्ञिरे जना बहिश्चरा वाऽप्यथ चान्तरेचराः ॥१४॥
11.14.en: There the self-subdued Dhananjaya began to live in disguise behaving amiably with them. The people within or without the palace could not recognize him.

12.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथापरोऽदृश्यत पाण्डवः प्रभुर्विराटराजं तरसा समेयिवान् । तमापतन्तं ददृशे पृथग्जनो विमुक्तमभ्रादिव सूर्यमण्डलम् ॥१॥
12.1.en: Vaishampayana said Then there was seen another mighty son of Pandu approaching king Virata in haste; the common people thereof saw him coming like solar orb freed from the clouds.

12.2.sa: स वै हयानैक्षत तांस्ततस्ततः समीक्षमाणं स ददर्श मत्स्यराट् । ततोऽब्रवीत्ताननुगान्नरेश्वरः कुतोऽयमायाति नरोऽमरोपमः ॥२॥
12.2.en: He began to observe the horses around; the king of the Matsya's, the lord of people, seeing him observing his horses minutely asked his followers "whence is this man lustrous like a celestials, coming"?

12.3.sa: स्वयं हयानीक्षति मामकान् दृढं ध्रुवं हयज्ञो भविता विचक्षणः । प्रवेश्यतामेष समीपमाशु मे विभाति वीरो हि यथाऽमरस्तथा ॥३॥
12.3.en: This person looks closely at my horses. Must he be proficient in horse-lore. Let him quickly enter into my presence. This heroic one seems to me as much as a celestials.

12.4.sa: अभ्येत्य राजानममित्रहाऽब्रवीज्जयोऽस्तु ते पार्थिव भद्रमस्तु वः । हयेषु युक्तो नृप संमतः सदा तवाश्वसूतो निपुणो भवाम्यहम् ॥४॥
12.4.en: That slaughterer of enemies, having approached the king addressed him thus "O king, let victory be to you and good betide you all. I am always esteemed by kings for my ability as a horse-painter. I will be an expert keeper of your horses.

12.5.sa: विराट उवाच । ददामि यानानि धनं निवेशनं ममाश्वसूतो भवितुं त्वमर्हसि । कुतोऽसि कस्यासि कथं त्वमागतः प्रबूहि शिल्पं तव विद्यते च यत् ॥५॥

12.6.sa: नकुल उवाच । पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणां ज्येष्ठो भ्राता युधिष्ठिरः। तेनाहमश्वेषु पुरा नियुक्तः शत्रुकर्शन ॥६॥
12.6.en: Nakula said O repressor of foes, of the five sons of Pandu, Yudhishthira is the eldest brother, by him I was formerly employed as a keeper of his horses.

12.7.sa: अश्वानां प्रकृतिं वेद्मि विनयं चापि सर्वशः । दुष्टानां प्रतिपतिं च कृत्स्नं चैव चिकित्सितम् ॥७॥

12.8.sa: न कातरं स्यान्मम जातु वाहनं न मेऽस्ति दुष्टा वडवा कुतो हयाः । जनस्तु मामाह स चापि पाण्डवो युधिष्ठिरो ग्रन्थिकमेव नामतः ॥८॥
12.8.en: Under my care hardly does any animal fall ill. What to speak of horses even mares in my hands are not to be found wicked. People called me by name, Granthika so also Yudhishthira the son of Pandu.

12.9.sa: विराट उवाच । यदस्ति किञ्चिन्मम वाजिवाहनं तदस्तु सर्वं त्वदधीनमद्य वै । ये चापि केचिन्मम वाजियोजकास्त्वदाश्रयाः सारथयश्च सन्तु मे ॥९॥

12.10.sa: इदं तवेष्टं यदि वै सुरोपम ब्रवीहि यत्ते प्रसमीक्षितं वसु । न तेऽनुरूपं हयकर्म विद्यते प्रभाति राजेव हि संमतो मम ॥१०॥
12.10.en: If this be your desire, O god-like one, tell me what remuneration is sought by you. This office of horse-training does not become you, because you look like a king and you are agreeable to me.

12.11.sa: युधिष्ठिरस्येव हि दर्शनेन मे समं तवेदं प्रियमत्र दर्शनम् । कथं तु भृत्यैः स विनाकृतो वने वसत्यनिन्द्यो रमते च पाण्डवः ॥११॥
12.11.en: Here, the very sight of you is as much pleasing to me as that of Yudhishthira himself. Oh how does that faultless son of Pandu, dwell and divert himself in the forest without his servants.

12.12.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तथा स गन्धर्ववरोपमो युवा विराटराज्ञा मुदितेन पूजितः । न चैनमन्येऽपि विदुः कथञ्चन प्रियाभिरामं विचरन्तमन्तरा ॥१२॥

12.13.sa: एवं हि मत्स्ये न्यवसन्त पाण्डवा यथाप्रतिज्ञाभिरमोघदर्शनाः । अज्ञातचर्यां व्यचरन् समाहिताः समुद्रनेमीपतयोऽतिदुःखिताः ॥१३॥
12.13.en: Thus the son of Pandu, whose very sight never proved abortive, began to live in the kingdom of Matsya; and in conformity with their pledge, the lords of the earth surrounded by seas although stricken with woe began to pass their days of non-discovery with composure.

13.1.sa: जनमेजय उवाच । एवं ते मत्स्यनगरे प्रच्छन्नाः कुरुनन्दनाः । अत ऊर्ध्वं महावीर्याः किमकुर्वत वै द्विज ॥१॥
13.1.en: Janamejaya said O twice-born one, living thus disguised in the city of the Matsyas what did the Kuru's sons of exceeding might do.

13.2.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवं मत्स्यस्य नगरे प्रच्छन्नाः कुरुनन्दनाः । आराधयन्तो राजानं यदकुर्वत तच्छृणु ॥२॥
13.2.en: Vaishampayana said Hear, what the descendants of Kuru did living thus disguised in the city of the Matsyas and serving the king thereof.

13.3.sa: तृणबिन्दुप्रसादाच्च धर्मस्य च महात्मनः । अज्ञातवासमेवं तु विराटनगरेऽवसन् ॥३॥
13.3.en: By the grace of the ascetic Trinabindu and of the high-souled Dharma they began to live incognito in the city of Virata.

13.4.sa: युधिष्ठिरः सभास्तारो मत्स्यानामभवत् प्रियः । तथैव च विराटस्य सपुत्रस्य विशाम्पते ॥४॥
13.4.en: Yudhishthira as a courtier made himself a favorite to Virata and his son, as well as to all the Matsyas, O lord of people.

13.5.sa: स ह्यक्षहृदयज्ञस्तान् क्रीडयामास पाण्डवः । अक्षवत्यां यथाकामं सूत्रबद्धानिव द्विजान् ॥५॥
13.5.en: Well versed in the mysteries of the dice he caused him to play at dice in the dice-hall in accordance with his pleasure like the birds bound by the string.

13.6.sa: अज्ञातं च विराटस्य विजित्य वसु धर्मराट् । भ्रातृभ्यः पुरुषव्याघ्रो यथार्हं संप्रयच्छति ॥६॥

13.7.sa: भीमसेनोऽपि मांसानि भक्ष्याणि विविधानि च । अतिसृष्टानि मत्स्येन विक्रीणीते युधिष्ठिरे ॥७॥
13.7.en: Bhimsena also sold to Yudhishthira, the meat and the viands of various sorts which were given by the king of the Matsyas.

13.8.sa: वासांसि परिजीर्णानि लब्धान्यन्तःपुरेऽर्जुनः । विक्रीणानश्च सर्वेभ्यः पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥८॥
13.8.en: Arjuna parted with the worn out clothes by sale, which he obtained from women's quarters, to the other sons of Pandu.

13.9.sa: सहदेवोऽपि गोपानां वेषमास्थाय पाण्डवः । दधि क्षीरं घृतं चैव पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥९॥
13.9.en: Sahadeva also, who had assumed the dress of a cow-herd, distributed to them curds, milk and clarified butter.

13.10.sa: नकुलोऽपि धनं लब्ध्वा कृते कर्मणि वाजिनाम् । तुष्टे तस्मिन्नरपतौ पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥१०॥
13.10.en: Nakula also gave the wealth to his brothers which he acquired from the king who was satisfied with him for his tending the horses.

13.11.sa: कृष्णा तु सर्वान् भर्तॄंस्तान्निरीक्षन्ती तपस्विनी । यथा पुनरविज्ञाता तथा चरति भामिनी ॥११॥
13.11.en: In the form of ascetic and very charmful draupadi served their husband, so nobody can identify their reality.

13.12.sa: एवं सम्पादयन्तस्ते तदाऽन्योन्यं महारथाः । विराटनगरे चेरुः पुनर्गर्भधृता इव ॥१२॥

13.13.sa: साशङ्का धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भयात् पाण्डुसुतास्तदा । प्रेक्षमाणास्तदा कृष्णामूषुश्छन्ना नराधिप ॥१३॥
13.13.en: Then the sons of Pandu, the lords of men, appending evil from the sons of Dhritarashtra, continued to live there in disguise keeping vigilant eyes upon their wife Krishna.

13.14.sa: अथ मासे चतुर्थे तु ब्रह्मणः सुमहोत्सवः । आसीत् समृद्धो मत्स्येषु पुरुषाणां सुसंमतः ॥१४॥

13.15.sa: तत्र मल्लाः समापेतुर्दिग्भ्यो राजन् सहस्रशः । समाजे ब्रह्मणो राजन् यथा पशुपतेरिव ॥१५॥
13.15.en: 0 king, there came, by thousands, wrestlers from all quarters in that field of festivity in honour of the divine Brahma, as also on the occasion of a festival held in honor of Shiva.

13.16.sa: महाकाया महावीर्याः कालखञ्जा इवासुराः । वीर्योन्मत्ता वलोदग्रा राज्ञा समभिपूजिताः ॥१६॥
13.16.en: They were of colossal forms and of exceeding might, like the demons named Kalakhanjas; they were maddened with their latent power; furious with their prowess and highly honored by the king.

13.17.sa: सिंहस्कन्धकटिग्रीवाः स्ववदाता मनस्विनः । असकृल्लब्धलक्षास्ते रङ्गे पार्थिवसन्निधौ ॥१७॥

13.18.sa: तेषामेको महानासीत् सर्वमल्लानथाह्वयत् । आवल्गमानं तं रङ्गे नोपतिष्ठति कश्चन ॥१८॥
13.18.en: Amongst them there was one who was the greatest of all and challenged all other combatants to a wrestle; there was none that ventured to encounter him as he strided over in the arena.

13.19.sa: यदा सर्वे विमनसस्ते मल्ला हतचेतसः । अथ सूदेन तं मल्लं योधयामास मत्स्यराट् ॥१९॥
13.19.en: When all the wrestlers stood stupefied and dejected in spirit then the king of the Matsyas made him fight with his cook.

13.20.sa: नोद्यमानस्तदा भीमो दुःखेनैवाकरोन्मतिम् । न हि शक्नोति विवृते प्रत्याख्यातुं नराधिपम् ॥२०॥
13.20.en: Impelled by the king, Bhima made up his mind with reluctance, for it was not in his power to openly disobey the royal mandate.

13.21.sa: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः शार्दूलशिथिलश्चरन् । प्रविवेश महारङ्गं विराटमभिपूजयन् ॥२१॥
13.21.en: Then that the best of men, having worshipped the king Virata, entered the spacious arena with listless steps like those of a lion.

13.22.sa: बबन्ध कक्षां कौन्तेयस्ततः संहर्षयन् जनम् । ततस्तु वृत्रसङ्काशं भीमो मल्लं समाह्वयत् ॥२२॥
13.22.en: Then Bhima, the son of Kunti, girded up his lions and caused the delight of the spectators. There he summoned the wrestler of distinguished prowess named Jimuta resembling Vritra himself. were

13.23.sa: जीमूतं नाम तं तत्र मल्लं प्रख्यातविक्रमम् । तावुभौ सुमहोत्साहावुभौ भीमपराक्रमौ ॥२३॥
13.23.en: Both of them were of exceeding energy and of terrible prowess, and they both were like a couple of infuriated elephants of gigantic form each being sixty years old. Then those two best of men became engaged in hand-tohand fight.

13.24.sa: मत्ताविव महाकायौ वारणौ षष्टिहायनौ । ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलौ बाहुयुद्धं समीयतुः ॥२४॥
13.24.en: Both of them were of exceeding energy and of terrible prowess, and they both were like a couple of infuriated elephants of gigantic form each being sixty years old. Then those two best of men became engaged in hand-tohand fight.

13.25.sa: वीरौ परमसंहृष्टावन्योन्यजयकाङ्क्षिणौ । आसीत् सुभीमः संपातो वज्रपर्वतयोरिव ॥२५॥
13.25.en: Those two heroic combatants exceedingly cheerful, each being desirous of gaining victory over the other; exceedingly terrible was the encounter between them, just like the clash of the thunderbolt against the mountain.

13.26.sa: उभौ परमसंहृष्टौ बलेनातिबलावुभौ । अन्योन्यस्यान्तरं प्रेप्सू परस्परजयैषिणौ ॥२६॥
13.26.en: Both of them were exceedingly powerful and were highly pleased with each other's strength; each of them was desirous of winning the victory over the other and was vigilant to take advantage of his rival's lapse.

13.27.sa: उभौ परमसंहृष्टौ मत्ताविव महागजौ । कृतप्रतिकृतैश्चित्रैर्बाहुभिश्च सुसङ्कटैः । सन्निपातावधूतैश्च प्रमाथोन्मथनैस्तथा ॥२७॥
13.27.en: Both of them were exceedingly delighted and resembled a couple of infuriated elephants of huge forms; and various were the manners of their attack and defence shown by means of their clenched fists.

13.28.en: They fought in a manner that each dashed against the other, threw his rival far off his stand, each crushed the other down, and pressed him hard on the ground, each showing the other off exchanged blows, and each whirled the other round with his head downward and threw him away with a loud noise.

13.31.sa: अरज्यत जनः सर्वः सोत्कृष्टनिनदोत्थितः । बालनोः संयुगे राजन् वृत्रवासवयोरिव ॥३१॥

13.32.en: O king, in the wrestling of the two mighty persons, resembling Vitra and Vasava respectively, they pulled, pressed, whirled and hurried down each other and struck each other with their knees and expressed their hatred for each other in loud voices.

13.33.sa: ततः शब्देन महता भर्त्सयन्तौ परस्परम् । व्यूढोरस्कौ दीर्घभुजौ नियुद्धकुशलावुभौ । बाहुभिः समसज्जेतामायसैः परिघैरिव ॥३३॥

13.34.sa: चकर्ष दोर्ज्यामुत्पात्य भीमो मल्लममित्रहा । निनदन्तमभिक्रोशन् शार्दूल इव वारणम् ॥३४॥
13.34.en: Bhima, the slayer of enemies, seized, with a big seized, his vociferous rival wrestler by the arms and drew him near even as the lion seizes the elephant.

13.35.sa: समुद्यम्य महाबाहुर्भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान् । ततो मल्लाश्च मत्स्याश्च विस्मयं चक्रिरे परम् ॥३५॥

13.36.sa: भ्रामयित्त्वा शतगुणं गतसत्त्वमचेतनम् । प्रत्यर्पिषन्महाबाहुर्मल्लं भुवि वृकोदरः ॥३६॥
13.36.en: Then having whirled him round and round a hundred times, the mighty armed Vrikodara inade him utterly insensible and threw him down lifeless on the ground.

13.37.sa: तस्मिन् विनिहते वीरे जीमूते लोकविश्रुते । विराटः परमं हर्षमगच्छद्बान्धवैः सह ॥३७॥
13.37.en: That distinguished athlete Jimuta being slain, Virata and his friends were exceedingly delighted.

13.38.sa: प्रहर्षात् प्रददौ वित्तं बहु राजा महामनाः । बल्लवाय महारङ्गे यथा वैश्रवणस्तथा ॥३८॥
13.38.en: In his great joy the high-minded king gave away to Ballava plenty of riches in the shape of a reward on the very field of combat with as much liberality as that of Kubera.

13.39.sa: एवं स सुबहून् मल्लान् पुरुषांश्च महाबलान् । विनिघ्नन् मत्स्यराजस्य प्रीतिमाहरदुत्तमाम् ॥३९॥
13.39.en: Having thus slain numerous athletes and many other persons of great strength he received the great favour of the king of the Matsya's.

13.40.sa: यदास्य तुल्यः पुरुषो न कश्चित्तत्र विद्यते । ततो व्याघ्रैश्च सिंहैश्च द्विरदैश्चाप्ययोधयत् ॥४०॥

13.41.sa: पुनरन्तःपुरगतः स्त्रीणां मध्ये वृकोदरः । योध्यते स विराटेन सिंहैर्मत्तैर्महाबलैः ॥४१॥
13.41.en: Again the king made Vrikodara fight with furious lions of exceeding strength in the assembly of the ladies of the harem.

13.42.sa: बीभत्सुरपि गीतेन स्वनृत्येन च पाण्डवः । विराटं तोषयामास सर्वाश्चान्तःपुरस्त्रियः ॥४२॥
13.42.en: Bibhatsu, the son of Pandu, pleased Virata and all the ladies of the harem by singing and dancing.

13.43.sa: अश्वैर्विनीतैर्जवनैस्तत्र तत्र समागतैः । तोषयामास राजानं नकुलो नृपसत्तमम् ॥४३॥
13.43.en: Nakula pleased the king, the best of kings by showing him the fast-going and well-trained horses and the king, pleased gave him a plenty of money as a reward.

13.44.sa: तस्मै प्रदेयं प्रायच्छत् प्रीतो राजा धनं बहु । विनीतान् वृषभान् दृष्ट्वा सहदेवस्य चाभितः । धनं ददौ वहुविधं विराटः पुरुषर्षभः ॥४४॥
13.44.en: Beholding a herd of well-trained bullocks around Sahadeva, Virata the best of men, gave him wealth of various kinds.

13.45.sa: द्रौपदी प्रेक्ष्य तान्सर्वान् क्लिश्यमानान्महारथान् । नातिप्रीतमना राजन्निःश्वासपरमाऽभवत् ॥४५॥
13.45.en: O king, beholding all these mighty warriors suffer pain, Draupadi felt herself dejected in mind and had recourse to constant sighs.

13.46.sa: एवं ते न्यवसंस्तत्र प्रच्छन्नाः पुरुषर्षभाः । कर्माणि तस्य कुर्वाणा विराटनृपतेस्तदा ॥४६॥
13.46.en: Those best among men began to live there in disguise rendering services to the king Virata.

14.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । वसमानेषु पार्थेषु मत्स्यस्य नगरे तदा । महारथेषु छन्नेषु मासा दश समाययुः ॥१॥

14.2.sa: याज्ञसेनी सुदेष्णां तु शुश्रूषन्ती विशाम्पते । आवसत् परिचारार्हा सुदुःखं जनमेजय ॥२॥
14.2.en: O lord of people, Yajnaseni, although herself worthy of being served by others, began to live, O Janamejaya, in great misery by waiting upon Sudeshna.

14.3.sa: तथा चरन्ती पाञ्चाली सुदेष्णाया निवेशने । तां देवीं तोषयामास तथा चान्तःपुरस्त्रियः ॥३॥
14.3.en: Conducting herself in this way in Sudeshna's apartments the daughter of Panchala pleased that lady as well as the other women of the harem.

14.4.sa: तस्मिन् वर्षे गतप्राये कीचकस्तु महाबलः । सेना पतिर्विराटस्य ददर्श द्रुपदात्मजाम् ॥४॥
14.4.en: That year being nearly expired the mighty Kichaka the commander of Virata's forces happened to see the daughter of Drupada.

14.5.sa: तां दृष्ट्वा देवगर्भाभां चरन्तीं देवतामिव । कीचकः कामयामास कामबाणप्रपीडितः ॥५॥

14.6.sa: स तु कामाग्निसंतप्तः सुदेष्णामभिगम्य वै । प्रहसन्निव सेनानीरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥६॥
14.6.en: Burning with the flame of lust, the leader of Virata's forces went to Sudeshna (his sister) and smilingly spoke to her in the following words.

14.7.sa: नेयं मया जातु पुरेह दृष्टा राज्ञो विराटस्य निवेशने शुभा । रूपेण चोन्मादयतीव मां भृशं गन्धेन जाता मदिरेव भामिनी ॥७॥
14.7.en: This damsel was never seen by me before in Virata palace. This beautiful lady maddenis me very much with her beauty as wine does with its odour.

14.8.sa: का देवरूपा हृदयङ्गमा शुभे ह्याचक्ष्व मे कस्य कुतोऽत्र शोभने । चित्तं हि निर्मथ्य करोति मां वशे न चान्यदत्रौषधमस्ति मे मतम् ॥८॥
14.8.en: Tell me, O lady, who is this be-witching girl of fine beauty, endued with the grace of a goddess and whose she is and where she comes from. She has brought me to subjection by grinding my heart. I think there is no other medicine to heal me (except her).

14.9.sa: अहो तवेयं परिचारिका शुभा प्रत्यग्ररूपा प्रतिभाति मामियम् । अयुक्तरूपं हि करोति कर्म ते प्रशास्तु मां यच्च ममास्ति किञ्चन ॥९॥

14.10.sa: प्रभूतनागाश्वरथं महाजनं समृद्धियुक्तं बहुपानभोजनम् । मनोहरं काञ्चनचित्रभूषणं गृहं महच्छोभयतामियं मम ॥१०॥

14.11.sa: ततः सुदेष्णामनुमन्त्र्य कीचकस्ततः समभ्येत्य नराधिपात्मजाम् । उवाच कृष्णामभिसान्त्वयंस्तदा मृगेन्द्रकन्यामिव जम्बुको वने ॥११॥

14.12.sa: का त्वं कस्यासि कल्याणि कुतो वा त्वं वरानने । प्राप्ता विराटनगरं तत्त्वमाचक्ष्व शोभने ॥१२॥
14.12.en: Who and whose are you, O graceful one? Whence are you come to this city of Virata, O you of beautiful countenance. Tell me truly, O fair one.

14.13.sa: रूपमग्र्यं तथा कान्तिः सौकुमार्यमनुत्तमम् । कान्त्या विभाति वक्त्रं ते शशाङ्क इव निर्मलम् ॥१३॥
14.13.en: Your beauty is rankled as the foremost of its order, so also is your gracefulness. Excellent is your tenderness; in respect of loveliness your countenance shines as clearly as the moon.

14.14.sa: नेत्रे सुविपुले सुभ्रु पद्मपत्रनिभे शुभे । वाक्यं ते चारुसर्वाङ्गि परपुष्टरुतोपमम् ॥१४॥
14.14.en: O one of lovely eye-brows, your eyes are large resembling the petals of lotuses. O you of graceful limbs, your voice is like the notes of the cuckoo.

14.15.sa: एवंरूपा मया नारी काचिदन्या महीतले । न दृष्टपूर्वा सुश्रोणि यादृशी त्वमनिन्दिते ॥१५॥
14.15.en: O you of fair hips, never before have I beheld in the world a woman endued with such beauty as you are, O blameless one.

14.16.sa: लक्ष्मीः पद्मालया का त्वमथ भूतिः सुमध्यमे । ह्रीः श्रीः कीर्तिरथो कान्तिरासां का त्वं वरानने ॥१६॥
14.16.en: Are you Lakshmi herself having lotuses for abode, or O slender-waisted one, are you Bhuti herself? Which of these-Hri, Sri, Kiriti and Kanti, are you the impersonation, O you of excellent features?

14.17.sa: अतीव रूपिणी किं त्वमनङ्गाङ्गविहारिणी । अतीव भ्राजसे सुभ्रु प्रभेवेन्दोरनुत्तमा ॥१७॥
14.17.en: Are you the one endued with the beauty of Rati, enjoying dalliance in the embrace of the god of love? O you of fair eye-brows, exceedingly do you shine like the excellent light of the moon.

14.18.sa: अपि चेक्षणपक्ष्माणां स्मितज्योत्स्नोपमं शुभम् । दिव्यांशुरश्मिभिर्वृत्तं दिव्यकान्तिमनोरमम् ॥१८॥
14.18.en: Who is there in the whole world that will not yield to the influence of Cupid beholding your face endued with matchless grace-your face endued with the halo of celestials light, are pleasant in consequence of the heavenly bcauty, resembles the moon in full having smile for its rays and eye-lashes for its spots.

14.19.sa: निरीक्ष्य वक्त्रचन्द्रं ते लक्ष्म्याऽनुपमया युतम् । कृत्स्ने जगति को नेह कामस्य वशगो भवेत् ॥१९॥

14.20.sa: हारालङ्कारयोग्यौ तु स्तनौ चोभौ सुशोभनौ । सुजातौ सहितौ लक्ष्म्या पीनौ वृत्तौ निरन्तरौ ॥२०॥
14.20.en: Both your breasts exceedingly graceful, well-shaped, endued with beauty, well rounded and without a space between, and are worthy of being decked with garlands.

14.21.sa: कुड्मलाम्बुरुहाकारौ तव सुभ्रु पयोधरौ । कामप्रतोदाविव मां तुदतश्चारुहासिनि ॥२१॥
14.21.en: Your breasts, O you of fair eye-brows, resemble lotus-buds in shape; like the whips of Kama they are afflicting me, O you of pleasant smiles.

14.22.sa: वलीविभङ्गचतुरं स्तनभारविनामितम् । कराग्रसंमितं मध्यं तवेदं तनुमध्यमे ॥२२॥

14.23.sa: दृष्ट्वैव चारु जघनं सरित्पुलिनसंनिभम् । कामव्याधिरसाध्यो मामप्याक्रामति भामिनि ॥२३॥
14.23.en: O slender-waisted lady, beholding this your waist marked with four waivy wrinkles, stooping forward with the veight of your breasts and measuring only a span, and also looking on your beautiful hips resembling the banks of the river the incurable disease of lust afflicts me greatly, O beautiful one.

14.24.sa: जज्वाल चाग्निमदनो दावाग्निरिव निर्दयः । त्वत्सङ्गमाभिसङ्कल्पविवृद्धो मां दहत्ययम् ॥२४॥

14.25.sa: आत्मप्रदानवर्षेण संगमाम्भोधरेण च । शमयस्व वरारोहे ज्वलन्तं मन्मथानलम् ॥२५॥

14.26.sa: मच्चित्तोन्मादनकरा मन्मथस्य शरोत्कराः । त्वत्संगमाशानिशितास्तीव्राः शशिनिभानने । मह्यं विदार्य हृदयमिदं निर्दयवेगिताः ॥२६॥

14.27.sa: प्रविष्टा ह्यसितापाङ्गि प्रचण्डाश्चण्डदारुणाः । अत्युन्मादसमारम्भाः प्रीत्युन्मादकरा मम । आत्मप्रदानसम्भोगैर्मामुद्धर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥२७॥
14.27.en: O you of a countenance resembling the moon, the dreadful, violent and cruel shafts of Cupid, capable of causing my mind quite out of sorts, sharpened by the desire of dalliance with you, piercing my heart with a rapid course, have penetrated into its core, O black eyed one. The maddening gestures and movements of yours are really transporting my joy into madness. It behoves you to save me from this plight by surrendering your person to me and allowing me to enjoy your company.

14.28.sa: चित्रमाल्याम्बरधरा सर्वाभरणभूषिता । कामं प्रकामं सेव त्वं मया सह विलासिनि ॥२८॥
14.28.en: Wearing beautiful garlands and clothes and adorned with all kinds of ornaments enjoy with ine. O sweet one, all the objects of your desire to your fill.

14.29.sa: नार्हसीहासुखं वस्तुं सुखार्हा सुखवर्जिता । प्राप्नुह्यनुत्तमं सौख्यं मत्तस्त्वं मत्तगामिनि ॥२९॥
14.29.en: you endued with the gait of an elephant in ruttish state, as you are accustomed to happiness, though deprived of it now, it behoves you not to live here in misery; pray receive from me all kinds of excellent things contributing to your happiness. Eating delightful and dainty viands of various kinds with taste almost equal to ambrosia, and sporting at your sweet will, attain fortune and all the enjoyable articles of superior and excellent kind and drink and wine, O blessed one.

14.30.sa: स्वादून्यमृतकल्पानि पेयानि विविधानि च । पिबमाना मनोज्ञानि रममाणा यथासुखम् ॥३०॥
14.30.en: you endued with the gait of an elephant in ruttish state, as you are accustomed to happiness, though deprived of it now, it behoves you not to live here in misery; pray receive from me all kinds of excellent things contributing to your happiness. Eating delightful and dainty viands of various kinds with taste almost equal to ambrosia, and sporting at your sweet will, attain fortune and all the enjoyable articles of superior and excellent kind and drink and wine, O blessed one.

14.31.sa: भोगोपचारान् ‌विविधान् सौभाग्यं चाप्यनुत्तमम् । पानं पिब महाभागे भोगैश्चानुत्तमैः शुभैः ॥३१॥
14.31.en: you endued with the gait of an elephant in ruttish state, as you are accustomed to happiness, though deprived of it now, it behoves you not to live here in misery; pray receive from me all kinds of excellent things contributing to your happiness. Eating delightful and dainty viands of various kinds with taste almost equal to ambrosia, and sporting at your sweet will, attain fortune and all the enjoyable articles of superior and excellent kind and drink and wine, O blessed one.

14.32.sa: इदं हि रूपं प्रथमं तवानघे निरर्थकं केवलमद्य भामिनि । अधार्यमाणा स्रगिवोत्तमा शुभा न शोभसे सुन्दरि शोभना सती ॥३२॥
14.32.en: This beauty and prime of your youth, O beauteous lady, is now totally useless. O beautiful and chaste lady, lovely as you are, do you not shine like fine garlands unused?

14.33.sa: त्यजामि दारान् मम ये पुरातना भवन्तु दास्यस्तव चारुहासिनि । अहं च ते सुन्दरि दासवत् स्थितः सदा भविष्ये वशगो वरानने ॥३३॥
14.33.en: I will renounce all my old wives. Let them be your serving hands, O one of sweet smile. O beautiful one, I will stay as a slave to you and be ever obedient to you, O you of fair face.

14.34.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । अप्रार्थनीयामिह मां सूतपुत्राभिमन्यसे । निहीनवर्णां सैरन्ध्रीं बीभत्सां केशकारिणीम् ॥३४॥
14.34.en: Draupadi said I am Sairandhri of low caste holding the hateful office of dressing hair; O Suta's son, in desiring me you desire one who is not worthy of such honour.

14.35.sa: परदाराऽस्मि भद्रं ते न युक्तं तव साम्प्रतम् । दयिताः प्राणिनां दारा धर्मं समनुचिन्तय ॥३५॥

14.36.sa: परदारे न ते बुद्धिर्जातु कार्या कथंचन । विवर्जनं ह्यकार्याणामेतत् सुपुरुषव्रतम् ॥३६॥
14.36.en: Let your heart never be inclined to adultery, because the complete abandonment of all improper acts is ever the duty of those that are good.

14.37.sa: मिथ्याभिगृध्नो हि नरः पापात्मा मोहमास्थितः । अयशः प्राप्नुयाद्घोरं महद्वा प्राप्नुयाद्भयम् ॥३७॥

14.38.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्तस्तु सैरन्ध्र्या कीचकः काममोहितः । जानन्नपि सुदुर्बुद्धिः परदाराभिमर्शने ॥३८॥

14.39.sa: दोषान् बहून् प्राणहरान् सर्वलोकविगर्हितान् । प्रोवाचेदं सुदुर्बुद्धिर्द्रौपदीमजितेन्द्रियः ॥३९॥
14.39.en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by Sairandhri the wickedminded Kichaka, with senses unsubdued and overcome by lust, in spite of the knowledge of numerous evils of adultery the evils denounced by every body and sometimes ending fatally, spoke the following to Draupadi.

14.40.sa: नार्हस्येवं वरारोहे प्रत्याख्यातुं वरानने । मां मन्मथसमाविष्टं त्वत्कृते चारुहासिनि ॥४०॥
14.40.en: O fair faced damsel of excellent hips, it is not seemly on your part thus to disregarded me who am quite under the influence of Cupid on your account, O you of sweet smiles.

14.41.sa: प्रत्याख्याय च मां भीरु वशगं प्रियवादिनम् । नूनं त्वमसितापाङ्गि पश्चात्तापं करिष्यसि ॥४१॥
14.41.en: O timid one, having disregarded me speaking so sweet to you and totally under your influence, surely, O black eyed one, you will have to true afterwards.

14.42.sa: अहं हि सुभ्रू राज्यस्य कृत्स्नस्यास्य सुमध्यमे । प्रभुर्वासयिता चैव वीर्ये चाप्रतिमः क्षितौ ॥४२॥

14.43.sa: पृथिव्यां मत्समो नास्ति कश्चिदन्यः पुमानिह । रूपयौवनसौभाग्यैर्भोगैश्चानुत्तमैः शुभैः ॥४३॥
14.43.en: In personal beauty, youth, prosperity as well as in the possession of all the excellent objects of luxury, there is no other man on earth that can stand equal to me.

14.44.sa: सर्वकामसमृद्धेषु भोगेष्वनुपमेष्विह । भोक्तव्येषु च कल्याणि कस्माद्दास्ये रता ह्यसि ॥४४॥
14.44.en: Having everything of luxury, comfort and enjoyment of no parallel at your command, why do you, O auspicious lady, prefer to remain enchained in servitude?

14.45.sa: मया दत्तमिदं राज्यं स्वामिन्यसि शुभानने । भजस्व मां वरारोहे भुङ्क्ष्व भोगाननुत्तमान् ॥४५॥

14.46.sa: एवमुक्ता तु सा साध्वी कीचकेनाशुभं वचः । कीचकं प्रत्युवाचेदं गर्हयन्त्यस्य तद्वचः ॥४६॥
14.46.en: Thus addressed by Kichaka in these foul words the chaste Draupadi set his word at naught and addressed him thus.

14.47.sa: सैरन्ध्युवाच । मा सूतपुत्र मुह्यस्व माऽद्य त्यक्ष्यस्व जीवितम् । जानीहि पञ्चभिर्घोरैर्नित्यं मामभिरक्षिताम् ॥४७॥
14.47.en: Sairandhri said O son of a Suta, do not play the fool and do not throw away your life this very day; know me always protected by five heroes.

14.48.sa: न चाप्यहं त्वया लभ्या गन्धर्वाः पतयो मम । ते त्वां निहन्युः कुपिताः साध्वलं मा व्यनीनशः ॥४८॥
14.48.en: I am not to be won by you; I have Gandharvas for my husband, they, if enraged, shall slay you. It is good for you not to bring destruction upon yourself.

14.49.sa: अशक्यरूपं पुरुषैरध्वानं गन्तुमिच्छसि । यथा निश्चेतनो वालः कूलस्थः कूलमुत्तरम् । तर्तुमिच्छति मन्दात्मा तथा त्वं कर्तुमिच्छसि ॥४९॥
14.49.en: You wish to go by the way which was never passed by men, O wicked one; you intend to act just like a foolish boy who standing on one bank of the ocean desires to go to the other side of it.

14.50.sa: अन्तर्महीं वा यदि वोर्ध्वमुत्पतेः समुद्रपारं यदि वा प्रधावसि । तथाऽपि तेषां न विमोक्षमर्हसि प्रमाथिनो देवसुता हि खेचराः ॥५०॥
14.50.en: If you enter the subterreneous pit of the earth or soar up the sky or go to the other shore of the ocean, still you will have no escape from their hands, for it is in the nature of these skyranging offspring of gods to crush enemies.

14.51.sa: त्वं कालरात्रीमिव कश्चिदातुरः किं मां दृढं प्रार्थयसेऽद्य कीचक । किं मातुरङ्के शयितो यथा शिशुश्चन्द्रं जिघृक्षुरिव मन्यसे हि माम् ॥५१॥
14.51.en: Why do you, O Kichaka, desire me today so firmly, just like a sick man who wishes for the night that will put an end to his existence. Why do you solicit me just like a child who lies on its mother's lap wishes to obtain the moon.

14.52.sa: तेषां प्रियां प्रार्थयतो न ते भुवि गत्वा दिवं वा शरणं भविष्यति । न वर्तते कीचक ते दृशा शुभं या तेन संजीवनमर्थयेत सा ॥५२॥
14.52.en: There will be nowhere any refuge for you soliciting their beloved wife whether you go to the earth or to the heaven. O Kichaka, you have no eyes that may win for you any good or safety of your life.

15.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । प्रत्याख्यातो राजपुत्र्या सुदेष्णां कीचकोऽब्रवीत्। अमर्यादेन कामेन घोरेणाभिपरिप्लुतः ॥१॥
15.1.en: Vaishampayana said Rejected thus by the princess Kichaka, over-pressed with fearful lust capable of making one forgetful of all sense of propriety, said to Sudeshna.

15.2.sa: यथा कैकेयि सैरन्ध्री समेयात्तद्विधीयताम् । येनोपायेन सैरन्ध्री भजेन्मां गजगामिनी । तं सुदेष्णे परीप्सस्व प्राणान्मोहात् प्रहासिषम् ॥२॥
15.2.en: O Kaikeyi, do that by which Sairandhri may be united with me. O Sudeshna, device a plan by which that Sairandhri of elephant-gait may accept me. Otherwise I intend putting end to my life.

15.3.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तस्य सा बहुशः श्रुत्वा वाचं विलपतस्तदा । विराटमहिषी देवी कृपां चक्रे मनस्विनी ॥३॥
15.3.en: Hearing the words of his thus lamenting in manifold terms the intelligent lady, Virata's queen, took pity on him.

15.4.sa: स्वमन्त्रमभिसन्धाय तस्यार्थमनुचिन्त्य च । उद्योगं चैव कृष्णायाः सुदेष्णा सूतमब्रवीत् ॥४॥
15.4.en: Holding counsel with her own self and pondering over his desire and over the perturbation of Krishna, Sudeshna said to Suta's son (Kichaka).

15.5.sa: पर्वणि त्वं समुद्दिश्य सुरामन्नं च कारय । तत्रैनां प्रेषयिष्यामि सुराहारीं तवान्तिकम् ॥५॥
15.5.en: Taking the advantage of some festival, better have wines and viands prepared. I shall then send her to you to bring some wine.

15.6.sa: तत्र संप्रेषितामेनां विजने निरवग्रहे । सान्त्वयेथा यथाकामं सान्त्व्यमाना रमेद्यदि॥६॥
15.6.en: Thus sent thereto you should, in uninterrupted solitude, humour her according to your will. Thus cajoled most likely she may be attached to you.

15.7.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । इत्युक्तः स विनिष्क्रम्य भगिन्या वचनात्तदा । सुरामाहारयामास राजार्हां सुपरिष्कृताम् ॥७॥
15.7.en: Thus addressed he, in pursuance of his sister's words, came out and procured very fine wines worthy of a king.

15.8.sa: भक्षांश्च विविधाकारान् बहूंश्चोच्चावचांस्तदा । कारयामास कुशलैरन्नं पानं सुशोभनम् ॥८॥
15.8.en: Then he had various kinds of food, diverse sorts of meat of excellent degree and delicious drinks, and dishes prepared by the cooks skilled in the business.

15.9.sa: तस्मिन् कृते तदा देवी कीचकेनोपमन्त्रिता । सुदेष्णा प्रेषयामास सैरन्ध्रीं कचिकालयम् ॥९॥
15.9.en: This being done Sudeshna as previously intimated by Kichaka sent her Sairandhri to the abode of Kichaka, saying.

15.10.sa: सुदेष्णोवाच । उत्तिष्ठ गच्छ सैरन्ध्रि कीचकस्य निवेशनम् । पानमानय कल्याणि पिपासा मां प्रबाधते ॥१०॥
15.10.en: Sudeshna said O Sairandhri, get up and repair to the abode of Kichaka. O gentle one, bring wine for ime, for thirst afflicts me.

15.11.sa: सैरन्ध्रयुवाच । न गच्छेयमहं तस्य राजपुत्रि निवेशनम् । त्वमेव राज्ञि जानासि यथा स निरपत्रपः ॥११॥

15.12.sa: न चाहमनवद्याङ्गि तव वेश्मनि भामिनि । कामवृत्ता भविष्यामि पतीनां व्यभिचारिणी ॥१२॥
15.12.en: O beautiful lady of excellent limbs, in your house, I shall never prove myself faithless to my husband and lead a life of chastity.

15.13.sa: त्वं चैव देवि जानासि यथा स समयः कृतः । प्रविशन्त्या मया पूर्वं तव वेश्मनि भामिनि ॥१३॥
15.13.en: O beautiful lady, you know full well the condition I made before I had entered your palace.

15.14.sa: कीचकस्तु सुकेशान्ते मूढो मदनदर्पितः । सोऽवमंस्यति मां दृष्ट्वा न यास्ये तत्र शोभने ॥१४॥
15.14.en: O you of beautiful hairs having good curls at the end, on seeing me that wicked Kichaka, rendered insolent by the god of desire, will dishonour me. O beautiful one, I shall not repair thither.

15.15.sa: सन्ति बह्व्यस्तव प्रेष्या राजपुत्रि वशानुगाः । अन्यां प्रेषय भद्रं ते स हि मामवमंस्यते ॥१५॥

15.16.sa: सुदेष्णोवाच । नैव त्वां जातु हिंस्यात् स इतः संप्रेषिता मया । इत्युक्त्वा प्रददौ पात्रं सपिधानं हिरण्मयम् ॥१६॥
15.16.en: Sudeshna said "Dispatched by me from my palace he will hardly do any harm to you"; saying this she handed out to her a golden pot with a cover.

15.17.sa: सा शङ्कमाना रुदती दैवं शरणमीयुषी । प्रातिष्ठत सुराहारी कीचकस्य निवेशनम् ॥१७॥
15.17.en: Filled with fear and shedding tears she asked for the divine protection, an then departed for Kichaka's house for fetching wine.

15.18.sa: सैरन्ध्र्युवाच । यथाऽहमन्यं भर्तृभ्यो नाभिजानामि कंचन । तेन सत्येन मां प्राप्तां मा कुर्यात् कीचको वशे ॥१८॥
15.18.en: Draupadi said As I do not know any other save and except my husband, let not Kichaka, by strength of that virtue, be able to bring me into his power.

15.19.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । उपातिष्ठत सा सूर्यं मुहूर्तमबला ततः । स तस्यास्तनुमध्यायाः सर्वं सूर्योऽवबुद्धवान् ॥१९॥
15.19.en: Vaishampayana said Then that helpless one worshipped the sungod for a moment and the deity understood all the prayers of her of slender waist.

15.20.sa: अन्तर्हितं ततस्तस्या रक्षो रक्षार्थमादिशत् । तच्चैनां नाजहात्तत्र सर्वावस्थास्वनिन्दिताम् ॥२०॥
15.20.en: Then he ordered a Rakshasa to protect her invisibly and from that time that Rakshasas also never left that blameless lady alone under any circumstances whatever.

15.21.sa: तां मृगीमिव सन्त्रस्तां दृष्ट्वा कृष्णां समीपगाम् । उदतिष्ठन्मुदा सूतो नावं लब्ध्वेव पारगः ॥२१॥
15.21.en: Beholding Krishna come to his presence like a terrified doe, the Suta rose up just like a person wishing to go to the other end of a river when he obtains a boat.

16.1.sa: कीचक उवाच । स्वागतं ते सुकेशान्ते सुव्युष्टा रजनी मम । स्वामिनी त्वमनुप्राप्ता प्रकुरुष्व मम प्रियम् ॥१॥
16.1.en: Kichaka said O fair one of beautiful tresses with curls at the end, you are welcome; very luckily for me the night has passed. I have got you as the mistress of my house, pray do what is good to me,

16.2.sa: सुवर्णमालाः कम्बूश्च कुण्डले परिहाटके । नानापत्तनजे शुभ्रे मणिरत्नं च शोभनम् ॥२॥
16.2.en: Let golden chains, couches, brilliant golden ear-rings of different countries, beautiful gems and jewels, silken garments and dcer skins be gathered for you.

16.3.sa: आहरन्तु च वस्त्राणि कौशिकान्यजिनानि च । अस्ति मे शयनं दिव्यं त्वदर्थमुपकल्पितम् । एहि तत्र मया सार्द्धं पिबस्व मधुमाधवीम् ॥३॥
16.3.en: I have a very fine bed prepared only for you; pray come there and drink with me the honeyed wine.

16.4.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । अप्रैषीद्राजपुत्री मां सुराहारीं तवान्तिकम् । पानमाहर मे क्षिप्रं पिपासा मेऽति चाब्रवीत् ॥४॥
16.4.en: Draupadi said The princess has sent me to you for taking away wine; give it to me quickly, she said to ine she has a great thirst.

16.5.sa: कीचक उवाच । अन्या भद्रे नयिष्यन्ति राजपुत्र्याः प्रतिश्रुतम् । इत्येतां दक्षिणे पाणौ सूतपुत्रः परामृशत् ॥५॥
16.5.en: Kichaka said O gentle one, others will take the wine that has been wromised to the princess, Saying this the Suta's son seized her by the right arm.

16.6.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । यथैवाहं नाभिचरे कदाचित् पतीन् मदाद्वै मनसाऽपि जातु । तेनैव सत्येन वशीकृतं त्वां द्रष्टाऽस्मि पापं परिकृष्यमाणम् ॥६॥
16.6.en: Draupadi said As I have never acted faithlessly towards my husbands, even at heart through infatuation; by virtue of that truth, O sinful one, I shall behold you overpowered and completely hurled down on the ground.

16.7.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । स तामभिप्रेक्ष्य विशालनेत्रां जिघृक्षमाणः परिभर्त्सयन्तीम् । जग्राह तामुत्तरवस्त्रदेशे स कीचकस्तां सहसाऽऽक्षिपन्तीम् ॥७॥
16.7.en: Vaishampayana said Wishing thus to take hold of her Kichaka, seeing that large-eyed lady reproaching him in this wise, seized her by the end of her upper garment while she was about to run away.

16.8.sa: प्रगृह्यमाणा तु महाजवेन मुहुर्विनिःश्वस्य च राजपुत्री । तया समाक्षिप्ततनुः स पापः पपात शाखीव निकृत्तमूलः ॥८॥
16.8.en: But seized with great force the princess of excellent limbs began to pant and unable to put up with it, she, with a frame trembling in wrath, hurled him hard on the ground. Being thus thrown down by her that sinful one fell to the ground like a tree whose root has been cut.

16.9.sa: सा गृहीता विधुन्वाना भूमावाक्षिप्य कीचकम् । सभां शरणमागच्छद्यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥९॥
16.9.en: Having thus thrown Kichaka down on the ground while seized by him she ran trembling to the court, where the king Yudhishthira was, to seek protection.

16.10.sa: तां कीचकः प्रधावन्तीं केशपाशे परामृशत् । अथैनां पश्यतो राज्ञः पातयित्वा पदाऽवधीत् ॥१०॥
16.10.en: Kichaka seized her by the locks while she was running with speed and struck her down by a kick in the very presence of the king.

16.11.sa: तस्य योऽसौ तदाऽर्केण राक्षसः संनियोजितः। स कीचकमपोवाह वातवेगेन भारत ॥११॥
16.11.en: 0 Bharata, the Rakshasa that was appointed by the sun-god for her protection, gave a push to Kichaka with as much force as that of the wind.

16.12.sa: स पपात तदा भूमौ रक्षोबलसमाहतः । विघूर्णमानो निश्चेष्टश्छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः ॥१२॥

16.13.sa: तां चासीनौ ददृशतुर्भीमसेनयुधिष्ठिरौ । अमृष्यमाणौ कृष्णायाः कीचकेन पराभवम् ॥१३॥
16.13.en: Both Bhimasena and Yudhishthira, who were seated there, beheld with unforgiving attitude, that outrage on Krishna committed by Kichaka.

16.14.sa: तस्य भीमो वधं प्रेप्सुः कीचकस्य दुरात्मनः । दन्तैर्दन्तांस्तदा रोषान्निष्पिपेष महामनाः ॥१४॥
16.14.en: Desiring the death of that wicked Kichaka the high-minded Bhima began to knash his teeth in wrath.

16.15.sa: धूमच्छाया ह्यभजतां नेत्रे चोछ्रितपक्ष्मणी । सस्वेदा भृकुटी चोग्रा ललाटे समवर्तत ॥१५॥
16.15.en: His eyes with their lashes upraised, assumed the aspect of smoky dark, and terrible wrinkles covered with sweat appeared on his forehead.

16.16.sa: हस्तेन ममृदे चैव ललाटं परवीरहा । भूयश्च त्वरितः क्रुद्धः सहसोत्थातुमैच्छत ॥१६॥
16.16.en: That slayer of hostile heroes rubbed his forehead with his hand and incensed with ire desired many times to rise up in haste.

16.17.sa: अथावमृ‌द्नादङ्गुष्ठमङ्गुष्ठेन युधिष्ठिरः । प्रबोधनभयाद्राजा भीमं तं प्रत्यषेधयत् ॥१७॥
16.17.en: The king Yudhishthira, apprehending discovery, pressed his thumb with his own and commanded Bhima to desist.

16.18.sa: तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं वीक्षमाणं वनस्पतिम् । स तमावारयामास भीमसेनं युधिष्ठिरः ॥१८॥
16.18.en: Yudhishthira forbade Bhimasena who looked like an infuriated elephant beholding a large tree.

16.19.sa: आलोकयसि किं वृक्षं सूद दारुकृतेन वै । यदि ते दारुभिः कृत्यं बहिर्वृक्षान्निगृह्यताम् ॥१९॥
16.19.en: O cook, do you behold trees for fuel? If you are in need of faggots better gather them up from the trees abroad.

16.20.sa: सा सभाद्वारमासाद्य रुदती मत्स्यमब्रवीत् । अवेक्षमाणा सुश्रोणी पतींस्तान् दीनचेतसः ॥२०॥
16.20.en: The weeping daughter of Draupadi, endowed with excellent hips, approaching the entrance of the court and beholding her lords of melancholy mood, tenacious in keeping up the disguise observing the pledge they had already sworn, burning with flashing eyes, spoke to the king of the Matsya's.

16.21.sa: आकारमभिरक्षन्ती प्रतिज्ञा धर्मसंहिता । दह्यमानेव रौद्रेण चक्षुषा द्रुपदात्मजा ॥२१॥
16.21.en: The weeping daughter of Draupadi, endowed with excellent hips, approaching the entrance of the court and beholding her lords of melancholy mood, tenacious in keeping up the disguise observing the pledge they had already sworn, burning with flashing eyes, spoke to the king of the Matsya's.

16.22.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । येषां वैरी न स्वपिति षष्ठेऽपि विषये वसन् । तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदाऽवधीत् ॥२२॥
16.22.en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the honored spouse of those whose enemies can never sleep even if they reside in regions of anchorites (what to speak of their living in a country of their own).

16.23.sa: ये दद्युर्ने च याचेयुर्ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः । तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदाऽवधीत् ॥२३॥
16.23.en: The son of a Suta has kicked me, the respected consort of those who are truthful, devoted to Brahmans and used to give away without asking any thing in gift.

16.24.sa: येषां दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषो ज्याघोषः श्रूयतेऽनिशम् । तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदाऽवधीत् ॥२४॥
16.24.en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the beloved wife of those, the sounds of whose drums and twangs of whose bow are constantly heard.

16.25.sa: ये च तेजस्विनो दान्ता बलवन्तोऽतिमानिनः । तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदाऽवधीत् ॥२५॥
16.25.en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the respected wife of those who are endowed with energy, and power of self-control, and who are exceedingly mighty and highly dignified.

16.26.sa: सर्वलोकमिमं हन्युर्धर्मपाशसितास्तु ये । तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदाऽवधीत् ॥२६॥
16.26.en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the honored wife of those who, if they had not been tied down by duty, could destroy the whole of this world.

16.27.sa: शरणं ये प्रपन्नानां भवन्ति शरणार्थिनाम् । चरन्ति लोके प्रच्छन्नाः क्व नु तेऽद्य महारथाः ॥२७॥
16.27.en: Alas where do those mighty warriors ramble in disguise today who grant refuge to those that come to solicit it.

16.28.sa: कथं ते सूतपुत्रेण वध्यमानां प्रियां सतीम् । मर्षयन्ति यथा क्लीबा बलवन्तोऽमितौजसः ॥२८॥

16.29.sa: क्व नु तेषाममर्षश्च वीर्यं तेजश्च वर्तते । न परीप्सन्ति ये भार्यां वध्यमानां दुरात्मना ॥२९॥

16.30.sa: मयाऽत्र शक्यं किं कर्तुं विराटे धर्मदूषके । यः पश्यन्मां मर्षयति वध्यमानामनागसम् ॥३०॥
16.30.en: What can I do in the city of Virata, the defiler of virtue, who coolly allows my innocent self thus to be insulted although he sees it (with his own eyes).

16.31.sa: न राजा राजवत्किञ्चित् समाचरति कीचके । दस्यूनामिव धर्मस्ते न हि संसदि शोभते ॥३१॥
16.31.en: The king does not act like a king in the slightest degree towards Kichaka. O king, your conduct is like that of a robber and does not become the royal court.

16.32.sa: नाहमेतेन युक्तं वै हन्तुं मत्स्य तवान्तिके। सभासदोऽत्र पश्यन्तु कीचकस्य व्यतिक्रमम् ॥३२॥
16.32.en: O Matsya, it is highly unbecoming that I should thus be outraged by this villain in the very presence of yours. Let all the courtiers mark this laxity on the part of Kichaka.

16.33.sa: कीचको न च धर्मज्ञो न च मत्स्यः कथंचन । सभासदोऽप्यधर्मज्ञा य एनं पर्युपासते ॥३३॥
16.33.en: Neither Kichaka is virtuous nor ever is Matsya. The courtiers who wait upon the king are also destitute of virtue.

16.34.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवंविधैर्वचोभिः सा तदा कृष्णाऽश्रुलोचना । उपालभत राजानं मत्स्यानां वरवर्णिनी ॥३४॥
16.34.en: Vaishampayana said With words like these the graceful Krishna, with eyes teeming with tears, rebuked the king of the Matsya.

16.35.sa: विराट उवाच । परोक्षं नाभिजानामि विग्रहं युवयोरहम् । अर्थतत्त्वमविज्ञाय किं नु स्यात् कौशलं मम ॥३५॥
16.35.en: Virata said I do not know anything of your quarrel that happened out of our light. How can there be any justice on that score unless I go through the true version of the case.

16.36.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततस्तु सभ्या विज्ञाय कृष्णां भूयोऽभ्यपूजयन् । साधु साध्विति चाप्याहुः कीचकं च व्यगर्हयन् ॥३६॥
16.36.en: Vaishampayana said Then the courtiers, hearing everything, praised Krishna and repeatedly exclaimed “well done well done,” and reproached Kichaka.

16.37.sa: सभ्या ऊचुः । यस्येयं चारुसर्वाङ्गी भार्या स्यादायतेक्षणा । परो लाभस्तु तस्य स्यान्न च शोचेत् कथंचन ॥३७॥
16.37.en: The Courtiers said Surely the man, who has this lady of expansive eyes and of all-graceful limbs for his wife, possesses every thing that is valuable and shall on.no occasion have to indulge in grief.

16.38.sa: न हीदृशी मनुष्येषु सुलभा वरवर्णिनी । नारी सर्वानवद्याङ्गी देवीं मन्यामहे वयम् ॥३८॥
16.38.en: Surely such a lady, of exceeding grace an perfectly faultless limbs, is hardly to be found among men. Indeed she seems in all wise to be a goddess to us.

16.39.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवं संपूजयन्तस्ते कृप्णां प्रेक्ष्य सभासदः । युधिष्ठिरस्य कोपात्तु ललाटे स्वेद आगमत् ॥३९॥
16.39.en: Vaishampayana said While the courtiers, seeing Krishna, were praising her in this way, there came from ire the drops of perspiration on the forehead of Yudhishthira.

16.40.sa: अथाब्रवीद्राजपुत्रीं कौरव्यो महिषीं प्रियाम् । गच्छ सैरन्ध्रि माऽत्रस्थाः सुदेष्णाया निवेशनम् ॥४०॥

16.41.sa: भर्तारमनुरुन्धन्त्यः क्लिश्यन्ते वीरपत्नयः । शुश्रूषया क्लिश्यमानाः पतिलोकं जयन्त्युत ॥४१॥
16.41.en: The wives of heroes endure pain for the sake of their husbands; but undergoing trouble in waiting upon their lords they at last go to the regions where their husbands depart.

16.42.sa: मन्ये न कालं क्रोधस्य पश्यन्ति पतयस्तव । तेन त्वां नाभिधावन्ति गन्धर्वाः सूर्यवर्चसः ॥४२॥
16.42.en: Me-seems your Gandharva husbands of sun-like effulgence do not consider this as a befitting opportunity of giving vent to their spleen, and therefore do not run on to your succour.

16.43.sa: अकालज्ञाऽसि सैरन्ध्रि शैलूषीव विरोदिषि । विघ्नं करोषि मत्स्यानां दीव्यतां राजसंसदि ॥४३॥
16.43.en: O Sairandhri, you are ignorant of opportunity and therefore weep like an actress; you are causing annoyance in the court of the Matsya's while they are diverting themselves with gaming.

16.44.sa: गच्छ सैरन्ध्रि गन्धर्वाः करिष्यन्ति तव प्रियम् । व्यपनेष्यन्तिं ते दुःखं येन ते विप्रियं कृतम् ॥४४॥

16.45.sa: सैरन्ध्युवाच । अतीव तेषां घृणिनामर्थेऽहं धर्मचारिणी । तस्य तस्यैव ते वध्या येषां ज्येष्ठोऽक्षदेविता ॥४५॥

16.46.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । इत्युक्त्वा प्राद्रवत् कृष्णा सुदेष्णाया निवेशनम् । केशान् मुक्त्वा च सुश्रोणी संरम्भाल्लोहितेक्षणा ॥४६॥
16.46.en: Vaishampayana said Having said this the fair Krishna with loosened hair and eyes reddened with wrath, rushed on towards the apartments of Sudeshna.

16.47.sa: शुशुभे वदनं तस्या रुदत्याः सुचिरं तदा । मेघलेखाविनिर्मुक्तं दिवीव शशिमण्डलम् ॥४७॥
16.47.en: On her having wept so long her countenance appeared like the lunar disc in the sky freed from the clouds.

16.48.sa: सुदेष्णोवाच । कस्त्वाऽवधीद्वरारोहे कस्माद्रोदिषि शोभने । कस्याद्य न सुखं भद्रे केन ते विप्रियं कृतम् ॥४८॥

16.49.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । कीचको माऽवधीत्तत्र सुराहारीं गतां तव । सभायां पश्यतो राज्ञो यथैव विजने वने ॥४९॥
16.49.en: Draupadi said As I went to fetch wine for you Kichaka struck me in the court in the very presence of the king as if in the midst of a lonely forest.

16.50.sa: सुदेष्णोवाच । घातयामि सुकेशान्ते कीचकं यदि मन्यसे । योऽसौ त्वां कामसंमत्तो दुर्लभामवमन्यते ॥५०॥

16.51.sa: सैरन्ध्युवाच । अन्ये चैनं वधिष्यन्ति येषामागः करोति सः । मन्ये चैवाद्य सुव्यक्तं यमलोकं गमिष्यति ॥५१॥
16.51.en: Sairandhri said Others whom he has wronged will slay him; I think he will certainly go this very day to the region of Yama (Death).

17.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । सा हता सूतपुत्रेण राजपत्नी यशस्विनी । वधं कृष्णा परीप्सन्ती सेनावाहस्य भामिनी ॥१॥
17.1.en: Vaishampayana said Thus outraged by the Suta's son that illustrious princess Krishna of exceeding beauty, brooding over the destruction of the leader of Virata's forces, repaired to her own apartments.

17.2.sa: जगामावासमेवाथ सा तदा द्रुपदात्मजा । कृत्वा शौचं यथान्यायं कृष्णा सा तनुमध्यमा ॥२॥
17.2.en: Having duly washed her body and clothes with water the slender-waisted Krishna, the daughter of Drupada, began to ponder weepingly on the means of discarding her grief.

17.3.sa: गात्राणि वाससी चैव प्रक्षाल्य सलिलेन सा । चिन्तयामास रुदती तस्य दुःखस्य निर्णयम् ॥३॥
17.3.en: Having duly washed her body and clothes with water the slender-waisted Krishna, the daughter of Drupada, began to ponder weepingly on the means of discarding her grief.

17.4.sa: किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि कथं कार्यं भवेन्मम । इत्येवं चिन्तयित्वा सा भीमं वै मनसाऽगमत् ॥४॥
17.4.en: What shall I do? Whither shall I go? How can my desire be accomplished? while she was thinking thus she thought of Bhima.

17.5.sa: नान्यः कर्ता ऋते भीमान्ममाद्य मनसः प्रियम् । तत उत्थाय रात्रौ सा विहाय शयनं स्वकम् ॥५॥
17.5.en: Save and except Bhima there is none else that can do this very day what is agreeable to me. Then afflicted with great woe that largeeyed Krishna of spacious breast and approved chastity, with mighty lords as her protectors, rose up at night, left her own bed and repaired speedily to the abode of Bhimasena, desirous of accosting her lord.

17.6.sa: प्राद्रवन्नाथमिच्छन्ती कृष्णा नाथवती सती । भवनं भीमसेनस्य क्षिप्रमायतलोचना ॥६॥
17.6.en: Save and except Bhima there is none else that can do this very day what is agreeable to me. Then afflicted with great woe that largeeyed Krishna of spacious breast and approved chastity, with mighty lords as her protectors, rose up at night, left her own bed and repaired speedily to the abode of Bhimasena, desirous of accosting her lord.

17.7.sa: दुःखेन महता युक्ता मानसेन मनस्विनी । सैरन्ध्युवाच । तस्मिन् जीवति पापिष्ठे सेनावाह मम द्विषि ॥७॥
17.7.en: Save and except Bhima there is none else that can do this very day what is agreeable to me. Then afflicted with great woe that largeeyed Krishna of spacious breast and approved chastity, with mighty lords as her protectors, rose up at night, left her own bed and repaired speedily to the abode of Bhimasena, desirous of accosting her lord.

17.8.sa: तत् कर्म कृतवानद्य कथं निद्रां निषेवसे । वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्त्वाऽथ तां शालां प्रविवेश मनस्विनी ॥८॥
17.8.en: Sairandhri said How can you enjoy the sweets of sleep while that foe of mine, the wretched commander of Virata's forces, lives still, having perpetrated that foul deed today?

17.9.sa: यस्यां भीमस्तथा शेते मृगराज इव श्वसन् । तस्या रूपेण सा शाला भीमस्य च महात्मनः ॥९॥
17.9.en: Vaishampayana said Having said this the high-minded Draupadi entered the chamber where Bhima lay asleep snoring like a lion.

17.10.sa: संमूर्छितेव कौरव्य प्रजज्वाल च तेजसा । सा वै महानसं प्राप्य भीमसेनं शुचिस्मिता ॥१०॥
17.10.en: O son of Kuru! Bhima's kitchen got grandeur and glamour as it was illumined with the divine touch of Draupadi's complexion and her presence. Draupadi with her innocent smile, accessed to great Bhima with her entrance in kitchen like (she) her on born in water (gradually access to heron, ox and elephant), parthiva cow of three years age and she elephant.

17.11.sa: सर्वश्वेतेव माहेयी वने जाता त्रिहायणी । उपातिष्ठत पाञ्चाली वासितेव वरर्षभम् ॥११॥
17.11.en: O son of Kuru! Bhima's kitchen got grandeur and glamour as it was illumined with the divine touch of Draupadi's complexion and her presence. Draupadi with her innocent smile, accessed to great Bhima with her entrance in kitchen like (she) her on born in water (gradually access to heron, ox and elephant), parthiva cow of three years age and she elephant.

17.12.sa: सा लतेव महाशालं फुल्लं गोमतितीरजम् । परिष्वजत पाञ्चाली मध्यमं पाण्डुनन्दनम् ॥१२॥
17.12.en: The daughter of Panchala embraced the second son of Pandu even as a creeper embraces a vigorous and huge Sala tree on the banks of the Gomati.

17.13.sa: बाहुभ्यां परिरभ्यैनं प्राबोधयदनिन्दिता । सिंहं सुप्तं वने दुर्गे मृगराजवधूरिव ॥१३॥
17.13.en: Having clasped him with her arms that faultless one roused him from his bed just as lioness awakes a sleeping lion in a solitary forest.

17.14.sa: भीमसेनमुपाश्लिष्यद्धस्तिनीव महागजम् । वीणेव मधुरालापा गान्धारं साधु मूर्छती । अभ्यभाषत पाञ्चाली भीमसेनमनिन्दिता ॥१४॥
17.14.en: Having embraced Bhimasena as a sheelephant embraces her mighty mate, that faultless daughter of Panchala, possessed of a voice sweet as the sound of a Vina, sounding out clearly the Gandharva tune addressed Bhimasena thus.

17.15.sa: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे भीमसेन यथा मृतः । नामृतस्य हि पापीयान् भार्यामालभ्य जीवति ॥१५॥
17.15.en: O Bhimasena, rise up, why do you sleep like a dead one? For a sinful wretch cannot live after insulting the wife of one that is not dead.

17.16.sa: स संप्रहाय शयनं राजपुत्र्या प्रबोधितः । उपातिष्ठत मेघाभः पर्यङ्के सोपसंग्रहे ॥१६॥

17.17.sa: अथाब्रवीद्राजपुत्रीं कौरव्यो महिषीं प्रियाम् । केनास्यथन संप्राप्ता त्वरितेव ममान्तिकम् ॥१७॥

17.18.sa: न ते प्रकृतिमान् वर्णः कृशा पाण्डुश्च लक्ष्यसे । आचक्ष्व परिषेशेण सर्वं विद्यामहं यथा ॥१८॥

17.19.sa: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं द्वेष्यं वा यदि वा प्रियम् । यथावत् सर्वमाचक्ष्व श्रुत्वा ज्ञास्यामि यत् क्षमम् ॥१९॥
17.19.en: Tell me everything clearly whether it be pleasurable; having heard all I shall do what lies in my power.

17.20.sa: अहमेव हि ते कृष्णे विश्वास्यः सर्वकर्मसु । अहमापत्सु चापि त्वां मोक्षयामि पुनः पुनः ॥२०॥

17.21.sa: शीघ्रमुक्त्वा यथाकामं यत्ते कार्यं विवक्षितम् । गच्छ वै शयनायैव पुरा नान्येन बुध्यते ॥२१॥
17.21.en: Telling me quickly what is your wish and what you purpose to do, repair to your bed before others are up.

18.1.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । अशोच्यत्वं कुतस्तस्या यस्या भर्ता युधिष्ठिरः । जानन् सर्वाणि दुःखानि किं मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥१॥
18.1.en: Draupadi said Whence can there be a freedom of grief to her who has Yudhishthira for her husband? Knowing all my griefs do you ask me?

18.2.sa: यन्मां दासीप्रवादेन प्रातिकामी तदाऽनयत् । सभापरिषदो मध्ये तन्मां दहति भारत ॥२॥
18.2.en: The grief, when Pratikami dragged me in the court in the midst of the courtiers calling me a slave, burns me still, C Bharata,

18.3.sa: पार्थिवस्य सुता नाम का नु जीवति मादृशी । अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमन्यत्र द्रौपदीं प्रभो ॥३॥
18.3.en: What other princess like me, would live enduring such a hard misery?

18.4.sa: वनवासगतायाश्च सैन्धवेन दुरात्मना । परामर्शो द्विर्तायो वै सोढुमुत्सहते तु का ॥४॥
18.4.en: Who else except me has so much energy as to suffer the insult offered by the wicked prince of Sindhu during our stay in the forest?

18.5.sa: मत्स्यराज्ञः समक्षं तु तस्य धूर्तस्य पश्यतः । कीचकेन परामृष्टा का नु जीवति मादृशी ॥५॥
18.5.en: Who else like me, can live having been kicked by Kichaka in the very presence of the wicked king of the Matsya's?

18.6.sa: एवं बहुविधैः क्लेशैः क्लिश्यमानां च भारत । न मां जानासि कौन्तेय किं फलं जीवितेन मे ॥६॥
18.6.en: O Bharata, of what use is the life to me, when you, O son of Kunti, do not think of me, who have been afflicted with various woes like these?

18.7.sa: योऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कीचको नाम भारत । सेनानीः पुरुषव्याघ्र श्यालः परमदुर्मतिः ॥७॥

18.8.sa: स मां सैरन्ध्रिवेषेण वसन्तीं राजवेश्मनि । नित्यमेवाह दुष्टात्मा भार्या मम भवेति वै ॥८॥

18.9.sa: तेनोपमन्त्र्यमाणाया वधार्हेण सपत्नहन् । कालेनेव फलं पक्कं हृदयं मे विदीर्यते ॥९॥
18.9.en: O slayer of foes, thus addressed by him deserving destruction, my heart is bursting like a fruit ripened in due time.

18.10.sa: भ्रातरं च विगर्हस्व ज्येष्ठं दुर्द्यूतदेविनम् । यस्याऽस्मि कर्मणा प्राप्ता दुःखमेतदनन्तकम् ॥१०॥
18.10.en: You should pass censure on your eldest brother who is sorely addicted to the despicable game of dice, through whose act alone I have received this endless woe.

18.11.sa: को हि राज्यं परित्यज्य सर्वस्वं चात्मना सह । प्रव्रज्यायैव दीव्येत विना दुर्द्यूतदेविनम् ॥११॥

18.12.sa: यदि निष्कसहस्रेण यच्चान्यत् सारवद्धनम् । सायंप्रातरदेविष्यदपि संवत्सरान् बहून् ॥१२॥
18.12.en: If he had played morning and evening for many years together pawning Nishkas by thousands and other treasures of value, still his silver and gold robes and cars, teams and goats, and sheep and horses and mules would have hardly suffered any diminution.

18.13.sa: रुक्मं हिरण्यं वासांसि यानं युग्यमजाविकम् । अश्वाश्वतरसङ्घांश्च न जातु क्षयमावहेत् ॥१३॥
18.13.en: If he had played morning and evening for many years together pawning Nishkas by thousands and other treasures of value, still his silver and gold robes and cars, teams and goats, and sheep and horses and mules would have hardly suffered any diminution.

18.14.sa: सोऽयं द्यूतप्रवादेन श्रियः प्रत्यवरोपितः । तूष्णीमास्ते यथा मूढः स्वानि कर्माणि चिन्तयन् ॥१४॥
18.14.en: But deprived of fortune by rivalry of dice he now holds silence like a fool meditating over his own misdeeds.

18.15.sa: दश नागसहस्त्राणि हयानां हेममालिनाम् । यं यान्तमनुयान्तीह सोऽयं द्यूतेन जीवति ॥१५॥
18.15.en: It is he, who while going out, was followed by ten thousand elephants, adorned with golden garlands, and he now supports himself by gambling at dice.

18.16.sa: रथाः शतसहस्राणि नृपाणाममितौजसाम् । उपासन्त महाराजमिन्द्रप्रस्थे युधिष्ठिरम् ॥१६॥
18.16.en: That great king, Yudhishthira, the best of the charitable, whom the kings by hundreds of thousands endowed with unparalleled power worshipped at the city of Indraprastha, at whose kitchen a hundred thousand maids, with plate in hand used to feed every day, day and night, numbers of guests, and who used to give away in charity a thousand nishkas, is also overpowered by great calamity caused by gambling.

18.17.sa: शतं दासीसहस्राणां यस्य नित्यं महानसे । पात्रीहस्तं दिवारात्रमतिथीन् भोजयत्युत ॥१७॥
18.17.en: That great king, Yudhishthira, the best of the charitable, whom the kings by hundreds of thousands endowed with unparalleled power worshipped at the city of Indraprastha, at whose kitchen a hundred thousand maids, with plate in hand used to feed every day, day and night, numbers of guests, and who used to give away in charity a thousand nishkas, is also overpowered by great calamity caused by gambling.

18.18.sa: एष निष्कसहस्त्राणि प्रदाय ददतां वरः । द्यूतजेन ह्यनर्थेन महता समुपाश्रितः ॥१८॥
18.18.en: That great king, Yudhishthira, the best of the charitable, whom the kings by hundreds of thousands endowed with unparalleled power worshipped at the city of Indraprastha, at whose kitchen a hundred thousand maids, with plate in hand used to feed every day, day and night, numbers of guests, and who used to give away in charity a thousand nishkas, is also overpowered by great calamity caused by gambling.

18.19.sa: एनं हि स्वरसंपन्ना बहवः सूतमागधाः । सायंप्रातरुपातिष्ठन्सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डलाः ॥१९॥

18.20.sa: सहस्त्रमृषयो यस्य नित्यमासन् सभासदः । तपःश्रुतोपसंपन्नाः सर्वकामैरुपस्थिताः ॥२०॥
18.20.en: That Yudhishthira, who had a number of sages versed in the Vedas, gifted with ascetic merit, and having all their wishes complied with, as his daily courtiers, and who maintained eighty-eight thousands of wedded snatakas, to each of whom there were assigned maids thirty in number, as well as ten thousand yatis abstaining from accepting any thing in shape of gift and having their vital seed totally drawn up, that lord of men lives in such a plight.

18.21.sa: अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि स्नातका गृहमेधिनः । त्रिंशद्दासीक एकैको यान् बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः ॥२१॥
18.21.en: That Yudhishthira, who had a number of sages versed in the Vedas, gifted with ascetic merit, and having all their wishes complied with, as his daily courtiers, and who maintained eighty-eight thousands of wedded snatakas, to each of whom there were assigned maids thirty in number, as well as ten thousand yatis abstaining from accepting any thing in shape of gift and having their vital seed totally drawn up, that lord of men lives in such a plight.

18.22.sa: अप्रतिग्राहिणां चैव यतीनामूर्धरेतसाम् । दश चापि सहस्राणि सोऽयमास्ते नरेश्वरः ॥२२॥
18.22.en: That Yudhishthira, who had a number of sages versed in the Vedas, gifted with ascetic merit, and having all their wishes complied with, as his daily courtiers, and who maintained eighty-eight thousands of wedded snatakas, to each of whom there were assigned maids thirty in number, as well as ten thousand yatis abstaining from accepting any thing in shape of gift and having their vital seed totally drawn up, that lord of men lives in such a plight.

18.23.sa: आनृशंस्यमनुक्रोशं संविभागस्तथैव च । यस्मिन्नेतानि सर्वाणि सोऽयमास्ते नरेश्वरः ॥२३॥
18.23.en: That lord of men, who is free from cruelty, full of compassion and used to give every one his legitimate due, is, inspite of all these excellent attributes, destined to live in such a guise.

18.24.sa: अन्धान्वृद्धांस्तथाऽनाथान्बालान् राष्ट्रेषु दुर्गतान् । बिभर्ति विविधान् राजा धृतिमान् सत्यविक्रमः । संविभागमना नित्यमानृशंस्याद्युधिष्ठिरः ॥॥२४॥
18.24.en: That very monarch Yudhishthira, who is forbearing, of unfailing prowess, and having a mind bent on giving every one his legitimate due, and in consequence of his not indulging in to a harmful feeling, maintained daily, in his kingdom, the blind, the old, the helpless, the orphans of various kinds and many others in such distress. That Yudhishthira, NOW becoming a servant of the king of the Matsya's, and a gambler in his court, and calling himself by the name Kanka, has surely attained the misery of hell.

18.25.sa: स एष निरयं प्राप्तो मत्स्यस्य परिचारकः । सभायां देविता राज्ञः कङ्को बूते युधिष्ठिरः ॥२५॥
18.25.en: That very monarch Yudhishthira, who is forbearing, of unfailing prowess, and having a mind bent on giving every one his legitimate due, and in consequence of his not indulging in to a harmful feeling, maintained daily, in his kingdom, the blind, the old, the helpless, the orphans of various kinds and many others in such distress. That Yudhishthira, NOW becoming a servant of the king of the Matsya's, and a gambler in his court, and calling himself by the name Kanka, has surely attained the misery of hell.

18.26.sa: इन्द्रप्रस्थे निवसतः समये यस्य पार्थिवाः । आसन् बलिभृतः सर्वे सोऽद्यान्यैर्भूतिमिच्छति ॥२६॥
18.26.en: Alas! even he begs for his subsistence at another's hands whom residing at Indraprastha, all the kings of earth used to pay tributes.

18.27.sa: पार्थिवाः पृथिवीपाला यस्यासन् वशवर्तिनः । स वशे विवशो राजा परेषामद्य वर्तते ॥२७॥
18.27.en: Alas! even that king, who had all the kings of earth in subjection, has lost his liberty and lives in subjection to others.

18.28.sa: प्रताप्य पृथिवीं सर्वां रश्मिमानिव तेजसा । सोऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य सभास्तारो युधिष्ठिरः ॥२८॥
18.28.en: Having dazzled, like the sun, the whole of this earth with his power, even that king Yudhishthira remains as a courtier of king Virata.

18.29.sa: यमुपासन्त राजानः सभायामृषिभिः सह । तमुपासीनमद्यान्यं पश्य पाण्डव पाण्डवम् ॥२९॥
18.29.en: O Pritha's son, behold that Pandava today waiting upon another, who was waited upon in court by the kings with sages.

18.30.sa: सदस्यं समुपासीनं परस्य प्रियवादिनम् । दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरं कोपो वर्धते मामसंशयम् ॥३०॥
18.30.en: Beholding Yudhishthira as a courtier sitting beside another and uttering eulogistic speeches, who is there that is not positively afflicted with grief.

18.31.sa: अतदर्हं महाप्राज्ञं जीवितार्थेऽभिसंस्थितम् । दृष्ट्वा कस्य न दुःखं स्याद्धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥३१॥
18.31.en: Beholding that virtuous Yudhishthira of great wisdom, undeserving of such a plight and serving another for maintenance who is there that is not overtaken by grief.

18.32.sa: उपास्ते स्म सभायां यं कृत्स्ना वीर वसुन्धरा । तमुपासीनमप्यन्यं पश्य भारत भारतम् ॥३२॥
18.32.en: 0 Bharata, behold that Bharata, who was worshipped by all the heroes of earth in court, even he is now serving another for subsistence.

18.33.sa: एवं बहुविधैर्दुःखैः पीड्यमानामनाथवत् । शोकसागरमध्यस्थां किं मां भीम न पश्यसि ॥३३॥
18.33.en: O Bhima, why do you not look at me who am stationed in the midst of the sea of sorrow and afflicted like a helpless one, with various woes.

19.1.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । इदं तु ते महद्दुःखं यत् प्रवक्ष्यामि भारत । न मेऽभ्यसूया कर्तव्या दुःखादेतद्ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥१॥
19.1.en: Draupadi said O Bharata, what I am going to tell you now is another great grief of mine; you should not get angry with me, as I tell you this out of a sheer sadness of heart.

19.2.sa: सूदकर्मणि हीने त्वमसमे भरतर्षभ । ब्रुवन् बल्लवजातीयः कस्य शोकं न वर्धयेः ॥२॥
19.2.en: Who is there whose grief is not enhanced seeing you employed in the abominable service of a cook, entirely unbecoming of you, and calling yourself as belonging to the sect of Ballava.

19.3.sa: सुपकारं विराटस्य बल्लवं त्वां विदुर्जनाः । प्रेष्यत्वं समनुप्राप्तं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥३॥
19.3.en: What can be more distressful than this that people should know you as Virata's cook Ballava by name and fallen into servitude. When you wait on the king Virata calling yourself as Ballava the cook after getting through the work of the kitchen, then my very niind sinks into despair.

19.4.sa: यदा महानसे सिद्धे विराटमुपतिष्ठसि । ब्रुवाणो बल्लवः सूदस्तदा सीदति मे मनः ॥४॥
19.4.en: What can be more distressful than this that people should know you as Virata's cook Ballava by name and fallen into servitude. When you wait on the king Virata calling yourself as Ballava the cook after getting through the work of the kitchen, then my very niind sinks into despair.

19.5.sa: यदा प्रहृष्टः सम्राट् त्वां संयोधयति कुञ्जरैः । हसन्त्यन्तःपुरे नार्यो मम तूद्विजते मनः ॥५॥
19.5.en: When the monarch in joy makes you fight with elephants and the women of his seraglio laugh my mind totally sinks in sorrow.

19.6.sa: शार्दूलैर्महिषैः सिंहैरागारे योध्यसे यदा । कैकेय्याः प्रेक्षमाणायास्तदा मे कश्मलं भवेत् ॥६॥
19.6.en: When you fought with lions, tigers and buffaloes in the inner apartment of the palace in the occular presence of Kaikayi then the faint came over me.

19.7.sa: तत उत्थाय कैकेयी सर्वास्ताः प्रत्यभाषत । प्रेष्याः समुत्थिताश्चापि कैकेयीं ताः स्त्रियोऽब्रुवन् ॥७॥
19.7.en: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

19.8.sa: प्रेक्ष्य मामनवद्याङ्गीं कश्मलोपहातमिव । स्नेहात् संवासजाद्धर्मात् सूदमेषा शुचिस्मिता ॥८॥
19.8.en: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

19.9.sa: योद्ध्यमानं महावीर्यमियं समनुशोचति । कल्याणरूपा सैरन्ध्री बल्लवश्चापि सुन्दरः ॥९॥
19.9.en: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

19.10.sa: स्त्रीणां चित्तं च दुर्ज्ञेयं युक्तरूपौ च मे मतौ । सैरन्ध्री प्रियसंवासान्नित्यं करुणवादिनी ॥१०॥
19.10.en: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

19.11.sa: अस्मिन् राजकुले चेमौ तुल्यकालनिवासिनौ । इति ब्रुवाणा वाक्यानि सा मां नित्यमतर्जयत् ॥११॥
19.11.en: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

19.12.sa: क्रुध्यन्तीं मां च संप्रेक्ष्य समशङ्कत मां त्वयि । तस्यां तथा ब्रुवत्यां तु दुःखं मां महदाविशत् ॥१२॥
19.12.en: Beholding me getting enraged she suspects me to be attached to you which she speaks; thus I am overtaken by great grief.

19.13.sa: त्वय्येवं निरयं प्राप्ते भीमे भीमपराक्रमे । शोके यौधिष्ठिरे मग्ना नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे ॥१३॥
19.13.en: Beholding you, O Bhima of terrible prowess, suffering from being fallen into such a dire calamity and sunk in grief for Yudhishthira I do not intend to live.

19.14.sa: यः सदेवान् मनुष्यांश्च सर्वांश्चैकरथोऽजयत् । सोऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कन्यानां नर्तको युवा ॥१४॥
19.14.en: Alas! that youthful one, who on a single car defeated all celestials and men, is now the dancing master of the daughters of the king Virata.

19.15.sa: योऽतर्पयद‌मेयात्मा खाण्डवे जातवेदसम् । सोन्तःपुरगतः पार्थ कूपेऽग्निरिव संवृतः ॥१५॥
19.15.en: That Pritha's son, who with his immeasurable energy gratified the fire-god in the Khandava forest, is now stationed in the seraglio like fire concealed in a well.

19.16.sa: यस्माद्भयममित्राणां सदैव पुरुषर्षभात् । स लोकपरिभूतेन वेषेणास्ते धनञ्जयः ॥१६॥

19.17.sa: यस्य ज्याक्षेपकाठिनौ बाहू परिघसन्निभौ । स शङ्खपरिपूर्णाभ्यां शोचन्नास्ते धनञ्जयः ॥१७॥
19.17.en: That Dhananjaya, whose arms are likes inaces of iron and are marked by the strokes of the bow-string, is living in grief with his wrists covered with conch-bracelets.

19.18.sa: यस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषात् समकम्पन्त शत्रवः । स्त्रियो गीतस्वनं तस्य मुदिताः पर्युपासते ॥१८॥
19.18.en: The singing sound of that one, the sound of whose bow-string caused tremble to his enemies, is now courted by only delightful women.

19.19.sa: किरीटं सूर्यसङ्काशं यस्य मूर्द्धन्यशोभत । वेणीविकृतकेशान्तः सोऽयमद्य धनञ्जयः ॥१९॥
19.19.en: That Dhananjaya, whose head was decked with a diadem of solar effulgence, is now appearing with braids ending in ugly curls.

19.20.sa: तं वेणीकृतकेशान्तं भीमधन्वानमर्जुनम् । कन्यापरिवृतं दृष्ट्वा भीम सीदति मे मनः ॥२०॥
19.20.en: O Bhima, seeing that mighty wielder of bow, Arjuna, with braids ending in ugly curls and surrounded by damsels, my heart is stricken with distress.

19.21.sa: यस्मिन्नस्त्राणि दिव्यानि समस्तानि महात्मनि । आधारः सर्वविद्यानां स धारयति कुण्डले ॥२१॥
19.21.en: That high-souled one, to whom all the celestials weapons are known, and who is the repository of all the sciences, is now wearing a pair of ear-rings.

19.22.sa: स्प्रष्टुं राजसहस्त्राणि तेजसाऽप्रतिमानि वै । समरे नाभ्यवर्तन्त वेलामिव महार्णवः ॥२२॥
19.22.en: That youthful one, whom myriads of kings of matchless prowess could not overcome in fight, even as the great ocean cannot overleap its banks, is now the dancing master of the daughters of king Virata and passes his days in disguise as one in the capacity of a servant to them.

19.23.sa: सोऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कन्यानां नर्तको युवा । आस्ते वेशप्रतिच्छन्नः कन्यानां परिचारकः ॥२३॥
19.23.en: That youthful one, whom myriads of kings of matchless prowess could not overcome in fight, even as the great ocean cannot overleap its banks, is now the dancing master of the daughters of king Virata and passes his days in disguise as one in the capacity of a servant to them.

19.24.sa: यस्य स्म रथघोषेण समकम्पत मेदिनी । सपर्वतवना भीम सहस्थावरजङ्गमा ॥२४॥
