19.24.en: O Bhima, that exalted younger brother of yours, the rattling sound of whose car-wheels made the entire earth with all her mountains and forests and with all things mobile and immobile, tremble, and O Bhimasena, who being born, all the grief's of Kunti vanished, now causes me to lament for him.

19.25.sa: यस्मिन् जाते महाभागे कुन्त्याः शोको व्यनश्यत । स शोचयति मामद्य भीमसेन तवानुजः ॥२५॥

19.26.sa: भूषितं तमलङ्कारैः कुण्डलैः परिहाटकैः । कम्बुपाणिनमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा सीदति मे मनः ॥२६॥
19.26.en: Beholding him approaching me adorned with golden ear-rings and other ornaments and with wrists with bracelets of conches, my heart sinks into sorrow.

19.27.sa: यस्य नास्ति समो वीर्ये कश्चिदुर्व्यां धनुर्धरः । सोऽद्य कन्यापरिवृतो गायन्नास्ते धनञ्जयः ॥२७॥
19.27.en: That Dhananjaya, to whom there is no bowman on the entire earth, equal in prowess, is now passing his days in singing surrounded by women.

19.28.sa: धर्मे शौर्ये च सत्ये च जीवलोकस्य संमतम् । स्त्रीवेषविकृतं पार्थं दृष्ट्वा सीदति मे मनः ॥२८॥
19.28.en: Beholding that son of Pritha honored to the world for virtue, prowess and truthfulness, now living in the hated guise of a woman, my heart sinks into sorrow.

19.29.sa: यदा होनं परिवृतं कन्याभिर्देवरूपिणम् । प्रभिन्नमिव मातङ्गं परिकीर्णं करेणुभिः ॥२९॥
19.29.en: When I look upon that good-like Partha surrounded by females in this music hall like an elephant of rent temples encircled by sheelephant before Virata, the king of the Matsyas, then all the cardinal points seem to me to have lost their existence.

19.30.sa: मत्स्यमर्थपतिं पार्थं विराटं समुपस्थितम् । पश्यामि तुर्यमध्यस्थं दिशो नश्यन्ति मे तदा ॥३०॥
19.30.en: When I look upon that good-like Partha surrounded by females in this music hall like an elephant of rent temples encircled by sheelephant before Virata, the king of the Matsyas, then all the cardinal points seem to me to have lost their existence.

19.31.sa: नूनमार्या न जानाति कृच्छ्रं प्राप्तं धनञ्जयम् । अजातशत्रु कौरव्यं मग्नं दुर्द्यूतदेविनम् ॥३१॥
19.31.en: Surely my mother-in-law does not know Dhananjaya sorely distressed with sorrow; nor does she know the descendant of Kuru, Ajatashatru, addicted to vicious gambling thus sunk in misery.

19.32.sa: तथा दृष्ट्वा यवीयांसं सहदेवं गवां पतिम् । गोषु गोवेषमायान्तं पाण्डुभूताऽस्मि भारत ॥३२॥
19.32.en: 0 Bharata, beholding Sahadeva, the youngest of you all, in the capacity of a protector of kine and in the guise of a cowherd, I grow pale.

19.33.sa: सहदेवस्य वृत्तानि चिन्तयन्ती पुनः पुनः । न निद्रामभिगच्छामि भीमसेन कुतो रतिम् ॥३३॥
19.33.en: Thinking over and over of Sahadeva's office I cannot obtain sleep what to speak of rest?

19.34.sa: न विन्दामि महाबाहो सहदेवस्य दुष्कृतम् । यस्मिन्नेवंविधं दुःखं प्राप्नुयात् सत्यविक्रमः ॥३४॥
19.34.en: 0 mighty-armed one, I know not of Sahadeva's sin for which that one of unfailing prowess suffers thus.

19.35.sa: दूयामि भरतश्रेष्ठ दृष्ट्वा ते भ्रातरं प्रियम् । गोषु गोवृषसङ्काशं मत्स्येनाभिनिवेशितम् ॥३५॥
19.35.en: O foremost of the Bharata's beholding the beloved brother of yours, the foremost of men, appointed by the king of the Matsyas in looking after his kine, I feel grieved.

19.36.sa: संरब्धं रक्तनेपथ्यं गोपालानां पुरोगमम् । विराटमभिनन्दन्तमथ मे भवति ज्वरः ॥३६॥
19.36.en: Beholding that hero clad in red garments, busy in gratifying Virata and posing himself at the head of the cowherds, fever comes on me.

19.37.sa: सहदेवं हि मे वीरं नित्यमार्या प्रशंसति । महाभिजनसंपन्नः शीलवान् वृत्तवानिति ॥३७॥
19.37.en: My mother-in-law always speaks of that heroic Sahadeva as one possessed of high reputation, good character and excellent conduct.

19.38.sa: ह्रीनिषेवो मधुरवाक् धार्मिकश्च प्रियश्च मे । स तेऽरण्येषु वोढव्यो याज्ञसेनि क्षपास्वपि ॥३८॥
19.38.en: Kunti, greatly attached to her sons, stood weeping with Sahadeva in her arms, while he was starting (with us) for the great forest and addressed me thus-"Sahadeva is bashful, sweet-voiced, virtuous, and very dear to me, therefore, Yajnaseni cheer him up while he feels dejected and tend him in the forest, day and night. He is tender and brave, devoted to the king, heroic and always respectful to his elder brother; O Panchali, feed him yourself."

19.39.sa: सुकुमारश्च शूरश्च राजानं चाप्यनुव्रतः । ज्येष्ठापचायिनं वीरं स्वयं पाञ्चालि भोजयेः ॥३९॥

19.40.sa: इत्युवाच हि मां कुन्ती रुदती पुत्रगृद्धिनी । प्रव्रजन्तं महारण्यं तं परिष्वज्य तिष्ठती ॥४०॥
19.40.en: Kunti, greatly attached to her sons, stood weeping with Sahadeva in her arms, while he was starting (with us) for the great forest and addressed me thus-"Sahadeva is bashful, sweet-voiced, virtuous, and very dear to me, therefore, Yajnaseni cheer him up while he feels dejected and tend him in the forest, day and night. He is tender and brave, devoted to the king, heroic and always respectful to his elder brother; O Panchali, feed him yourself."

19.41.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा व्यापृतं गोषु वत्सचर्मक्षपाशयम् । सहदेवं युधां श्रेष्ठं किं नु जीवामि पाण्डव ॥४१॥
19.41.en: Beholding that Sahadeva, the best of warriors, engaged in tending kine and lying on calf skins at night, O Pandava, how can I live?

19.42.sa: यस्त्रिभिर्नित्यसंपन्नो रूपेणास्त्रेण मेधया । सोऽश्वबन्धो विराटस्य पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम् ॥४२॥

19.43.sa: अभ्यकीर्यन्त वृन्दानि दामग्रन्थिमुदीक्ष्य तम् । विनयन्तं जवेनाश्वान् महाराजस्य पश्यतः ॥४३॥
19.43.en: Granthika, at whose presence hostile forces ran away from the field of battle, is now engaged in training horses before the king driving them with speed.

19.44.sa: अपश्यमेनं श्रीमन्तं मत्स्यं भ्राजिष्णुमुत्तमम् । विराटमुपतिष्ठन्तं दर्शयन्तं च वाजिनः ॥४४॥
19.44.en: I now see that graceful one wait upon the richly dressed and excellent Virata, the king of the Matsya's and make a show of his horses before the king.

19.45.sa: किं नु मां मन्यसे पार्थ सुखिनीति परन्तप । एवं दुःखशताविष्टा युधिष्ठिरनिमित्ततः ॥४५॥
19.45.en: O Pritha's son, afflicted with hundreds of sorrows on account of Yudhishthira, do you deem me happy, O repressor of foes.

19.46.sa: अतः प्रतिविशिष्टानि दुःखान्यन्यानि भारत । वर्तन्ते मयि कौन्तेय वक्ष्यामि शृणु तान्यपि ॥४६॥
19.46.en: O Bharata, there are various other woes greater than these which I am afflicted with; listen, O son of Kunti, I shall relate tell them all to you.

19.47.sa: युष्मासु ध्रियमाणेषु दुःखानि विविधान्युत । शोषयन्ति शरीरं मे किं नु दुःखमतः परम् ॥४७॥
19.47.en: Alas, you being all alive these various woes (render my person emaciated) undermine my system; what can be sadder than this?

20.1.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । अहं सैरन्ध्रिवेषेण चरन्ती राजवेश्मनि । शौचदाऽस्मि सुदेष्णाया अक्षधूर्तस्य कारणात् ॥१॥

20.2.sa: विक्रियां पश्य मे तीव्रां राजपुत्र्याः परन्तप । आत्मकालमुदीक्षन्ती सर्वं दुःखं किलान्तवत् ॥२॥
20.2.en: O repressor of foes, princess as I am, see what pitiful change has come upon me I am living in expectation of a hopeful future, but my misery has reached its extremity.

20.3.sa: अनित्या किल मर्त्यानामर्थसिद्धिर्जयाजयौ । इतिकृत्वा प्रतीक्षामि भर्तॄणामुदयं पुनः ॥३॥

20.4.sa: चक्रवत्परिवर्तन्ते ह्यर्थाश्च व्यसनानि च । इतिकृत्वा प्रतीक्षामि भर्तॄणामुदयं पुनः ॥४॥

20.5.sa: य एव हेतुर्भवति पुरुषस्य जयावहः । पराजये च हेतुश्च स इति प्रतिपालये । किं मां न प्रतिजानीषे भीमसेन मृतामिव ॥५॥
20.5.en: That which becomes a cause of a man's victory may become the cause of his defeat as well. I live in that hope.

20.6.sa: दत्वा याचन्ति पुरुषा हत्वा वध्यन्ति चापरे । पातयित्वा च पात्यन्ते परैरिति च मे श्रुतम् ॥६॥

20.7.sa: न दैवस्यातिभारोऽस्ति न चैवास्यातिवर्तनम् । इति चाप्यागमं भूयो दैवस्य प्रतिपालये ॥७॥
20.7.en: O Bhimasena, why do you not consider me as dead? I am told that persons that give may beg, persons that slaughter may be slaughtered by others, and that persons that ever throw others may be over-thrown by enemies. There is nothing difficult for destiny nor can any one over-rule destiny.

20.8.sa: स्थितं पूर्वं जलं यत्र पुनस्तत्रैव गच्छति । इति पर्यायमिच्छन्ती प्रतीक्षे उदयं पुनः ॥८॥
20.8.en: It is with this hope, I am expecting the return of favorable fortune; once before where there was water, there comes it back again. Hoping for this change, I am awaiting the return of prosperity.

20.9.sa: दैवेन किल यस्यार्थः सुनीतोऽपि विपद्यते । दैवस्य चागमे यत्नस्तेन कार्यो विजानता ॥९॥
20.9.en: When a man's business, although brought into a stage of completion, is seen to be endangered then a wise man should strive hard for the getting of good fortune.

20.10.sa: यत्तु मे वचनस्यास्य कथितस्य प्रयोजनम् । पृच्छ मां दुःखितां तत्त्वं पृष्टा चात्र ब्रवीमि ते ॥१०॥
20.10.en: Immersed as I am in grief, whether you ask me or not I shall tell you in detail, the purpose of these words now spoken by me.

20.11.sa: महिषी पाण्डुपुत्राणां दुहिता द्रुपदस्य च । इमामवस्थां संप्राप्ता मदन्या का जिजीविषेत् ॥११॥

20.12.sa: कुरून् परिभवेत् सर्वान् पाञ्चालानपि भारत । पाण्डवेयांश्च संप्राप्तो मम क्लेशो हारिन्दम ॥१२॥
20.12.en: () repressor of foes, this my misery surely brings humiliation, O Bharata, on all the Kurus, the Panchalas and the Pandavas.

20.13.sa: भ्रातृभिः श्वशुरैः पुत्रैर्बहुभिः परिवारिता । एवं समुदिता नारी का त्वन्या दुःखिता भवेत् ॥१३॥
20.13.en: Being surrounded by numerous brothers, father-in-law and sons and thus having ample cause for rejoicing what other woman but myself has become so miserable?

20.14.sa: नूनं हि बालया धातुर्मया वै विप्रियं कृतम् । यस्य प्रसादाद्दुर्नीतं प्राप्ताऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥१४॥
20.14.en: O foremost of the Bharata race, certainly in my childhood I did some wrongful act to Dhata and through his displeasure I have fallen into such a woeful plight.

20.15.sa: वर्णावकाशमपि मे पश्य पाण्डव यादृशम् । तादृशो मे न तत्रासीद्दुःखे परमके तदा ॥१५॥
20.15.en: Behold, O son of Pandu, the paleness of my complexion which even in the extremely miserable life in the forest could not come over me.

20.16.sa: त्वमेव भीम जानीषे यन्मे पार्थ सुखं पुरा । साऽहं दासीत्वमापन्ना न शान्तिमवशा लभे ॥१६॥

20.17.sa: नादैविकमहं मन्ये यत्र पार्थो धनञ्जयः । भीमधन्वा महाबाहुरास्ते छन्न इवानलः ॥१७॥
20.17.en: As the mighty-armed and terrible bowman Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha, lives here, like a fire covered over by ashes, then must I think that all these actions are due to Destiny.

20.18.sa: अशक्या वेदितुं पार्थ प्राणिनां वै गतिर्नरैः । विनिपातमिमं मन्ये युष्माकं ह्यविचिन्तितम् ॥१८॥
20.18.en: O son of Pritha, it is not possible for people to understand the destiny of creatures. Therefore this your downfall, I think, could not have been thwarted by fore-thought.

20.19.sa: यस्या मम मुखप्रेक्षा यूयमिन्द्रसमाः सदा । सा प्रेक्षे मुखमन्यासामवराणां वरा सती ॥१९॥
20.19.en: Alas, she who has you all resembling Indra always to look after her comforts, even that one, who is so chaste and bears so lofty a station in life, is ministering to the comforts of others who are far below in rank to her.

20.20.sa: पश्य पाण्डव मेऽवस्थां यथा नार्हामि वै तथा । युष्मासु ध्रियमाणेषु पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम् ॥२०॥
20.20.en: Though all of you are alive, behold O Pandava, my plight. It is such as is quite undeserving of me. Lo! how times change.

20.21.sa: यस्याः सागरपर्यन्ता पृथिवी वशवर्तिनी । आसीत् साऽद्य सुदेष्णाया भीताऽहं वशवर्तिनी ॥२१॥
20.21.en: Alas! she, who had the entire earth as far as the verge of the sea under her command, is now living in fear of Sudeshna and in subjugation to her. a

20.22.sa: यस्याः पुरःसरा आसन् पृष्ठतश्चानुगामिनः । साऽहमद्य सुदेष्णायाः पुरः पश्चाच्च गामिनी ॥२२॥
20.22.en: Even she, who had number of dependents to walk both in van and rear, is now walking before and behind Sudeshna. O Kunti's son, listen to another grief of mine; it is unbearable to me.

20.23.sa: इदं तु दुःखं कौन्तेय ममासह्यं निबोध तत् । या न जातु स्वयं पिंषे गात्रोद्वर्तनमात्मनः । अन्यत्र कुन्त्या भद्रं ते सा पिनष्म्यद्य चन्दनम् ॥२३॥

20.24.sa: पश्य कौन्तेय पाणी मे नैवाभूतां हि यौ पुरा । इत्यस्य दर्शयामास किणवन्तौ करावुभौ ॥२४॥
20.24.en: O Kunti's son, behold these hands of mine, they were not so before.” Saying this she showed both of her hands marked with corns.

20.25.sa: बिभेमि कुन्त्या या नाहं युष्माकं वा कदाचन । साऽद्याग्रतो विराटस्य भीता तिष्ठामि किङ्करी ॥२५॥

20.26.sa: किं नु वक्ष्यति सम्राण्मां वर्णकः सुकृतो न वा । नान्यपिष्टं हि मत्स्यस्य चन्दनं किल रोचते॥२६॥
20.26.en: (Always do I remain in fear thinking) what the king of kings will say to me as about the unguents if they are not well pounded; because the king of the Matsya's does not like the sandal pounded by others.

20.27.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । सा कीर्तयन्ती दुःखानि भीमसेनस्य भामिनी । रुरोद शनकैः कृष्णा भीमसेनमुदीक्षती ॥२७॥

20.28.sa: सा बाष्पकलया वाचा निःश्वसन्ती पुनः पुनः । हृदयं भीमसेनस्य घट्टयन्तीदमब्रवीत् ॥२८॥

20.29.sa: नाल्पं कृतं मया भीम देवानां किल्बिषं पुरा । अभाग्या यत्र जीवामि कर्तव्ये सति पाण्डव ॥२९॥
20.29.en: O Bhima, surely had I committed many sinful acts to gods in my former days. Unfortunate as I am, I am still alive, my death is preferable to me, O Pandava.

20.30.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच। ततस्तस्याः करौ सूक्ष्मौ किणबद्धौ वृकोदरः । सुखमानीय वे पत्न्या रुरोद परवीरहा ॥३०॥
20.30.en: Then Vrikodara the slayer of hostile heroes, covering his face with the delicate hands of his wife, marked with scars, began to weep.

20.31.sa: तौ गृहीत्वा च कौन्तेयो बाष्पमुत्सृज्य वीर्यवान् । ततः परमदुःखार्त इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥३१॥
20.31.en: The powerful son of Kunti, having held both of her hands in his own, began to shed tears, and stricken with great woe spoke the following.

21.1.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । धिगस्तु मे बाहुबलं गाण्डीवं फाल्गुनस्य च । यत्ते रक्तौ पुरा भूत्वा पाणी कृतकिणाविमौ ॥१॥
21.1.en: Bhima said Fie to the strength of my arms and fie to the Gandiva of Phalguni, since these your hands red before have now become marked with scars.

21.2.sa: सभायां तु विराटस्य करोमि कदनं महत् । तत्र मे कारणं भाति कौन्तेयो यत् प्रतीक्षते ॥२॥
21.2.en: I would have caused a great havoc in the court of Virata but the son of Kunti looked at me (by way of forbidding); that was the reason of my forbearance.

21.3.sa: अथवा कीचकस्याहं पोथयामि पदा शिरः । ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तस्य क्रीडन्निव महाद्विपः ॥३॥
21.3.en: Or like a mighty elephant I would have easily crushed with a single kick the head of Kichaka intoxicated with the pride of wealth.

21.4.sa: अपश्यं त्वां यदा कृष्णे कीचकेन पदा हताम् । तदैवाहं चिकीर्षामि मत्स्यानां कदनं महत् ॥४॥
21.4.en: O Krishna, when I saw you kicked by Kichaka, I intended the very moment to bring about a great devastation of the whole of the Matsya's.

21.5.sa: तत्र मां धर्मराजस्तु कटाक्षेण न्यवारयत् । तदहं तस्य विज्ञाय स्थित एवास्मि भामिनि ॥५॥
21.5.en: But the lord of justice forbade me by a glance, O beautiful one; knowing his intention I desisted from the purpose and kept quiet.

21.6.sa: यच्च राष्ट्रात् प्रच्यवनं कुरूणामवधश्च यः । सुयोधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेः सौबलस्य च ॥६॥
21.6.en: That we have been expelled from our kingdom, that I have not yet killed the Kurus, and that I have not yet taken the heads of Suyodhana, Karna, Shakuni the son of Subala the sinful Duryodhana, have been scorching every limb of mine and causing pain to my heart as if a peg is thrust into it.

21.7.sa: दुःशासनस्य पापस्य यन्मया नाहृतं शिरः। तन्मे दहति गात्राणि हृदि शल्यमिवार्पितम् । मा धर्मं जहि सुश्रोणि क्रोधं जहि महामते ॥७॥
21.7.en: That we have been expelled from our kingdom, that I have not yet killed the Kurus, and that I have not yet taken the heads of Suyodhana, Karna, Shakuni the son of Subala the sinful Duryodhana, have been scorching every limb of mine and causing pain to my heart as if a peg is thrust into it.

21.8.sa: इमं तु समुपालम्भं त्वत्तो राजा युधिष्ठिरः । शृणुयाद्वाऽपि कल्याणि कृत्स्नं जह्यात् स जीवितम् ॥८॥
21.8.en: O you beautiful, do not give up virtue; O noble minded lady, renounce your wrath. O auspicious one, if king Yudhishthira hears from you such rebukes, he is sure to give up his life.

21.9.sa: धनञ्जयो वा सुश्रोणि यमौ वा तनुमध्यमे । लोकान्तरगतेष्वेषु नाहं शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम् ॥९॥
21.9.en: O slender-waisted lady of beautiful hips, if Dhananjaya or the twins hear you speak thus, they will surely put an end to their lives; and they having given up life I shall not be able to keep up my own.

21.10.sa: पुरा सुकन्या भार्या च भार्गवं च्यवनं वने । वल्मीकभूतं शाम्यन्तमन्वपद्यत भामिनी ॥१०॥
21.10.en: In days of yore, the body of sage Chyavana had turned into a termite like feature due to incessant and long term penance. It seemed that the camp of his life will shortly cease illumine, yet his wife Sukanya did not show any way negligence towards him and kept on serving

21.11.sa: नारायणी चेन्द्रसेना रूपेण यदि ते श्रुता । पतिमन्वचरद्वृद्धं पुरा वर्षसहस्त्रिणम् ॥११॥
21.11.en: In olden days, perhaps you may have heard that Indrasena, who resembled Narayani in beauty, followed her old husband or a thousand years of age.

21.12.sa: दुहिता जनकस्यापि वैदेही यदि ते श्रुता । पतिमन्वचरत् सीता महारण्यनिवासिनम् ॥१२॥
21.12.en: You may have heard that Janaka's daughter Sita, the princess of Videha, went in the wake of her lord while he was dwelling in a great dreary forest.

21.13.sa: रक्षसा निग्रहं प्राप्य रामस्य महिषी प्रिया । क्लिश्यमानाऽपि सुश्रोणि राममेवान्वपद्यत ॥१३॥
21.13.en: That lady of beautiful hips, the beloved queen of Rama, although she received a great calamity at the hands of the Rakshasas and was afflicted with woe, was at length reunited with Rama.

21.14.sa: लोपामुद्रा तथा भीरु वयोरूपसमन्विता । अगस्तिमन्वयाद्धित्वा कामान् सर्वानमानुषान् ॥१४॥
21.14.en: O excellent one, Lopamudra also, endued with youth and beauty, followed her lord Agastya, renouncing all objects of enjoyments hardly to be attained by men.

21.15.sa: द्युमत्सेनसुतं वीरं सत्यवन्तमनिन्दिता । सावित्र्यनुचचारैका यमलोकं मनस्विनी ॥१५॥
21.15.en: The noble-minded lady of spotless beauty, Savitri, followed the heroic Satyavana, the son of Dyumatsena, alone into the reign of death.

21.16.sa: यथैताः कीर्तिता नार्यो रूपवत्यः पतिव्रताः । तथा त्वमपि कल्याणि सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः ॥१६॥
21.16.en: As these beautiful and chaste ladies are described by me, so also, by you, O auspicious one, appear endued with every virtue.

21.17.sa: मा दीर्घं क्षम कालं त्वं मासमर्धं च संमितम् । पूर्णे त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्ञां राज्ञी भविष्यसि ॥१७॥

21.18.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । आर्तयैतन्मया भीम कृतं बाष्पप्रमोचनम् । अपारयन्त्या दुःखानि न राजानमुपालभे ॥१८॥
21.18.en: Draupadi said O Bhima, I am unable to endure my griefs; it is out of sheer grief, I have shed these tears, I do not rebuke the king (Yudhishthira).

21.19.sa: किमुक्तेन व्यतीतेन भीमसेन महाबल । प्रत्युपस्थितकालस्य कार्यस्यानन्तरो भव ॥१९॥
21.19.en: O Bhimsena, what is the use of dwelling on what is passed. Be ready for the present.

21.20.sa: ममेह भीम कैकेयी रूपाभिभवशङ्कया । नित्यमुद्विजते राजा कथं नेयादिमामिति ॥२०॥
21.20.en: O Bhima, Kaikeyi, fearing that the king might take a fancy for me for my beauty, tries how to send me away from this place.

21.21.sa: तस्या विदित्वा तं भावं स्वयं चानृतदर्शनः । कीचकोऽयं सुदुष्टात्मा सदा प्रार्थयते हि माम्॥२१॥
21.21.en: Understanding her intention, that wickedsouled Kichaka of sinful conduct, always solicits me himself.

21.22.sa: तमहं कुपिता भीम पुनः कोपं नियम्य च । अब्रुवं कामसम्मूढमात्मानं रक्ष कीचक ॥२२॥
21.22.en: O Bhima, getting enraged with him and then again suppressing my anger I said to Kichaka, rendered senseless by lust in the following words)-0Kichaka save yourself; I am the dear queen and wife of five Gandharvas; those heroes if enraged will kill you who are going to act so rashly.”

21.23.sa: गन्धर्वाणामहं भार्या पञ्चानां महिषी प्रिया । ते त्वां निहन्युः कुपिताः शूराः साहसकारिणः ॥२३॥

21.24.sa: एवमुक्तः सुदुष्टात्मा कीचकः प्रत्युवाच ह । नाहं बिभेमि सैरन्ध्रि गन्धर्वाणां शुचिस्मिते ॥२४॥

21.25.sa: शतं शतसहस्राणि गन्धर्वाणामहं रणे । समागतं हनिष्यामि त्वं भीरु कुरु मे क्षणम् ॥२५॥
21.25.en: I will do away with a hundred thousand Gandharvas in battle, O timid one, give me your consent."

21.26.sa: इत्युक्ते चाब्रुवं मत्तं कामातुरमहं पुनः । न त्वं प्रतिबलश्चैषां गन्धर्वाणां यशस्विनाम् ॥२६॥
21.26.en: Thus replied to, I addressed again that lust stricken Suta saying, "you are no rival to those illustrious Gandharvas.

21.27.sa: धर्मे स्थिताऽस्मि सततं कुलशीलसमन्विता । नेच्छामि कञ्चिद्वध्यन्तं तेन जीवसि कीचक ॥२७॥
21.27.en: Born of a noble family and endued with good disposition, do I even regard virtue as my stay and never wish for the death of any one. O Kichaka, therefore you live still.

21.28.sa: एवमुक्तः स दुष्टात्मा प्राहसत् स्वनवत्तदा । अथ मां तत्र कैकेयी प्रेषयत् प्रणयेन तु ॥२८॥
21.28.en: Thus addressed, that wicked-souled Kichaka burst out into a loud laughter. Then Kaikeyi, out of affection for her brother, and previously urged by him and having a mind to do good to him, sent me to Kichaka saying, “O auspicious one, bring wine from Kichaka's house."

21.29.sa: तेनैव देशिता पूर्वं भ्रातृप्रियचिकीर्षया । सुरामानय कल्याणि कीचकस्य निवेशनात् ॥२९॥
21.29.en: Thus addressed, that wicked-souled Kichaka burst out into a loud laughter. Then Kaikeyi, out of affection for her brother, and previously urged by him and having a mind to do good to him, sent me to Kichaka saying, “O auspicious one, bring wine from Kichaka's house."

21.30.sa: सूतपुत्रस्तु मां दृष्ट्वा महत्सान्त्वमवर्तयत् । सान्त्वे प्रतिहते क्रुद्धः परामर्शमनाऽभवत् ॥३०॥
21.30.en: Beholding me, the Suta's son began to court me in sweet words; when his court failed, he became enraged and attempted to use violence on me.

21.31.sa: विदित्वा तस्य सङ्कल्पं कीचकस्य दुरात्मनः । तथाऽहं राजशरणं जवेनैव प्रधाविता ॥३१॥
21.31.en: Having understood the intention of that wicked-souled Kichaka, I ran with speed to the royal protection.

21.32.sa: सन्दर्शने तु मां राज्ञः सूतपुत्रः परामृशत् । पातयित्वा तु दुष्टात्मा पदाऽहं तेन ताडिता ॥३२॥
21.32.en: In the presence of the king, I was thrown down on the ground and kicked by the Suta's son of wicked soul.

21.33.sa: प्रेक्षते स्म विराटस्तु कङ्कस्तु बहवो जनाः । रथिनः पीठमर्दाश्च हस्त्यारोहाश्च नैगमाः ॥३३॥
21.33.en: This scene was witnessed by Virata, Kanka and many others, namely the charioteers, royal favorites, elephant riders, and merchants. Then he was neither prevented nor any punishment was inflicted on him by the king.

21.34.sa: उपालब्धो मया राजा कङ्कश्चापि पुनः पुनः । ततो न वारितो राज्ञा न तस्याविनयः कृतः ॥३४॥
21.34.en: This scene was witnessed by Virata, Kanka and many others, namely the charioteers, royal favorites, elephant riders, and merchants. Then he was neither prevented nor any punishment was inflicted on him by the king.

21.35.sa: योऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कीचको नाम सारथिः । त्यक्तधर्मा नृशंसश्च नरस्त्रीसम्मतः प्रियः ॥३५॥
21.35.en: This very Kichaka is the principal ruler of the king Virata. He is devoid of virtue, cruel, favoured by the king and liked by women at large.

21.36.sa: शूरोऽभिमानी पापात्मा सर्वार्थेषु च मुग्धवान् । दारामर्शी महाभाग लभतेऽर्थान् बहूनपि ॥३६॥
21.36.en: That wicked-souled Kichaka is war-like, proud, outrager of female modesty and engrossed in all objects of pleasure; O blessed one, he acquires plenty of money (from the king).

21.37.sa: आहरेदपि वित्तानि परेषां क्रोशतामपि । न तिष्ठते स्म सन्मार्गे न च धर्मं बुभूषति ॥३७॥
21.37.en: He extorts money from others, even if they cry in woe; he never stays in paths of rectitude nor does he even feel inclined to virtue.

21.38.sa: पापात्मा पापभावश्च कामबाणवशानुगः। अविनीतश्च दुष्टात्मा प्रत्याख्यातः पुनः पुनः ॥३८॥
21.38.en: He is wicked-souled, of sinful disposition, impudent, villaneous and afflicted by Cupid's shaft. Although I have repeatedly rejected him, he will, I am sure, outrage me, whenever he happens to see me, and then I shall surely give up my life; although you are striving to acquire that virtue but on my death, surely you will lose that great one.

21.39.sa: दर्शने दर्शने हन्याद्यदि जह्यां च जीवितम् । तद्धर्मे यतमानानां महान् धर्मो नशिष्यति ॥३९॥
21.39.en: He is wicked-souled, of sinful disposition, impudent, villaneous and afflicted by Cupid's shaft. Although I have repeatedly rejected him, he will, I am sure, outrage me, whenever he happens to see me, and then I shall surely give up my life; although you are striving to acquire that virtue but on my death, surely you will lose that great one.

21.40.sa: समयं रक्षमाणानां भार्या वो न भविष्यति । भार्यायां रक्ष्यमाणायां प्रजा भवति रक्षिता ॥४०॥
21.40.en: You, who are trying to keep your pledge, will lose your wife; wife being protected, one's offspring will be protected.

21.41.sa: प्रजायां रक्ष्यमाणायामात्मा भवति रक्षितः । आत्मा हि जायते तस्यां तेन जायां विदुर्बुधाः ॥४१॥
21.41.en: Offspring being protected, soul is saved. In a wife one's own self is begotten and it is therefore the wife is called Jaya by the wise.

21.42.sa: भर्ता तु भार्यया रक्ष्यः कथं जायान्ममोदरे । वदतां वर्णधर्मश्च ब्राह्मणानामिति श्रुतः ॥४२॥
21.42.en: The wife should also protect the husband, thinking "How then can he take his birth in my womb?" I have heard it from Brahmanas, who are expert in expounding the duties of all orders.

21.43.sa: क्षत्रियस्य सदा धर्मो नान्यः शत्रुनिबर्हणात् । पश्यतो धर्मराजस्य कीचको मां पदाऽवधीत् ॥४३॥
21.43.en: There is no other duty of Kshatriyas but the repressing of their foes. Taking no notice of the presence of Dharmaraja, as well as of yours, O mighty Bhimasena, Kichaka kicked me.

21.44.sa: तव चैव समक्षे वै भीमसेन महाबल । त्वया ह्यहं परित्राता तस्माद्धोराज्जटासुरात् ॥४४॥
21.44.en: It was you that rescued me from that terrible Jatasura, it was you only, who also with the help of your brothers, defeated Jayadratha. I entreat you to kill this wretch who has insulted me.

21.45.sa: जयद्रथं तथैव त्वमजैषीर्भ्रातृभिः सह । जहीममपि पापिष्ठं योऽयं मामवमन्यते ॥४५॥
21.45.en: It was you that rescued me from that terrible Jatasura, it was you only, who also with the help of your brothers, defeated Jayadratha. I entreat you to kill this wretch who has insulted me.

21.46.sa: कीचको राजवाल्लभ्याच्छोककृन्मम भारत । तमेवं कामसंमत्तं भिन्धि कुम्भमिवाश्मनि ॥४६॥
21.46.en: O Bharata, Kichaka, out of confidence that he is a favourite of the king, causes woe to me. I solicit you to crush this beloved one maddened with lust, even as an earthen pot dashed against a stone.

21.47.sa: यो निमित्तमनर्थानां बहूनां मम भारत । तं चेज्जीवन्तमादित्यः प्रातरभ्युदयिष्यति ॥४७॥
21.47.en: If, O Bharata, the men make him rise up again in the morning living, who is the root of all these griefs of mine, I shall mix poison with some drink and swallow it up, but never shall I yield myself to the power of Kichaka. O Bhimasena, certainly death is preferable to me in the very sight of you.

21.48.sa: विषमालोड्य पास्यामि मा कीचकवशं गमम् । श्रेयो हि मरणं मह्यं भीमसेन तवाग्रतः ॥४८॥
21.48.en: If, O Bharata, the men make him rise up again in the morning living, who is the root of all these griefs of mine, I shall mix poison with some drink and swallow it up, but never shall I yield myself to the power of Kichaka. O Bhimasena, certainly death is preferable to me in the very sight of you.

21.49.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । इत्युक्त्वा प्रारुदत् कृष्णा भीमस्योरः समाश्रिता । भीमश्च तां परिष्वज्य महत्सान्त्वं प्रयुज्य च ॥४९॥
21.49.en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, Krishna, lying on the breast of Bhima, began to weep. Having clasped her, Bhima also afforded her a great consolation.

21.50.en: Having consoled that greatly afflicted lady of slender waist in various ways, and having wiped with his hands her face flooded with tears, Bhima filled with ire, began to think of Kichaka in his mind, licking repeatedly the corners of his mouth with his tongue; and he addressed the daughter of Drupada afflicted with woe with words replete with reason.

21.51.sa: प्रमृज्य वदनं तस्याः पाणिनाऽश्रुसमाकुलम् । कीचकं मनसाऽगच्छत् सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन् । उवाच चैनां दुःखार्तां भीमः क्रोधसमन्वितः ॥५१॥

22.1.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । तथा भद्रे करिष्यामि यथा त्वं भीरु भाषसे । अद्य तं सूदयिष्यामि कीचकं सहबान्धवम् ॥१॥
22.1.en: Bhima said O gentle one, I will do that which you say. O timid one, I will kill Kichaka today with all his friends.

22.2.sa: अस्याः प्रदोषे शर्वर्याः कुरुष्वानेन सङ्गतम् । दुःखं शोकं च निर्धूय याज्ञसेनि शुचिस्मिते ॥२॥

22.3.sa: यैषा नर्तनशालेह मत्स्यराजेन कारिता । दिवाऽत्र कन्या नृत्यन्ति रात्रौ यान्ति यथागृहम् ॥३॥
22.3.en: There is the dancing house which the king of the Matsya's has caused to be built; there the girls dance during the day and retire to their respective homes at night.

22.4.sa: तत्रास्ति शयनं दिव्यं दृढाङ्गं सुप्रतिष्ठितम् । तत्रास्य दर्शयिष्यामि पूर्वप्रेतान् पितामहान् ॥४॥
22.4.en: In that hall there is a bedstead fixed firm and conveniently placed; there I will make him see the spirits of his deceased manes.

22.5.sa: यथा च त्वां न पश्येयुः कुर्वाणां तेन संविदम् । कुर्यास्तथा त्वं कल्याणि यथा सन्निहितो भवेत् ॥५॥
22.5.en: In course of holding conversation with him, do such as others might not see you. O auspicious one, also manage in such a way as he might come near you.

22.6.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तथा तौ कथयित्वा तु बाष्पमुत्सृज्य दुःखितौ । रात्रिशेषं तमत्युग्रं धारयामासतुर्हृदि ॥६॥
22.6.en: Vaishampayana said Having thus held their mutual conversation, and shedding tears in grief, they both awaited the dawn of that night with an anxious heart.

22.7.sa: तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां प्रातरुत्थाय कीचकः । गत्वा राजकुलायैव द्रौपदीमिदमब्रवीत् ॥७॥
22.7.en: That night being passed, Kichaka rose up in the morning, and having gone to the royal house, addressed Draupadi in the following terms.

22.8.sa: सभायां पश्यतो राज्ञः पातयित्वा पदाऽहनम् । न चैवालभसे त्राणमभिपन्ना बलीयसा ॥८॥
22.8.en: I hurled you down in the court and kicked you in the very presence of the king. Having fallen under the grasp of my mighty self you could not obtain deliverance.

22.9.sa: प्रवादेनेह मत्स्यानां राजा नाम्नाऽयमुच्यते । अहमेव हि मत्स्यानां राजा वै वाहिनीपतिः ॥९॥
22.9.en: Virata is said to be the king of the Matsya's, but that is only in name; lord of the forces, it is I alone who am verily the king of the Matsya's.

22.10.sa: मां सुखं प्रतिपद्यस्व दासो भीरु भवामि ते । अह्नाय तव सुश्रोणि शतं निष्कान् ददाम्यहम्॥१०॥
22.10.en: O timid one, accept me happily; I shall become your slave. O you of beautiful hips, I shall give you anon a hundred Nishkas and a hundred male and a hundred female servants. I shall also bestow on you cars yoked with mules; ( beautiful one, let us be united.

22.11.sa: दासीशतं च ते दद्यां दासानामपि चापरम् । रथं चाश्वतरीयुक्तमस्तु नौ भीरु सङ्गमः ॥११॥
22.11.en: O timid one, accept me happily; I shall become your slave. O you of beautiful hips, I shall give you anon a hundred Nishkas and a hundred male and a hundred female servants. I shall also bestow on you cars yoked with mules; ( beautiful one, let us be united.

22.12.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । एवं मे समयं त्वद्य प्रतिपद्यस्व कीचक । न त्वां सखा वा भ्राता वा जानीयात् सङ्गतं मया ॥१२॥

22.13.sa: अनुप्रवादाद्भीताऽस्मि गन्धर्वाणां यशस्विनाम् । एवं मे प्रतिजानीहि ततोऽहं वशगा तव ॥१३॥

22.14.sa: कीचक उवाच । एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथा सुश्रोणि भाषसे । एको भद्रे गमिष्यामि शून्यमावसथं तव ॥१४॥
22.14.en: Kichaka said O you of beautiful hips, I will do what you say; overcome by the god of love O gentle one, I shall go alone to your lonely abode for the purpose of being united with you, so that, O you of elegant thighs, the Gandharvas, as brilliant as the sun, might not be able to see you.

22.15.sa: समागमार्थं रम्भोरु त्वया मदनमोहितः । यथा त्वां नैव पश्येयुर्गन्धर्वाः सूर्यवर्चसः ॥१५॥

22.16.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । यदेतन्नर्तनागारं मत्स्यराजेन कारितम् । दिवाऽत्र कन्या नृत्यन्ति रात्रौ यान्ति यथागृहम् ॥१६॥
22.16.en: Draupadi said Behold there is the dancing hall erected by the king of the Matsya's. Here the girls dance during the day and retire to their respective homes at night.

22.17.sa: तमिस्रे तत्र गच्छेथा गन्धर्वास्तन्न जानते । तत्र दोषः परिहृतो भविष्यति न संशयः ॥१७॥

22.18.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तमर्थमपि जल्पन्त्याः कृष्णायाः कीचकेन ह । दिवसार्धं समभवन्मासेनैव समं नृप ॥१८॥
22.18.en: Vaishampayana said O king, thinking of the conversation she had with Kichaka, that half day appeared to Krishna as long as a whole month.

22.19.sa: कीचकोऽथ गृहं गत्वा भृशं हर्षपरिप्लुतः । सैरन्ध्रीरूपिणं मूढो मृत्युं तं नावबुद्धवान् ॥१९॥
22.19.en: Thereupon she again informed Bhimasena of his conduct; Kichaka too, going to his house, was filled with joy.

22.20.sa: गन्धाभरणमाल्येषु व्यासक्तः सविशेषतः । अलञ्चके तदाऽऽत्मानं सत्वरः काममोहितः ॥२०॥
22.20.en: That stupid could not understand that his death was in the shape of Sairandhri and he became especially busy with perfumeries, ornaments and garlands.

22.21.sa: तस्य तत्कुर्वतः कर्म कालो दीर्घ इवाभवत् । अनुचिन्तयतश्चापि तामेवायतलोचनाम् ॥२१॥
22.21.en: He, then possessed by lust adorned himself speedily. While he was doing this and thinking of the female with large eyes, the time appeared to him to be long; and the beauty which was about to forsake him, appeared to him to be increased,

22.22.sa: आसीदभ्यधिका चापि श्रीः श्रियं प्रमुमुक्षतः । निर्वाणकाले दीपस्य वर्तीमिव दिधक्षतः ॥२२॥
22.22.en: He, then possessed by lust adorned himself speedily. While he was doing this and thinking of the female with large eyes, the time appeared to him to be long; and the beauty which was about to forsake him, appeared to him to be increased,

22.23.sa: कृतसंप्रत्ययस्तस्याः कीचकः काममोहितः । नाजानाद्दिवसं यान्तं चिन्तयानः समागमम् ॥२३॥

22.24.sa: ततस्तु द्रौपदी गत्वा तदा भीमं महानसे । उपातिष्ठत कल्याणी कौरव्यं पतिमन्तिकम् ॥२४॥
22.24.en: Thinking of the meeting could not perceive that the day had passed away. Thereupon going to Bhima in the kitchen Draupadi.

22.25.sa: तमुवाच सुकेशान्ता कीचकस्य मया कृतः । सङ्गमो नर्तनागारे यथाऽवोचः परन्तप ॥२५॥

22.26.sa: शून्यं स नर्तनागारमागमिष्यति कीचकः । एको निशि महाबाहो कीचकं तं निषूदय ॥२६॥
22.26.en: Of auspiciousness, sat by his husband, the descendant of Kuru; that lady of beautiful hair said to him: “O slayer of foes, as directed by you, I have given Kichaka to understand that our meeting shall take place in the theatre hall. Kichaka shall come to that empty dancing-hall.

22.27.sa: तं सूतपुत्रं कौन्तेय कीचकं मददर्पितम् । गत्वा त्वं नर्तनागारं निर्जीवं कुरु पाण्डव ॥२७॥
22.27.en: Alone at night, O son of Kunti, slay him, that son of a Suta inflated with pride.

22.28.sa: दर्पाच्च सूतपुत्रोऽसौ गन्धर्वानवमन्यते । तं त्वं प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठ ह्रदान्नागमिवोद्धर ॥२८॥
22.28.en: O Pandava, going to that dancing hall, take his life. From pride only, that son of a Suta slights the Gandharvas.

22.29.sa: अश्रु दुःखाभिभूताया मम मार्जस्व भारत । आत्मनश्चैव भद्रं ते कुरु मानं कुलस्य च ॥२९॥

22.30.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । स्वागतं ते वरारोहे यन्मां वेदयसे प्रियम् । न ह्यन्यं कञ्चिदिच्छामि सहायं वरवर्णिनि ॥३०॥
22.30.en: Bhimasena said O fair and timid lady, I shall do what you say, welcome, O fair damsel, you, who have communicated this pleasant news to me.

22.31.sa: या मे प्रीतिस्त्वयाऽऽख्याता कीचकस्य समागमे । हत्वा हिडिम्बं सा प्रीतिर्ममासीद्वरवर्णिनि ॥३१॥
22.31.en: O beautiful lady, I do not wish to have any other help from you. My joy on hearing from you of my coming encounter with Kichaka is equal to what I felt when I slew Hidimba. I swear this by truth, morality and my brothers.

22.32.sa: सत्यं भ्रातॄंश्च धर्मं च पुरस्कृत्य ब्रवीमि ते । कीचकं निहनिष्यामि वृत्रं देवपतिर्यथा ॥३२॥

22.33.sa: तं गह्वरे प्रकाशे वा पोथयिष्यामि कीचकम् । अथ चेदपि योत्स्यन्ति हिंसे मत्स्यानपि ध्रुवम् ॥३३॥

22.34.sa: ततो दुर्योधनं हत्वा प्रतिपत्स्ये वसुन्धराम् । कामं मत्स्यमुपास्तां हि कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ॥३४॥
22.34.en: If the Matsya's side with him, I shall kill them too; and then slaying Duryodhana, I shall regain the earth; let Kunti's son Yudhishthira continue to pay his homage to the king of the Matsya's.

22.35.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । यथा न सन्त्यजेथास्त्वं सत्यं वै मत्कृते विभो । निगूढस्त्वं तथा पार्थ कीचकं तं निषूदय ॥३५॥
22.35.en: Draupadi said O lord, if you do not wish to transgress the pledge you have taken to me, you should, of Partha, slay Kichaka in secret.

22.36.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथा त्वं भीरु भाषसे । अद्य तं सूदयिष्यामि कीचकं सह बान्धवैः ॥३६॥
22.36.en: Bhimasena said O timid lady, I shall do what you say; I shall slay today Kichaka with his friends.

22.37.sa: अदृश्यमानस्तस्याथ तमस्विन्यामनिन्दिते । नागो बिल्वमिवाक्रम्य पोथयिष्याम्यहं शिरः । अलभ्यामिच्छतस्तस्य कीचकस्य दुरात्मनः ॥३७॥
22.37.en: O you of faultless feature, hidden from the view of others in darkness, I shall crush, as an elephant crushes a Bel fruit, the head of the wicked Kichaka, who desires for a thing that cannot be acquired by him.

22.38.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । भीमोऽथ प्रथमं गत्वा रात्रौ छन्न उपाविशत् । मृगं हरिरिवादृश्यः प्रत्याकाङ्क्षत कीचकम् ॥३८॥
22.38.en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon going there hidden at night, Bhima sat expecting Kichaka like a lion for deer.

22.39.sa: कीचकश्चाप्यलङ्कृत्य यथाकाममुपागमत् । तां वेलां नर्तनागारं पाञ्चालीसङ्गमाशया ॥३९॥
22.39.en: Having adorned himself to his liking, Kichaka arrived at the dancing hall at the appointed hour with a view to meet Panchali.

22.40.sa: मन्यमानः स सङ्केतमागारं प्राविशच्च तत् । प्रविश्य च स तद्वेश्म तमसा संवृतं महत् ॥४०॥
22.40.en: Considering this as sign, he entered there. Entering the hall enshrouded in darkness, that highly wicked one, came up to Bhima of unequalled prowess, who had gone there before and was waiting in a corner.

22.41.sa: पूर्वागतं ततस्तत्र भीममप्रतिमौजसम् । एकान्तावस्थितं चनमाससाद स दुर्मतिः ॥४१॥
22.41.en: Considering this as sign, he entered there. Entering the hall enshrouded in darkness, that highly wicked one, came up to Bhima of unequalled prowess, who had gone there before and was waiting in a corner.

22.42.sa: शयानं शयने तत्र सूतपुत्रः परामृशत् । जाज्वल्यमानं कोपेन कृष्णाधर्षणजेन ह ॥४२॥
22.42.en: Suta's son approached him who was lying on a bed, burning in anger begotten of the insult (offered to Krishna).

22.43.sa: उपसङ्गम्य चैवैनं कीचकः काममोहितः । हर्षोन्मथितचित्तात्मा स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत ॥४३॥
22.43.en: Approaching him, Kichaka possessed by lust, having his heart filled with delight, smilingly said.

22.44.sa: प्रापितं ते मया वित्तं बहुरूपमनन्तकम् । यत्कृतं धनरत्नाढ्यं दासीशतपरिच्छदम् ॥४४॥
22.44.en: I have already given to you immense and various wealth and for you a hundred maid servants, with riches and jems and finest robes; O you of air eye-brows, also a palace with inner apartment filled with beautiful, lovely and youthful maid servants and adorned with various sorts of sports and amusements. Having arranged all this, I have all on a sudden come here; the women of my house have begun to praise me, saying: 'There is none like you amongst all the people so well-dressed and beautiful.

22.45.sa: रूपलावण्ययुक्ताभिर्युवतीभिरलङ्कृतम् । गृहं चान्तःपुरं सुभ्रु क्रीडारतिविराजितम् । तत्सर्वं त्वां समुद्दिश्य सहसाऽहमुपागतः ॥४५॥
22.45.en: I have already given to you immense and various wealth and for you a hundred maid servants, with riches and jems and finest robes; O you of air eye-brows, also a palace with inner apartment filled with beautiful, lovely and youthful maid servants and adorned with various sorts of sports and amusements. Having arranged all this, I have all on a sudden come here; the women of my house have begun to praise me, saying: 'There is none like you amongst all the people so well-dressed and beautiful.

22.46.sa: अकस्मान्मां प्रशंसन्ति सदा गृहगताः स्त्रियः। सुवासा दर्शनीयश्च नान्योऽस्ति त्वादृशः पुमान् ॥४६॥
22.46.en: I have already given to you immense and various wealth and for you a hundred maid servants, with riches and jems and finest robes; O you of air eye-brows, also a palace with inner apartment filled with beautiful, lovely and youthful maid servants and adorned with various sorts of sports and amusements. Having arranged all this, I have all on a sudden come here; the women of my house have begun to praise me, saying: 'There is none like you amongst all the people so well-dressed and beautiful.

22.47.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । दिष्ट्या त्वं दर्शनीयोऽथ दिष्ट्याऽऽत्मानं प्रशंससि । ईदृशस्तु त्वया स्पर्शः स्पृष्टपूर्वो न कर्हिचित् ॥४७॥
22.47.en: Bhimasena said By my good fortune, you are handsome and you are praising yourself; I think you had not before any such pleasurable touch.

22.48.sa: स्पर्शं वेत्सि विदग्धस्त्वं कामधर्मविचक्षणः । स्त्रीणां प्रीतिकरो नान्यस्त्वत्समः पुरुषस्त्विह ॥४८॥

22.49.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । इत्युक्त्वा तं महाबाहुर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः । सहसोत्पत्य कौन्तेयः प्रहस्येद‌मुवाच ह ॥४९॥
22.49.en: Vaishampayana said Having said this to him, and jumping up all on a sudden, the mighty-armed Bhima, the son of Kunti, endued with dreadful prowess, smilingly said.

22.50.sa: अद्य त्वां भगिनी पापं कृष्यमाणं मया भुवि । द्रक्ष्यतेऽद्रिप्रतीकाशं सिंहेनेव महागजम् ॥५०॥
22.50.en: Your sister shall behold you, vile as you are, today drawn by me on earth, like a mighty elephant huge as a mountain dragged by another to the ground.

22.51.sa: निराबाधा त्वयि हते सैरन्ध्री विचरिष्यति । सुखमेव चरिष्यन्ति सैरन्ध्र्याः पतयः सदा ॥५१॥

22.52.sa: ततो जग्राह केशेषु माल्यवत्सु महाबलः । स केशेषु परामृष्टो बलेन बलिनां वरः ॥५२॥
22.52.en: The highly powerful Bhima seized him by the hair which were adorned with garlands. Thus caught with force by the hair, that foremost of the powerful, speedily freed his hair and grasped the arms of Bhima. Then there arose a hand to hand fight between those who foremost of men worked up with anger.

22.53.sa: आक्षिप्य केशान् वेगेन बाह्वोर्जग्राह पाण्डवम् । बाहुयुद्धं तयोरासीत् क्रुद्धयोर्नरसिंहयोः ॥५३॥
22.53.en: The highly powerful Bhima seized him by the hair which were adorned with garlands. Thus caught with force by the hair, that foremost of the powerful, speedily freed his hair and grasped the arms of Bhima. Then there arose a hand to hand fight between those who foremost of men worked up with anger.

22.54.sa: वसन्ते वासिताहेतोर्बलवद्गजयोरिव । कीचकानां तु मुख्यस्य नराणामुत्तमस्य च ॥५४॥
22.54.en: The fight of Kichaka and the foremost of men was like that between two powerful elephants for one she-elephants in the season of spring,

22.55.sa: वालिसुग्रीवयोर्भ्रात्रोः पुरेव कपिसिंहयोः । अन्योन्यमपि संरब्धौ परस्परजयैषिणौ ॥५५॥
22.55.en: Or like what took place in the days of yore between the two leading monkeys the brothers Bali and Sugriva. Both equally enraged and desirous of victory,

22.56.sa: ततः समुद्यम्य भुजौ पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ । नखदंष्ट्राभिरन्योन्यं घ्नतः क्रोधविषोद्धतौ ॥५६॥
22.56.en: They raised up their arms like two snakes having five hoods; and worked up with the poison of anger, they attacked each other with nails and teeth.

22.57.sa: वेगेनाभिहतो भीमः कीचकेन बलीयसा । स्थिरप्रतिज्ञः स रणे पदान्न चलितः पदम् ॥५७॥
22.57.en: Being struck with great force by the powerful Kichaka, the resolute (Bhima) did not waver a step in the encounter.

22.58.sa: तावन्योन्यं समाश्लिष्य प्रकर्षन्तौ परस्परम् । उभावपि प्रकाशेते प्रवृद्धौ वृषभाविव ॥५८॥
22.58.en: Then embracing and dragging each other, they appeared there like two powerful bulls.

22.59.sa: तयोर्ह्यासीत् सुतुमुलः संप्रहारः सुदारुणः । नखदन्तायुधवतोर्व्याघ्रयोरिव दृप्तयोः ॥५९॥
22.59.en: They having nails and teeth for their weapon, there arose a fierce and great encounter between them like that between two maddened tigers.

22.60.sa: अभिपत्याथ बाहुभ्यां प्रत्यगृह्णादमर्षितः । मातङ्ग इव मातङ्गं प्रभिन्नकरटामुखम् ॥६०॥
22.60.en: Throwing each other down with their arms and then again seizing in great anger, they fought like two elephants with rent temples.

22.61.sa: स चाप्येनं तदा भीमः प्रतिजग्राह वीर्यवान् । तमाक्षिपत् कीचकोऽथ बलेन बलिनां वरः॥६१॥
22.61.en: Then the powerful Bhima seized Kichaka, and Kichaka too, the foremost of the strong, again threw him down with force.

22.62.en: Those two powerful (heroes) thus fighting, the crush of their arms engendered a sound resembling the clatter of splitting bamboo's.

22.63.sa: अथैनमाक्षिप्य बलाद्गृहमध्ये वृकोदरः । धूनयामास वेगेन वायुश्चण्ड इव द्रुमम् ॥६३॥

22.64.sa: भीमेन च परामृष्टो दुर्बलो बलिना रणे । प्रास्पन्दत यथाप्राणं विचकर्ष च पाण्डवम् ॥६४॥
22.64.en: Being thus assailed by the powerful Bhima in the encounter, he grew weak, trembled and tugged at the Pandava to his very best.

22.65.sa: ईषदाकलितं चापि क्रोधाद्द्रुतपदं स्थितम् । कीचको बलवान् भीमं जानुभ्यामाक्षिपद्भुवि ॥६५॥
22.65.en: Making him waver a little, the powerful Kichaka speedily stuck Bhima on the breast with his knees and felled him on the ground.

22.66.sa: पातितो भुवि भीमस्तु कीचकेन बलीयसा । उत्पपाताथ वेगेन दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः ॥६६॥
22.66.en: Being thrown on the ground by the powerful Kichaka, Bhima rose up again with force, like Yama with mace in his hands.

22.67.sa: स्पर्धया च बलोन्मत्तौ तावुभौ सूतपाण्डवौ । निशीये पर्यकर्षेतां बलिनौ निर्जने स्थले ॥६७॥
22.67.en: Then both Suta and Pandava, maddened with their strength, challenged and grappled with each other at night in that secluded hall.

22.68.sa: ततस्तद्भवनं श्रेष्ठं प्राकम्पत मुहुर्मुहुः । बलवच्चापि संक्रुद्धावन्योन्यं प्रति गर्जतः ॥६८॥
22.68.en: While enraged they were thus roaring at each other, that best of houses shook at every moment.

22.69.sa: तलाभ्यां स तु भीमेन वक्षस्यभिहतो बली । कीचको रोषसंतप्तः पदान्न चलितः पदम् ॥६९॥
22.69.en: Slapped on the breast by the powerful Bhima, Kichaka worked up with anger, did not move for a single step.

22.70.sa: मुहूर्तं तु स तं वेगं सहित्वा भुवि दुःसहम् । बलादहीयत तदा सूतो भीमबलार्दितः ॥७०॥

22.71.sa: तं हीयमानं विज्ञाय भीमसेनो महाबलः । वक्षस्यानीय वेगेन ममर्दैनं विचेतसम् ॥७१॥

22.72.sa: क्रोधाविष्टो विनिःश्वस्य पुनश्चैनं वृकोदरः । जग्राह जयतां श्रेष्ठः केशेष्वेव तदा भृशम् ॥७२॥
22.72.en: Breathing hard again and again in anger, Vrikodara the foremost of the victorious held him up always by the hair.

22.73.sa: गृहीत्वा कीचकं भीमो विरराज महाबलः । शार्दूलः पिशिताकाङ्क्षी गृहीत्त्वेव महामृगम् ॥७३॥
22.73.en: Seizing Kichaka, the powerful Bhima began to roar like a hunger tiger that has slain a large animal.

22.74.sa: तत एनं परिश्रान्तमुपलभ्य वृकोदरः । योक्त्रयामास बाहुभ्यां पशुं रशनया यथा ॥७४॥
22.74.en: Thereupon on serving him greatly exhausted, Vrikodara bound him fast with his arms like one binding a beast with a rope.

22.75.sa: नदन्तं च महानादं भिन्नभेरीसमस्वनम् । भ्रामयामास सुचिरं विस्फुरन्तमचेतसम् ॥७५॥
22.75.en: Then Bhima began to whirl him who was senseless, for a considerable time, and he roared terribly like a discordant bugle.

22.76.sa: प्रगृह्य तरसा दोर्भ्यां कण्ठं तस्य वृकोदरः । अपीडयत कृष्णायास्तदा कोपोपशान्तये ॥७६॥
22.76.en: Then to console Krishna, Vrikodara got hold of Kichaka's throat with his arms and began to squeeze it.

22.77.sa: अथ तं भग्नसर्वाङ्गं व्याविद्धनयनाम्बरम् । आक्रम्य च कटीदेशे जानुना कीचकाधमम् । अपीडयत बाहुभ्यां पशुमारममारयत् ॥७७॥
22.77.en: Then striking with his knees the waist of that wretch of Kichaka, all whose limbs had been broken into pieces and whose eye-lids were closed, that descendant of Pandu killed him like one killing a beast. Then beholding Kichaka senseless,

22.78.sa: तं विषीदन्तमाज्ञाय कीचकं पाण्डुनन्दनः । भूतले भ्रामयामास वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ॥७८॥
22.78.en: Then striking with his knees the waist of that wretch of Kichaka, all whose limbs had been broken into pieces and whose eye-lids were closed, that descendant of Pandu killed him like one killing a beast. Then beholding Kichaka senseless,

22.79.sa: अद्याहमनृणो भूत्वा भ्रातुर्भार्यापहारिणम् । शान्तिं लब्धाऽस्मि परमां हत्वा सैरन्ध्रिकण्टकम् ॥७९॥
22.79.en: He rolled him on earth and said: “Killing this wretch who has wished to ravish our wife, this thorn of Sairandhri, I am freed from the debt I owed to my brother and am in peace."

22.80.sa: इत्येवमुक्त्वा पुरुषप्रवीरस्तं कीचकं क्रोधसरागनेत्रः । आस्रस्तवस्त्राभरणं स्फुरन्तमुद्भ्रान्तनेत्रं व्यसुमुत्ससर्ज ॥८०॥
22.80.en: Saying this, that foremost of men, with eyes reddened with ire, left off Kichaka, whose dress and ornaments had been thrown off his body, whose eyes were rolling and who was even then trembling.

22.81.sa: निष्पिष्य पाणिना पाणिं संद‌ष्टौष्ठपुटं बली । समाक्रम्य च संक्रुद्धो बलेन बलिनां वरः ॥८१॥
22.81.en: Squeezing his own hand and biting his lips in anger, that foremost of the powerful, attacked him with great force and thrust his arms, legs, neck and head into his body, as did the holder of Pinaka the beast.

22.82.sa: तस्य पादौ च पाणी च शिरो ग्रीवां च सर्वशः। काये प्रवेशयामास पशोरिव पिनाकधृक् ॥८२॥
22.82.en: Squeezing his own hand and biting his lips in anger, that foremost of the powerful, attacked him with great force and thrust his arms, legs, neck and head into his body, as did the holder of Pinaka the beast.

22.83.sa: तं संमथितसर्वाङ्गं मांसपिण्डोपमं कृतम् । कृष्णाया दर्शयामास भीमसेनो महाबलः ॥८३॥
22.83.en: The highly-powerful Bhimasena then showed him to Krishna; all his limbs were crushed and he was reduced into a ball of flesh.

22.84.sa: उवाच च महातेजा द्रौपदीं योषितां वराम् । पश्यैनमेहि पाञ्चालि कामुकोऽयं यथा कृतः ॥८४॥

22.85.sa: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज भीमो भीमपराक्रमः । पादेन पीडयामास तस्य कायं दुरात्मनः ॥८५॥
22.85.en: Saying this, O king, Bhima, endued with dreadful prowess, struck with his foot the body of that vicious-souled one.

22.86.sa: ततोऽग्निं तत्र प्रज्वाल्य दर्शयित्वा तु कीचकम् । पाञ्चालीं स तदा वीर इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥८६॥
22.86.en: Then lighting a lamp there and showing her Kichaka, that hero addressed the following to Panchali.

22.87.sa: प्रार्थयन्ति सुकेशान्ते ये त्वां शीलगुणान्विताम् । एवं ते भीरु वध्यन्ते कीचकः शोभते यथा ॥८७॥
22.87.en: "O you of fair hair, O timid damsel, all those who seek you who are gifted with a good character and accomplishments, will be slain by me like this Kichaka."

22.88.sa: तत् कृत्वा दुष्करं कर्म कृष्णायाः प्रियमुत्तमम् । तथा स कीचकं हत्वा गत्वा रोषस्य वै शमम्‌ ॥८८॥
22.88.en: Performing that difficult work, highly pleasing to Krishna, and slaying Kichaka, his anger was pacified.

22.89.sa: आमन्त्र्य द्रौपदीं कृष्णां क्षिप्रमायान्महानसम् । कीचकं घातयित्वा तु द्रौपदी योषितां वरा । प्रहृष्टा गतसंतापा सभापालानुवाच ह ॥८९॥

22.90.sa: कीचकोऽयं हतः शेते गन्धर्वैः पतिभिर्मम । परस्त्रीकामसंमत्तस्तत्रागच्छत पश्यत ॥९०॥

22.91.sa: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्या नर्तनागाररक्षिणः । सहसैव समाजग्मुरादायोल्काः सहस्रशः ॥९१॥
22.91.en: He who desired for another's wife; come and see.” Hearing her words the guards of the assembly-hall.

22.92.sa: ततो गत्वाऽथ तद्वेश्म कीचकं विनिपातितम् । गतासुं ददृशुर्भूमौ रुधिरेण समुक्षितम् ॥९२॥
22.92.en: Came there by thousands, with torches in their hands. And going to that room they saw Kichaka fallen on the ground lifeless, bathing in a pool of blood. Beholding him without arms and legs they were pained.

22.93.sa: पाणिपादविहीनं तु दृष्ट्वा च व्यथिताऽभवन् । निरीक्षन्ति ततः सर्वे परं विस्मयमागताः ॥९३॥
22.93.en: Came there by thousands, with torches in their hands. And going to that room they saw Kichaka fallen on the ground lifeless, bathing in a pool of blood. Beholding him without arms and legs they were pained.

22.94.sa: अमानुषं कृतं कर्म तं दृष्ट्वा विनिपातितम् । क्वास्य ग्रीवा क्व चरणौ क्व पाणी क्व शिरस्तथा । इति स्म तं परीक्षन्ते गन्धर्वेण हतं तदा ॥९४॥
22.94.en: When they saw him they were struck with wonder. Seeing that super-human work of his destruction. (They said) : “Where is his neck, where are his feet, arms and where is his head.” They then concluded that he had been slain by the Gandharvas.

23.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तस्मिन् काले समागम्य सर्वे तत्रास्य बान्धवाः । रुरुदुः कीचकं दृष्ट्वा परिवार्य समन्ततः ॥१॥
23.1.en: Vaishampayana said Coming there at that time and beholding Kichaka and surrounding him all sides his friends began to lament.

23.2.sa: सर्वे संहृष्टरोमाणः संत्रस्ताः प्रेक्ष्य कीचकम् । तथा संभिन्नसर्वाङ्गं कूर्मं स्थल इवोद्धृतम् ॥२॥

23.3.sa: पोथितं भीमसेनेन तमिन्द्रेणेव दानवम् । संस्कारयितुमिच्छन्तो बहिर्नेतुं प्रचक्रमुः ॥३॥
23.3.en: Then seeing him crushed by Bhimasena like a Danava by Indra they tried to take him out side for performing his obsequial ceremonies.

23.4.sa: ददृशुस्ते ततः कृष्णां सूतपुत्राः समागताः । अदूराच्चानवद्याङ्गीं स्तम्भमालिङ्ग्य तिष्ठतीम् ॥४॥
23.4.en: Then the assembled sons of Suta beheld Krishna of faultless features standing hard by reclining on a pillar.

23.5.sa: समवेतेषु सर्वेषु तामूचुरुपकीचकाः । हन्यतां शीघ्रमसती यत्कृते कीचको हतः ॥५॥
23.5.en: Amongst those assembled, some wicked Kichaka's exclaimed: "soon kill this unchaste woman for whom Kichaka has been slain.

23.6.sa: अथवा नैव हन्तव्या दह्यतां कामिना सह । मृतस्यापि प्रियं कार्यं सूतपुत्रस्य सर्वथा ॥६॥
23.6.en: Or without slaying her, let us burn her, with him who desired to have her; for we should do by all means what was liked by the deceased son of a Suta."

23.7.sa: ततो विराटमूचुस्ते कीचकोऽस्याः कृते हतः । सहानेनाद्य दह्येम तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ॥७॥
23.7.en: Then they said to Virata: "For her, Kichaka has been slain; we shall burn her with him; it behoves you to give permission.”

23.8.sa: पराक्रमं तु सूतानां मत्वा राजाऽन्वमोदत । सैरन्ध्र्याः सूतपुत्रेण सह दाहं विशाम्पतिः ॥८॥

23.9.sa: तां समासाद्य वित्रस्तां कृष्णां कमललोचनाम् । मोमुह्यमानां ते तत्र जगृहुः कीचका भृशम् ॥९॥

23.10.sa: ततस्तु तां समारोप्य निबध्य च सुमध्यमाम् । जग्मुरुद्यम्य ते सर्वे श्मशानाभिमुखास्तदा ॥१०॥
23.10.en: Then binding that youthful damsel and placing her upon the bier they started with great joy towards the cremation ground.

23.11.sa: ह्रियमाणा तु सा राजन् सूतपुत्रैरनिन्दिता । प्राक्रोशन्नाथमिच्छन्ती कृष्णा नाथवती सती ॥११॥
23.11.en: Being thus carried away by the sons of Suta, O king, the faultless fertured and chaste Krishna, having lord, bewailed for the help of her husbands.

23.12.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । जयो जयन्तो विजयो जयत्सेनो जयद्बलः । ते मे वाचं विजानन्तु सूतपुत्रा नयन्ति माम् ॥१२॥
23.12.en: Draupadi said Let Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Jayatsena and Jayadbala hear my words. The Sutas are taking me away.

23.13.sa: येषां ज्यातलनिर्घोषो विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः । व्यश्रूयत महायुद्धे भीमघोषस्तरस्विनाम् ॥१३॥
23.13.en: Let those powerful and quick-coursing Gandharvas, the clatter of whose cars is very great and the twang of whose bows in a great encounter is heard like the roar of thunder, understand that the Sutas are taking me away.

23.14.sa: रथघोषश्च बलवान् गन्धर्वाणां तरस्विनाम् । ते मे वाचं विजानन्तु सूतपुत्रा नयन्ति माम् ॥१४॥
23.14.en: Let those powerful and quick-coursing Gandharvas, the clatter of whose cars is very great and the twang of whose bows in a great encounter is heard like the roar of thunder, understand that the Sutas are taking me away.

23.15.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तस्यास्ताः कृपणा वाचः कृष्णायाः परिदेवितम् । श्रुत्वैवाभ्यापतद्भीमः शयनादविचारयन् ॥१५॥
23.15.en: Vaishampayana said Hearing those sorrowful words and bewailing of Krishna, Bhima, without reflecting the least, got up from his bed.

23.16.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । अहं शृणोमि ते वाचं त्वया सैरन्ध्रि भाषिताम् । तस्मात्ते सूतपुत्रेभ्यो भयं भीरु न विद्यते ॥१६॥
23.16.en: Bhimasena said: I have heard those which O Sairandhri, you have said; you have no fear any more, O timid lady, from the Sutas.

23.17.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । इत्युक्त्वा स महाबाहुर्विजजृम्भे जिघांसया । ततः स व्यायतं कृत्वा वेषं विपरिवर्त्य च ॥१७॥
23.17.en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, the mighty-armed; Bhima, to slay them, began to swell his body and then carefully changing his dress.

23.18.sa: अद्वारेणाभ्यवस्कन्द्य निर्जगाम बहिस्तदा । स भीमसेनः प्राकारादारुह्य तरसा द्रुमम् ॥१८॥
23.18.en: He went out of the palace by a wrong way. Then speedily scaling the walls, Bhimasena.

23.19.sa: श्मशानाभिमुखः प्रायाद्यत्र ते कीचका गताः । स लङ्घयित्वा प्राकारं निःसृत्य च पुरोत्तमात् । जवेन पतितो भीमः सूतानामग्रतस्तदा ॥१९॥
23.19.en: Went to the cremation ground where the Kichaka's had-gone. Then scaling the walls and issuing out of the excellent city.

23.20.sa: चितासमीपे गत्वा स तत्रापश्यद्वनस्पतिम् । तालमात्रं महास्कन्धं मूर्धशुष्कं विशाम्पते ॥२०॥
23.20.en: Bhima furiously rushed before the Sutas. And going near the funeral pyre he saw there a tree.

23.21.sa: तं नागवदुपक्रम्य बाहुभ्यां परिरभ्य च । स्कन्धमारोपयामास दशव्यामं परन्तपः ॥२१॥
23.21.en: Tall as a palmyra, with huge branches and with red top; then holding it like an elephant with his arms, he uprooted it.

23.22.sa: स तं वृक्षं दशव्यामं सस्कन्धविटपं बली । प्रगृह्याभ्यद्रवत् सूतान् दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः ॥२२॥
23.22.en: Measuring ten Vyamas and placed it on his shoulders. Then taking that tree up with its trunk and branches, measuring ten Vyamas that slayer of foes rushed towards the Sutas like Yama with mace in his hand. By the velocity of his movement, the banian, Nyagrodha, Kinshukh and other trees fell down on earth an lay in a heap. Beholding that Gandharva approach enraged like a lion, all those Sutas were afraid and trembled in sorrow and fear, Then beholding the Gandharva approach like death, the Kichaka's cremated their cldest brother and spoke amongst themselves trembling in fear and sorrow.

23.23.sa: ऊरुवेगेन तस्याथ न्यग्रोधाश्वत्थविंशुकाः । भूमौ निपतिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशस्तत्र शेरते ॥२३॥
23.23.en: Measuring ten Vyamas and placed it on his shoulders. Then taking that tree up with its trunk and branches, measuring ten Vyamas that slayer of foes rushed towards the Sutas like Yama with mace in his hand. By the velocity of his movement, the banian, Nyagrodha, Kinshukh and other trees fell down on earth an lay in a heap. Beholding that Gandharva approach enraged like a lion, all those Sutas were afraid and trembled in sorrow and fear, Then beholding the Gandharva approach like death, the Kichaka's cremated their cldest brother and spoke amongst themselves trembling in fear and sorrow.

23.24.sa: तं सिंहमिव संक्रुद्धं दृष्ट्वा गन्धर्वमागतम् । वित्रेसुः सर्वशः सूता विषादभयकम्पिताः ॥२४॥
23.24.en: Measuring ten Vyamas and placed it on his shoulders. Then taking that tree up with its trunk and branches, measuring ten Vyamas that slayer of foes rushed towards the Sutas like Yama with mace in his hand. By the velocity of his movement, the banian, Nyagrodha, Kinshukh and other trees fell down on earth an lay in a heap. Beholding that Gandharva approach enraged like a lion, all those Sutas were afraid and trembled in sorrow and fear, Then beholding the Gandharva approach like death, the Kichaka's cremated their cldest brother and spoke amongst themselves trembling in fear and sorrow.

23.25.sa: गन्धर्वो बलवानेति क्रुद्ध उद्यम्य पादपम् । सैरन्ध्री मुच्यतां शीघ्रं यतो नो भयमागतम् ॥२५॥
23.25.en: “Here comes the powerful Gandharva enraged uprooting a tree. Soon release Sairandhri from whom this fear has come."

23.26.sa: ते तु दृष्ट्वा तदाऽऽविद्धं भीमसेनेन पादपम् । विमुच्य द्रौपदीं तत्र प्राद्रवन्नगरं प्रति ॥२६॥
23.26.en: Then seeing the tree that had been uprooted by Bhimaseni they set Draupadi free and ran towards the city.

23.27.sa: द्रवतस्तांस्तु संप्रेक्ष्य स वज्री दानवानिव । शतं पञ्चाधिकं भीमः प्राहिणोद्यमसादनम् ॥२७॥

23.28.sa: वृक्षेणैतेन राजेन्द्र प्रभञ्जनसुतो बली । तत आश्वासयत् कृष्णां स विमुच्य पिशाम्पते ॥२८॥
23.28.en: Beholding them thus taking to their heels, the powerful Bhima, the son of the Wind-god, dispatched with that tree, O king, hundred and five of them to the abode of death, like the wielder of thunder-bolt, the Danavas. Then releasing Krishna he comforted her.

23.29.sa: उवाच च महाबाहुः पाञ्चालीं तत्र द्रौपदीम् । अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं दीनां दुर्धर्षः स वृकोदरः ॥२९॥
23.29.en: Then the irrepressible mighty-armed Vrikodara Bhima said to the poor Panchali, Draupadi, with tearful eyes.

23.30.sa: एवं ते भीरु वध्यन्ते ये त्वां क्लिश्यन्त्यनागसम् । प्रैहि त्वं नगरं कृष्णे न भयं विद्यते तव ॥३०॥

23.31.en: Then, O timid lady, all those from whom proceeded you misery, have been killed. Return O Krishna, to the city, you have no fear. I shall go to Virata's kitchen by another way.

23.32.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । पञ्चाधिकं शतं तच्च निहतं तेन भारत । महावनमिव छिन्नं शिश्ये विगलितद्रुमम् ॥३२॥

23.33.sa: एवं ते निहता राजन् शतं पञ्च च कीचकाः । स च सेनापतिः पूर्वमित्येतत् सूतषट्शतम् ॥३३॥
23.33.en: Thus, Oking, one hundred and five Kichaka's killed. Including the commander-in-chief who was slain before, they were one hundred and six.

23.34.sa: तद्दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं नरा नार्यश्च सङ्गताः । विस्मयं परमं गत्वा नोचुः किञ्चन भारत ॥३४॥
23.34.en: Beholding that wonderful deed men and women assembled; O descendant of Bharata, they were filled with surprise and could not speak any thing.

24.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ते दृष्ट्वा निहतान् सूतान् राज्ञे गत्वा न्यवेदयन् । गन्धर्वैर्निहता राजन् सूतपुत्रा महाबलाः ॥१॥
24.1.en: Vaishampayana said Beholding the Suta's slain, people went and communicated to the king: "O king, the highly powerful sons of Suta have been slain by the Gandharvas.

24.2.sa: यथा वज्रेण वै दीर्णं पर्वतस्य महच्छिरः । व्यतिकीर्णाः प्रदृश्यन्ते तथा सूता महीतले ॥२॥

24.3.sa: सैरन्ध्री च विमुक्ताऽसौ पुनरायाति ते गृहम् । सर्वं संशयितं राजन् नगरं ते भविष्यति ॥३॥
24.3.en: And released Sairandhri comes back to your city; your (whole) city, o king, indeed shall be in danger.

24.4.sa: यथारूपा च सैरन्ध्री गन्धर्वाश्च महाबलाः । पुंसामिष्टश्च विषयो मैथुनाय न संशयः ॥४॥
24.4.en: Sairandhri is highly beautiful and the Gandharvas are greatly powerful and forsooth, men are undoubtedly lustful.

24.5.sa: यथा सैरन्ध्रिदोषेण न ते राजन्निदं पुरम् । विनाशमेति वै क्षिप्रं तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् ॥५॥

24.6.sa: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विराटो वाहिनीपतिः । अब्रवीत्क्रियतामेषां सूतानां परमक्रिया ॥६॥
24.6.en: Hearing their words, Virata, the king of armies, said : “Perform the obsequial rites of the Sutas."

24.7.sa: एकस्मिन्नेव ते सर्वे सुसमिद्धे हुताशने । दह्यन्तां कीचकाः शीघ्रं रत्नैर्गन्धैश्च सर्वशः ॥७॥
24.7.en: Let all the Kichaka's be burnt down on one burning, funeral pyre with profuse jems and perfumes.

24.8.sa: सुदेष्णामब्रवीद्राजा महिषीं जातसाध्वसः । सैरन्ध्रीमागतां ब्रूया ममैव वचनादिदम् ॥८॥
24.8.en: Then filled with fear, the king said to his queen Sudeshna: 'When Sairandhri comes, tell her these words of mine.

24.9.sa: गच्छ सैरन्ध्रि भद्रं ते यथाकामं वरानने । बिभेति राजा सुश्रोणि गन्धर्वेभ्यः पराभवात् ॥९॥
24.9.en: Go Sairandhri, wherever you like; may good betide you, O fair one, O you having beautiful eye-brows, the king is afraid of defeat from the Gandharvas.

24.10.sa: न हित्वामुत्सहे वक्तुं स्वयं गन्धर्वरक्षिताम् । स्त्रियास्त्वदोषस्तां वक्तुमतस्त्वां प्रब्रवीम्यहम् ॥१०॥
24.10.en: I dare not speak all this to you in person, protected as you are by the Gandharvas. A woman cannot offend (any body) so I speak this through her.

24.11.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथ मुक्ता भयात्कृष्णा सूतपुत्रान्निरस्य च । मोक्षिता भीमसेनेन जगाम नगरं प्रति ॥११॥
24.11.en: Vaishampayana said Thus released by Bhimasena after the destruction of Sutas, the intelligent Krishna freed from fear, washed her body and raiment in water and went towards the city like a doe put to fright by a tiger,

24.12.sa: त्रासितेव मृगी बाला शार्दूलेन मनस्विनी । गात्राणि वाससी चैव प्रक्षाल्य सलिलेन सा ॥१२॥
24.12.en: Vaishampayana said Thus released by Bhimasena after the destruction of Sutas, the intelligent Krishna freed from fear, washed her body and raiment in water and went towards the city like a doe put to fright by a tiger,

24.13.sa: तां दृष्ट्वा पुरुषा राजन् प्राद्रवन्त दिशो दश । गन्धर्वाणां भयत्रस्ताः केचिद्दृष्ट्वा न्यमीलयन् ॥१३॥
24.13.en: Beholding her, O king, people fled away in all directions in fear of the Gandharvas and some even shut up their eyes.

24.14.sa: ततो महानसद्वारि भीमसेनमवस्थितम् । ददर्श राजन् पाञ्चाली यथा मत्तं महाद्विपम् ॥१४॥
24.14.en: Then, o king, Panchali saw Bhimsena, waiting at the kitchen door like a huge infuriated elephant.

24.15.sa: तं विस्मयन्ती शनकैः संज्ञाभिरिदमब्रवीत् । गन्धर्वराजाय नमो येनास्मि परिमोचिता ॥१५॥
24.15.en: She wonderingly said to him in words intelligible to them: “Salutation to that king of Gandharvas by whom I have been released.

24.16.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । ये पुरा विचरन्तीह पुरुषा वशवर्तिनः । तस्यास्ते वचनं श्रुत्वा ह्यनृणा विहरन्त्वतः ॥१६॥
24.16.en: Bhima said Hearing these words of hers under which those persons were till then living in that city, they will now live there freed from debt.

24.17.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततः सा नर्तनागारे धनञ्जयमपश्यत । राज्ञः कन्या विराटस्य नर्तयानं महाभुजम् ॥१७॥

24.18.sa: ततस्ता नर्तनागाराद्विनिष्क्रम्य सहार्जुनाः । कन्या ददृशुरायान्तीं क्लिष्टां कृष्णामनागसम् ॥१८॥
24.18.en: Then coming out with Arjuna from the dancing hall, those daughters saw the innocent saw Krishna (though) sorely persecuted coming. Beholding her arrive there they all delightedly said.

24.19.sa: कन्या ऊचुः । दिष्ट्या सैरन्ध्रि मुक्तासि दिष्ट्याऽसि पुनरागता । दिष्ट्या विनिहताः सूता ये त्वां क्लिश्यन्त्यनागसम् ॥१९॥
24.19.en: The Daughters said By good luck, O Sairandhri, you have been released and by good-luck you have returned. And by good luck the Sutas have been slain from whom this your misery came.

24.20.sa: बृहन्नलोवाच । कथं सैरन्ध्रि मुक्ताऽसि कथं पापाश्च ते हताः । इच्छामि वै तव श्रोतुं सर्वमेव यथातथम् ॥२०॥

24.21.sa: सैरन्ध्र्युवाच । बृहन्नले किं नु तव सैरन्ध्र्या कार्यमद्य वै । या त्वं वससि कल्याणि सदा कन्यापुरे सुखम् ॥२१॥

24.22.sa: न हि दुःखं समाप्नोषि सैरन्ध्री यदुपाश्नुते । तेन मां दुःखितामेवं पृच्छसे प्रहसन्निव ॥२२॥
24.22.en: You shall not meet with grief when Sairandhri does it. You are asking me thus in jest who am stricken with sorrow.

24.23.sa: बृहन्नलोवाच । बृहन्नलाऽपि कल्याणि दुःखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् । तिर्यग्योनिगता बाले न चैनामवबुद्ध्यसे ॥२३॥
24.23.en: Brihannala said O blessed lady, Brihannala also has sorrow of her own without any comparison; she has been born in the species of brutes, you do not understand this, O girl.

24.24.sa: त्वया सहोषिता चास्मि त्वं च सर्वैः सहोषिता । क्लिश्यन्त्यां त्वयि सुश्रोणि को नु दुःखं न चिन्तयेत् ॥२४॥
24.24.en: I have lived with you and you also have lived with us; why should not one, O you of beautiful hips, feel sorrow for you who are afflicted with sorrow.

24.25.sa: न तु केनचिदन्त्यन्तं कस्यचिद्धृदयं क्वचित् । वेदितुं शक्यते नूनं तेन मां नावबुद्ध्यसे ॥२५॥
24.25.en: No one can definitely read another's heart; therefore O fair one, you cannot understand me.

24.26.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततः सहैव कन्याभिर्द्रौपदी राजवेश्म तत् । प्रविवेश सुदेष्णायाः समीपमुपगामिनी ॥२६॥
24.26.en: Then accompanied by those girls Draupadi entered the palace with a view to appear before Sudeshna.

24.27.sa: तामब्रवीद्राजपुत्री विराटवचनादिदम् । सैरन्ध्रि गम्यतां शीघ्रं यत्र कामयले गतिम् ॥२७॥
24.27.en: Then the queen communicated to her Virata's words: 'Sairandhri, soon go wherever you wish.

24.28.sa: राजा बिभेति ते भद्रे गन्धर्वेभ्यः पराभवात् । त्वं चापि तरुणी सुभ्रु रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि । पुंसामिष्टश्च विषयो गन्धर्वाश्चातिकोपनाः ॥२८॥

24.29.sa: सैरन्ध्र्युवाच । त्रयोदशाहमात्रं मे राजा क्षम्यतु भामिनि । कृतकृत्या भविष्यन्ति गन्धर्वास्ते न संशयः॥२९॥

24.30.sa: ततो मामुपनेष्यन्ति करिष्यन्ति च ते प्रियम् । ध्रुवं च श्रेयसा राजा योक्ष्यते सह बान्धवैः ॥३०॥
24.30.en: They will then take me away from here and will do what is agreeable to you. Forsooth the king with his friends shall meet with wellbeing.

25.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । कीचकस्य तु घातेन सानुजस्य विशाम्पते । अत्याहितं चिन्तयित्वा व्यस्मयन्त पृथक् जनाः ॥१॥
25.1.en: Vaishampayana said O king, at the destruction of Kichaka and his brothers and thinking of this calamity, people were filled with surprise.

25.2.sa: तस्मिन् पुरे जनपदे सञ्जल्पोऽभूच्च सङ्घशः । शौर्याद्धि वल्लभो राज्ञो महासत्त्वः स कीचकः ॥२॥
25.2.en: All over the city and provinces, it was widely known that the kings Vallabha and Kichaka were both brave and powerful heroes.

25.3.sa: आसीत् प्रहर्ता सैन्यानां दारामर्षी च दुर्मतिः । स हतः खलु पापात्मा गन्धर्वैर्दुष्टपूरुषः ॥३॥
25.3.en: The wicked-minded Kichaka was the oppressor of men and the ravisher of soldier's wives; that vicious, wicked man has been slain by the Gandharvas.

25.4.sa: इत्यजल्पन्महाराज परानीकविनाशनम् । देशे देशे मनुष्याश्च कीचकं दुष्प्रधर्षणम् ॥४॥
25.4.en: It is in this way, O great king, that people of various countries spoke about the irrepressible Kichaka, the slayer of hostile armies.

25.5.sa: अथ वै धार्तराष्ट्रेण प्रयुक्ता ये बहिश्चराः । मृगयित्वा बहून् ग्रामान् राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च ॥५॥
25.5.en: In the meantime spies, engaged by Dhritarashtra's son, searching many villages, provinces and cities.

25.6.sa: संविधाय यथा दृष्टं यथादेशप्रदर्शनम् । कृतकृत्या न्यवर्तन्त ते चरा नगरं प्रति ॥६॥
25.6.en: Accomplishing all they had been commanded and seeing all countries, returned to the city; being successful (in one thing).

25.7.sa: तत्र दृष्ट्वा तु राजानं कौरव्यं धृतराष्ट्रजम् । द्रोणकर्णकृपैः सार्धं भीष्मेण च महात्मना ॥७॥

25.8.sa: सङ्गतं भ्रातृभिश्चापि त्रिगर्तैश्च महारथैः । दुर्योधनं सभामध्ये आसीनमिद‌मब्रुवन् ॥८॥
25.8.en: Then beholding Dhritarashtra's son, king Duryodhana of the Kuru race, seated in his court, with Drona, Karna, Kripa, the noble Bhishma, his brothers and the great heroes, the Trigarthas, they said to him.

25.9.sa: चरा ऊचुः । कृतोऽस्माभिः परो यत्नस्तेषामन्वेषणे सदा । पाण्डवानां मनुष्येन्द्र तस्मिन् महति कानने ॥९॥
25.9.en: The spies said O king of men, we have with great care searched the sons of Pandu in that huge forest.

25.10.en: Solitary, abounding in wild animals, filled with various trees, creepers, entwining creepers and various groves.

25.11.sa: न च विद्मो गता येन पार्थाः सुदृढविक्रमाः । मार्गमाणाः पदन्यासं तेषु तेषु तथा तथा ॥११॥
25.11.en: 1But we haven failed to find out the way (stamped) with their footsteps, by which the highly powerful sons of Pritha might have gone.

25.12.sa: गिरिकूटेषु तुङ्‌गेषु नानाजनपदेषु च । जनाकीर्णेषु देशेषु खर्वटेषु पुरेषु च ॥१२॥

25.13.sa: नरेन्द्र बहुशोऽन्विष्टा नैत्र विद्मश्च पाण्डवान् । अत्यन्तं वा विनष्टास्ते भद्रं तुभ्यं नरर्षभ ॥१३॥
25.13.en: We have made many inquires, O king, but we have not found out the Pandavas; may good betide you. O king; it seems they have perished.

25.14.sa: वर्त्मन्यन्वेष्यमाणा वै रथिनां रथिसत्तम । न हि विद्मो गतिं तेषां वासं हि नरसत्तम ॥१४॥
25.14.en: O foremost of car-warriors, we pursued (also) the track of those car-warriors, but O foremost of men, we have not found out their whereabouts and movements.

25.15.sa: किंचित्काले मनुष्येन्द्र सूतानामनुगा वयम् । मृगयित्वा यथान्यायं वेदितार्थाः स्म तत्त्वतः ॥१५॥
25.15.en: O king of men, for sometime we pursued their charioteers; and making due enquiries we have got at the truth.

25.16.sa: प्राप्ता द्वारवतीं सूता विना पार्थैः परन्तप । न तत्र कृष्णा राजेन्द्र पाण्डवाश्च महाव्रताः ॥१६॥
25.16.en: O slayer of enemies, the charioteers reached, Dvaravati without the son of Pritha. O king, there is neither Krishna nor are the Pandavas of great vows.

25.17.sa: सर्वथा विप्रनष्टास्ते नमस्ते भरतर्षभ । न हि विद्मो गतिं तेषां वासं वाऽपि महात्मनाम् ॥१७॥
25.17.en: They have all perished. We bow to you. O foremost of Bharata. We do no know the movements and whereabouts of those highsouled ones.

25.18.sa: पाण्डवानां प्रवृत्तिं च विद्मः कर्मापि वा कृतम् । स नः शाधि मनुष्येन्द्र अत ऊर्ध्वं विशाम्पते ॥१८॥
25.18.en: We know of the inclination of ht Pandavas and some of their deeds. After this, give us instructions, O king, O lord of men.

25.19.sa: अन्वेषणे पाण्डवानां भूयः किं करवामहे । इमां च नः प्रियां वीर वाचं भद्रवतीं शृणु ॥१९॥
25.19.en: As to what we should again do in our search after the Pandavas. O heroes, listen to these pleasing words tending to your wellbeing.

25.20.sa: येन त्रिगर्ता निहता बलेन महता नृप । सूतेन राज्ञो मत्स्यस्य कीचकेन बलीयसा ॥२०॥
25.20.en: Oking, the Trigarthas were repeatedly vanquished by the great prowess of Kichaka, the charioteer of the king of Matsya.

25.21.sa: स हतः पतितः शेते गन्धर्वैर्निशि भारत । अदृश्यमानैर्दुष्टात्मा भ्रातृभिः सह सोदरैः ॥२१॥
25.21.en: O descendant of Bharata, that vicioussouled one lies slain on earth with his brother by some invisible Gandharvas at night.

25.22.sa: प्रियमेतदुपश्रुत्य शत्रूणां च पराभवम् । कृतकृत्यश्च कौरव्य विधत्स्व यदनन्तरम् ॥२२॥
25.22.en: Hearing this pleasant news of the defeat of our enemy, do you decide, O Kauravya, as to what you should do hereafter.

26.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततो दुर्योधनो राजा ज्ञात्वा तेषां वचस्तदा । चिरमन्तर्मना भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच सभासदः ॥१॥
26.1.en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon hearing their words, the king Duryodhana thought in his mind and then said to his courtiers.

26.2.sa: सुदुःखा खलु कार्याणां गतिर्विज्ञातुमन्ततः । तस्मात् सर्वे निरीक्षध्वं क्क नु ते पाण्डवा गताः ॥२॥
26.2.en: It is very difficult to ascertain definitely the tide of affairs. Do you all ascertain where the Pandavas have gone.

26.3.sa: अल्पावशिष्टं कालस्य गतभूयिष्ठमन्ततः । तेषामज्ञातचर्यायामस्मिन् वर्षे त्रयोदशे ॥३॥
26.3.en: Of these thirteen years which they have to pass hidden from us all, the greater portion has well-high elapsed and only a little remains.

26.4.sa: अस्य वर्षस्य शेषं चेद्व्यतीयुरिहः पाण्डवाः । निवृत्तसमयास्ते हि सत्यव्रतपरायणाः ॥४॥
26.4.en: And if they can truly pass the remaining portion of this year hidden from our view in pursuance of their vow they will then have fulfilled their pledge.

26.5.sa: क्षरन्त इव नागेन्द्राः सर्वे ह्याशीविषोपमाः । दुःखा भवेयुः संरब्धाः कौरवान् प्रति ते ध्रुवम् ॥५॥
26.5.en: Forsooth, they, worked up with anger, will torment the Kauravas like the elephants in rut or virulent snakes.

26.6.sa: सर्वे कालस्य वेत्तारः कृच्छ्ररूपधराः स्थिताः । प्रविशेयुर्जितक्रोधास्तावदेव पुनर्वनम् ॥६॥
26.6.en: Let them, with anger controlled, acquainted with all seasons, living in painful disguise, enter the woods again.

26.7.sa: तस्मात् क्षिप्रं बुभूषध्वं यथा तेऽत्यन्तमव्ययम् । राज्यं निर्द्वन्द्वमव्यग्रं निःसपत्नं चिरं भवेत् ॥७॥
26.7.en: Do you all concert measures speedily for this, so that our kingdom may remain without enemies, rivals and diminution.

26.8.sa: अथाब्रवीत्ततः कर्णः क्षिप्रं गच्छन्तु भारत । अन्ये धूर्ता नरा दक्षा निभृताः साधुकारिणः ॥८॥
26.8.en: Thereupon Karna said : “O descendant of Bharata, let other spies, more, cunning, capable and better fitted for this work, proceed in disguise.

26.9.sa: चरन्तु देशान् संवीताः स्फीताञ्जनपदाकुलान् । तत्र गोष्ठीषु रम्यासु सिद्धप्रव्रजितेषु च ॥९॥
26.9.en: Let them range all over the country, various provinces over-flowing with population, assemblies of learned men and charming retreats of ascetics.

26.10.sa: परिचारेषु तीर्थेषु विविधेष्वाकरेषु च । विज्ञातव्या मनुष्यैस्तैस्तर्कया सुविनीतया ॥१०॥
26.10.en: In inner apartments, places of pilgrimage, mines and various other places (they should be searched after) with vigilance and humility.

26.11.sa: विविधैस्तत्परैः सम्यक् तज्ज्ञैर्निपुणसंवृतैः । अन्वेष्टव्याः सुनिपुणैः पाण्डवाश्छन्नवासिनः ॥११॥
26.11.en: The Pandavas, living in disguise, should be searched after by a number of expert spies, devoted to this work, themselves disguised and well acquainted with the object of search.

26.12.sa: आश्रमेषु च रम्येषु पर्वतेषु गुहासु च । नदीकुञ्जेषु तीर्थेषु ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च ॥१२॥

26.13.sa: अथाग्रजानन्तरजः पापभावानुरागवान् । ज्येष्ठं दुःशासनस्तत्र भ्राता भ्रातरमब्रवीत् ॥१३॥
26.13.en: Thereupon his younger brother Dushasana, taking delight in sins, said before his elder brother.

26.14.sa: येषु नः प्रत्ययो राजंश्चारेषु मनुजाधिप । ते यान्तु दत्तदेया वे भूयस्तान् परिमार्गितुम् ॥१४॥
26.14.en: O king, O lord of men, let those spies, in whom we have confidence, receive their remuneration in advance and proceed in search of them.

26.15.sa: एतच्च कर्णो यत्प्राह सर्वमीहामहे तथा । यथोद्दिष्टं चराः सर्वे मृगयन्तु यतस्ततः ॥१५॥
26.15.en: This and what Karna has said have my full approbation. As directed let all those spies search at all those places.

26.16.sa: एते चान्ये च भूयांसो देशाद्देशं यथाविधि । न तु तेषां गतिर्वासः प्रवृत्तिश्चोपलभ्यते ॥१६॥
26.16.en: Let those and others make a due search in various countries. My belief is that their movements and whereabouts are not to be known.

26.17.sa: अत्यन्तं वा निगूढास्ते पारं चोर्मिमतो गताः। व्यालैश्चापि महारण्ये भक्षिताः शूरमानिनः ॥१७॥
26.17.en: They are living in very great secrecy; or perhaps they have gone to the other side of the ocean. Those respecters of heroes might have been devoured by wild animals in that huge forest.

26.18.sa: अथवा विषमं प्राप्य विनष्टाः शाश्वतीः समाः । तस्मान्मानसमव्यग्रं कृत्वा त्वं कुरुनन्दन । कुरु कार्यं महोत्साहं मन्यसे यन्नराधिप ॥१८॥
26.18.en: Or overtaken by some dreadful calamity, they have perished for ever. Therefore, O Kuru chief, removing all anxiety from your heart, acquire what you may, working with your energy, O king.

27.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथाब्रवीन्महावीर्यो द्रोणस्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिवान् । न तादृशा विनश्यन्ति न प्रयान्ति पराभवम् ॥१॥
27.1.en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon the highly energetic and greatly wise Drona said : "Persons like them can never meet with destruction of discomfiture."

27.2.sa: शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च बुद्धिमन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः । धर्मज्ञाश्च कृतज्ञाश्च धर्मराजमनुव्रताः ॥२॥
27.2.en: Heroic, well educated, intelligent, selfcontrolled, pious, grateful, observant of vows, ever following their eldest brother, the pious Yudhishthira like a father, stationed in morality and truthful-all these brothers, O king, are obedient to this high-souled brother, graceful and having no enemy and himself (also) obeying his brothers.

27.3.sa: नीतिधर्मार्थतत्त्वज्ञं पितृवच्च समाहितम् । धर्मे स्थितं सत्यधृतिं ज्येष्ठं ज्येष्ठानुयायिनः ॥३॥
27.3.en: Heroic, well educated, intelligent, selfcontrolled, pious, grateful, observant of vows, ever following their eldest brother, the pious Yudhishthira like a father, stationed in morality and truthful-all these brothers, O king, are obedient to this high-souled brother, graceful and having no enemy and himself (also) obeying his brothers.

27.4.sa: अनुव्रता महात्मानं भ्रातरो भ्रातरं नृप । अजातशत्रुं श्रीमन्तं सर्वभ्रातॄननुव्रतम् ॥४॥
27.4.en: Heroic, well educated, intelligent, selfcontrolled, pious, grateful, observant of vows, ever following their eldest brother, the pious Yudhishthira like a father, stationed in morality and truthful-all these brothers, O king, are obedient to this high-souled brother, graceful and having no enemy and himself (also) obeying his brothers.

27.5.sa: तेषां तथा विधेयानां निभृतानां महात्मनाम् । किमर्थं नीतिमान् पार्थः श्रेयो नैषां करिष्यति ॥५॥
27.5.en: Why not Partha conversant with policy should look to the well being of such highsouled brothers obedient to him?

27.6.sa: तस्माद्यत्नात् प्रतीक्षन्ते कालस्योदयमागतम् । न हि ते नाशमृच्छेयुरिति पश्याम्यहं धिया ॥६॥
27.6.en: It is for this they are carefully waiting for the opportune hour. Such persons never die; this is what I perceive by my good sense.

27.7.sa: साम्प्रतं चैव यत्कार्यं तच्च क्षिप्रमकालिकम् । क्रियतां साधु सञ्चिन्त्य वासश्चैषां प्रचिन्त्यताम् ॥७॥
27.7.en: Do you immediately without any loss of time and after proper thought what should be done. Also appoint duly the habitation of those sons of Pandu, who are self-controlled in all things. Those heroic, sinless and devout Pandavas are hard to be discovered.

27.8.sa: यथावत् पाण्डुपुत्राणां सर्वार्थेषु धृतात्मनाम् । दुर्ज्ञेयाः खलु शूरास्ते दुरापास्तपसा वृताः ॥८॥
27.8.en: Do you immediately without any loss of time and after proper thought what should be done. Also appoint duly the habitation of those sons of Pandu, who are self-controlled in all things. Those heroic, sinless and devout Pandavas are hard to be discovered.

27.9.sa: शुद्धात्मा गुणवान् पार्थः सत्यवान्नीतिमान् शुचिः । तेजोराशिरसङ्ख्येयो गृह्णीयादपि चक्षुषा ॥९॥
27.9.en: The pure-souled, accomplished, truthful, honest son of Pritha, conversant with policy, and a very collection of effulgence, is capable of consuming by his very look.

27.10.sa: विज्ञाय क्रियतां तस्माद्भूयश्च मृगयामहे । ब्राह्मणैश्चारकैः सिद्धैर्ये चान्ये तद्विदो जनाः ॥१०॥

28.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो भरतानां पितामहः । श्रुतवान् देशकालज्ञस्तत्त्वज्ञः सर्वधर्मवित् ॥१॥
28.1.en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon the grand-father, of Bharatas, Shantanu's son, Bhishma, well-read in the Vedas, and informed of the truth of the place and time and endued with a knowledge of his own duties, after the speech of the preceptor Drona, applauded it and said the following words to the descendants of Bharata for their interest.

28.2.sa: आचार्यवाक्योपरमे तद्वाक्यमभिसन्दधत् । हितार्थं समुवाचैनां भारतीं भारतान् प्रति ॥२॥
28.2.en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon the grand-father, of Bharatas, Shantanu's son, Bhishma, well-read in the Vedas, and informed of the truth of the place and time and endued with a knowledge of his own duties, after the speech of the preceptor Drona, applauded it and said the following words to the descendants of Bharata for their interest.

28.3.sa: युधिष्ठिरे समासक्तां धर्मज्ञे धर्मसंवृताम् । असत्सु दुर्लभां नित्यं सतां चाभिमतां सदा ॥३॥
28.3.en: Bespeaking his attachment to the pious Yudhishthira, words that are rarely given vent to by the dishonest men and always liked by the honest.

28.4.sa: भीष्मः समवदत्तत्र गिरं साधुभिरर्चिताम् । यश्चैष ब्राह्मणः प्राह द्रोणः सर्वार्थतत्त्ववित् ॥४॥
