28.4.en: Bhishma gave bent to impartial words always liked by the wise: “I have nothing to say on and fully approve of the words, which the Brahmana Drona, acquainted with the truth of all things, has said.

28.5.en: Gifted with all auspicious marks, observant of religious vows, well-read in the Vedas and intent upon the performance of various religious observances, (always) engaged in carrying out the orders of elderly men, of truthful vows, acquainted with the use of time, always satisfying their condition, pure, always performing the duties of the Kshatriya order, always following Keshava, those high-souled and highly powerful heroes.

28.6.sa: वृद्धानुशासने युक्ताः सत्यव्रतपरायणाः । समयं समयज्ञास्ते पालयन्तः शुचिव्रताः ॥६॥
28.6.en: Gifted with all auspicious marks, observant of religious vows, well-read in the Vedas and intent upon the performance of various religious observances, (always) engaged in carrying out the orders of elderly men, of truthful vows, acquainted with the use of time, always satisfying their condition, pure, always performing the duties of the Kshatriya order, always following Keshava, those high-souled and highly powerful heroes.

28.7.sa: क्षत्रधर्मरता नित्यं केशवानुगताः सदा । प्रवीरपुरुषास्ते वै महात्मानो महाबलाः । नावसीदितुमर्हन्ति उद्वहन्तः सतां धुरम् ॥७॥
28.7.en: Gifted with all auspicious marks, observant of religious vows, well-read in the Vedas and intent upon the performance of various religious observances, (always) engaged in carrying out the orders of elderly men, of truthful vows, acquainted with the use of time, always satisfying their condition, pure, always performing the duties of the Kshatriya order, always following Keshava, those high-souled and highly powerful heroes.

28.8.sa: धर्मतश्चैव गुप्तास्ते सुवीर्येण च पाण्डवाः । न नाशमधिगच्छेयुरिति मे धीयते मतिः ॥८॥
28.8.en: Carrying the burden of the wise do not seem to wither away. Protected, by their own great energy, the Pandavas ever treading virtue shall not die. This is what I surmise. O descendant of Bharata, I tell you what I think we should do towards the Pandavas,

28.9.sa: तत्र बुद्धिं प्रवक्ष्यामि पाण्डवान् प्रति भारत । न तु नीतिः सुनीतस्य शक्यतेऽन्वेषितुं परैः ॥९॥
28.9.en: Carrying the burden of the wise do not seem to wither away. Protected, by their own great energy, the Pandavas ever treading virtue shall not die. This is what I surmise. O descendant of Bharata, I tell you what I think we should do towards the Pandavas,

28.10.sa: यत्तु शक्यमिहास्माभिस्तान्वै सञ्चिन्त्य पाण्डवान् । बुद्ध्या प्रयुक्तं न द्रोहात् प्रवक्ष्यामि निबोध तत् ॥१०॥
28.10.en: To search them through mean spies would not be the policy of a (really wise man.) Consulting with others we should decide what we should do towards the Pandavas.

28.11.sa: न त्वियं मादृशैर्नीतिस्तस्य वाच्या कथञ्चन । सा त्वियं साधु वक्तव्या न त्वनीतिः कथञ्चन ॥११॥
28.11.en: Know that I say nothing out of ill will towards you. I shall never give such counsels to him who is dishonest.

28.12.sa: वृद्धानुशासने तात तिष्ठता सत्यशीलिना । अवश्यं त्विह धीरेण सतां मध्ये विवक्षता ॥१२॥
28.12.en: Good counsels should be given and never evil. O child, one following the words of the aged and truthful.

28.13.sa: यथार्हमिह वक्तव्यं सर्वथा धर्मलिप्सया । तत्र नाहं तथा मन्ये यथाऽयमितरो जनः ॥१३॥
28.13.en: And calm, while speaking in the midst of an assembly, should always speak the truth if he wishes to acquire virtue.

28.14.sa: निवासं धर्मराजस्य वर्षेऽस्मिन्वै त्रयोदशे । तत्र तात न तेषां हि राज्ञां भाव्यमसाम्प्रतम् ॥१४॥
28.14.en: I think differently from all these ordinary people here regarding the whereabouts of the pious Yudhishthira in this thirteenth year of his exile.

28.15.sa: पुरे जनपदे चापि यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः । दानशीलो वदान्यश्च निभृतो ह्रीनिषेवकः । जनो जनपदे भाव्यो यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥१५॥
28.15.en: Wherever the king Yudhishthira lives o my child, the rulers, either of cities or of provinces there never meet with calamity. The people, of the country where the king Yudhishthira lives, become charitable, liberal, humble and modest.

28.16.sa: प्रियवादी सदा दान्तो भव्यः सत्यपरो जनः । हृष्टः पुष्टः शुचिर्दक्षो यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥१६॥
28.16.en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the people become sweet-speeched, selfcontrolled, observant of truth, cheerful, healthy, pure in conduct and expert in works.

28.17.sa: नासूयको न चापीर्षुर्नाभिमानी न मत्सरी । भविष्यति जनस्तत्र स्वयं धर्ममनुव्रतः ॥१७॥
28.17.en: The people of the place where Yudhishthira lives envious, malicious, vain or proud but they always perform their respective duties.

28.18.sa: ब्रह्मघोषाश्च भूयांसः पूर्णाहुत्यस्तथैव च । क्रतवश्च भविष्यन्ति भूयांसो भूरिदक्षिणाः ॥१८॥
28.18.en: There the Vedic hymns are chanted all over, sacrifices are performed, the last full libations are offered to clarified butter and the gifts to Brahmanas are always abundant.

28.19.sa: सदा च तत्र पर्जन्यः सम्यग्वर्षी न संशयः । सम्पन्नसस्या च मही निरातङ्का भविष्यति ॥१९॥
28.19.en: are never There undoubtedly the clouds always pour heavy showers; the earth, filled with crops, shall be freed from fear.

28.20.sa: गुणवन्ति च धान्यानि रसवन्ति फलानि च । गन्धवन्ति च माल्यानि शुभशब्दा च भारती ॥२०॥
28.20.en: There the paddy is full of grain and the fruits are juicy-the garlands are fragrant and the conversation is full of auspicious words.

28.21.sa: वायुश्च सुखसंस्पर्शो निष्प्रतीपं च दर्शनम् । न भयं त्वाविशेत्तत्र यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥२१॥
28.21.en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the breezes are sweet, the meetings of men are friendly and there exists no cause of fear.

28.22.sa: गावश्च बहुलास्तत्र न कृशा न च दुर्बलाः । पयांसि दधिसर्पींषि रसवन्ति हितानि च ॥२२॥
28.22.en: The kine there are plentiful, none of them being weak or lean and milk, curd and butter are all savoury and nutritious.

28.23.sa: गुणवन्ति च पेयानि भोज्यानि रसवन्ति च । तत्र देशे भविष्यन्ति यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥२३॥
28.23.en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the drinks and edibles are sweet and wholesome.

28.24.sa: रसाः स्पर्शाश्च गन्धाश्च शब्दाश्चापि गुणान्विताः । दृश्यानि च प्रसन्नानि यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥२४॥
28.24.en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the objects of taste, touch, smell and hearing are all of excellent quality and the views are all delightful.

28.25.sa: धर्माश्च तत्र सर्वैस्तु सेविताश्च द्विजातिभिः । स्वैः स्वैर्गुणैश्च संयुक्ता अस्मिन् वर्षे त्रयोदशे ॥२५॥
28.25.en: In those places, religious duties are observed by twice-born ones endued with all their respective qualities in this thirteenth year.

28.26.sa: देशे तस्मिन् भविष्यन्ति तात पाण्डवसंयुते । संप्रीतिमाञ्जनस्तत्र सन्तुष्टः शुचिरव्ययः ॥२६॥
28.26.en: O my child, in countries where the Pandavas will live, people will all be contented, cheerful, pure and of eternal virtue.

28.27.en: Whole-mindedly devoted to the worship of guests and deities they, with great energy, perform charities and shall be devoted to eternal virtue.

28.28.sa: अशुभाद्धि शुभप्रेप्सुरिष्टयज्ञः शुभव्रतः । भविष्यति जनस्तत्र यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥२८॥
28.28.en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives people, discarding all that is evil, acquire what is good only, they always perform sacrifices and observe pure vows.

28.29.sa: त्यक्तवाक्यानृतस्तात शुभकल्याणमङ्गलः । शुभार्थेप्सुः शुभमतिर्यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥२९॥
28.29.en: Where the king Yudhishthira is, people, renouncing untruth, shall acquire what is good, auspicious and beneficial and thus good mind shall be inclined towards the good.

28.30.sa: भविष्यति जनस्तत्र नित्यं चेष्टप्रियव्रतः । धर्मात्मा शक्यते ज्ञातुं नापि तात द्विजातिभिः॥३०॥
28.30.en: People there shall daily perform sacrifices and observe holy vows. O child, the pious son of Pritha, in whom exist, truth fortitude, intelligence, excellent forgiveness, highest tranquility, modest, prosperity, fame, great energy, simplicity and love for all creatures, cannot with be known by Brahmanas, what to speak of ordinary people.

28.31.sa: किं पुनः प्राकृतैस्तात पार्थो विज्ञायते क्वचित् । यस्मिन् सत्यं धृतिर्दानं परा शान्तिर्ध्रुवा क्षमा ॥३१॥
28.31.en: People there shall daily perform sacrifices and observe holy vows. O child, the pious son of Pritha, in whom exist, truth fortitude, intelligence, excellent forgiveness, highest tranquility, modest, prosperity, fame, great energy, simplicity and love for all creatures, cannot with be known by Brahmanas, what to speak of ordinary people.

28.32.sa: ह्रीः श्रीः कीर्तिः परं तेज आनृशंस्यमथार्जवम् । तस्मात्तत्र निवासं तु छन्नं यत्नेन धीमतः । गतिं च परमां तत्र नोत्सहे वक्तुमन्यथा ॥३२॥
28.32.en: People there shall daily perform sacrifices and observe holy vows. O child, the pious son of Pritha, in whom exist, truth fortitude, intelligence, excellent forgiveness, highest tranquility, modest, prosperity, fame, great energy, simplicity and love for all creatures, cannot with be known by Brahmanas, what to speak of ordinary people.

28.33.sa: एवमेतत्तु सञ्चिन्त्य यत्कृते मन्यसे हितम् । तत् क्षिप्रं कुरु कौरव्य यद्येवं श्रद्दधासि मे ॥३३॥
28.33.en: I have with great care described the secret habitation of that intelligent one; about his excellent mode of life I do not dare speak anything more. Thinking well of this do you without any loss of time what you think proper, foremost of Kurus, if you have any faith in my words. eveni care

29.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततः शारद्वतो वाक्यमित्युवाच कृपस्तदा । युक्तं प्राप्तं च वृद्धेन पाण्डवान् प्रति भाषितम् ॥१॥
29.1.en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon Sharadvata's son Kripa said the following words: “What the aged Bhishma has said about the Pandavas is reasonable and suited to the occasion.

29.2.sa: धर्मार्थसहितं श्लक्ष्णं तत्त्वतश्च सहेतुकम् । तत्रानुरूपं भीष्मेण ममाप्यत्र गिरं शृणु ॥२॥
29.2.en: Consistent with Dharma and Artha, praise worthy, reasonable, truthful and is worthy of him. Hear my words on this.

29.3.sa: तेषां चैव गतिस्तीर्थैर्वासश्चैषां प्रचिन्त्यताम् । नीतिर्विधीयतां चापि साम्प्रतं या हिता भवेत् ॥३॥
29.3.en: It is proper for you to find out the way they have followed and their whereabouts through spies and adopt what may conduce to your well-being.

29.4.sa: नावज्ञेयो रिपुस्तात प्राकृतोऽपि बुभूषता । किं पुनः पाण्डवास्तात सर्वास्त्रकुशला रणे ॥४॥
29.4.en: O my child, one seeking his welfare should not disregard an enemy, even if he be an ordinary man, what to speak of the Pandavas, well-versed in forms of warfare.

29.5.sa: तस्मात् सत्रं प्रविष्टेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु । गूढभावेषु छन्नेषु काले चोदयमागते ॥५॥
29.5.en: When the time for the return of the highsoul Pandavas comes, who are now passing their days in close disguise in woods you should gauge your own strength in your own kingdom and in those of other kings. Forsooth, the time of the return of the Pandavas is near at hand.

29.6.sa: स्वराष्ट्रे परराष्ट्रे च ज्ञातव्यं बलमात्मनः । उदयः पाण्डवानां च प्राप्ते काले न संशयः ॥६॥
29.6.en: When the time for the return of the highsoul Pandavas comes, who are now passing their days in close disguise in woods you should gauge your own strength in your own kingdom and in those of other kings. Forsooth, the time of the return of the Pandavas is near at hand.

29.7.sa: निवृत्तसमयाः पार्था महात्मानो महाबलाः । महोत्साहा भविष्यन्ति पाण्डवा ह्यमितौजसः ॥७॥
29.7.en: When the time of their exile shall be over, the high-minded and the greatly powerful son of Pritha, of incomparable prowess, shall be brimful with energy.

29.8.sa: तस्माद्बलं च कोशश्च नीतिश्चापि विधीयताम् । यथाकालोदये प्राप्ते सम्यक्तैः सन्दधामहे ॥८॥
29.8.en: Therefore (replenish) your treasury and (increase) your forces; and take recourse to a sound policy to conclude an advantageous treaty with them, when the proper time of their return comes.

29.9.sa: तात बुद्ध्याऽपि तत् सर्वं बुद्ध्यस्व बलमात्मनः । नियतं सर्वमित्रेषु बलवत्स्वबलेषु च ॥९॥
29.9.en: Knowing all this, determine your own strength, O my child, with respect to your allies, weak and powerful.

29.10.sa: उच्चावचं बलं ज्ञात्वा मध्यस्थं चापि भारत । प्रहृष्टमप्रहृष्टं च सन्दधाम तथा परैः ॥१०॥
29.10.en: Determining the efficiency, weakness or indifference of your forces, as well as who amongst them are satisfied and dissatisfied we should enter into fight with our enemies or form a treaty.

29.12.sa: सान्त्वयित्वा तु मित्राणि बलं चाभाष्यतां सुखम् । सुकोशबलसंवृद्धः सम्यक् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥१२॥
29.12.en: Resorting to the expedients of conciliation, disunion, chastisement, bribery, presents and fair conduct attack your-enemies and vanquish the weak by strength and reconcile the allies and soldiers by sweet speeches. When you shall be able to reinforce your army and replenish your treasury success shall be yours.

29.13.sa: योत्स्यसे चापि बलिभिररिभिः प्रत्युपस्थितैः । अन्यैस्त्वं पाण्डवैर्वाऽपि हीनैः स्वबलवाहनैः ॥१३॥

29.14.sa: एवं सर्वं विनिश्चित्य व्यवसायं स्वधर्मतः । यथाकालं मनुष्येन्द्र चिरं सुखमवाप्स्यसि ॥१४॥
29.14.en: Having determined all these expedients according to the practice of your order, you shall, O king of men, acquire lasting happiness in due time.

30.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथ राजा त्रिगर्तानां सुशर्मा रथयूथपः । प्राप्तकालमिदं वाक्यमुवाच त्वरितो बली ॥१॥
30.1.en: Vaishampayana said Vanquished repeatedly by the Matsya king's charioteer, Kichaka, backed by other Matsya's, the powerful king of Trigartas, Susharma, owning many cars, gave vent to the following words at the opportune moment.

30.2.sa: असकृन्निकृताः पूर्वं मत्स्यशाल्वेयकैः प्रभो । सुतेनैव च मत्स्यस्य कीचकेन पुनः पुनः ॥२॥
30.2.en: Vaishampayana said Vanquished repeatedly by the Matsya king's charioteer, Kichaka, backed by other Matsya's, the powerful king of Trigartas, Susharma, owning many cars, gave vent to the following words at the opportune moment.

30.3.sa: बाधितो बन्धुभिः सार्धं बलाद्बलवतां विभौ । स कर्णमभ्युदीक्ष्याथ दुर्योधनमभाषत ॥३॥
30.3.en: O King of the powerful, being forcibly defeated along with his relatives, he, looking askance at Karna, said to Duryodhana.

30.4.sa: असकृत्मत्स्यराज्ञा मे राष्ट्रं बाधितमोजसा । प्रणेता कीचकस्तस्य बलवानभवत् पुरा ॥४॥
30.4.en: My kingdom has been again and again forcibly invaded by the king of Matsya's. Formerly the mighty Kichaka was his general.

30.5.sa: क्रूरोऽमर्षी स दुष्टात्मा भुवि प्रख्यातविक्रमः । निहतः स तु गन्धर्वैः पापकर्मा नृशंसवान् ॥५॥
30.5.en: Crooked, wrathful, wicked-minded, having his powers kuown all over the world, that crucl and vicious one has been slain by the Gandharvas.

30.6.sa: तस्मिन् विनिहते राजा हतदर्पो निराश्रयः । भविष्यति निरुत्साहो विराट इति मे मतिः ॥६॥
30.6.en: He being slain, the king Virata, me-thinks, shorn of pride an refugc, will lose energy.

30.7.sa: तत्र यात्रा मम मता यदि ते रोचतेऽनघ । कौरवाणां च सर्वेषां कर्णस्य च महात्मनः ॥७॥
30.7.en: I think, O sinless one, we should go there, if it pleases you as well as all the Kauravas and the high-souled Karna.

30.8.sa: एतत् प्राप्तमहं मन्ये कार्यमात्ययिकं हि नः । राष्ट्रं तस्याभियास्यामो बहुधान्यसमाकुलम् ॥८॥
30.8.en: I consider, this accident, which has occurred, as favorable to us. Let us all go to his kingdom abounding in corn.

30.9.sa: आददामोऽस्य रत्नानि विविधानि वसूनि च । ग्रामान् राष्ट्राणि वा तस्य हरिष्यामो विभागशः ॥९॥
30.9.en: We will all take his various jewels and wealth and divide amongst ourselves his villages and provinces.

30.10.sa: अथवा गोसहस्राणि शुभानि च बहूनि च । विविधानि हरिष्यामः प्रतिपीड्य पुरं बलात् ॥१०॥
30.10.en: Invading his city by force we shall carry away his thousands of excellent kine of varicus kinds.

30.11.sa: कौरवैः सह सङ्गत्य त्रिगर्तैश्च विशाम्पते । गास्तस्यापहरामोऽद्य सर्वैश्चैव सुसंहताः ॥११॥
30.11.en: O emperor, uniting the Kaurava army with Trigarta, we will today carry away his collections of kine with all.

30.12.sa: संविभागेन कृत्वा तु निबघ्नीमोऽस्य पौरुषम् । हत्वा चास्य चमूं कृत्स्नां वशमेवानयामहे ॥१२॥
30.12.en: Arranging our army we shall destroy his manliness; or completely destroying his army we shall bring him under our subjection.

30.13.sa: तं वशे न्यायतः कृत्वा सुखं वत्स्यामहे वयम् । भवतां बलवृद्धिश्च भविष्यति न संशयः ॥१३॥
30.13.en: Having brought him under our control by lawful means we shall live happily in our kingdom and undoubtedly your power shall increase.

30.14.sa: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य कर्णो राजानमब्रवीत् । सूक्तं सुशर्मणा वाक्यं प्राप्तकालं हितं च नः ॥१४॥
30.14.en: Hearing those words Karna said to the king Susharman has spoken well; it is a good opportunity and is likely to be beneficial to us.

30.15.sa: तस्मात् क्षिप्रं विनिर्यामो योजयित्वा वरूथिनीम् । विभज्य चाप्यनीकानि यथा वा मन्यसेऽनघ ॥१५॥
30.15.en: If you like, O sinless one, we shall speedily issue out by collecting our forces and arranging them in divisions.

30.16.sa: प्राज्ञो वा कुरुवृद्धोऽयं सर्वेषां नः पितामहः । आचार्यश्च यथा द्रोणः कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा । मन्यन्ते ते यथा सर्वे तथा यात्रा विधीयताम् ॥१६॥
30.16.en: Or so arrange the expedition, as is liked by Sharadvata's son Kripa, the preceptor Drona and the wise and the aged grand-father of the Kurus; O king of the earth, consulting with each other we shall speedily start to gainour end.

30.17.sa: संमन्त्र्य चाशु गच्छामः साधनार्थं महीपतेः । किं च नः पाण्डवैः कार्यं हीनार्थबलपौरुषैः ॥१७॥
30.17.en: What business have we with the Pandavas who have been shorn of wealth, army and manliness. They have either gone away for good or repaired to the abode of Yama.

30.18.sa: अत्यन्तं वा प्रनष्टास्ते प्राप्ता वाऽपि यमक्षयम् । यामो राजन्निरुद्विग्ना विराटनगरं वयम् ॥१८॥
30.18.en: Shorn of anxiety, O king, we will repair to the city of Virata and bring his kine and diverse wealth.

30.19.sa: आदास्यामो हि गास्तस्य विविधानि वसूनि च । वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततो दुर्योधनो राजा वाक्यमादाय तस्य तत् । वैकर्तनस्य कर्णस्य क्षिप्रमाज्ञापयत् स्वयम् ॥१९॥

30.20.sa: शासने नित्यसंयुक्तं दुःशासनमनन्तरम् । सह वृद्धैस्तु संमन्त्र्य क्षिप्रं योजय वाहिनीम् ॥२०॥

30.21.sa: यथोद्देशं च गच्छामः सहितास्तत्र कौरवैः । सुशर्मा च यथोद्दिष्टं देशं यातु महारथः । त्रिगर्तैः सहितो राजा समग्रबलवाहनः ॥२१॥
30.21.en: We, with all the Kauravas will go to the place, appointed. Let the mighty car-warrior Susharma also go as commanded.

30.22.sa: प्रागेव हि सुसंवीतो मत्स्यस्य विषयं प्रति । जघन्यतो वयं तत्र यास्यामो दिवसान्तरे । विषयं मत्स्यराजस्य सुसमृद्धं सुसंहताः ॥२२॥
30.22.en: Following them, we will start the next day, well-prepared, for the prosperous territory of the king of Matsya's.

30.23.sa: ते यान्तु सहितास्तत्र विराटनगरं प्रति । क्षिप्रं गोपान् समासाद्य गृह्णन्तु विपुलं धनम् ॥२३॥
30.23.en: Let them with (Trigarta) go to the city of Virata and securing speedily his kine, let them take his immense wealth.

30.24.sa: गवां शतसहस्राणि श्रीमन्ति गुणवन्ति च । वयमप्यनुगृह्णीमो द्विधा कृत्वा वरूथिनीम् ॥२४॥

30.25.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ते स्म गत्वा यथोद्दिष्टां दिशं वह्नेर्महीपते । सन्नद्धा रथिनः सर्वे सपदाता बलोत्कटाः ॥२५॥
30.25.en: king, those heroes, Trigartas, accompanied by their terribly powerful infantry, proceeded towards the south east। wishing to fight with Virata in order to take possession of his kine. Susharma also started on the dark half of the month. Then on the day following the Kauravas, accompanied by their army, began to seize kine by thousands.

30.26.sa: प्रति वैरं चिकीर्षन्तो गोषु गृद्धा महाबलाः । आदातुं गाः सुशर्माऽथ कृष्णपक्षस्य सप्तमीम् ॥२६॥
30.26.en: king, those heroes, Trigartas, accompanied by their terribly powerful infantry, proceeded towards the south east। wishing to fight with Virata in order to take possession of his kine. Susharma also started on the dark half of the month. Then on the day following the Kauravas, accompanied by their army, began to seize kine by thousands.

30.27.sa: अपरे दिवसे सर्वे राजन् संभूय कौरवाः । अष्टम्यां ते न्यगृह्णन्त गोकुलानि सहस्रशः ॥२७॥
30.27.en: king, those heroes, Trigartas, accompanied by their terribly powerful infantry, proceeded towards the south east। wishing to fight with Virata in order to take possession of his kine. Susharma also started on the dark half of the month. Then on the day following the Kauravas, accompanied by their army, began to seize kine by thousands.

31.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततस्तेषां महाराज तत्रैवामिततेजसाम् । छद्मलिङ्गप्रविष्टानां पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम् ॥१॥
31.1.en: Vaishampayana said O great king, entering the service of the king Virata and living in that excellent city, the high-souled Pandavas of immeasurable prowess, passed the promised period in disguise, without being detected.

31.2.sa: व्यतीतः समयः सम्यग्वसतां वै पुरोत्तमे । कुर्वतां तस्य कर्माणि विराटस्य महीपतेः ॥२॥
31.2.en: Vaishampayana said O great king, entering the service of the king Virata and living in that excellent city, the high-souled Pandavas of immeasurable prowess, passed the promised period in disguise, without being detected.

31.3.sa: कीचके तु हते राजा विराटः परवीरहा । परां संभावनां चक्रे कुन्तीपुत्रे युधिष्ठिरे ॥३॥

31.4.sa: ततस्त्रयोदशस्यान्ते तस्य वर्षस्य भारत । सुशर्मणा गृहीतं तद्गोधनं तरसा बहु ॥४॥
31.4.en: Thereupon, O descendant of Bharata, after the expiration of the thirteenth year, Susharma by force seized many of his kine.

31.5.sa: ततो जवेन महता गोपः पुरमथाव्रजत् । स दृष्ट्वा मत्स्यराजं च रथात् प्रस्कन्द्य कुण्डली ॥५॥
31.5.en: Then a herdsman came with great speed to the city; coming down from the car and seeing the king of Matsya with ear-rings, consulting with his counsellors, the high-souled Pandavas and surrounded by heroes and warriors, adorned with ear-rings and bracelets,

31.6.sa: शूरैः परिवृतं योधैः कुण्डलाङ्गदधारिभिः । संवृतं मन्त्रिभिः सार्धं पाण्डवैश्च महात्मभिः ॥६॥
31.6.en: Then a herdsman came with great speed to the city; coming down from the car and seeing the king of Matsya with ear-rings, consulting with his counsellors, the high-souled Pandavas and surrounded by heroes and warriors, adorned with ear-rings and bracelets,

31.7.sa: तं सभायां महाराजमासीनं राष्ट्रवर्धनम् । सोऽब्रवीदुपसंगम्य विराटं प्रणतस्तदा ॥७॥
31.7.en: And approaching the great king Virata, the enhancer of kingdom, seated in the court, he, with humility, said.

31.8.sa: अस्मान् युधि विनिर्जित्य परिभूय सबान्धवान् । गवां शतसहस्राणि त्रिगर्ताः कालयन्ति ते ॥८॥
31.8.en: Vanquishing and humiliating us with our relatives in battle, the Trigartas are taking away thousands of your kine.'

31.9.sa: तान् परीप्सस्व राजेन्द्र मा नेशुः पशवस्तव । तच्छ्रुत्वा नृपतिः सेनां मत्स्यानां समयोजयत् ॥९॥
31.9.en: O king of kings, "rescue them speedily so that they may not be lost.” Hearing his words the king collected his Matsya, army.

31.10.sa: रथनागाश्वकलिलां पत्तिध्वजसमाकुलाम् । राजानो राजपुत्राश्च तनुत्राण्यथ भेजिरे ॥१०॥
31.10.en: Consisting of cars, elephants, horses, infantry and pennons. The kings and princes put on their respective armours.

31.11.sa: भानुमन्ति विचित्राणि शूरसेव्यानि भागशः । सवज्रायसगर्भं तु कवचं तत्र काञ्चनम् ॥११॥
31.11.en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

31.12.sa: विराटस्य प्रियो भ्राता शतानीकोऽभ्यहारयत् । सर्वपारसवं वर्म कल्याणपटलं दृढम् ॥१२॥
31.12.en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

31.13.sa: शतानीकादवरजो मदिराक्षोऽभ्यहारयत् । शतसूर्यं शतावर्तं शतबिन्दु शताक्षिमत् ॥१३॥
31.13.en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

31.14.sa: अभेद्यकल्पं मत्स्यानां राजा कवचमाहरत् । उत्सेधे यस्य पद्मानि शतं सौगन्धिकानि च ॥१४॥
31.14.en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

31.15.sa: सुवर्णपृष्ठं सूर्याभं सूर्यदत्तोऽभ्यहारयत् । दृढमायसगर्भं च श्वेतं वर्म शताक्षिमत् ॥१५॥
31.15.en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

31.16.sa: विराटस्य सुतो ज्येष्ठो वीरः शङ्खोऽभ्यहारयत् । शतशश्च तनुत्राणि यथास्वं ते महारथाः ॥१६॥
31.16.en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

31.17.sa: योत्स्यमाना अनह्यन्त देवरूपाः प्रहारिणः । सूपस्करेषु शुभ्रेषु महत्सु च महारथाः ॥१७॥
31.17.en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

31.18.sa: पृथक् काञ्चनसन्नाहान् रथेष्वश्वानयोजयन् । सूर्यचन्द्रप्रतीकाशे रथे दिव्ये हिरण्मये ॥१८॥
31.18.en: Then they yoked to their excellent white cars, horses, equipped in mail. Matsya's glorious standard was hoisted on his beautiful car decked with gold and resembling the sun or moon in lustre. Other Kshatriya heroes too hoisted on their own cars golden flags of various forms and contrivances. Then the king of Matsya said to his younger brother Shatanika.

31.19.sa: महानुभावो मत्स्यस्य ध्वज उच्छिश्रिये तदा । अथान्यान् विविधाकारान्ध्वजान् हेमपरिष्कृतान् ॥१९॥
31.19.en: Then they yoked to their excellent white cars, horses, equipped in mail. Matsya's glorious standard was hoisted on his beautiful car decked with gold and resembling the sun or moon in lustre. Other Kshatriya heroes too hoisted on their own cars golden flags of various forms and contrivances. Then the king of Matsya said to his younger brother Shatanika.

31.20.sa: यथास्वं क्षत्रियाः शूरा रथेषु समयोजयन् । अथ मत्स्योऽब्रवीद्राजा शतानीकं जघन्यजम् ॥२०॥

31.21.sa: कङ्कबल्लवगोपाला दामग्रन्थिश्च वीर्यवान् । युद्ध्येयुरिति मे बुद्धिर्वर्तते नात्र संशयः ॥२१॥
31.21.en: There is no doubt Kanka, Ballava, Tantipala and the greatly energetic Damagranthi will fight.

31.22.sa: एतेषामपि दीयन्तां रथा ध्वजपताकिनः । कवचानि च चित्राणि दृढानि च मृदूनि च ॥२२॥
31.22.en: Give them cars adorned with flags and pennons, and variegated armours, invulnerable, and easy to wear.

31.23.sa: प्रतिमुञ्चन्तु गात्रेषु दीयन्तामायुधानि च । वीराङ्गरूपाः पुरुषा नागराजकरोपमाः ॥२३॥
31.23.en: Let them put on these on their persons; give them also weapons. That persons thus assuming heroic forms and resembling arms of elephant chiefs,

31.24.sa: नेमे जातु न युध्येरन्निति मे धीयते मतिः । एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु नृपतेर्वाक्यं त्वरितमानसः । शतानीकस्तु पार्थेभ्यो रथान् राजन् समादिशत् ॥२४॥
31.24.en: Cannot fight, I can not lead myself to believe.” Hearing those words of the king, who was anxiously hurrying on,

31.25.sa: सहदेवाय राज्ञे च भीमाय नकुलाय च । तान् प्रहृष्टांस्ततः सूता राजभक्तिपुरस्कृताः ॥२५॥
31.25.en: O king, Shatanika, ordered chariots for the sons of Pritha-Sahadeva, the king Bhima and Nakula.

31.26.sa: निर्दिष्टा नरदेवेन रथान् शीघ्रमयोजयन् । कवचानि विचित्राणि मृदूनि च दृढानि च ॥२६॥
31.26.en: Then those charioteers, delightedly having the devotion to the king always before them, speedily got the cars ready as commanded by the king.

31.27.sa: विराटः प्रादिशद्यानि तेषामक्लिष्टकर्मणाम् । तान्यामुच्य शरीरेषु दंशितास्ते परन्तपाः ॥२७॥
31.27.en: Those slayers of foes then put on their persons those strong, easy and variegated armours which the king Virata had ordered for (those heroes) of unwearied actions. Then ascending cars drawn by good horses, those best of men,

31.28.sa: रथान् हयैः सुसंपन्नानास्थाय च नरोत्तमाः । निर्ययुर्मुदिताः पार्थाः शत्रुसङ्घावमर्दिनः ॥२८॥
31.28.en: Those slayers of foes then put on their persons those strong, easy and variegated armours which the king Virata had ordered for (those heroes) of unwearied actions. Then ascending cars drawn by good horses, those best of men,

31.29.sa: तरस्विनश्छन्नरूपाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः । रथान् हेमपरिच्छन्नानास्थाय च महारथाः ॥२९॥
31.29.en: The repressors of hostile army, the sons of Pritha, delightedly issued out. Those mighty car-warriors, the four heroic brothers, the Pandavas, of unfailing prowess, living in disguise, endue with celerity of movements and all well-skilled in the art of war, the sons of Pritha, ascending golden cars, those foi most of Kurus, followed Virata. Dreadful and infuriated elephants, sixty years old with beautiful tusks and rent temples and temporal juice trickling down, appearing like clouds pouring rain, driven by trained and skilled heroes, followed the king like so many moving hills. The leading heroes of Matsya who delightedly followed the king had eight thousand cars, a thousand elephants and sixty thousand horses.

31.30.sa: विराटमन्वयुः पार्थाः सहिताः कुरुपुङ्गवाः । चत्वारो भ्रातरः शूराः पाण्डवाः सत्यविक्रमाः ॥३०॥
31.30.en: The repressors of hostile army, the sons of Pritha, delightedly issued out. Those mighty car-warriors, the four heroic brothers, the Pandavas, of unfailing prowess, living in disguise, endue with celerity of movements and all well-skilled in the art of war, the sons of Pritha, ascending golden cars, those foi most of Kurus, followed Virata. Dreadful and infuriated elephants, sixty years old with beautiful tusks and rent temples and temporal juice trickling down, appearing like clouds pouring rain, driven by trained and skilled heroes, followed the king like so many moving hills. The leading heroes of Matsya who delightedly followed the king had eight thousand cars, a thousand elephants and sixty thousand horses.

31.31.sa: भीमाश्च मत्तमातङ्गा प्रभिन्नकरटामुखाः । क्षरन्तश्चैव नागेन्द्राः सुदन्ताः षष्टिहायनाः ॥३१॥
31.31.en: Throwing each other down with their arms and then again seizing in great anger, they fought like two elephants with rent temples.

31.32.sa: स्वारूढा युद्धकुशलैः शिक्षिता हस्तिसादिभिः । राजानमन्वयुः पश्चाच्चलन्त इव पर्वताः ॥३२॥
31.32.en: The repressors of hostile army, the sons of Pritha, delightedly issued out. Those mighty car-warriors, the four heroic brothers, the Pandavas, of unfailing prowess, living in disguise, endue with celerity of movements and all well-skilled in the art of war, the sons of Pritha, ascending golden cars, those foi most of Kurus, followed Virata. Dreadful and infuriated elephants, sixty years old with beautiful tusks and rent temples and temporal juice trickling down, appearing like clouds pouring rain, driven by trained and skilled heroes, followed the king like so many moving hills. The leading heroes of Matsya who delightedly followed the king had eight thousand cars, a thousand elephants and sixty thousand horses.

31.33.sa: विशारदानां मुख्यानां हृष्टानां चारुजीविनाम् । अष्टौ रथसहस्राणि दश नागशतानि च ॥३३॥
31.33.en: The repressors of hostile army, the sons of Pritha, delightedly issued out. Those mighty car-warriors, the four heroic brothers, the Pandavas, of unfailing prowess, living in disguise, endue with celerity of movements and all well-skilled in the art of war, the sons of Pritha, ascending golden cars, those foi most of Kurus, followed Virata. Dreadful and infuriated elephants, sixty years old with beautiful tusks and rent temples and temporal juice trickling down, appearing like clouds pouring rain, driven by trained and skilled heroes, followed the king like so many moving hills. The leading heroes of Matsya who delightedly followed the king had eight thousand cars, a thousand elephants and sixty thousand horses.

31.34.sa: षष्टिश्चाश्वसहस्त्राणि मत्स्यानामभिनिर्ययुः । तदनीकं विराटस्य शुशुभे भरतर्षभ ॥३४॥
31.34.en: The repressors of hostile army, the sons of Pritha, delightedly issued out. Those mighty car-warriors, the four heroic brothers, the Pandavas, of unfailing prowess, living in disguise, endue with celerity of movements and all well-skilled in the art of war, the sons of Pritha, ascending golden cars, those foi most of Kurus, followed Virata. Dreadful and infuriated elephants, sixty years old with beautiful tusks and rent temples and temporal juice trickling down, appearing like clouds pouring rain, driven by trained and skilled heroes, followed the king like so many moving hills. The leading heroes of Matsya who delightedly followed the king had eight thousand cars, a thousand elephants and sixty thousand horses.

31.35.sa: संप्रयातं तदा राजन्निरीक्षन्तं गवां पदम् । तद्बलाग्र्यं विराटस्य संप्रस्थितमशोभत । दृढायुधजनाकीर्णं गजाश्वरथसङ्कुलम् ॥३५॥
31.35.en: O foremost of the Bharatas, that army of Virata, issuing out marking the foot-prints of the kine, looked beautiful.

32.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । निर्याय नगराच्छूरा व्यूढानीकाः प्रहारिणः । त्रिगर्तानस्पृशन् मत्स्याः सूर्ये परिणते सति ॥१॥
32.1.en: Vaishampayana said Issuing out from the city, those heroic repressors, the Matsya's, arranged in battle array, met the Trigartas when the sun had passed the meridian.

32.2.sa: ते त्रिगर्ताश्च मत्स्याश्च संरब्धा युद्धदुर्मदाः । अन्योन्यमभिगर्जन्तो गोषु गृद्धा महाबलाः ॥२॥
32.2.en: The mighty and powerful Trigartas and Matsya's, both worked up with ire and irrepressible in battle, desirous of possessing kine, sent up a loud war-cry.

32.3.en: Terrible and infuriated elephants, mounted by skillful heroes of both sides, were urged on with spikes and hooks.

32.4.sa: तेषां समागमो घोरस्तुमुलो लोमहर्षणः । घ्नतां परस्परं राजन् यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः ॥४॥
32.4.en: The combat that took place, O king, when the sun was declining, between the infantry and cavalry, chariots and elephants of both sides, resembling that which took place in the days of yore between the gods and demons, was dreadful, fierce, hair-stirring and calculated to increase the dominion of Yama.

32.5.en: The combat that took place, O king, when the sun was declining, between the infantry and cavalry, chariots and elephants of both sides, resembling that which took place in the days of yore between the gods and demons, was dreadful, fierce, hair-stirring and calculated to increase the dominion of Yama.

32.6.sa: अन्योन्यमभ्यापततां निघ्नतां चेतरेतरम् । उदतिष्ठद्रजो भौमं न प्राज्ञायत किञ्चन ॥६॥

32.7.en: Covered with dust raised by the soldiers the birds began to drop down on earth and the sun himself disappeared behind the thick cloud of arrows.

32.8.sa: खद्योतैरिव संयुक्तमन्तरिक्षं व्यराजत । रुक्मपृष्ठानि चापानि व्यतिषिक्तानि धन्विनाम् ॥८॥
32.8.en: The sky shone resplendent as if with (a number of) fire-flies. Changing their bows feathered in gold from one hand to another, the heroes began to smite each other discharging their shafts right and left. The charioteers fought with charioteers, the infantry fought with infantry.

32.9.sa: पततां लोकवीराणां सव्यदक्षिणमस्यताम् । रथा रथैः समाजग्मुः पादातैश्च पदातयः ॥९॥
32.9.en: The sky shone resplendent as if with (a number of) fire-flies. Changing their bows feathered in gold from one hand to another, the heroes began to smite each other discharging their shafts right and left. The charioteers fought with charioteers, the infantry fought with infantry.

32.10.sa: सादिनः सादिभिश्चैव गजैश्चापि महागजाः । असिभिः पट्टिशैः प्रासैः शक्तिभिस्तोमरैरपि ॥१०॥
32.10.en: The cavalry with cavalry and elephants with mighty elephants. With sword axes, Prasas, Shaktis, and Tomaras,

32.11.sa: संरब्धाः समरे राजन्निजघ्नुरितरेतरम् । निघ्नन्तः समरेऽन्योन्यं शूराः परिघबाहवः ॥११॥
32.11.en: They, enraged, O king, struck each other in the encounter. Although these mighty armed heroes struck each other,

32.12.sa: न शेकुरभिसंरब्धाः शूरान् कर्तुं पराङ्मुखान् । कृत्तोत्तरोष्ठं सुनसं कृत्तकेशमलङ्कृतम् ॥१२॥
32.12.en: None of them succeeded in weakening the other. And severed heads, some with beautiful noses, some with upper lips wounded, some adorned with ear-rings, some cut into twain about the well-arranged hair, were seen rolling in the field covered with dust. And in that battle field were seen the limbs of Kshatriya heroes cut off by shafts and lying like trunks of Sala trees. And spread over with heads adorned with car-rings and arms smeared with sandal looking like the bodies of snakes the battlefield appeared in beauty. The charioteers approached the charioteers striking each other.

32.13.sa: अदृश्यत शिरश्छिन्नं रजोध्वस्तं सकुण्डलम् । अदृश्यंस्तत्र गात्राणि शरैश्छिन्नानि भागशः ॥१३॥
32.13.en: None of them succeeded in weakening the other. And severed heads, some with beautiful noses, some with upper lips wounded, some adorned with ear-rings, some cut into twain about the well-arranged hair, were seen rolling in the field covered with dust. And in that battle field were seen the limbs of Kshatriya heroes cut off by shafts and lying like trunks of Sala trees. And spread over with heads adorned with car-rings and arms smeared with sandal looking like the bodies of snakes the battlefield appeared in beauty. The charioteers approached the charioteers striking each other.

32.14.en: None of them succeeded in weakening the other. And severed heads, some with beautiful noses, some with upper lips wounded, some adorned with ear-rings, some cut into twain about the well-arranged hair, were seen rolling in the field covered with dust. And in that battle field were seen the limbs of Kshatriya heroes cut off by shafts and lying like trunks of Sala trees. And spread over with heads adorned with car-rings and arms smeared with sandal looking like the bodies of snakes the battlefield appeared in beauty. The charioteers approached the charioteers striking each other.

32.15.sa: आस्तीर्णा वसुधा भाति शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः । रथिनां रथिभिश्चात्र संप्रहारोऽभ्यवर्तत ॥१५॥
32.15.en: None of them succeeded in weakening the other. And severed heads, some with beautiful noses, some with upper lips wounded, some adorned with ear-rings, some cut into twain about the well-arranged hair, were seen rolling in the field covered with dust. And in that battle field were seen the limbs of Kshatriya heroes cut off by shafts and lying like trunks of Sala trees. And spread over with heads adorned with car-rings and arms smeared with sandal looking like the bodies of snakes the battlefield appeared in beauty. The charioteers approached the charioteers striking each other.

32.16.sa: सादिभिः सादिनां चापि पदातीनां पदातिभिः । उपाशाम्यद्रजो भौमं रुधिरेण प्रसर्पता ॥१६॥
32.16.en: The cavalry (encountered) the cavalry and the infantry the infantry and the dreadful dust was drenched by the over-spreading blood.

32.17.sa: कश्मलं चाविशद्धोरं निर्मर्यादमवर्तत । उपाविशन् गरुत्मन्तः शरैर्गाढं प्रवेजिताः । अन्तरिक्षे गतिर्येषां दर्शनं चाप्यरुध्यत ॥१७॥
32.17.en: There arose a dreadful combat shorn of all considerations. And having their course and vision obstructed by the shower of arrows the vultures began to come down. Although these mighty-armed heroes struck cach other in the battle none of them could overpower his antagonist. Shatanika slaying a hundred, and Vishalaksha a four hundred,

32.18.sa: ते घ्नन्तः समरेऽन्योन्यं शूराः परिघबाहवः । न शेकुरभिसंरब्धाः शूरान् कर्तुं पराङ्मुखान् ॥१८॥

32.19.sa: शतानीकः शतं हत्वा विशालाक्षश्चतुःशतम् । प्रविष्टौ महतीं सेनां त्रिगर्तानां महारथौ ॥१९॥

32.20.sa: तौ प्रविष्टौ महासेनां बलवन्तौ मनस्विनौ । आर्च्छेतां बाहुसंरब्धौ केशाकेशि रथारथि ॥२०॥
32.20.en: These two mighty car-warriors entered into the huge army of Trigartas. And having entered into the great army those two intelligent and powerful.

32.21.sa: लक्षयित्वा त्रिगर्तानां तौ प्रविष्टौ रथव्रजम् । अग्रतः सूर्यदत्तश्च मदिराक्षश्च पृष्ठतः ॥२१॥
32.21.en: (Heroes) (began an encounter) hand-tohand, hair to hair and car to car. And marking they entered into the collection of cars belonging to the Trigartas.

32.22.sa: विराटस्तत्र संग्रामे हत्वा पञ्चशतान् रथान् । हयानां च शतान्यष्टौ हत्वा पञ्च महारथान् ॥२२॥
32.22.en: Destroying five hundred cars in that encounter with Suryadatta before and Madiraksha after him,

32.23.sa: चरन् स विविधान् मार्गान् रथेन रथसत्तमः । त्रिगर्तानां सुशर्माणमार्च्छद्रुक्मरथं रणे ॥२३॥
32.23.en: And slaying eight hundred horses, five mighty car-warriors, that foremost of charioteers began to display many manuvaeres in that field of battle.

32.24.sa: तौ व्यवाहरतां तत्र महात्मानौ महाबलौ । अन्योन्यमभिगर्जन्तौ गोष्ठेषु वृषभाविव ॥२४॥
32.24.en: He then came upon Susharma, the king of Trigartas mounted on a golden chariot; there those two high-souled and highly powerful (heroes) struck (each other)

32.25.sa: ततो राजा त्रिगर्तानां सुशर्मा युद्धदुर्मदः । मत्स्यं समीयाद्राजानं द्वैरथेन नरर्षभः ॥२५॥
32.25.en: Roaring like two bulls in a pasture. Thereupon the king of Trigartas, Susharman, irrepressible in battle,

32.26.sa: ततो रथाभ्यां रथिनौ व्यतीयतुरमर्षणौ । शरान् व्यसृजतां शीघ्रं तोयधारा घना इव ॥२६॥
32.26.en: That foremost of men invited the king of Matsya to a single combat on the chariot. Thereupon those two car-warriors, worked up with fury, rushed upon each other in their cars.

32.27.sa: अन्योन्यं चापि संरब्धौ विचेरतुरमर्षणौ । कृतास्त्रौ निशितैर्बाणैरसिशक्तिगदाभृतौ ॥२७॥
32.27.en: They discharged arrows quickly like clouds pouring torrents of rain. Enraged with each other the (two) wrathful (heroes) moved about,

32.28.sa: ततो राजा सुशर्माणं विव्याध दशभिः शरैः । पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिश्चास्य विव्याध चतुरो हयान् ॥२८॥
32.28.en: Skilled in weapons, and armed with sharpened arrows, swords, shaktis and maces. Then the king pierced Susharman with ten arrows,

32.29.sa: तथैव मत्स्यराजानं सुशर्मा युद्धदुर्मदः । पञ्चाशद्भिः शितैर्बाणैर्विव्याध परमास्त्रवित् ॥२९॥
32.29.en: Each of his four horses also with five arrows. Susharma too, irrepressible in battle and acquainted with the use of fatal weapons, pierced, the king of Matsya with fifty sharpened arrows. Then, Ogreat king, on account of the dust in the field of battle, the soldiers of both Susharma and the king of Matsya could not recognise each other.

32.30.sa: ततः सैन्यं महाराज मत्स्यराजसुशर्मणोः । नाभ्यजानत्तदाऽन्योन्यं सैन्येन रजसाऽऽवृतम् ॥३०॥
32.30.en: Each of his four horses also with five arrows. Susharma too, irrepressible in battle and acquainted with the use of fatal weapons, pierced, the king of Matsya with fifty sharpened arrows. Then, Ogreat king, on account of the dust in the field of battle, the soldiers of both Susharma and the king of Matsya could not recognise each other.

33.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तमसाऽभिप्लुते लोके रजसा चैव भारत । अतिष्ठन् वै मुहूर्तं तु व्यूढानीकाः प्रहारिणः ॥१॥
33.1.en: Vaishampayana said O descendant of Bharata, the whole world being enshrouded in dust and natural darkness, the soldiers of both sides, without breaking the battle array, stopped for some time.

33.2.sa: ततोऽन्धकारं प्रणुदन्नुदतिष्ठत चन्द्रमाः । कुर्वाणो विमलां रात्रिं नन्दयन् क्षत्रियान् युधि ॥२॥
33.2.en: Then dispelling the darkness the moon rose, making the night clear and gladdening the Kshatriyas in the battle field.

33.3.sa: ततः प्रकाशमासाद्य पुनर्युद्धमवर्तत । घोररूपं ततस्ते स्म नावैक्षन्त परस्परम् ॥३॥
33.3.en: When every thing came in view, the battle began again; and it became so dreadful that they could not see each other.

33.4.sa: ततः सुशर्मा त्रैगर्तः सह भ्रात्रा यवीयसा । अभ्यद्रवन्मत्स्यराजं रथव्रातेन सर्वशः ॥४॥

33.5.sa: ततो रथाभ्यां प्रस्कन्द्य भ्रातरौ क्षत्रियर्षभौ । गदापाणी सुसंरब्धौ समभ्यद्रवतां रथान् ॥५॥

33.6.sa: तथैव तेषां तु बलानि तानि क्रुद्धान्यथान्योन्यमभिद्रवन्ति । गदासिखड्गैश्च परश्वधैश्च प्रासैश्च तीक्ष्णाग्रसुपीतधारैः ॥६॥
33.6.en: The hostile armies fiercely assailed each other with maces, swords, scimitars, axes, nooses, and with sharpened points.

33.7.sa: बलं तु मत्स्यस्य बलेन राजा सर्वं त्रिगर्ताधिपतिः सुशर्मा । प्रमथ्य जित्वा च प्रसह्य मत्स्यं विराटमोजस्विनमभ्यधावत् ॥७॥
33.7.en: Having assailed and vanquished with energy the entire army of the king of Matsya's, Susharman, the king of Trigartas, rushed furiously at the highly energetic Virata.

33.8.sa: तौ निहत्य पृथक् धुर्यावुभौ तौ पार्ष्णिसारथी । विरथं मत्स्यराजानं जीवग्राहमगृह्णताम् ॥८॥
33.8.en: Having slain severally his two horses, his charioteer as also the soldiers who protected him in the rear they took the king of Matsya captive, even alive, deprivation of his car.

33.9.sa: तमुन्मथ्य सुशर्माऽथ युवतीमिव कामुकः । स्यन्दनं स्वं समारोप्य प्रययौ शीघ्रवाहनः ॥९॥
33.9.en: Then assailing him fiercely like a lustful person (oppressing) a female, they placed him on the car and speedily went out.

33.10.sa: तस्मिन् गृहीते विरथे विराटे बलवत्तरे । प्राद्रवन्त भयान्मत्स्यास्त्रिगतैरर्दिता भृशम् ॥१०॥
33.10.en: After the powerful Virata, deprived of his car, had been taken captive, the Matsya's, greatly assailed by Trigartas, fled away to different directions in fear.

33.11.sa: तेषु सन्त्रस्यमानेषु कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । प्रत्यभाषन्महाबाहुं भीमसेनमरिन्दमम् ॥११॥
33.11.en: Beholding them thus terrified Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, said to the mighty-armed Bhimasena, the slayer of enemies.

33.12.sa: मत्स्यराजः परामृष्टस्त्रिगर्तेन सुशर्मणा । तं मोचय महाबाहो न गच्छेद्द्विषतां वशम् ॥१२॥
33.12.en: The king of Matsya has been captivated by Susharman, the king of Trigartas; O you of mighty arms, release him so that he may not be subject to the enemies.

33.13.sa: उषिताः स्म सुखं सर्वे सर्वकामैः सुपूजिताः । भीमसेन त्वया कार्या तस्य वासस्य निष्कृतिः॥१३॥
33.13.en: We have lived happily in his house with our desire satisfied O Bhimasena, you should satisfy that debt.

33.14.sa: भीमसेन उवाच । अहमेनं परित्रास्ये शासनात् तव पार्थिव । पश्य मे सुमहत् कर्म युध्यतः सह शत्रुभिः ॥१४॥
33.14.en: Bhimasena said By your command, O king, I shall set him free: behold my great feat of fighting with the enemies.

33.15.sa: स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य तिष्ठ त्वं भ्रातृभिः सह । एकान्तमाश्रितो राजन् पश्य मेऽद्य पराक्रमम् ॥१५॥
33.15.en: Stay aside with brothers at a corner depending on the strength of your arms and behold my prowess today.

33.16.sa: सुस्कन्धोऽयं महावृक्षो गदारूप इव स्थितः । अहमेनमपारुज्य द्रावयिष्यामि शात्रवान् ॥१६॥
33.16.en: uprooting this huge tree with a trunk looking like a mace I shall assail the enemies.

33.17.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं वीक्षमाणं वनस्पतिम् । अब्रवीद्भ्रातरं वीरं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः ॥१७॥
33.17.en: Vaishampayana said Seeing Bhima look at that tree like an infuriated elephant the heroic and pious king Yudhishthira said to his brother.

33.18.sa: मा भीम साहसं कार्षीस्तिष्ठत्वेष वनस्पतिः । मा त्वं वृक्षेण कर्माणि कुर्वाणमतिमानुषम् ॥१८॥
33.18.en: "Do not commit such a rash act, О Bhima, let the tree stand there." You should not with a tree perform superhuman deeds.

33.19.sa: जनाः समवबुध्येरन् भीमोऽयमिति भारत । अन्यदेवायुधं किञ्चित् प्रतिपद्यस्व मानुषम् ॥१९॥
33.19.en: O descendant of Bharata, people will then recognize you and say “This is Bhima". Take you therefore, some other human weapon,

33.20.sa: चापं वा यदि वा शक्तिं निस्त्रिंशं वा परश्वधम् । यदेव मानुषं भीम भवेदन्यैरलक्षितम् ॥२०॥
33.20.en: A bow, or a dart, sword or battle-axe. Taking a weapon that is human, release the king, O Bhima, speedily, so that people may not recognize you. The highly powerful twins will be the protectors of your wheels. Being united together in battle, release the king of Matsya.

33.21.sa: तदेवायुधमादाय मोक्षयाशु महीपतिम् । यमौ च चक्ररक्षौ ते भवितारौ महाबलौ ॥२१॥
33.21.en: A bow, or a dart, sword or battle-axe. Taking a weapon that is human, release the king, O Bhima, speedily, so that people may not recognize you. The highly powerful twins will be the protectors of your wheels. Being united together in battle, release the king of Matsya.

33.22.sa: सहिताः समरे तत्र मत्स्यराजं परीप्सत । वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्तस्तु वेगेन भीमसेनो महाबलः ॥२२॥
33.22.en: A bow, or a dart, sword or battle-axe. Taking a weapon that is human, release the king, O Bhima, speedily, so that people may not recognize you. The highly powerful twins will be the protectors of your wheels. Being united together in battle, release the king of Matsya.

33.23.sa: गृहीत्वा तु धनुः श्रेष्ठं जवेन सुमहाजवः । व्यमुञ्चच्छरवर्षाणि सतोय इव तोयदः ॥२३॥
33.23.en: Thus accosted the highly powerful Bhimasena, gifted with great speed, took up with great force his best of bows,

33.24.sa: तं भीमो भीमकर्माणं सुशर्माणमथाद्रवत् । विराटं समवीक्ष्यैनं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चावदत् ॥२४॥
33.24.en: And discharged from it a shower of shafts like a cloud surcharged with water. Bhima then fell upon Susharma of dreadful deeds.

33.25.sa: सुशर्मा चिन्तयामास कालान्तकयमोपमम् । तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भाषन्तं पृष्ठतो रथपुङ्गवः ॥२५॥
33.25.en: Casting his looks on Virata he said to (Susharma) “stay stay.” Susharma thought him to be Yama-the very regent of death.

33.26.sa: पश्यतां सुमहत् कर्म महद्युद्ध‌मुपस्थितम् । परावृत्तो धनुर्गुह्य सुशर्मा भ्रातृभिः सह । निमेषान्तरमात्रेण भीमसेनेन ते रथाः ॥२६॥
33.26.en: Taking up his bow, Susharma with his brothers turned back and within the twinkling of an eye those cars (were destroyed by) Bhimasena.

33.27.sa: रथानां च गजानां च वाजिनां च ससादिनाम् । सहस्रशतसङ्घाताः शूराणामुग्रधन्विनाम् ॥२७॥
33.27.en: And hundreds of thousand of chariots, elephants, horses, horsemen and brave and powerful bowmen were over thrown by him before the very presence of Virata.

33.28.sa: पातिता भीमसेनेन विराटस्य समीपतः । पत्तयो निहतास्तेषां गदां गृह्य महात्मना ॥२८॥
33.28.en: Their infantry was slain by the high-souled (Bhima with mace in hand): Beholding such a fight Susharma, irrepressible in battle,

33.29.sa: तद्दृष्ट्वा तादृशं युद्धं सुशर्मा युद्धदुर्मदः । चिन्तयामास मनसा किं शेषं हि बलस्य मे । अपरो दृश्यते सैन्ये पुरा मग्नो महाबले ॥२९॥
33.29.en: Thought within his mind: "Is this the end of my army. I see my brother drowned in the midst of his powerful army.”

33.30.sa: आकर्णपूर्णेन तदा धनुषा प्रत्यदृश्यत । सुशर्मा सायकांस्तीक्ष्णान् क्षिपते च पुनः पुनः ॥३०॥
33.30.en: Stretching his bow to his ear Susharma began to retreat and discharge repeatedly sharpened shafts.

33.31.sa: ततः समस्तास्ते सर्वे तुरगानभ्यचोदयन् । दिव्यमस्त्रं विकुर्वाणास्त्रिगर्तान् प्रत्यमर्षणाः ॥३१॥
33.31.en: Beholding the Pandavas return to their cars the entire huge army urged on their horses and began to assail the Trigartas with excellent weapons. Virata's son, greatly enraged, began to display highly wonderful feats in battle.

33.32.sa: तान्निवृत्तरथान् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवान् सा महाचमूः । वैराटिः परमक्रुद्धो युयुधे परमाद्भुतम् ॥३२॥
33.32.en: Beholding the Pandavas return to their cars the entire huge army urged on their horses and began to assail the Trigartas with excellent weapons. Virata's son, greatly enraged, began to display highly wonderful feats in battle.

33.33.sa: सहस्त्रमवधीत्तत्र कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । भीमः सप्त सहस्राणि यमलोकमदर्शयत् ॥३३॥
33.33.en: Kunti's son Yudhishthira killed one thousand and Bhima dispatched seven thousand.

33.34.sa: नकुलश्चापि सप्तैव शतानि प्राहिणोच्छरैः । शतानि त्रीणि शूराणां सहदेवः प्रतापवान् ॥३४॥
33.34.en: Nakula killed with arrows seven hundred and powerful Sahadeva the foremost of men, commanded by Yudhishthira, slew three hundreds of heroes. Slaying that huge army of Trigartas, the mighty car-warrior, Yudhishthira, with uplifted weapon, attacked him sorely with shafts.

33.35.en: Nakula killed with arrows seven hundred and powerful Sahadeva the foremost of men, commanded by Yudhishthira, slew three hundreds of heroes. Slaying that huge army of Trigartas, the mighty car-warrior, Yudhishthira, with uplifted weapon, attacked him sorely with shafts.

33.36.sa: हत्वा तां महतीं सेनां त्रिगर्तानां महारथः । ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा त्वरमाणो महारथः ॥३६॥
33.36.en: Nakula killed with arrows seven hundred and powerful Sahadeva the foremost of men, commanded by Yudhishthira, slew three hundreds of heroes. Slaying that huge army of Trigartas, the mighty car-warrior, Yudhishthira, with uplifted weapon, attacked him sorely with shafts.

33.37.sa: अभिपत्य सुशर्माणं शरैरभ्याहनद्भृशम् । सुशर्माऽपि सुसंरब्धस्त्वरमाणो युधिष्ठिरम् ॥३७॥
33.37.en: Susharma, too greatly enraged, with impetuosity pierced Yudhishthira with nine shafts and his four horses with four. Then 0 king, the quick-coursing son of Kunti, Vrikodara, nearing Susharma, assailed his horses. Having slain the soldiers that were in the rear with huge shafts, he, in anger, brought down his (Susharmas') charioteer from his car. The heroic protector of the wheels celebrated as Madiraksha,

33.38.sa: अविध्यन्नवभिर्बाणैश्चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान् । ततो राजन्नाशुकारी कुन्तीपुत्रो वृकोदरः ॥३८॥
33.38.en: Susharma, too greatly enraged, with impetuosity pierced Yudhishthira with nine shafts and his four horses with four. Then 0 king, the quick-coursing son of Kunti, Vrikodara, nearing Susharma, assailed his horses. Having slain the soldiers that were in the rear with huge shafts, he, in anger, brought down his (Susharmas') charioteer from his car. The heroic protector of the wheels celebrated as Madiraksha,

33.39.sa: समासाद्य सुशर्माणमश्वानस्य व्यपोथयत् । पृष्ठगोपांश्च तस्याथ हत्वा परमसायकैः ॥३९॥
33.39.en: Susharma, too greatly enraged, with impetuosity pierced Yudhishthira with nine shafts and his four horses with four. Then 0 king, the quick-coursing son of Kunti, Vrikodara, nearing Susharma, assailed his horses. Having slain the soldiers that were in the rear with huge shafts, he, in anger, brought down his (Susharmas') charioteer from his car. The heroic protector of the wheels celebrated as Madiraksha,

33.40.sa: अथास्य सारथिं क्रुद्धो रथोपस्थादपातयत् । चक्ररक्षश्च शूरो वै मदिराक्षोऽतिविश्रुतः ॥४०॥
33.40.en: Susharma, too greatly enraged, with impetuosity pierced Yudhishthira with nine shafts and his four horses with four. Then 0 king, the quick-coursing son of Kunti, Vrikodara, nearing Susharma, assailed his horses. Having slain the soldiers that were in the rear with huge shafts, he, in anger, brought down his (Susharmas') charioteer from his car. The heroic protector of the wheels celebrated as Madiraksha,

33.41.sa: समायाद्विरथं दृष्ट्वा त्रिगर्तं प्राहरत् तदा । ततो विराटः प्रस्कन्द्य रथादथ सुशर्मणः ॥४१॥
33.41.en: Seeing Trigarta deprived of his car, came there. Then coming down from Susharma's car Virata.

33.42.sa: गदां तस्य परामृश्य तमेवाभ्यद्रवद्बली । स चचार गदापाणिर्वृद्धोऽपि तरुणो यथा ॥४२॥
33.42.en: Heroic (as he was) took up his Susharma's mace and rushed upon him, And he, with mace in hand moved about like a young man, although an old man.

33.43.sa: पलायमानं त्रैगर्तं दृष्ट्वा भीमोऽभ्यभाषत । राजपुत्र निवर्तस्व न ते युक्तं पलायनम् ॥४३॥
33.43.en: Beholding the king of Trigarta taking to his heels, Bhima said :"Desist, O prince, it does not behove you to fly away.

33.44.sa: अनेन वीर्येण कथं गास्त्वं प्रार्थयसे बलात् । कथं चानुचरांस्त्यक्त्वा शत्रुमध्ये विषीदसि ॥४४॥
33.44.en: With such powers how could you think of taking away the kine? Why forsaking your followers do you droop in the midst of your enemies?

33.45.sa: इत्युक्तः स तु पार्थेन सुशर्मा रथयूथपः । तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भीमं स सहसाऽभ्यद्रवद्वली ॥४५॥
33.45.en: Being thus addressed by Partha, the powerful Susharma, owner of cars, all on a sudden rushed upon Bhima (saying "stay! stay!!').

33.46.sa: भीमस्तु भीमसंकाशो रथात् प्रस्कन्द्य पाण्डवः । प्राद्रवत्तूर्णमव्यग्रो जीवितेप्सुः सुशर्मणः ॥४६॥
33.46.en: Getting down from the car the dreadful Bhimasena, the son of Pandu, rushed towards him with coolness, desirous of taking Susharma's life.

33.47.sa: तं भीमसेनो धावन्तमभ्यधावत वीर्यवान् । त्रिगर्तराजमादातुं सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा ॥४७॥
33.47.en: With a view to get hold of the king of Trigarta approaching towards him the energetic Bhimasena rushed upon him like a lion upon a small deer.

33.48.sa: अभिद्रुत्य सुशर्माणं केशपक्षे परामृशत् । समुद्यम्य तु रोषात् तं निष्पिपेष महीतले ॥४८॥
33.48.en: Rushing upon Susharma he held him by the hair; and lifting him up in anger he dashed him against the earth.

33.49.sa: पदा मूर्ध्नि महाबाहुः प्राहरद्विलपिष्यतः । तस्य जानुं ददौ भीमो जघ्ने चैनमरत्निना । स मोहमगमद्राजा प्रहारवरपीडितः ॥४९॥

33.50.sa: तस्मिन् गृहीते विरथे त्रिगर्तानां महारथे । अभज्यत बलं सर्वं त्रैगर्तं तद्भयातुरम् ॥५०॥

33.51.sa: निवर्त्य गास्ततः सर्वाः पाण्डुपुत्रा महारथाः । अवजित्य सुशर्माणं धनं चादाय सर्वशः ॥५१॥

33.52.sa: स्वबाहुबलसम्पन्ना ह्रीनिषेवा यतव्रताः । विराटस्य महात्मानः परिक्लेशविनाशनाः ॥५२॥
33.52.en: Discomfitting Susharma and taking all his wealth-they, endued with the strength of their own arms, humble and observant of vows,

33.53.sa: स्थिताः समक्षं ते सर्वे त्वथ भीमोऽभ्यभाषत । नायं पापसमाचारो मत्तो जीवितुमर्हति । किं तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं यद्राजा सततं घृणी ॥५३॥
33.53.en: This perpetrator of impious deeds does not deserve living at my hands. But what can I do, the king is always merciful.

33.54.sa: गले गृहीत्वा राजानमानीय विवशं वशम् । तत एनं विचेष्टन्तं बध्वा पार्थो वृकोदरः ॥५४॥
33.54.en: Then holding the king (Susharma) by the neck who was unconscious, bringing him and binding him who could make no exertion, Vrikodara, the son of Pritha,

33.56.en: Placed him on the chariot who was insensible and covered with dust. Then approaching Yudhishthira who was in the midst of the battle field,

33.57.sa: दर्शयामास भीमस्तु सुशर्माणं नराधिपम् । प्रोवाच पुरुषव्याघ्रो भीममाहवशोभिनम् ॥५७॥
33.57.en: Bhima showed to him the king Susharma. The foremost of men then said to Bhima. beautifying the battle field.

33.58.sa: तं राजा प्राहसत् दृष्ट्वा मुच्यतां वै नराधमः । एवमुक्तोऽब्रवीद्भीमः सुशर्माणं महाबलम् ॥५८॥
33.58.en: Then seeing him the king smilingly said: “Release this wretch." Thus addressed Bhima said to the highly powerful Susharma.

33.59.sa: भीम उवाच । जीवितुं चेच्छसे मूढ हेतुं मे गदतः शृणु । दासोऽस्मीति त्वया वाच्यं संसत्सु च सभासु च ॥५९॥
33.59.en: “If you wish to live, O wretch, hear my words. You should say in courts and assemblies that you are our slave.

33.60.sa: एवं ते जीवितं दद्यामेष युद्धजितो विधिः । तमुवाच ततो ज्येष्ठो भ्राता सप्रणयं वचः ॥६०॥
33.60.en: Under this condition I can grant you your life: such is the custom of the victorious." Then his eldest brother addressed to him affectionate words.

33.61.sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच । मुञ्च मुञ्चाधमाचारं प्रमाणं यदि ते वयम् । दासभावं गतो ह्येष विराटस्य महीपतेः । अदासो गच्छ मुक्तोऽसि मैवं कार्षीः कदाचन ॥६१॥
33.61.en: "If you regard me, release this wicked wretch. He has already become the slave of the great king Virata. (Then he said to Susharma): “You are free, go and never do such a thing."

34.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्ते तु सव्रीडः सुशर्माऽऽसीद‌धोमुखः । स मुक्तोऽभ्येत्य राजानमभिवाद्य प्रतस्थिवान् ॥१॥
34.1.en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed Susharma was filled with shame and bent down his head. And liberated and bowing to the king he went away.

34.2.sa: विसृज्य तु सुशर्माणं पाण्डवास्ते हतद्विषः । स्वबाहुबलसंपन्ना हीनिषेवा यतव्रताः । संग्रामशिरसो मध्ये तां रात्रिं सुखिनोऽवसन् ॥२॥

34.3.sa: ततो विराटः कौन्तेयानतिमानुषविक्रमान् । अर्चयामास वित्तेन मानेन च महारथान् ॥३॥
34.3.en: Having released Susharma, the Pandavas, then enemies slain, endowed with the strength of arms, observant of vows, and modest, passed that night happily in the midst of the battle-field. Then Virata honoured, with wealth and respect, those mighty car-warriors, the of Kunti, who were gifted with superhuman prowess.

34.4.sa: विराट उवाच । यथैव मम रत्नानि युष्माकं तानि वै तथा । कार्यं कुरुत वै सर्वे यथाकामं यथासुखम् ॥४॥
34.4.en: sons Virata said All these my jewels are as much mine as yours; do you all work as you like and as may conduce to your happiness.

34.5.sa: ददाम्यलङ्कृताः कन्या वसूनि विविधानि च । मनसश्चाप्यभिप्रेतं युद्धे शत्रुनिबर्हणाः ॥५॥
34.5.en: O repressors of foes in battle, I shall center upon you women adorned with ornaments, plentiful riches and other things that you may like.

34.6.sa: युष्माकं विक्रमादद्य मुक्तोऽहं स्वस्तिमानिह । तस्माद्भवन्तो मत्स्यानामीश्वराः सर्व एव हि ॥६॥
34.6.en: By your prowess today I have been saved from peril. I am now crowned with victory. Do you all become the kings of Matsya's.

34.7.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तथेतिवादिनं मत्स्यं कौरवेयाः पृथक् पृथक् । ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे युधिष्ठिरपुरागमाः ॥७॥
34.7.en: Vaishampayana said Those Kauravas, headed by Yudhishthira, with folded heads, said each severally to the king of the Matsya who had addressed them thus.

34.8.sa: प्रतिनन्दाम ते वाक्यं सर्वं चैव विशाम्पते । एतेनैव प्रतीताः स्म यत्त्वं मुक्तोऽद्य शत्रुभिः ॥८॥
34.8.en: O king, we have been perfectly pleased with what you have said. It is a matter of gratification to us that you have been released from the enemies.

34.9.sa: ततोऽब्रवीत् प्रतिमना मत्स्यराजो युधिष्ठिरम् । पुनरेव महाबाहुर्विराटो राजसत्तमः ॥९॥
34.9.en: Then the mighty armed, Virata, the king of Matsya's, the foremost of monarchs, again delightedly said to Yudhishthira.

34.10.sa: एहि त्वामभिषेक्ष्यामि मत्स्यराजस्तु नो भवान् । मनसश्चाप्यभिप्रेतं यथेष्टं भुवि दुर्लभम् । तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रदास्यामि सर्वमर्हति नो भवान् ॥१०॥
34.10.en: Come, I shall install you and be the king of us, the Matsya's. Whatever you desire in mind, any thing, even though rare on earth,

34.11.sa: रत्नानि गाः सुवर्णं च मणिमुक्तमथापि च । वैयाघ्रपद्य विप्रेन्द्र सर्वथैव नमोऽस्तु ते ॥११॥

34.12.sa: त्वत्कृते ह्यद्य पश्यामि राज्यं सन्तानमेव च । यतश्च जातसंरम्भो न च शत्रुवशं गतः ॥१२॥
34.12.en: I bow to you, it is for you that once more today I see my kingdom and children.

34.13.sa: ततो युधिष्ठिरो मत्स्यं पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत । प्रतिनन्दामि ते वाक्यं मनोज्ञं मत्स्य भाषसे ॥१३॥

34.14.sa: आनृशंस्यपरो नित्यं सुसुखी सततं भव । गच्छन्तु दूतास्त्वरितं नगरं तव पार्थिव ॥१४॥

34.15.sa: सुहृदां प्रियमाख्यातुं घोषयन्तु च ते जयम् । ततस्तद्वचनान्मत्स्यो दूतान्राजा समादिशत् ॥१५॥
34.15.en: O king, let emissaries speedily go to your city, to communicate this pleasant tidings to your friends and announce your victory.

34.16.sa: आचक्षध्वं पुरं गत्वा संग्रामविजयं मम । कुमार्यः समलंकृत्य पर्यागच्छन्तु मे पुरात् ॥१६॥
34.16.en: At his words the king of Matsya's dispatched his emissaries, saying: “Going to my city do you announce my victory.

34.17.sa: वादित्राणि च सर्वाणि गणिकाश्च स्वलंकृताः । एतां चाज्ञां ततः श्रुत्वा राज्ञा मत्स्येन नोदिताः । तामाज्ञां शिरसा कृत्वा प्रस्थिता हृष्टमानसाः ॥१७॥
34.17.en: Hearing this his command and being thus addressed by the Matsya king, they, placing his command on their heads, delightedly went away.

34.18.sa: ते गत्वा तत्र तां रात्रिमथ सूर्योदयं प्रति । विराटस्य पुराभ्याशे दूता जयमघोषयन् ॥१८॥
34.18.en: Going to the city that very night they announced, at the hour of sun-rise, the victory of the king.

35.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । याते त्रिगर्तान्मत्स्ये तु पशूंस्तान्वै परीप्सति । दुर्योधनः सहामात्यो विराटमुपयादथ ॥१॥
35.1.en: Vaishampayana said After the king of Matsya's had gone out in pursuit of Trigartas for recovering his kine, Duryodhana, with his courtiers, attacked his kingdom.

35.2.sa: भीष्मो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च परमास्त्रवित् । द्रौणिश्च सौबलश्चैव तथा दुःशासनः प्रभो ॥२॥
35.2.en: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Kripa, versed in the use of the best of weapons, Ashvathama, Subala's son, Dushasana, O king, Vivinshati, Vikarana, the greatly energetic Chitrasena, Durmukha, Dushasana and many other highly powerful heroes, overtaking Matsya, speedily drove away his cow-herds and got possession of the king by force.

35.3.sa: विविंशतिर्विकर्णश्च चित्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान् । दुर्मुखो दुःशलश्चैव ये चैवान्ये महारथाः ॥३॥
35.3.en: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Kripa, versed in the use of the best of weapons, Ashvathama, Subala's son, Dushasana, O king, Vivinshati, Vikarana, the greatly energetic Chitrasena, Durmukha, Dushasana and many other highly powerful heroes, overtaking Matsya, speedily drove away his cow-herds and got possession of the king by force.

35.4.sa: एते मत्स्यानुपागम्य विराटस्य महीपतेः । घोषान् विद्राव्य तरसा गोधनं जह्रुरोजसा ॥४॥

35.5.sa: षष्टिं गवां सहस्राणि कुरवः कालयन्ति च । महता रथवंशेन परिवार्य समन्ततः ॥५॥
35.5.en: Encircling all sides with a huge array of cars, the Kauravas seized the sixty thousand kine.

35.6.sa: गोपालानां तु घोषस्य हन्यतां तैर्महारथैः । आरावः सुमहानासीत् संप्रहारे भयङ्करे ॥६॥
35.6.en: A great cry was set up in that dreadful combat by the cow-herds struck by those inighty car-warriors.

35.7.sa: गोपाध्यक्षो भयत्रस्तो रथमास्थाय सत्वरः । जगाम नगरायैव परिक्रोशंस्तदार्तवत् ॥७॥
35.7.en: Greatly stricken with grief the chief, of the cow-herds, quickly got upon a chariot and started for the city bewailing in affliction.

35.8.sa: स प्रविश्य पुरं राज्ञो नृपवेश्माभ्ययात् ततः । अवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णमाख्यातुं प्रविवेश ह ॥८॥
35.8.en: Entering the city of the king, he went to the palace and getting down from the car proceeded to relate (what took place).

35.9.sa: दृष्ट्वा भूमिञ्जयं नाम पुत्रं मत्स्यस्य मानिनम् । तस्मै तत् सर्वमाचष्ट राष्ट्रस्य पशुकर्षणम् ॥९॥
35.9.en: Seeing the haughty son of Matsya Bhuminjaya, he described to him everything about the royal kine being taken away.

35.10.sa: षष्टिं गवां सहस्त्राणि कुरवः कालयन्ति ते । तद्विजेतुं समुत्तिष्ठ गोधनं राष्ट्रवर्धन ॥१०॥
35.10.en: The Kauravas are taking away your sixty thousand kine; rise up, o increaser of territories, to bring them back.

35.11.sa: राजपुत्र हितप्रेप्सुः क्षिप्रं निर्याहि च स्वयम् । त्वां हि मत्स्यो महीपालः शून्यपालमिहाकरोत् ॥११॥
35.11.en: If you wish your well-being, speedily go out yourself, O prince. The emperor Matsya left you alone in the city.

35.12.sa: त्वया परिषदो मध्ये श्लाघते स नराधिपः । पुत्रो ममानुरूपश्च शूरश्चेति कुलोद्वहः ॥१२॥
35.12.en: The king speaks highly of you in the court: My son, after me, is heroic and the supporter (of the prestige) of the race.

35.13.sa: इष्वस्त्रे निपुणो योधः सदावीरश्च मे सुतः । तस्य तत्सत्यमेवास्तु मनुष्येन्द्रस्य भाषितम् ॥१३॥

35.14.sa: आवर्तय कुरून् जित्वा पशून् पशुमतां वर । निर्दहैषामनीकानि भीमेन शरतेजसा ॥१४॥
35.14.en: O you the foremost of those who own cattle, having discomfited the Kurus, do you bring back the animals, consume their soldiers with the dreadful prowess of your shafts,

35.15.sa: धनुश्च्युतै रुक्मपुङ्खैः शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः । द्विषतां भिन्ध्यनीकानि गजानामिव यूथपः ॥१५॥
35.15.en: Crush down the enemics' life, with straight shafts feathered in gold discharged off your bow like an elephant chief rushing at a herd.

35.16.sa: पाशोपधानां ज्यातन्त्रीं चापदण्यां महास्वनाम् । शरवर्णां धनुर्वीणां शत्रुमध्ये प्रवादय ॥१६॥

35.17.sa: श्वेता रजतसङ्काशा रथे युज्यन्तु ते हयाः । ध्वजं च सिंहं सौवर्णमुछ्रयन्तु तव प्रभो ॥१७॥
35.17.en: Let your horses, white as silver, be yoked to the cars and let your flag, having the emblem of a golden lion, he hoisted up, O lord.

35.18.sa: रुक्मपुङ्खाः प्रसन्नाग्रा मुक्ता हस्तवता त्वया । छादयन्तु शराः सूर्यं राज्ञां मार्गनिरोधकाः ॥१८॥

35.19.sa: रणे जित्वा कुरून् सर्वान् वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान्। यशो महदवाप्य त्वं प्रविशेदं पुरं पुनः ॥१९॥
35.19.en: Defeating all the Kurus in battle like the holder of Vajra the Asuras and acquiring great fame, return to your city.

35.20.sa: त्वं हि राष्ट्रस्य परमा गतिर्मत्स्यपतेः सुतः । यथा हि पाण्डुपुत्राणामर्जुनो जयतां वरः ॥२०॥
35.20.en: You are the greatest support of the kingdom, the son of Matsya king, like Arjuna, the foremost of the victors amongst the sons of Pandu.

35.21.sa: एवमेव गतिर्नूनं भवान् विषयवासिनाम् । गतिमन्तो वयं त्वद्य सर्वे विषयवासिनः ॥२१॥
35.21.en: Even like him you are forsooth the refuge of those who live in this country; we all look upon you as our protector.

35.22.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । स्त्रीमध्य उक्तस्तेनासौ तद्वाक्यमभयंकरम् । अन्तःपुरे श्लाघमान इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥२२॥
35.22.en: Vaishampayana said Being thus addressed by him in the midst of females with fearless words in the inner apartment he gave went to the following praiseworthy words.

36.1.sa: उत्तर उवाच । अद्याहमनुगच्छेयं दृढधन्वा गवां पदम् । यदि मे सारथिः कश्चिद्भवेदश्वेषु कोविदः ॥१॥
36.1.en: Uttara said An expert in the use of bow as I am, I shall today go out in pursuit of kine, if some body, skilled in the management of horses, becomes my charioteer.

36.2.sa: तं त्वहं नावगच्छामि यो मे यन्ता भवेन्नरः । पश्यध्वं सारथिं क्षिप्रं मम युक्तं प्रयास्यतः ॥२॥
36.2.en: I do not know of a man who may be iny charioteer; find out out therefore quickly a charioteer who may suit me who am going out.

36.3.sa: अष्टाविंशतिरात्रं वा मासं वा नूनमन्ततः । यत्तदासीन्महद्युद्धं तत्र मे सारथिर्हतः ॥३॥
36.3.en: My charioteer was killed in the great encounter that lasted for a month or at least twenty nights certain.

36.4.sa: स लभेयं यदा त्वन्यं हययानविदं नरम् । त्वरावानद्य यात्वाहं समुच्छ्रितमहाध्वजम् ॥४॥
36.4.en: As soon as I shall get a man experienced in the management of horses I shall immediately start hoisting the huge standard.

36.5.sa: विगाह्य तत्परानीकं गजवाजिरथाकुलम् । शस्त्रप्रतापनिर्वीर्यान् कुरून् जित्वाऽऽनये पशून् ॥५॥
36.5.en: Entering into the hostile army filled with elephants, horses and chariots and defeating the Kurus who are weak in power and weapons I shall bring back the animals.

36.6.sa: दुर्योधनं शान्तनवं कर्णं वैकर्तनं कृपम् । द्रोणं च सहपुत्रेण महेष्वासान् समागतान् ॥६॥
36.6.en: Having struck terror into Duryodhana, the son of Shantanu, (Bhishma) Vikartana's son (Kripa), Karna, Drona with his son and other powerful bowmen assembled there, like the wielder of thunderbolt afflicting the Danavas I shall this very moment bring back the kine.

36.7.sa: वित्रासयित्वा सङ्ग्रामे दानवानिव वज्रभृत् । अनेनैव मुहूर्तेन पुनः प्रत्यानये पशून् ॥७॥
36.7.en: Having struck terror into Duryodhana, the son of Shantanu, (Bhishma) Vikartana's son (Kripa), Karna, Drona with his son and other powerful bowmen assembled there, like the wielder of thunderbolt afflicting the Danavas I shall this very moment bring back the kine.

36.8.sa: शून्यमासाद्य कुरवः प्रयान्त्यादाय गोधनम् । किं तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं यदहं तत्र नाभवम् ॥८॥
36.8.en: Finding none the Kurus are taking away the precious kine; what can I do when I am not there?

36.9.sa: पश्येयुरद्य मे वीर्यं कुरवस्ते समागताः । किं नु पार्थोऽर्जुनः साक्षादयमस्मान् प्रबाधते ॥९॥
36.9.en: The assembled Kurus shall see today my prowess: (and they shall say). “Is it Arjuna's self who is contending us?”

36.10.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । श्रुत्वा तदर्जुनो वाक्यं राज्ञः पुत्रस्य भाषतः । अतीतसमये काले प्रियां भार्यामनिन्दिताम् ॥१०॥
36.10.en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words of the Prince, Arjuna, informed of all, after some time delightedly spoke in private to his beloved and faultless wife Krishna the princess of Panchala, the slender-made daughter of Drupada, born of sacrifice, gifted with the virtues of truthfulness and honesty and ever devoted to the well-being of her husband. "O auspicious lady, speak quickly to Uttara, at my request, that this (Brihannala) was formerly the firm and approved charioteer of Pandu's son (Arjuna); experienced in very many great battles he shall be your charioteer.”

36.11.sa: द्रुपदस्य सुतां तन्वीं पाञ्चालीं पावकात्मजाम् । सत्यार्जवगुणोपेतां भर्तुः प्रियहिते रताम् ॥११॥
36.11.en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words of the Prince, Arjuna, informed of all, after some time delightedly spoke in private to his beloved and faultless wife Krishna the princess of Panchala, the slender-made daughter of Drupada, born of sacrifice, gifted with the virtues of truthfulness and honesty and ever devoted to the well-being of her husband. "O auspicious lady, speak quickly to Uttara, at my request, that this (Brihannala) was formerly the firm and approved charioteer of Pandu's son (Arjuna); experienced in very many great battles he shall be your charioteer.”

36.12.sa: उवाच रहसि प्रीतः कृष्णां सर्वार्थकोविदः । उत्तरं ब्रूहि कल्याणि क्षिप्रं मद्वचनादिदम् ॥१२॥
36.12.en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words of the Prince, Arjuna, informed of all, after some time delightedly spoke in private to his beloved and faultless wife Krishna the princess of Panchala, the slender-made daughter of Drupada, born of sacrifice, gifted with the virtues of truthfulness and honesty and ever devoted to the well-being of her husband. "O auspicious lady, speak quickly to Uttara, at my request, that this (Brihannala) was formerly the firm and approved charioteer of Pandu's son (Arjuna); experienced in very many great battles he shall be your charioteer.”

36.13.sa: अयं वै पाण्डवस्यासीत् सारथिः संमतो दृढः । महायुद्धेषु संसिद्धः स ते यन्ता भविष्यति ॥१३॥
36.13.en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words of the Prince, Arjuna, informed of all, after some time delightedly spoke in private to his beloved and faultless wife Krishna the princess of Panchala, the slender-made daughter of Drupada, born of sacrifice, gifted with the virtues of truthfulness and honesty and ever devoted to the well-being of her husband. "O auspicious lady, speak quickly to Uttara, at my request, that this (Brihannala) was formerly the firm and approved charioteer of Pandu's son (Arjuna); experienced in very many great battles he shall be your charioteer.”

36.14.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तस्य तद्वचनं स्त्रीषु भाषतश्च पुनः पुनः । न साऽमर्षत पाञ्चाली बीभत्सोः परिकीर्तनम् ॥१४॥
36.14.en: Hearing him speak again and again thus to women Panchali could not bear his reference to Arjuna.

36.15.sa: अथैनमुपसंगम्य स्त्रीमध्यात् सा तपस्विनी । व्रीडमानेव शनकैरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥१५॥
36.15.en: Then stepping out from the midst of the women, the poor (princess) bashfully and gently gave vent to the following words.

36.16.sa: योऽसौ बृहद्वारणाभो युवा सुप्रियदर्शनः । बृहन्नलेति विख्यातः पार्थस्यासीत् स सारथिः॥१६॥
36.16.en: "This greatly beautiful youth resembling a huge elephant and known under the name Brihannala was the charioteer of Partha.

36.17.sa: धनुष्यनवरश्चासीत् तस्य शिष्यो महात्मनः। दृष्टपूर्वो मया वीर चरन्त्या पाण्डवान् प्रति ॥१७॥
36.17.en: A mighty bowman he was the disciple of the high-souled (Arjuna); O hero, I saw him before while I was living with the Pandavas.

36.18.sa: यदा तत्पावको दावमदहत् खाण्डवं महत् । अर्जुनस्य तदाऽनेन संगृहीता हयोत्तमाः ॥१८॥
36.18.en: While the fire consumed the forest of Khandava it was he who governed the excellent steeds of Arjuna.

36.19.sa: तेन सारथिना पार्थः सर्वभूतानि सर्वशः । अजयत् खाण्डवप्रस्थेन हि यन्ताऽस्ति तादृशः ॥१९॥
36.19.en: Having him as his charioteer Partha vanquished all creatures at Khandavaprastha; indeed there is no charioteer like him.

36.20.sa: उत्तर उवाच । सैरन्ध्रि जानासि तथा युवानं नपुंसको नैव भवेद्यथाऽसौ । अहं न शक्नोमि बृहन्नलां शुभे वक्तुं स्वयं यच्छ हयान् ममेति वै ॥२०॥
36.20.en: Uttara said You know this youth, O Sairandhri whether he is of neuter sex or otherwise; O fair lady, I shall not be able myself to request him to govern my horses.

36.21.sa: द्रौपद्युवाच । येयं कुमारी सुश्रोणी भगिनी ते यवीयसी । अस्याः सा वीर वचनं करिष्यति न संशयः ॥२१॥

36.22.sa: यदि वै सारथिः स स्यात् कुरून् सर्वान्न संशयः। जित्वा गाश्च समादाय ध्रुवमागमनं भवेत् ॥२२॥
36.22.en: If he becomes your charioteer, you will undoubtedly come back with kine having vanquished the Kurus.

36.23.sa: एवमुक्तः स सैरन्ध्र्या भगिनीं प्रत्यभाषत । गच्छ त्वमनवद्याङ्गि तामानय बृहन्नलाम् ॥२३॥

36.24.sa: सा भ्रात्रा प्रेषिता शीघ्रमगच्छन्नर्तनागृहम् । यत्रास्ते स महाबाहुश्छन्नः सत्रेण पाण्डवः ॥२४॥
36.24.en: Sent by her brother she quickly went to the dancing hall where that mighty-armed son of Pandu was waiting in disguise.

37.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । सा प्राद्रवत्काञ्चनमाल्यधारिणी ज्येष्ठेन भ्रात्रा प्रहिता यशस्विनी । सुदक्षिणा वेदिविलग्नमध्या सा पद्मपत्राभनिभा शिखण्डिनी ॥१॥
37.1.en: Vaishampayana said Dispatched by her elder brother, the illustrious daughter of the king of Matsya's, wearing a golden necklace, ever obedient, having a waist slender like that of a wasp, beautiful like Lakshmi, adorned with the plumes of a peacock, of a slender make, beautiful limbs, wearing a zone of pearls, graceful, having slightly curved eye-lashes, speedily went to the dancing-hall like a flash of lightning towards of clouds.

37.2.sa: तन्वी शुभाङ्गी मणिचित्रमेखला मत्स्यस्य राज्ञो दुहिता श्रिया वृता । तन्नर्तनागारमरालपक्ष्मा शतह्रदा मेघमिवान्वपद्यत ॥२॥
37.2.en: Vaishampayana said Dispatched by her elder brother, the illustrious daughter of the king of Matsya's, wearing a golden necklace, ever obedient, having a waist slender like that of a wasp, beautiful like Lakshmi, adorned with the plumes of a peacock, of a slender make, beautiful limbs, wearing a zone of pearls, graceful, having slightly curved eye-lashes, speedily went to the dancing-hall like a flash of lightning towards of clouds.

37.3.sa: सा हस्तिहस्तोपमसंहितोरूः स्वनिन्दिता चारुदती सुमध्यमा । आसाद्य तं वै वरमाल्यधारिणी पार्थं शुभा नागवधूरिव द्विपम् ॥३॥
