49.4.en: It is by favourable signs that the advisability of an action is determined upon. Learned men never act depending upon the words of a car maker. Taking all this into consideration it is not proper for us to enter into an encounter with Partha.

49.5.sa: पारिचिन्त्य तु पार्थेन संनिपातो न नः क्षमः । एकः कुरूनभ्यगच्छदेकश्चाग्निमतपर्यत् ॥५॥

49.6.sa: एकश्च पञ्च वर्षाणि ब्रह्मचर्यमधारयत् । एकः सुभद्रामारोप्य द्वैरथे कृष्णमाह्वयत् ॥६॥

49.7.sa: एकः किरातरूपेण स्थितं रुद्रमयोधयत् । अस्मिन्नेव वने पार्थो हृतां कृष्णामवाजयत् ॥७॥
49.7.en: Taking Subhadra on his car alone did he challenge Krishna to a duel. And alone did he fight with Rudra who came before him in the disguise of a hunter.

49.8.sa: एकश्च पञ्च वर्षाणि शक्रादस्त्राण्यशिक्षत । एकः सोऽयमरिं जित्वा कुरूणामकरोद्दशः ॥८॥

49.9.sa: एको गन्धर्वराजानं चित्रसेनमरिन्दमः । विजिग्ये तरसा सङ्ख्ये सेनां प्राप्य सुदुर्जयाम् ॥९॥
49.9.en: Defeating alone all the enemies he has spread the glory of the Kurus. Alone did that chastiser of foes defeat in battle Chitrasena, the king of the Gandharvas and in a moment his invincible army also. He defeated alone in battle the dreadful Nivatakavachas and Kalakhanjas who were both incapable of being slain even by the celestials. What however, O Karna, have you accomplished single-handed like any one of the sons of Pandu each of whom had vanquished many kings? Even Indra is unable to face Partha in battle.

49.10.sa: तथा निवातकवचाः कालखञ्जाश्च दानवाः । दैवतैरप्यवध्यास्ते एकेन युधि पातिताः ॥१०॥

49.11.sa: एकेन हि त्वया कर्ण किं नामेह कृतं पुरा । एकैकेन यथा तेषां भूमिपाला वशे कृताः ॥११॥
49.11.en: Defeating alone all the enemies he has spread the glory of the Kurus. Alone did that chastiser of foes defeat in battle Chitrasena, the king of the Gandharvas and in a moment his invincible army also. He defeated alone in battle the dreadful Nivatakavachas and Kalakhanjas who were both incapable of being slain even by the celestials. What however, O Karna, have you accomplished single-handed like any one of the sons of Pandu each of whom had vanquished many kings? Even Indra is unable to face Partha in battle.

49.12.sa: इन्द्रोऽपि हि न पार्थेन संयुगे योद्धुमर्हति । यस्तेनाशंसते योद्धुं कर्तव्यं तस्य भेषजम् ॥१२॥

49.13.sa: आशीविषस्य क्रुद्धस्य पाणिमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम् । अवमुच्य प्रदेशिन्या दंष्ट्रामादातुमिच्छसि ॥१३॥
49.13.en: He who wishes to fight with Arjuna should take some medicine. You desire to take out the fangs of an angry, venomous snake by stretching out your right hand and extending your fore-finger. Or going alone in the forest you wish to ride an infuriated elephant and go to a town without a hook in hand. Or rubbed over with clarified butter and clad in silken raiment you wish to go through a burning fire blazing with fat, tallow and clarified butter.

49.14.sa: अथवा कुञ्जरं मत्तमेक एव चरन् वने । अनङ्कुशं समारुह्य नगरं गन्तुमिच्छसि ॥१४॥
49.14.en: He who wishes to fight with Arjuna should take some medicine. You desire to take out the fangs of an angry, venomous snake by stretching out your right hand and extending your fore-finger. Or going alone in the forest you wish to ride an infuriated elephant and go to a town without a hook in hand. Or rubbed over with clarified butter and clad in silken raiment you wish to go through a burning fire blazing with fat, tallow and clarified butter.

49.15.sa: समिद्धं पावकं चैव घृतमेदोवसाहुतम् । घृताक्तश्चीरवासास्त्वं मध्येनोत्सर्तुमिच्छसि ॥१५॥
49.15.en: He who wishes to fight with Arjuna should take some medicine. You desire to take out the fangs of an angry, venomous snake by stretching out your right hand and extending your fore-finger. Or going alone in the forest you wish to ride an infuriated elephant and go to a town without a hook in hand. Or rubbed over with clarified butter and clad in silken raiment you wish to go through a burning fire blazing with fat, tallow and clarified butter.

49.16.sa: आत्मानं कः समुद्वध्य कण्ठे बध्वा महाशिलाम् । समुद्रं तरते दोर्भ्यां तत्र किं नाम पौरुषम् ॥१६॥

49.17.sa: अकृतास्त्रः कृतास्त्रं वै बलवन्तं सुदुर्बलः । तादृशं कर्ण यः पार्थं योद्धुमिच्छेत् स दुर्मतिः ॥१७॥
49.17.en: Who, binding himself hand and foot and tying a huge stone to his neck, would wish to swim across the ocean with his bare arms? What manliness is there? O Karna, a fool is he, who, without strength and skill in arms, desires to fight with Partha who is so powerful and skilled in weapons? Oppressed by us and freed from thirteen years' exile, will he not destroy us like a lion liberated from the noose? Having unknowingly come to a place where Partha lay hidden like fire we have been exposed to a great danger. Although dreadful in battle we should fight against him.

49.18.sa: अस्माभिर्ह्येष निकृतो वर्षाणीह त्रयोदश । सिंहः पाशविनिर्मुक्तो न नः शेषं करिष्यति ॥१८॥
49.18.en: Who, binding himself hand and foot and tying a huge stone to his neck, would wish to swim across the ocean with his bare arms? What manliness is there? O Karna, a fool is he, who, without strength and skill in arms, desires to fight with Partha who is so powerful and skilled in weapons? Oppressed by us and freed from thirteen years' exile, will he not destroy us like a lion liberated from the noose? Having unknowingly come to a place where Partha lay hidden like fire we have been exposed to a great danger. Although dreadful in battle we should fight against him.

49.19.sa: एकान्ते पार्थमासीनं कूपेऽग्निमिव संवृतम् । अज्ञानादभ्यवस्कन्द्य प्राप्ताः स्मो भयमुत्तमम् ॥१९॥

49.20.sa: सह युध्यामहे पार्थमागतं युद्धदुर्मदम् । सैन्यास्तिष्ठन्तु संनद्धा व्यूढानीकाः प्रहारिणः ॥२०॥

49.21.sa: द्रोणो दुर्योधनो भीष्मो भवान् द्रौणिस्तथा वयम् । सर्वे युध्यामहे पार्थं कर्ण मा साहसं कृथाः ॥२१॥
49.21.en: Let our army, clad in coats of mail, stand here in battle array ready to strike. Let Drona, Duryodhana, Bhishma, yourself, Drona's son and ourselves all fight with Partha. Do not, O Karna, act rashly. If we six are united and set forth our energy we may fight with or stand before Partha, fierce like the wielder of thunderbolt. With our soldiers in battle array, we, great bowmen as we are, will fight carefully with Arjuna as the Danavas fought with Vasava.

49.22.sa: वयं व्यवसितं पार्थं वज्रपाणिमिवोद्धतम् । षड्रथाः प्रतियुध्येम तिष्ठेम यदि संहताः ॥२२॥
49.22.en: Let our army, clad in coats of mail, stand here in battle array ready to strike. Let Drona, Duryodhana, Bhishma, yourself, Drona's son and ourselves all fight with Partha. Do not, O Karna, act rashly. If we six are united and set forth our energy we may fight with or stand before Partha, fierce like the wielder of thunderbolt. With our soldiers in battle array, we, great bowmen as we are, will fight carefully with Arjuna as the Danavas fought with Vasava.

49.23.sa: व्यूढानीकानि सैन्यानि यत्ताः परमधन्विनः । युध्यामहेऽर्जुन संख्ये दानवा इव वासवम् ॥२३॥
49.23.en: Let our army, clad in coats of mail, stand here in battle array ready to strike. Let Drona, Duryodhana, Bhishma, yourself, Drona's son and ourselves all fight with Partha. Do not, O Karna, act rashly. If we six are united and set forth our energy we may fight with or stand before Partha, fierce like the wielder of thunderbolt. With our soldiers in battle array, we, great bowmen as we are, will fight carefully with Arjuna as the Danavas fought with Vasava.

50.1.sa: अश्वत्थामोवाच । न च तावज्जिता गावो न च सीमान्तरं गताः । न हास्तिनपुरं प्राप्तास्त्वं च कर्ण विकत्थसे ॥१॥
50.1.en: Ashvathama said The kine have not yet been acquired. Nor have they gone over the boundary. Nor have they gone to Hastinapur. Why do you, Karna, boast?

50.2.sa: सङ्ग्रामांश्च बहूञ्जित्वा लब्ध्वा च विपुलं धनम् । विजित्य च परां सेनां नाहुः किंचन पौरुषम् ॥२॥
50.2.en: Even having won many a battle, amassed a vast fortune, vanquished their enemies, armies, truly heroic men do not utter a single word of their prowess.

50.3.sa: दहत्यग्निरवाक्यस्तु तूष्णीं भाति दिवाकरः । तूष्णीं धारयते लोकान् वसुधा सचराचरान् ॥३॥
50.3.en: Fire burns silently and silently does the sun shine. And the earth does bear creatures mobile and immobile without a single word.

50.4.sa: चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य कर्माणि विहितानि स्वयंभुवा । धनं यैरधिगन्तव्यं यच्च कुर्वन्न दुष्यति ॥४॥
50.4.en: The actions of the four orders have been ordained by the Self Sprung (Brahma) so that they may acquire wealth without committing a sinful act.

50.5.sa: अधीत्य ब्राह्मणो वेदान् याजयेत यजेत वा । क्षत्रियो धनुराश्रित्य यजेच्चैव न याजयेत् ॥५॥
50.5.en: Having studied the Vedas, the Brahmanas should perform sacrifices and officiate as priests. Resorting to their vows the Kshatriyas should perform sacrifices and never officiate as priests.

50.6.sa: वैश्योऽधिगम्य वित्तानि ब्रह्मकर्माणि कारयेत् । शूद्रः शुश्रूषणं कुर्यास्त्रिषु वर्णेषु नित्यशः । वन्दनायोगविधिभिर्वैतसीं वृत्तिमास्थितः ॥६॥
50.6.en: Having amassed wealth the Vaishyas should perform the Vedic rites there with. A Shudra should always attend to and serve the other three orders, having recourse to flattery as the means of livelihood and behaving (cringlingly) like the cane.

50.7.sa: वर्तमाना यथाशास्त्रं प्राप्य चापि महीमिमाम् । सत्कुर्वन्ति महाभागा गुरून् सुविगुणानपि ॥७॥
50.7.en: Duly following the the scriptures they obtained this entire earth and those great men always act respectfully to their elders even if the latter prove adverse to them,

50.8.sa: प्राप्य द्यूतेन को राज्यं क्षत्रियस्तोष्टुमर्हति । तथा नृशंसरूपोऽयं धार्तराष्ट्रश्च निर्घृणः ॥८॥
50.8.en: What Kshatriya on this earth expresses joy for having acquired a kingdom by gambling like this wicked and shameless son of Dhritarashtra?

50.9.sa: तथाऽधिगम्य वित्तानि को विकत्थेद्विचक्षणः । निकृत्या वञ्चनायोगैश्चरन् वैतंसिको यथा ॥९॥
50.9.en: Having acquired riches in this way by deceit and fraud like a seller of meat what wise man would boast of it?

50.10.sa: कतमं द्वैरथं युद्धं यत्राजैषीर्धनञ्जयम् । नकुलं सहदेवं वा धनं येषां त्वया हृतम् ॥१०॥

50.11.sa: युधिष्ठिरो जितः कस्मिन् भीमश्च बलिनां वरः । इन्द्रप्रस्थं त्वया कस्मिन् सङ्ग्रामे निर्जितं पुरा ॥११॥
50.11.en: Has Yudhishthira, or Bhima the foremost of the strong, been defeated by you? In what battle was Indraprastha conquered by you?

50.12.sa: तथैव कतमद्युद्धं यस्मिन् कृष्णा जिता त्वया । एकवस्त्रा सभां नीता दुष्टकर्मन् रजस्वला ॥१२॥
50.12.en: By what battle did you win Krishna, that, O you of wicked deeds, you did drag her to the assembly when she was in her course and had one cloth on?

50.13.sa: मूलमेषां महत्कृत्तं सारार्थी चन्दनं यथा । कर्म कारयिथाः सूत तत्र किं विदुरोऽब्रवीत् ॥१३॥
50.13.en: You have cut the great root of the Sala tree. Actuated by greed when you made them work as slaves what did Vidura say?

50.14.sa: यथाशक्ति मनुष्याणां शममालक्षयामहे । अन्येषामपि सत्त्वानामपि कीटपिपीलिकैः । द्रौपद्याः संपरिक्लेशं न क्षन्तुं पाण्डवोऽर्हति ॥१४॥
50.14.en: Men and others, even insects and ants show forgiveness as much as lies in their power.

50.15.sa: क्षयाय धार्तराष्ट्राणां प्रादुर्भूतो धनञ्जयः । त्वं पुनः पण्डितो भूत्वा वाचं वक्तुमिहेच्छसि ॥१५॥
50.15.en: The Pandava can never forgive your distressing Draupadi. Dhananjaya is born for the destruction of Dhritarashtra's sons.

50.16.en: Appearing as a learned man you are making speeches, but will not Bibhatsu, the slayer of enemies, exterminate us all?

50.17.sa: नैष देवान् न गन्धर्वान् न सुरान् न च राक्षसान् । भयादिह न युध्येत कुन्तीपुत्रो धनञ्जयः ॥१७॥
50.17.en: Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, never from fear, withdraws himself from fighting even if it be with the Gandharvas, Asuras or Rakshasas.

50.18.sa: यं यमेषोऽतिसंक्रुद्धः सङ्ग्रामे निपतिष्यति । वृक्षं गरुत्मान् वेगेन विनिहत्य तमेष्यति ॥१८॥
50.18.en: On whom he will fall enraged in battle he will over-throw him like a tree by the velocity of Garuda.

50.19.sa: त्वत्तो विशिष्टं वीर्येण धनुष्यमरराट्समम् । वासुदेवसमं युद्धे तं पार्थं को न पूजयेत् ॥१९॥
50.19.en: Who will not praise Partha, who is superior to yourself in prowess, equal to the king of the gods in bowmanship and equal to Vasudeva himself in battle?

50.20.sa: देवं देवेन युध्येत मानुषेण च मानुषम् । अस्त्रं ह्यस्त्रेण यो हन्यात् कोऽर्जुनेन समः पुमान् ॥२०॥
50.20.en: What man is equal to Arjuna who counteracts the celestials weapons with celestials and human weapons with human?

50.21.sa: पुत्रादनन्तरं शिष्य इति धर्मविदो विदुः । एतेनापि निमित्तेन प्रियो द्रोणस्य पाण्डवः ॥२१॥
50.21.en: Persons conversant with virtue say that a disciple is not different from a son. It is for this reason Arjuna is favourite with Drona.

50.22.sa: यथा त्वमकरोर्द्यूतमिन्द्रप्रस्थं यथाऽहरः । यथाऽऽनैषीः सभां कृष्णां तथा युध्यस्व पाण्डवम् ॥२२॥
50.22.en: Do you fight with the Pandavas in the same way by which you defeated them at dice, by which you conquered Indraprastha and dragged Krishna to the assembly hall.

50.23.sa: अयं ते मातुलः प्राज्ञः क्षत्रधर्मस्य कोविदः । दुर्द्यूतदेवी गान्धारः शकुनिर्युध्यतामिह ॥२३॥

50.24.sa: नाक्षान् क्षिपति गाण्डीवं न कृतं द्वापरं न च । ज्वलतो निशितान्बाणांस्तांस्तांन्क्षिपति गाण्डिवम् ॥२४॥
50.24.en: The Gandiva (bow) does not cast dice such as, the Krita or Dwapara but it discharges burning and sharpened arrows.

50.25.sa: न हि गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्ता गार्ध्रपक्षाः सुतेजनाः । नान्तरेष्ववतिष्ठन्ते गिरीणामपि दारणाः ॥२५॥
50.25.en: The dreadful arrows, shot from Gandiva of great might and winged like vultures, can rend even the mountains.

50.26.sa: युध्यन्तां कामतो योधा नाहं योत्स्ये धनञ्जयम् । मत्स्यो ह्यस्माभिरायोध्यो यद्यागच्छेद्गवां पदम् ॥२६॥

50.27.sa: यथा सभायां द्यूतं त्वं मातुलेन सहाकरोः । तथा युध्यस्व सङ्ग्रामे सौबलेन सुरक्षितः ॥२७॥
50.27.en: As backed by your uncle you played at dice in the assembly hall so do you now fight well-protected by Subala's son?

51.1.sa: भीष्म उवाच । साधु पश्यति वै द्रौणिः कृपः साध्वनुपश्यति । कर्णस्तु क्षत्रधर्मेण केवलं योद्धमिच्छति ॥१॥
51.1.en: Bhishma said Drona's son observes well. Kripa observes well. Only for the observance of Kshatriya duties Karna wishes to fight.

51.2.sa: आचार्यो नाभिवक्तव्यः पुरुषेण विजानता । देशकालौ तु संप्रेक्ष्य योद्धव्यमिति मे मतिः ॥२॥

51.3.sa: यस्य सूर्यसमाः पञ्च सपत्नाः स्युः प्रहारिणः । कथमभ्युदये तेषां न प्रमुह्येत पण्डितः ॥३॥
51.3.en: Why should not a wise man be bewildered who has five adversaries effulgent as the sun, who are experts in smiting and have just come out from adversity?

51.4.sa: स्वार्थे सर्वे विमुह्यन्ति येऽपि धर्मविदो जनाः । तस्माद्राजन् ब्रवीम्येष वाक्यं ते यदि रोचते ॥४॥
51.4.en: Even persons, conversant with morality, are bewildered in their own interests. It is for this I tell you, O king, whether my words be acceptable to you or not.

51.5.sa: कर्णो हि यदवोचत् त्वां तेजः संजननाय तत् । आचार्यपुत्रः क्षमतां महत् कार्यमुपस्थितम् ॥५॥
51.5.en: What Karna said to you was for inciting our energy. The preceptor's son should forgive us for a very important business is present.

51.6.sa: नायं कालो विरोधस्य कौन्तेये समुपस्थिते । क्षन्तव्यं भवता सर्वमाचार्येण कृपेण च ॥६॥
51.6.en: When the son of Kunti has come it is not the time for dissension. Yourself and the preceptor and Kripa should forgive everything

51.7.sa: भवतां हि कृतास्त्रत्वं यथाऽऽदित्ये प्रभा तथा । यथा चन्द्रमसो लक्ष्मीः सर्वथा नापकृष्यते ॥७॥
51.7.en: The mastery of weapons is in you as the rays are in the sun. As Lakshmi is never separated from the moon, so the Vedas and the Brahma weapons are always established in you. It is seen that the four Vedas exist in one place and all the attributes of a Kshatriya exist in another place.

51.8.sa: एवं भवत्सु ब्राह्मण्यं ब्रह्मास्त्रं च प्रतिष्ठितम् । चत्वार एकतो वेदाः क्षात्रमेकत्र दृश्यते ॥८॥
51.8.en: The mastery of weapons is in you as the rays are in the sun. As Lakshmi is never separated from the moon, so the Vedas and the Brahma weapons are always established in you. It is seen that the four Vedas exist in one place and all the attributes of a Kshatriya exist in another place.

51.9.sa: नैतत् समस्तमुभयं कस्मिंश्चिदनुशुश्रुम । अन्यत्र भारताचार्यात् सपुत्रादिति मे मतिः ॥९॥
51.9.en: We have never heard of these two living together in any man than in the preceptor of the Bharata's race and his son. This is my conviction.

51.10.sa: वेदान्ताश्च पुराणानि इतिहासं पुरातनम् । जामदग्न्यमृते राजन् को द्रोणादधिको भवेत् ॥१०॥
51.10.en: In Vedantas, in Puranas and in Itihasas, who, O king except Jamadagni, is superior to Drona?

51.11.sa: ब्रह्मास्त्रं चैव वेदाश्च नैतदन्यत्र दृश्यते । आचार्यपुत्रः क्षमतां नायं कालो विभेदने ॥११॥
51.11.en: The (mastery) of Brahma weapons and (the knowledge of) the Vedas combined are not seen in any other person than that best of men, the preceptor of Bharatas. The preceptor's son should forgive us. This is not the time for disunion. Let us all united fight with the son of the chastiser of Paka (Arjuna) who has come here.

51.12.sa: बलस्य व्यसनानीह यान्युक्तानि मनीषिभिः । मुख्यो भेदो हि तेषां तु पापिष्ठो विदुषां मतः ॥१३॥
51.12.en: The (mastery) of Brahma weapons and (the knowledge of) the Vedas combined are not seen in any other person than that best of men, the preceptor of Bharatas. The preceptor's son should forgive us. This is not the time for disunion. Let us all united fight with the son of the chastiser of Paka (Arjuna) who has come here.

51.14.sa: अश्वत्थामोवाच । नैव न्याय्यमिदं वाच्यमस्माकं पुरुषर्षभ । किं तु रोषपरीतेन गुरुणा भाषिता गुणाः ॥१४॥
51.14.en: Ashvatthama said O foremost of men, the words that you have spoken to us are all just. The preceptor, filled with anger, has dilated upon his (Arjuna's) accomplishments.

51.15.sa: शत्रोरपि गुणा ग्राह्या दोषा वाच्या गुरोरपि । सर्वथा सर्वयत्नेन पुत्रे शिष्ये हितं वदेत् ॥१५॥
51.15.en: The accomplishments even of the enemies should be mentioned and the defect of a preceptor should be pointed out. Therefore, one should, to the best of his power, describe the merit of his son or disciple.

51.16.sa: दुर्योधन उवाच । आचार्य एष क्षमतां शान्तिरत्र विधीयताम् । अभिद्यमाने तु गुरौ तद्वृत्तं रोषकारितम् ॥१६॥
51.16.en: Duryodhana said May the preceptor forgive us and establish peace. If the preceptor is not alienated everything would be done.

51.17.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततो दुर्योधनो द्रोणं क्षमयामास भारत । सह कर्णेन भीष्मेण कृपेण च महात्मना ॥१७॥

51.18.sa: द्रोण उवाच । यदेतत् प्रथमं वाक्यं भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत् । तेनैवाहं प्रसन्नो वै नीतिरत्र विधीयताम् ॥१८॥
51.18.en: Drona said I have already been pleased by the words, which Bhishma, the son of Shantanu at first gave vent to. Such a procedure should now be resorted to that the son of Pritha may not approach Duryodhana in the encounter and the latter may not pass into the hands of the enemies,

51.19.sa: यथा दुर्योधनं पार्थो नोपसर्पति सङ्गरे । साहसाद्यदि वा मोहात् तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् ॥१९॥

51.20.sa: वनवासे ह्यनिर्वृत्ते दर्शयेन्न धनञ्जयः । धनं चालभमानोऽत्र नाद्य तत् क्षन्तुमर्हति ॥२०॥

51.21.sa: यथा नायं समायुञ्ज्याद्धार्तराष्ट्रान् कथञ्चन । न च सेना पराजय्यात् तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम्॥२१॥
51.21.en: By (merely) recovering the kine he will not forgive us. let therefore such a procedure be adopted that he can, by no means, vanquish the sons of Dhritarashtra and defeat our army. Similarly did Duryodhana speak before. Remembering all this, O Bhishma, tell us what you think proper.

51.22.sa: उक्तं दुर्योधनेनापि पुरस्ताद्वाक्यमीदृशम् । तदनुस्मृत्य गाङ्गेय यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥२२॥
51.22.en: By (merely) recovering the kine he will not forgive us. let therefore such a procedure be adopted that he can, by no means, vanquish the sons of Dhritarashtra and defeat our army. Similarly did Duryodhana speak before. Remembering all this, O Bhishma, tell us what you think proper.

52.1.sa: भीष्म उवाच । कलाः काष्ठाश्च युज्यन्ते मुहूर्ताश्च दिनानि च । अर्धमासाश्च मासाश्च नक्षत्राणि ग्रहास्तथा ॥१॥
52.1.en: Bhishma said The wheel of time revolves with various divisions such as Kalas, Kashthas, Muhurtas, days, fortnights months, stars, planets, seasons and years.

52.2.sa: ऋतवश्चापि युज्यन्ते तथा संवत्सरा अपि । एवं कालविभागेन कालचक्रं प्रवर्तते ॥२॥

52.3.sa: तेषां कालातिरेकेण ज्योतिषां च व्यतिक्रमात् । पञ्चमे पञ्चमे वर्षे द्वौ मासावुपजायतः ॥३॥
52.3.en: On account of the excess of time and the constellations going on their courses there is an increase of two months in every five years.

52.4.sa: एषामभ्यधिका मासाः पञ्च च द्वादश क्षपाः । त्रयोदशानां वर्षाणामिति मे वर्तते मतिः ॥४॥
52.4.en: I think, calculating in this way, there will be an addition of five months and twelve nights within thirteen vears.

52.5.sa: सर्वं यथावच्चरितं यद्यदेभिः प्रतिश्रुतम् । एवमेतद्‌ध्रुवं ज्ञात्वा ततो बीभत्सुरागतः ॥५॥
52.5.en: They all have duly acted up to what they promised. Knowing all for certain Arjuna has come here.

52.6.sa: सर्वे चैव महात्मानः सर्वे धर्मार्थकोविदाः । येषां युधिष्ठिरो राजा कस्माद्धर्मेऽपराध्नुयुः ॥६॥
52.6.en: All of them are noble and well acquainted with virtue and worldly profit. They have Yudhishthira as their king. How can they injure virtue?

52.7.sa: अलुब्धाश्चैव कौन्तेयाः कृतवन्तश्च दुष्करम् । न चापि केवलं राज्यमिच्छेयुस्तेऽनुपायतः ॥७॥

52.8.sa: तदैव ते हि विक्रान्तुमीषुः कौरवनन्दनाः । धर्मपाशनिबद्धास्तु न चेलुः क्षत्रियव्रतात् ॥८॥
52.8.en: (If so) the descendants of Kuru would have liked to show their prowess at that time; virtuous as they are, they did not deviate from the duties of the Kshatriyas.

52.9.sa: यच्चानृत इति ख्यायाद्यः स गच्छेत् पराभवम् । वृणुयुर्मरणं पार्था नानृतत्वं कथंचन ॥९॥
52.9.en: Whoever will regard them as dishonest will meet with discomfiture today. The sons of Pritha will rather invite death but will never speak an untruth.

52.10.sa: प्राप्तकाले तु प्राप्तव्यं नोत्सृजेयुर्नरर्षभाः । अपि वज्रभृता गुप्तं तथावीर्या हि पाण्डवाः ॥१०॥

52.11.sa: प्रतियुध्येम समरे सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम् । तस्माद्यदत्र कल्याणं लोके सद्भिरनुष्ठितम् ॥ तत् संविधीयतां शीघ्रं मा वो ह्यर्थोऽभ्यगात् परम् ॥११॥
52.11.en: We shall have to content against, in battle, the foremost of all of all heroes; let such arrangements be made speedily, which are good and approved by the honest so that our properties may not pass into the hands of the enemies. O Kaurava, O emperor, I have never seen a battle in which one party is sure to come off victorious. (Besides) Arjuna has come. When a battle begins there is victory and defeat, prosperity and adversity. Therefore one must have either of the two. I have observed it without doubt.

52.12.sa: न हि पश्यामि सङ्ग्रामे कदाचिदपि कौरव । एकान्तसिद्धिं राजेन्द्र संप्राप्तश्च धनंजयः ॥१२॥

52.13.sa: संप्रवृत्ते तु सङ्ग्रामे भावाभावौ जयाजयौ । अवश्यमेकं स्पृशतो दृष्टमेतदसंशयम् ॥१३॥

52.14.sa: तस्माद्युद्धोचितं कर्म कर्म वा धर्मसंहितम् । क्रियतामाशु राजेन्द्र संप्राप्तश्च धनञ्जयः ॥१४॥

52.15.sa: दुर्योधन उवाच । नाहं राज्यं प्रदास्यामि पाण्डवानां पितामह । युद्धोपचारिकं यत्तु तच्छीघ्रं प्रविधीयताम् ॥१५॥
52.15.en: Duryodhana said I shall not, O grandfather, give back their kingdom to Pandavas. Therefore without delay, make arrangements for the battle.

52.16.sa: भीष्म उवाच । अत्र या मामिका बुद्धिः श्रूयतां यदि रोचते । सर्वथा हि मया श्रेयो वक्तव्यं कुरुनन्दन ॥१६॥
52.16.en: Bhishma said Hear what I think about this, if you like. I should always speak what is good, O descendant of Kuru.

52.17.sa: क्षिप्रं बलचतुर्भागं गृह्य गच्छ पुरं प्रति । ततोऽपरश्चतुर्भागो गाः समादाय गच्छतु ॥१७॥
52.17.en: Quickly proceed towards the city with onefourth of the army. Let the other fourth part go away with the kine.

52.18.sa: वयं चार्धेन सैन्यस्य प्रतियोत्स्याम पाण्डवम् । अहं द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च अश्वत्थामा कृपस्तथा । प्रतियोत्स्याम बीभत्सुमागतं कृतनिश्चयम् ॥१८॥
52.18.en: With half the army we shall fight with Arjuna. Myself, Drona, Karna, the son of Drona, as well as Sharadvata's son, Shall firmly fight with Arjuna or the king of Matsya if he has come back or even with the performer of hundred sacrifices. I shall face them like the bank (obstructing the motion of the) ocean.

52.19.sa: मत्स्यं वा पुनरायातमागतं वा शतक्रतुम् । अहमावारयिष्यामि वेलेव मकरालयम् ॥१९॥
52.19.en: With half the army we shall fight with Arjuna. Myself, Drona, Karna, the son of Drona, as well as Sharadvata's son, Shall firmly fight with Arjuna or the king of Matsya if he has come back or even with the performer of hundred sacrifices. I shall face them like the bank (obstructing the motion of the) ocean.

52.20.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तद्वाक्यं रुरुचे तेषां भीष्मणोक्तं महात्मना । तथा हि कृतवान् राजा कौरवाणामनन्तरम् ॥२०॥
52.20.en: Vaishampayana said These words of the great Bhishma found favour with them and the king of Kauravas immediately carried them out.

52.21.sa: भीष्मः प्रस्थाप्य राजानं गोधनं तदनन्तरम् । सेनामुख्यान् व्यवस्थाप्य व्यूहितुं संप्रचक्रमे ॥२१॥

52.22.sa: भीष्म उवाच । आचार्य मध्ये तिष्ठ त्वमश्वत्थामा तु सव्यतः । कृपः शारद्वतो धीमान् पार्श्वं रक्षतु दक्षिणम् ॥२२॥
52.22.en: Bhishma said Stand you, O preceptor, in the middle; let Ashvathama defend the left wing and the intelligent son of Sharadvata Kripa protect the right wing.

52.23.sa: अग्रतः सूतपुत्रस्तु कर्णस्तिष्ठतु दंशितः । अहं सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य पश्चात् स्थास्यामि पालयन् ॥२३॥
52.23.en: Let Karna, the son of charioteer, clad in a coat of mail, stand in the front. And I shall command the entire army in the rear.

53.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । तथा व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु कौरवेयेषु भारत । उपायाद‌र्जुनस्तूर्णं रथघोषण नादयन् ॥१॥
53.1.en: Vaishampayana said After the mighty car-warriors of the Kurus had arrayed themselves in battle, sending out the rattle of their chariots, he quickly proceeded towards them.

53.2.sa: ददृशुस्ते ध्वजाग्रं वै शुश्रुवुश्च महास्वनम् । दोधूयमानस्य भृशं गाण्डीवस्य च निःस्वनम् ॥२॥
53.2.en: They saw the top of his banner, heard the rattle of his car and the twang of his Gandiva bow, stretched greatly by him.

53.3.sa: ततस्तु सर्वमालोक्य द्रोणो वचनमब्रवीत् । महारथमनुप्राप्तं दृष्ट्वा गाण्डीवधन्विनम् ॥३॥
53.3.en: Observing all this and that the great carwarrior, the holder of the Gandiva bow has come, Drona said:

53.4.sa: द्रोण उवाच । एतत् ध्वजाग्रं पार्थस्य दूरतः संप्रकाशते । एष घोषः स रथजो रोरवीति च वानरः ॥४॥
53.4.en: The top of the banner which shines at a distance belongs to Arjuna; this is the rattle of his chariot and this is the monkey which is roaring.

53.5.sa: एष तिष्ठन् रथश्रेष्ठे रथे च रथिनां वरः । उत्कर्षति धनुः श्रेष्ठं गाण्डीवमशनिस्वनम् ॥५॥
53.5.en: The monkey strikes great terror into the hearts of all the soldiers. And sitting on that best of cars, the foremost of car-warriors.

53.6.sa: इमौ च बाणौ सहितौ पाद‌योर्मे व्यवस्थितौ । अपरौ चाप्यतिक्रान्तौ कणा संस्पृश्य मे शरौ ॥६॥
53.6.en: Draws his best of bows Gandiva, that emits the sound of thunder. Those two arrows coming together touch my feet.

53.7.sa: निरुष्य हि वने वासं कृत्वा कर्मातिमानुषम् । अभिवादयते पार्थः श्रोत्रे च परिपृच्छति ॥७॥
53.7.en: Passing by others they touch my ears. Having completed the term of his exile in the forest and performed superhuman deeds,

53.8.sa: चिरदृष्टोऽयमस्माभिः प्रज्ञावान् बान्धवप्रियः । अतीव ज्वलितो लक्ष्म्या पाण्डुपुत्रो धनंजयः ॥८॥
53.8.en: Partha salutes me and speaks to my ears. After a long time we have seen the wise son of Pandu, Dhananjaya, ever a favourite to his friends and greatly shining in prosperity.

53.9.sa: रथी शरी चारुतली निषङ्गी शङ्खी पताकी कवची किरीटी । खड्गी च धन्वी च विभाति पार्थः शिखी वृतः स्रुग्भिरिवाज्यसिक्तः ॥९॥
53.9.en: Possessed of chariot and shafts, beautiful gloves and quivers, conch, flag, armour; and adorned with a crest, scimitar and bow Partha shines like fire fed with clarified butter and sacrificial laddles.

53.10.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । इषुपाते च सेनाया हयान् संयच्छ सारथे । यावत् समीक्षे सैन्येऽस्मिन् क्वासौ कुरुकुलाधमः ॥१०॥
53.10.en: “O charioteer, stop your horses at a place from which my arrows may reach the soldiers so long I do not single out from among them the wretch of the Kuru race (Duryodhana).

53.11.sa: सर्वानेताननादृत्य दृष्ट्वा तमतिमानिनम् । तस्य मूर्ध्नि पतिष्यामि तत एते पराजिताः ॥११॥
53.11.en: Disregarding all these I shall find that vain wretch out and strike him down and then all these will be defeated.

53.12.sa: एष व्यवस्थितो द्रोणो द्रौणिश्च तदनन्तरम् । भीष्मः कृपश्च कर्णश्च महेष्वासाः समागताः ॥१२॥
53.12.en: There stands Drona and thereafter his son and then those great bowmen Bhishma, Kripa and Karna.

53.13.sa: राजानं नात्र पश्यामि गाः समादाय गच्छति । दक्षिणं मार्गमास्थाय शङ्के जीवपरायणः ॥१३॥
53.13.en: I do not see the king, I am afraid, anxious to save his life he is going by the southern road. Leaving the car-warriors here go where Suyodhana is. I shall fight there, O son of Virata, for it will not be without result. Vanquishing him I will come back with the kine.

53.14.sa: उत्सृजैतद्रथानीकं गच्छ यत्र सुयोधनः । तत्रैव योत्स्ये वैराटे नास्ति युद्धं निरामिषम् । तं जित्वा विनिवर्तिष्ये गाः समादाय वै पुनः ॥१४॥
53.14.en: I do not see the king, I am afraid, anxious to save his life he is going by the southern road. Leaving the car-warriors here go where Suyodhana is. I shall fight there, O son of Virata, for it will not be without result. Vanquishing him I will come back with the kine.

53.15.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्तः स वैराटिर्हयान् संयम्य यत्नतः । नियम्य च ततो रश्मीन् यत्र ते कुरुपुङ्गवाः । अचोदयत् ततो वाहान् यत्र दुर्योधनो गतः ॥१५॥
53.15.en: Thus addressed the son of Virata, carefully governing the horses and holding the reins, took the horses where the leading Kurus and the king Suyodhana were. As Arjuna, having white steeds, left that place,

53.16.sa: उत्सृज्य रथवंशं तु प्रयाते श्वेतवाहने । अभिप्रायं विदित्वा च कृपो वचनमब्रवीत् ॥१६॥

53.17.sa: नैषोऽन्तरेण राजानं बीभत्सुः स्थातुमिच्छति । तस्य पार्ष्णिं ग्रहीष्यामो जवेनाभिप्रयास्यतः ॥१७॥

53.18.sa: न ह्येनमतिसंक्रुद्धमेको युध्येत संयुगे । अन्यो देवात् सहस्राक्षात् कृष्णाद्वा देवकी सुतात् । आचार्याच्च सपुत्राद्वा भारद्वाजान्महारथात् ॥१८॥
53.18.en: We shall attach his sides who is advancing quickly. None can alone fight with him in battle when worked up with anger

53.19.sa: किं नो गावः करिष्यन्ति धनं वा विपुलं तथा । दुर्योधनः पार्थजले पुरा नौरिव मज्जति ॥१९॥
53.19.en: What shall we do with these kine or the vast wealth if Duryodhana were to sink like a bark in the Partha water.

53.20.sa: तथैव गत्वा बीभत्सुर्नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः । शलभैरिव तां सेनां शरैः शीघ्रमवाकिरत् ॥२०॥
53.20.en: (In the mean time) going there ard announcing himself as Bibhatsu by name he speedily covered the soldiers with shafts like a swarm of locusts.

53.21.sa: कीर्यमाणाः शरौघैस्तु योधास्ते पार्थचोदितैः । नापश्यन्नावृतां भूमिं नान्तरिक्षं च पत्रिभिः ॥२१॥
53.21.en: Assailed by the mass of shafts discharged by Partha the warriors couldn't see anything, the sky and the earth being covered therewith.

53.22.sa: तेषामापततां युद्धे नापयानेऽभवन्मतिः । शीघ्रत्वमेव पार्थस्य पूजयन्ति स्म चेतसा ॥२२॥
53.22.en: They who came to fight were so confounded that they even could not prepare themselves to fly away and began quickly to adore Partha in their minds.

53.23.sa: ततः शङ्खं प्रदध्मौ स द्विषतां लोमहर्षणम् । विस्फार्य च धनुःश्रेष्ठं ध्वजे भूतान्यचोदयत् ॥२३॥

53.24.sa: तस्य शङ्खस्य शब्देन रथनेमिस्वनेन च । गाण्डीवस्य च घोषेण पृथिवी समकम्पत ॥२४॥
53.24.en: The earth shook with the sound of his conch, the rattle of his chariot and the twang of his Gandiva bow,

53.25.sa: अमानुषाणां भूतानां तेषां च ध्वजवासिनाम् । ऊर्ध्वं पुच्छान् विधुन्वाना रेभमाणाः समन्ततः । गावः प्रतिन्यवर्तन्त दिशमास्थाय दक्षिणाम् ॥२५॥
53.25.en: As well as with the cries of all the superhuman creatures placed on the flag staff. Then raising up their tails and running to and fro the king came back by the southern road.

54.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । स शत्रुसेनां तरसा प्रणुद्य गास्ता विजित्याथ धनुर्धराग्र्यः । दुर्योधनायाभिमुखं प्रयातो भूयो रणं सोऽभिचिकीर्षमाणः ॥१॥
54.1.en: Vaishampayana said Having quickly routed the enemy's host and recovered the kine, that foremost of bowmen, with a view to fight again, proceeded towards Duryodhana.

54.2.sa: गोषु प्रयातासु जवेन मत्स्यान् किरीटिनं कृतकार्यं च मत्वा । दुर्योधनायाभिमुखं प्रयातं कुरुप्रवीराः सहसा निपेतुः ॥२॥
54.2.en: Seeing the kine run towards the city of Matsya's and considering Kiritin successful, the heroic Kurus all on a sudden withstood him who was proceeding towards Duryodhana.

54.3.sa: तेषामनीकानि बहूनि गाढं व्यूढानि दृष्ट्वा बहुलध्वजानि । मत्स्यस्य पुत्रं द्विषतां निहन्ता वैराटिमामन्त्र्य ततोऽभ्युवाच ॥३॥
54.3.en: Beholding their army and various well arranged divisions as well as numberless flags, that destroyer of enemies, addressing the son of Virata, the king of Matsya's, said,

54.4.sa: एतेन तूर्णं प्रतिपादयेमान् श्वेतान् हयान् काञ्चनरश्मियोक्त्रान् । जवेन सर्वेण कुरु प्रयत्नमासादयेऽहं कुरुसिंहवृन्दम् ॥४॥
54.4.en: Soon take these white horses by this way, governed by golden reins. Do you quickly and carefully take me to the row of the leading Kuru heroes.

54.5.sa: गजो गजेनेव मया दुरात्मा योद्धुं समाकाङ्क्षति सूतपुत्रः । तमेव मां प्रापय राजपुत्र दुर्योधनापाश्रयजातदर्पम् ॥५॥
54.5.en: The wicked-souled son of the charioteer (Karna) wishes to fight with me as an elephant does with another (elephant). Do you take me to him, O prince, who has grown insolent for the protection afforded to him by Duryodhana.

54.6.sa: स तैर्हयैर्वातजवैर्बृहद्भिः पुत्रो विराटस्य सुवर्णकक्षैः । व्यध्वंसयत् तद्रथिनामनीकं ततोऽवहत् पाण्डवमाजिमध्ये ॥६॥
54.6.en: Then breaking through the array of carwarriors with big horses fleet as the wind the son of Virata took Arjuna to the middle of the battle field.

54.7.sa: तं चित्रसेनो विशिखैर्विपाठैः सङ्ग्रामजिच्छत्रुसहो जयश्च । प्रत्युद्ययुर्भारतमापतन्तं महारथाः कर्णमभीप्समानाः ॥७॥
54.7.en: Seeing this, those powerful car-warriors, Chitrasena, Sangramajit, Shatrusaha and Jaya with a view to help Karna, rushed towards the advancing Arjuna.

54.8.sa: ततः स तेषां पुरुषप्रवीरः शरासनार्चिः शरवेगतापः । व्रातं रथानामदहत् समन्युर्वनं यथाग्निः कुरुपुङ्गवानाम् ॥८॥
54.8.en: Thereupon worked up with anger that foremost of men began to consume, with blazing shafts, discharged from his bow, the cars of the leading Kurus like fire consuming the forest.

54.9.sa: तस्मिंस्तु युद्धे तुमुले प्रवृत्ते पार्थं विकर्णोऽतिरथं रथेन । विपाठवर्षेण कुरुप्रवीरो भीमेन भीमानुजमाससाद ॥९॥

54.10.sa: ततो विकर्णस्य धनुर्विकृष्य जाम्बूनदाग्र्योपचितं दृढज्यम् । अपातयत् तं ध्वजमस्य मथ्य छिन्नध्वजः सोऽप्यपयाज्जवेन ॥१०॥

54.11.sa: तं शात्रवाणां गणबाधितारं कर्माणि कुर्वन्तममानुषाणि । शत्रुंतपः पार्थममृष्यमाणः समार्दयच्छरवर्षेण पार्थम् ॥११॥
54.11.en: Unable to check his anger, Shatruntapa, with a downpour of shafts, began to afflict Partha-the obstructor of the enemies and the author of superhuman deeds.

54.12.sa: स तेन राज्ञाऽतिरथेन विद्धो विगाहमानो ध्वजिनीं कुरूणाम् । शत्रुंतपं पञ्चभिराशु विद्ध्वा ततोऽस्य सूतं दशभिर्जघान ॥१२॥

54.13.sa: ततः स विद्धो भरतर्षभेण बाणेन गात्रावरणातिगेन । गतासुराजौ निपपात भूमौ नगो नगाग्रादिव वातरुग्णः ॥१३॥
54.13.en: Then wounded by that foremost of Bharatas with a greatly piercing shaft the king leaving his armour fell down dead on the ground like a rock from the mountain summit clapped by the wind.

54.14.sa: नरर्षभास्तेन नरर्षभेण वीरा रणे वीरतरेण भग्नाः । चकम्पिरे वातवशेन काले प्रकम्पितानीव महावनानि ॥१४॥
54.14.en: Assailed by the foremost of men, a greater hero, those heroic leaders of the Kurus began to tremble in battle like a huge forest shaken by the wind at the time of the universal dissolution.

54.15.sa: हतास्तु पार्थेन नरप्रवीरा गतासवोर्व्यां सुषुपुः सुवेषाः । वसुप्रदा वासवतुल्यवीर्याः पराजिता वासवजेन संख्ये ॥१५॥
54.15.en: Vanquished in battle and slain by Partha, the son of Indra, those heroes, givers of wealth and endued with the prowess of Vasava and well-dressed, slept on the ground, deprived of their lives,

54.16.sa: सुवर्णकार्ष्णायसवर्मनद्धा नागा यथा हैमवताः प्रवृद्धाः । तथा स शत्रून् समरे विनिघ्नन् गाण्डीवधन्वा पुरुषप्रवीरः ॥१६॥
54.16.en: Like huge Himalaya elephants dressed with armours made of black steel decked with gold. Thus slaying his enemies in battle that heroic man, the holder of Gandiva bow,

54.17.sa: चचार संख्ये विदिशो दिशश्च दहन्निवाग्निर्वनमातपान्ते । प्रकीर्णपर्णानि यथा वसन्ते विशातयित्वा पवनोऽम्बुदांश्च ॥१७॥
54.17.en: Began to move about in the field in all direction like fire consuming a forest at the end of summer. As the wind blows in the spring scattering the withered leaves and clouds.

54.18.sa: तथा सपत्नान् विकिरन् किरीटी चचार संख्येऽतिरथो रथेन । शोणाश्ववाहस्य हयान् निहत्य वैकर्तनभ्रातुरदीनसत्त्वः । एकेन सङ्ग्रामजितः शरेण शिरो जहाराथ किरीटमाली ॥१८॥
54.18.en: So the mighty car-warrior Kiritin ranged in the battle field in his chariot dispersing his enemies. Then killing the horses of the brother of Vikartana's son, that one of undeteriorating energy. Ever victorious in battle and decked with a brilliant diadem, with one shaft, speedily cut off his head.

54.19.sa: तस्मिन् हते भ्रातरि सूतपुत्रो वैकर्तनो वीर्यमथाददानः । प्रगृह्य दन्ताविव नागराजो महर्षभं व्याघ्र इवाभ्यधावत् ॥१९॥
54.19.en: His brother being slain, the son of Suta, Vikartana's son, gathering his energy. Rushed towards that foremost of men like an elephant chief, with the two tusks out or like a tiger. And Vikartana's son quickly wounded Arjuna with twelve arrows.

54.20.sa: स पाण्डवं द्वादशभिः पृषत्कैर्वैकर्तनः शीघ्रमथो जघान । विव्याध गात्रेषु हयांश्च सर्वान् विराटपुत्रं च करे निजघ्ने ॥२०॥
54.20.en: All the horses on their bodies, and the son of Virata on the hand. Furiously hastening towards Vikartana's son who was quickly proceeding towards him, Kiritin attacked him with great force like Garuda of variegated plumage falling upon snakes.

54.21.sa: तमापतन्तं सहसा किरीटी वैकर्तनं वे तरसाऽभिपत्य । प्रगृह्य वेगं न्यपतज्जवेन नागं गरुत्मानिव चित्रपक्षः ॥२१॥
54.21.en: All the horses on their bodies, and the son of Virata on the hand. Furiously hastening towards Vikartana's son who was quickly proceeding towards him, Kiritin attacked him with great force like Garuda of variegated plumage falling upon snakes.

54.22.sa: तावुत्तमौ सर्वधनुर्धराणां महाबलौ सर्वसपत्नसाहौ । कर्णस्य पार्थस्य निशम्य युद्धं दिदृक्षमाणाः कुरवोऽमितस्थुः ॥२२॥
54.22.en: Both of them were best of bowmen, were greatly powerful and capable of killing all enemies. Understanding that an encounter was soon to take place between Karna and Partha, the Kurus, wishing to witness it, stood at a distance.

54.23.sa: स पाण्डवस्तूर्णमुदीर्णकोपः कृतागसं कर्णमुदीक्ष्य हर्षात् । क्षणेन साध्वं सरथं ससारथिमन्तर्दधे घोरशरौघवृष्ट्या ॥२३॥
54.23.en: Seeing the iniquitous Karna, Arjuna, excited with anger, in great pleasure, quickly made him, his horses and his charioteer invisible by a thick downpour of arrows.

54.24.sa: ततः सुविद्धाः सरथाः सनागा योधा विनेदुर्भरतर्षभाणाम् । अन्तर्हिता भीष्ममुखाः सहाश्वाः किरीटिना कीर्णरथाः पृषत्कैः ॥२४॥
54.24.en: The warriors of the Bharatas, headed by Bhishma, with their horses, elephants and chariots rendered invisible and pierced and having their cars broken by Kiritin with shafts, began to bewail.

54.25.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । स चापि तानर्जुनबाहुमुक्तान् शरान् शरौघैः प्रतिहत्य वीरः । तस्थौ महात्मा सधनुः सबाणः सविस्फुलिङ्गोऽग्निरिवाशु कर्णः ॥२५॥
54.25.en: Then baffaling with his own arrows those shot by the hands of Arjuna the hero, the highsouled Karna, all on a sudden came into view with his bow and arrow like fire with scintillations.

54.26.sa: ततस्त्वभूद्वै तलतालशब्दः सशङ्खभेरीपणवप्रणादः । प्रक्ष्वेडितज्यातलनिःस्वनं तं वैकर्तनं पूजयतां कुरूणाम् ॥२६॥
54.26.en: Then there arose the sound of the clapping of hands and that of conchs, trumpets and bugles while the Kurus spoke highly of Vikartana's son who filled the welkin with the sound of his bow-string striking against his gloves.

54.27.en: Then seeing Kiritin fill the sky with the twang of his Gandiva bow, the upraised tail of the monkey that was on his Flag-staff and the dreadful creatures yelling hideously from the Flag-staff, Karna sent up a shout.

54.28.sa: स चापि वैकर्तनमर्दयित्वा साश्वं ससूतं सरथं पृषत्कैः । तमाववर्ष प्रसभं किरीटी पितामहं द्रोणकृपौ च दृष्ट्वा ॥२८॥
54.28.en: Then assailing with his arrows Vikartana's son, together with his horses, car and charioteer, Arjuna showered a downpour of shafts on him, casting his looks on Bhishma, Drona and Kripa Vikartana's son too covered Partha with a downpour of shafts like a cloud.

54.29.sa: स चापि पार्थं बहुभिः पृषत्कैर्वैकर्तनो मेघ इवाभ्यवर्षत् । तथैव कर्णं च किरीटमाली संछादयामास शितैः पृषत्कैः ॥२९॥
54.29.en: Then assailing with his arrows Vikartana's son, together with his horses, car and charioteer, Arjuna showered a downpour of shafts on him, casting his looks on Bhishma, Drona and Kripa Vikartana's son too covered Partha with a downpour of shafts like a cloud.

54.30.sa: तयोः सुतीक्ष्णान् सृजतोः शरौघान् महाशरौघास्त्रविवर्धने रणे । रथे विलग्नाविव चन्द्रसूर्यौ घनान्तरेणानुददर्श लोकः ॥३०॥
54.30.en: And he too, decked with a diadem, covered Karna with sharp arrows. Creating clouds of sharp arrows in a battle rendered furious by huge weapons and shafts.

54.31.sa: अथाशुकारी चतुरो हयांश्च विव्याध कर्णो निशितैः किरीटिनः । त्रिभिश्च यन्तारममृष्यमाणो विव्याध तूर्णं त्रिभिरस्य केतुम् ॥३१॥
54.31.en: The two, stationed on cars, appeared to men like the sun and the moon covered by clouds. Then the light-handed and intelligent Karna wounded the horses of Partha with shafts,

54.32.sa: ततोऽभिविद्धः समरावमर्दी प्रबोधितः सिंह इव प्रसुप्तः । गाण्डीवधन्वा ऋषभः कुरूणामजिह्मगैः कर्णमियाय जिष्णुः ॥३२॥
54.32.en: Assailed his driver with three arrows and struck down his Flag-staff with three. Thus struck like a sleeping lion awaking, that repressor of enemies in battle,

54.33.sa: शरास्त्रवृष्ट्या निहतो महात्मा प्रादुश्चकारातिमनुष्यकर्म । प्राच्छादयत् कर्णरथं पृषत्कैर्लोकानिमान् सूर्य इवांशुजालैः ॥३३॥
54.33.en: The holder of Gandiva, the heroic Vishnu, assailed Karna with straight shafts, And assailed with a downpour of arrows and weapons the high-souled performer of superhuman deeds displayed (mighty feats).

54.34.sa: स हस्तिनेवाभिहतो गजेन्द्रः प्रगृह्य भल्लान् निशितान् निषङ्गात् । आकर्णपूर्णं च धनुर्विकृष्य विव्याध गात्रेष्वथ सूतपुत्रम् ॥३४॥
54.34.en: He covered Karna's car with shafts like the sun covering the regions with its rays. Like a lion attacked by an elephant he, taking out sharpened arrows from the quiver.

54.35.sa: अथास्य बाहू‌रुशिरोललाटं ग्रीवां वराङ्गानि परावमर्दी । शितैश्च बाणैर्युधि निर्बिभेद गाण्डीवमुक्तैरशनिप्रकाशैः ॥३५॥
54.35.en: And drawing the bow to his ear wounded the charioteer's son on every part of his body. Then that repressor of enemies pierced Karna's arms, thighs, head, forehead and other parts of his body with sharpened arrows fleet as the thunderbolt, shot from his Gandiva bow.

54.36.sa: स पार्थमुक्तैरिषुभिः प्रणुन्नो गजो गजेनेव जितस्तरस्वी । विहाय सङ्ग्रामशिरः प्रयातो वैकर्तनः पाण्डवबाणतप्तः ॥३६॥
54.36.en: Thus wounded by the arrows shot by Partha, the son of Pandu, Vikartana's son lef the battle-field and took to his heels like a elephant defeated by another.

55.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अपयाते तु राधेये दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः । अनीकेन यथास्वेन शनैरार्छन्त पाण्डवम् ॥१॥
55.1.en: Vaishampayana said After the son of Radha had fled away fi the battle-field all other heroes, headed Duryodhana attacked Arjuna with respective detachments.

55.2.sa: बहुधा तस्य सैन्यस्य व्यूढस्यापततः शरैः । अधारयत वेगं स वेलेव तु महोदधेः ॥२॥
55.2.en: Like the bank (obstructing the surging) deep he withstood the various well-arranged divisions of the army falling upon him with arrows.

55.3.sa: ततः प्रहस्य बीभत्सुः कौन्तेयः श्वेतवाहनः । दिव्यमस्त्रं प्रकुर्वाणः प्रत्यायाद्रथसत्तमः ॥३॥
55.3.en: Then smiling, the foremost of car-warriors Bibhatsu, the son of Kunti, having white, steeds, advanced (towards them) displaying celestials weapons.

55.4.sa: यथा रश्मिभिरादित्यः प्रच्छादयति मेदिनीम् । तथा गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैः शरैः पार्थो दिशो दश ॥४॥
55.4.en: Partha soon filled the ten quarters with arrows shot from his Gandiva bow as the sun covers the earth with its rays.

55.5.sa: न रथानां न चाश्वानां न गजानां न वर्मणाम् । अनिविद्धं शितैर्बाणैरासीत् द्व्यङ्गुलमन्तरम् ॥५॥
55.5.en: Of the chariots, horses, elephants and coats of mail there was not space measuring even two fingers that was nor pierced with shafts.

55.6.sa: दिव्ययोगाच्च पार्थस्य हयानामुत्तरस्य च । शिक्षाशिल्पोपपन्नत्वादस्त्राणां च परिक्रमात् । वीर्यवत्त्वं द्रुतं चाग्र्यं दृष्ट्वा जिष्णोरपूजयन् ॥६॥
55.6.en: On account of his cleverly handling the celestials weapons, the training of his horses, the skill of Uttara and the coursing of his weapons.

55.7.sa: कालाग्निमिव बीभत्सुं निर्दहन्तमिव प्रजाः । नारयः प्रेक्षितुं शेकुर्ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् ॥७॥

55.8.sa: तानि ग्रस्तान्यनीकानि रेजुरर्जुनमार्गणैः । शैलं प्रति बलाभ्राणि व्याप्तानीवार्करश्मिभिः ॥८॥
55.8.en: None amongst the enemies could look at Arjuna shining like the burning fire. Assailed by the shafts of Arjuna the various divisions of the army appeared.

55.9.sa: अशोकानां वनानीव छन्नानि बहुशः शुभैः । रेजुः पार्थशरैस्तत्र तदा सैन्यानि भारत ॥९॥
55.9.en: Like the newly risen clouds on a mountain, filled with the rays of the sun or like the gioves of the Ashoka trees covered with full blown flowers.

55.10.sa: स्रजोऽर्जुनशरैः शीर्णं शुष्यत्पुष्पं हिरण्मयम् । छत्राणि च पताकाश्च खे दधार सदागतिः ॥१०॥
55.10.en: Thus assailed by Partha's shafts the army appeared, O Bharata, like a garland from which the withered but golden flowers drop down.

55.11.sa: स्वबलत्रासनात्त्रस्ताः परिपेतुर्दिशो दश । रथाङ्गदेशानादाय पार्थच्छिन्नयुगा हयाः ॥११॥
55.11.en: The wind carried away to the sky the umbrellas and the flags. Terrified at the destruction of their own species and having their reins cut off by Partha's arrows the horses, taking with them, portions of cars, fled away in different directions. Struck on their ears, ribs, tusks, the lower lips and other vital parts the elephants began to drop down in the battle-field. Filled in no time with the dead elephants of the Kurus the earth looked like the sky filled with black clouds. As the blazing fire burns up all mobile and immobile, at the time of the universal dissolution, so did Partha, O king, consume the enemies in battle. Then with the power of all his weapons, the twang of his bow and superhuman cries of the creatures stationed on his Flag-staff.

55.12.sa: कर्णकक्षविषाणेषु अन्तरोष्ठेषु चैव ह । मर्मस्वङ्गेषु चाहत्य पातयत् समरे गजान् ॥१२॥
55.12.en: The wind carried away to the sky the umbrellas and the flags. Terrified at the destruction of their own species and having their reins cut off by Partha's arrows the horses, taking with them, portions of cars, fled away in different directions. Struck on their ears, ribs, tusks, the lower lips and other vital parts the elephants began to drop down in the battle-field. Filled in no time with the dead elephants of the Kurus the earth looked like the sky filled with black clouds. As the blazing fire burns up all mobile and immobile, at the time of the universal dissolution, so did Partha, O king, consume the enemies in battle. Then with the power of all his weapons, the twang of his bow and superhuman cries of the creatures stationed on his Flag-staff.

55.13.sa: कौरवाग्रगजानां तु शरीरैर्गतचेतसाम् । क्षणेन संवृता भूमिर्मेघैरिव नभस्तलम् ॥१३॥
55.13.en: The wind carried away to the sky the umbrellas and the flags. Terrified at the destruction of their own species and having their reins cut off by Partha's arrows the horses, taking with them, portions of cars, fled away in different directions. Struck on their ears, ribs, tusks, the lower lips and other vital parts the elephants began to drop down in the battle-field. Filled in no time with the dead elephants of the Kurus the earth looked like the sky filled with black clouds. As the blazing fire burns up all mobile and immobile, at the time of the universal dissolution, so did Partha, O king, consume the enemies in battle. Then with the power of all his weapons, the twang of his bow and superhuman cries of the creatures stationed on his Flag-staff.

55.14.sa: युगान्तसमये सर्वं यथा स्थावरजङ्गमम् । कालक्षयमशेषेण दहत्यग्रशिखः शिखी । तद्वत् पार्थो महाराज ददाह समरे रिपून् ॥१४॥
55.14.en: The wind carried away to the sky the umbrellas and the flags. Terrified at the destruction of their own species and having their reins cut off by Partha's arrows the horses, taking with them, portions of cars, fled away in different directions. Struck on their ears, ribs, tusks, the lower lips and other vital parts the elephants began to drop down in the battle-field. Filled in no time with the dead elephants of the Kurus the earth looked like the sky filled with black clouds. As the blazing fire burns up all mobile and immobile, at the time of the universal dissolution, so did Partha, O king, consume the enemies in battle. Then with the power of all his weapons, the twang of his bow and superhuman cries of the creatures stationed on his Flag-staff.

55.15.sa: ततः सर्वास्त्रतेजोभिर्धनुषो निःस्वनेन च । शब्देनामानुषाणां च भूतानां ध्वजवासिनाम् । भैरवं शब्दमत्यर्थं वानरस्य च कुर्वतः ॥१५॥
55.15.en: The wind carried away to the sky the umbrellas and the flags. Terrified at the destruction of their own species and having their reins cut off by Partha's arrows the horses, taking with them, portions of cars, fled away in different directions. Struck on their ears, ribs, tusks, the lower lips and other vital parts the elephants began to drop down in the battle-field. Filled in no time with the dead elephants of the Kurus the earth looked like the sky filled with black clouds. As the blazing fire burns up all mobile and immobile, at the time of the universal dissolution, so did Partha, O king, consume the enemies in battle. Then with the power of all his weapons, the twang of his bow and superhuman cries of the creatures stationed on his Flag-staff.

55.16.sa: दैवारिपाच्च बीभत्सुस्तस्मिन् दौर्योधने बले । भयमुत्पादयामास बलवानरिमर्दनः ॥१६॥
55.16.en: And the dreadful yell of the monkey, Bibhatsu struck terror into the hearts of Duryodhana's soldiers. A highly powerful repressor of enemies as he was, he had already crushed to the ground the strength of the hostile heroes.

55.17.sa: रथशक्तिममित्राणां प्रागेव निपतद्भुवि । सोपयात् सहसा पश्चात् साहसाच्चाभ्युपेयिवान् ॥१७॥
55.17.en: And the dreadful yell of the monkey, Bibhatsu struck terror into the hearts of Duryodhana's soldiers. A highly powerful repressor of enemies as he was, he had already crushed to the ground the strength of the hostile heroes.

55.18.sa: शरव्रातैः सुतीक्ष्णाग्रैः समादिष्टैः खगैरिव । अर्जुनस्तु खमावव्रे लोहितप्राशनैः खगैः ॥१८॥
55.18.en: He all on a sudden from behind attacked the army with a net of sharpened arrows like birds ordered (by fowlers).

55.19.sa: अत्रमध्ये यथार्कस्य रश्मयस्तिग्मतेजसः । दिशासु च तथा राजन्नसंख्याताः शरास्तदा ॥१९॥
55.19.en: Arjuna covered the entire sky with blooddrinking arrows. As the fierce rays of the sun are within a small vessel. O king, those numberless shafts of his were in the sky. They could see once his car only when brought near.

55.20.sa: सकृदेवानतं शेकू रथमभ्यसितुं परे । अलभ्यः पुनरश्वैस्तु रथात्सोऽतिप्रपादयेत् ॥२०॥
55.20.en: Arjuna covered the entire sky with blooddrinking arrows. As the fierce rays of the sun are within a small vessel. O king, those numberless shafts of his were in the sky. They could see once his car only when brought near.

55.21.sa: ते शरा द्विट्शरीरेषु यथैव न ससज्जिरे । द्विडनीकेषु बीभत्सोर्न ससज्जे रथस्तदा ॥२१॥
55.21.en: And no sooner they saw him he felled them from the chariot with their horses. As his arrows were not impeded by the bodies of his enemies.

55.22.sa: स तद्विक्षोभयामास ह्यरातिबलमञ्जसा । अनन्तभोगो भुजगः क्रीडन्निव महार्णवे ॥२२॥
55.22.en: So the car of Bibhatsu was not obstructed by the army of the enemy. He, with great force, began to agitate the army of the enemy.

55.23.sa: अस्यतो नित्यमत्यर्थं सर्वमेवातिगस्तथा । अश्रुतः श्रूयते भूतैर्धर्घोषः किरीटिनः ॥२३॥
55.23.en: Like the thousand headed serpent Vasuki sporting in the great ocean. As Kiriti continually shot his arrows such was the twang of his bow, going above every sound that the like of if was never heard by creatures. The elephants, that were there with their bodies thickly covered with arrows, looked like black clouds filled with the rays of the sun. Moving in all directions and shooting arrows right and left Arjuna's bow was always seen in the battle like a circle.

55.24.sa: संततास्तत्र मातङ्गा बाणैरल्पान्तरान्तरे । संवृतास्तेन दृश्यन्ते मेघा इव गभस्तिभिः ॥२४॥
55.24.en: Like the thousand headed serpent Vasuki sporting in the great ocean. As Kiriti continually shot his arrows such was the twang of his bow, going above every sound that the like of if was never heard by creatures. The elephants, that were there with their bodies thickly covered with arrows, looked like black clouds filled with the rays of the sun. Moving in all directions and shooting arrows right and left Arjuna's bow was always seen in the battle like a circle.

55.25.sa: दिशोऽनुभ्रमतः सर्वाः सव्यदक्षिणमस्यतः । सततं दृश्यते युद्धे सायकासनमण्डलम् ॥२५॥
55.25.en: Like the thousand headed serpent Vasuki sporting in the great ocean. As Kiriti continually shot his arrows such was the twang of his bow, going above every sound that the like of if was never heard by creatures. The elephants, that were there with their bodies thickly covered with arrows, looked like black clouds filled with the rays of the sun. Moving in all directions and shooting arrows right and left Arjuna's bow was always seen in the battle like a circle.

55.26.sa: पतन्त्यरूपेषु यथा चक्षूंषि न कदाचन । नालक्ष्येषु शराः पेतुस्तथा गाण्डीवधन्वनः ॥२६॥
55.26.en: The arrows of the holder of the Gandiva bow never fell upon anything except the aim as the eye does not fall upon anything except what is beautiful. As the passage for a thousand of elephants is made of itself when they simultaneously pass through a forest so the track of the chariot of Kiritin was made out. Greatly assailed by Partha the enemies thought, “Desirous of securing victory to Partha forsooth, Indra, in the company of all the immortals, is destroying us."

55.27.sa: मार्गो गजसहस्रस्य युगपद्गच्छतो वने । यथा भवेत्तथा जज्ञे रथमार्गः किरीटिनः ॥२७॥
55.27.en: The arrows of the holder of the Gandiva bow never fell upon anything except the aim as the eye does not fall upon anything except what is beautiful. As the passage for a thousand of elephants is made of itself when they simultaneously pass through a forest so the track of the chariot of Kiritin was made out. Greatly assailed by Partha the enemies thought, “Desirous of securing victory to Partha forsooth, Indra, in the company of all the immortals, is destroying us."

55.28.sa: नूनं पार्थजयैषित्वाच्छक्रः सर्वामरैः सह । हन्त्यस्मानित्यमन्यन्त पार्थेने निहताः परे ॥२८॥
55.28.en: The arrows of the holder of the Gandiva bow never fell upon anything except the aim as the eye does not fall upon anything except what is beautiful. As the passage for a thousand of elephants is made of itself when they simultaneously pass through a forest so the track of the chariot of Kiritin was made out. Greatly assailed by Partha the enemies thought, “Desirous of securing victory to Partha forsooth, Indra, in the company of all the immortals, is destroying us."

55.29.sa: घ्नन्तमत्यर्थमहितान् विजयं तत्र मेनिरे । कालमर्जुनरूपेण संहरन्तमिव प्रजाः ॥२९॥
55.29.en: The arrows of the holder of the Gandiva bow never fell upon anything except the aim as the eye does not fall upon anything except what is beautiful. As the passage for a thousand of elephants is made of itself when they simultaneously pass through a forest so the track of the chariot of Kiritin was made out. Greatly assailed by Partha the enemies thought, “Desirous of securing victory to Partha forsooth, Indra, in the company of all the immortals, is destroying us."

55.30.en: They also took Vijaya, who was making a dreadful havoc all round, to be Death himself, who in the guise of Arjuna, was putting an end to all creatures around. And wounded by Partha the bodies of the Kuru soldiers were distressed like those slain by Partha by his superhuman deed. He sundered the heads of the enemies like the tops of Oshadhis.

55.31.sa: ओषधीनां शिरांसीव द्विषच्छीर्षाणि सोऽन्वयात् । अवनेशुः कुरूणां हि वीर्याण्यर्जुनजाद्भयात् ॥३१॥
55.31.en: They also took Vijaya, who was making a dreadful havoc all round, to be Death himself, who in the guise of Arjuna, was putting an end to all creatures around. And wounded by Partha the bodies of the Kuru soldiers were distressed like those slain by Partha by his superhuman deed. He sundered the heads of the enemies like the tops of Oshadhis.

55.32.en: The Kurus lost all their energy in fear of Arjuna. Uprooted by Arjuna wind, the trees of the Arjuna's enemies reddened the earth with purple secretions. And with the dust saturated with blood and raised up by the wind the rays of the sun were greatly reddened. The sky with the sun being reddened soon appeared like the evening.

55.33.sa: लोहितेन समायुक्तैः पांसुभिः पवनोद्धृतैः । बभूवुर्लोहितास्तत्र भृशमादित्यरश्मयः ॥३३॥
55.33.en: The Kurus lost all their energy in fear of Arjuna. Uprooted by Arjuna wind, the trees of the Arjuna's enemies reddened the earth with purple secretions. And with the dust saturated with blood and raised up by the wind the rays of the sun were greatly reddened. The sky with the sun being reddened soon appeared like the evening.

55.34.sa: सार्कं खं तत्क्षणेनासीत् सन्ध्यायामिव लोहितम् । अप्यस्तं प्राप्य सूर्योऽपि निवर्तेत न पाण्डवः ॥३४॥
55.34.en: The Kurus lost all their energy in fear of Arjuna. Uprooted by Arjuna wind, the trees of the Arjuna's enemies reddened the earth with purple secretions. And with the dust saturated with blood and raised up by the wind the rays of the sun were greatly reddened. The sky with the sun being reddened soon appeared like the evening.

55.35.sa: तान्सर्वान् समरे शूरः पौरुषे समवस्थितान् । दिव्यैरस्त्रैरचिन्त्यात्मा सर्वानार्छद्धनुर्धरान् ॥३५॥
55.35.en: Even the sun ceases to pour its rays when he sets but the son of Pandu did not cease to discharge his arrows. In the battle that hero of incomprehensible energy assailed with celestials weapons all the heroic and leading bow men. He discharged seventy arrows, sharp as razors at Drona, Twelve at Dushasana and three at Kirpa, the son of Sharadvata.

55.36.sa: स तु द्रोणं त्रिसप्तत्या क्षुरप्राणां समार्पयत् । दुःसहं दशभिर्बाणैद्रौणिमष्टाभिरेव च ॥३६॥
55.36.en: Even the sun ceases to pour its rays when he sets but the son of Pandu did not cease to discharge his arrows. In the battle that hero of incomprehensible energy assailed with celestials weapons all the heroic and leading bow men. He discharged seventy arrows, sharp as razors at Drona, Twelve at Dushasana and three at Kirpa, the son of Sharadvata.

55.37.sa: दुःशासनं द्वादशभिः कृपं शारद्वतं त्रिभिः । भीष्मं शान्तनवं षष्ठ्या राजानं च शतेन ह । कर्णं च कर्णिना कर्णे विव्याध परवीरहा ॥३७॥
55.37.en: That slayer of hostile heroes pierced with six shafts Bhishma, the son of Shantanu and the king Duryodhana with hundred and Karna in the car with a bearded shaft.

55.38.sa: तस्मिन्विद्धे महेष्वासे कर्णे सर्वास्त्रकोविदे । हताश्वसूते विरथे ततोऽनीकमभज्यत ॥३८॥
55.38.en: When that great bowman Karna expert in the use of all weapons, was thus pierced and his steeds, chariot and charioteer destroyed, his army were routed.

55.39.sa: तत् प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा पार्थमाजिस्थितं पुनः । अभिप्रायं समाज्ञाय वैराटिरिद‌मब्रवीत् ॥३९॥
55.39.en: Beholding the army thus routed and with a view to decipher Partha intention the son of Virata addressed Partha in the battle-field saying:

55.40.sa: आस्थाय रुचिरं जिष्णो रथं सारथिना मया । कतमं यास्यसेऽनीकमुक्तो यास्याम्यहं त्वया ॥४०॥
55.40.en: O Partha, stationed on this beautiful car with myself as charioteer, towards what division of the army shall I go?

55.41.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । लोहिताश्वमरिष्टं यं वैयाघ्रमनुपश्यसि । नीलां पताकामाश्रित्य रथे तिष्ठन्तमुत्तर ॥४१॥
55.41.en: Arjuna said O Uttara, the hero, whom you see before, clad in a coat of tiger-skin, on a car with blue flag drawn by red horses, is Kripa-and there is the van of his army. Do you take me there. I shall show that great bowman my light handedness in the use of weapons.

55.42.sa: कृपस्यैतदनीकाग्र्यं प्रापयस्वैतदेव माम् । एतस्य दर्शयिष्यामि शीघ्रास्त्रं दृढधन्विनः ॥४२॥
55.42.en: Arjuna said O Uttara, the hero, whom you see before, clad in a coat of tiger-skin, on a car with blue flag drawn by red horses, is Kripa-and there is the van of his army. Do you take me there. I shall show that great bowman my light handedness in the use of weapons.

55.43.sa: ध्वजे कमण्डलुर्यस्य शातकौम्भमयः शुभः । आचार्य एष हि द्रोणः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः ॥४३॥
55.43.en: That hero, on whose flag is the emblem of a beautiful golden water pot, is the preceptor Drona-the foremost of the wielders of all weapons.

55.44.sa: सदा ममैष मान्यस्तु सर्वशस्त्रभृतामपि । सुप्रसन्नं महावीरं कुरुष्वैनं प्रदक्षिणम् ॥४४॥
55.44.en: He is ever worshipful to me as well as to other heroes. Do you cheerfully go round him the foremost of the Kuru warriors.

55.45.en: I shall salute him there for such is the ever abiding duty. If Drona at first strikes my body. I shall strike him then and he will not be angry for it. Near him at whose flag the mark of a bow is seen.

55.46.sa: अस्याविदूरे हि धनुर्ध्वजाग्रे यस्य दृश्यते । आचार्यस्यैष पुत्रो वै अश्वत्थामा महारथः ॥४६॥

55.47.sa: सदा ममैष मान्यस्तु सर्वशस्त्रभृतामपि । एतस्य त्वं रथं प्राप्य निवर्तेथाः पुनः पुनः ॥४७॥
55.47.en: He is ever worshipful to me as well as to other heroes. Do you cheerfully go round him the foremost of the Kuru warriors.

55.48.sa: य एष तु रथानीके सुवर्णकवचावृतः । सेनाग्र्येण तृतीयेन व्यावहार्येण तिष्ठति ॥४८॥

55.49.sa: यस्य नागो ध्वजाग्रेऽसौ हेमकेतनसंवृतः । धृतराष्ट्रात्मजः श्रीमानेष राजा सुयोधनः ॥४९॥
55.49.en: Who stands there surrounded by the third portion of the army, the flower (of the entire army) on whose flag is the emblem of an elephant on the ground of gold,

55.50.sa: एतस्याभिमुखं वीर रथं पररथारुजम् । प्रापयस्वैष राजा हि प्रमाथी युद्धदुर्मदः ॥५०॥
55.50.en: Is the son of Dhritarashtra, the graceful king Duryodhana. O hero, take before him this car that is capable of destroying other cars of the enemies.

55.51.sa: एष द्रोणस्य शिष्याणां शीघ्रास्त्रे प्रथमो मतः । एतस्य दर्शयिष्यामि शीघ्रास्त्रं विपुलं रणे ॥५१॥
55.51.en: The king is irrepressible in battle and capable of grinding (enemies); in lightness of hand he is regarded as the foremost amongst the disciples of Drona.

55.52.sa: नागकक्षा तु रुचिरा ध्वजाग्रे यस्य तिष्ठति । एष वैकर्तनः कर्णो विदितः पूर्वमेव ते ॥५२॥
55.52.en: I shall in battle show him my superior light handedness in the discharge of arrows. That warrior, on whose flag is the emblem of a strong rope for binding elephants, is Karna, the son of Vikartana, already known to you. When you come near the car of the wicked-souled son of Radha

55.53.sa: एतस्य रथमास्थाय राधेयस्य दुरात्मनः । यत्तो भवेथाः सङ्ग्रामे स्पर्धते हि सदा मया ॥५३॥

55.54.sa: यस्तु नीलानुसारेण पञ्चतारेण केतुना । हस्तावापी बृहद्धन्वा रथे तिष्ठति वीर्यवान् ॥५४॥
55.54.en: Be you very careful for he always challenges me to fight. That hero, whose flag is blue and on which is the emblem of five stars and who, powerful as he is, waits on his car with a huge bow in his hands with gloves and on whose car is placed a Flag-staff variegated with the sun and stars.

55.55.sa: यस्य तारार्कचित्रोऽसौ ध्वजो रथवरे स्थितः । यस्यैतत् पाण्डुरं छत्रं विमलं मूर्ध्नि तिष्ठति ॥५५॥

55.56.sa: महतो रथवंशस्य नानाध्वजपताकिनः । बलाहकाग्रे सूर्यो वा य एष प्रमुखे स्थितः ॥५६॥

55.57.sa: हेमं चन्द्रार्कसंकाशं कवचं यस्य दृश्यते । जातरूपशिरस्त्राणं मनस्तापयतीव मे ॥५७॥
55.57.en: Like the sun before the collection of clouds and whose golden coat of mail looks like the sun or moon

55.58.sa: एष शांतनवो भीष्मः सर्वेषां नः पितामहः । राजश्रियाभिवृद्धश्च सुयोधनवशानुगः ॥५८॥

55.59.sa: पश्चादेष प्रयातव्यो न मे विघ्नकरो भवेत् । एतेन युध्यमानस्य यत्तः संयच्छ मे हयान् ॥५९॥

55.60.sa: ततोऽभ्यवहदव्यग्रो वैराटिः सव्यसाचिनम् । यत्रातिष्ठत्कृपो राजन्योत्स्यमानो धनंजयम् ॥६०॥

56.1.sa: वैशंपायन उवाच । तान्यनीकान्यदृश्यन्त कुरूणामुग्रधन्विनाम् । संसर्पन्ते यथा मेघा घर्मान्ते मन्दमारुताः ॥१॥

56.2.sa: अभ्याशे वाजिनस्तस्थुः समारूढाः प्रहारिणः । भीमरूपाश्च मातङ्गास्तोमराङ्कुशनोदिताः । महामात्रैः समारूढा विचित्रकवचोज्ज्वलाः ॥२॥
56.2.en: And near them stood the enemy's cavalry managed by warriors. There were also terrible looking elephants bedecked with beautiful armours governed by clever heroes and urged by Tomaras and gaudas. There came on a beautiful car Shakra accompanied by the celestials, Vishvas and Maruts, O king. Filled with the celestials, Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Nagas the sky looked resplendent as it does when freed from cloud sand crested with stars. The celestials came there in their respective cars to witness the efficacy of their weapons in a human battle as well as the dreadful and great fight between Kripa and Arjuna.

56.3.sa: ततः शक्रः सुरगणैः समारुह्य सुदर्शनम् । सहोपायात् तदा राजन्विश्वाश्विमरुतां गणैः ॥३॥

56.4.en: And near them stood the enemy's cavalry managed by warriors. There were also terrible looking elephants bedecked with beautiful armours governed by clever heroes and urged by Tomaras and gaudas. There came on a beautiful car Shakra accompanied by the celestials, Vishvas and Maruts, O king. Filled with the celestials, Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Nagas the sky looked resplendent as it does when freed from cloud sand crested with stars. The celestials came there in their respective cars to witness the efficacy of their weapons in a human battle as well as the dreadful and great fight between Kripa and Arjuna.

56.5.sa: अस्त्राणां च बलं तेषां मानुषेषु प्रयुञ्जताम् । तच्च भीमं महद्युद्धं कृपार्जुनसमागमे । द्रष्टुमभ्यागता देवाः स्वविमानैः पृथक् पृथक् ॥५॥
56.5.en: And near them stood the enemy's cavalry managed by warriors. There were also terrible looking elephants bedecked with beautiful armours governed by clever heroes and urged by Tomaras and gaudas. There came on a beautiful car Shakra accompanied by the celestials, Vishvas and Maruts, O king. Filled with the celestials, Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Nagas the sky looked resplendent as it does when freed from cloud sand crested with stars. The celestials came there in their respective cars to witness the efficacy of their weapons in a human battle as well as the dreadful and great fight between Kripa and Arjuna.

56.6.sa: शतं शतसहस्राणां यत्र स्थूणा हिरण्मयी । मणिरत्नमयी चान्या प्रासादं तदधारयत् ॥६॥
56.6.en: The celestial car of the king of the celestials coursing at will, crested with pearls and jewels and the roof of which was upheld by hundreds and thousands of golden pillars and the one which was made of pearls and jewels, shone in the clear sky.

56.7.sa: ततः कामगमं दिव्यं सर्वरत्नविभूषितम् । विमानं देवराजस्य शुशुभे खेचरं तदा ॥७॥
56.7.en: The celestial car of the king of the celestials coursing at will, crested with pearls and jewels and the roof of which was upheld by hundreds and thousands of golden pillars and the one which was made of pearls and jewels, shone in the clear sky.

56.8.sa: तत्र देवास्त्रयस्त्रिंशत्तिष्ठन्ति सहवासवाः । गन्धर्वा राक्षसाः सर्पाः पितरश्च महर्षिभिः ॥८॥
56.8.en: There were the thirty three deities headed by Vasava and with Gandharvas, Rakshasas, Nagas, Pitris and the great Rishis.

56.9.sa: तथा राजा वसुमना बलाक्षः सुप्रतर्दनः। अष्टकश्च शिबिश्चैव ययातिर्नहुषो गयः ॥९॥

56.10.sa: मनुः पूरू रघुर्भानुः कृशाश्वः सगरो नलः । विमाने देवराजस्य समदृश्यन्त सुप्रभाः ॥१०॥
56.10.en: There shone on the car of the king of the celestials the king Vasumanas, Balakshas, Supratardana, Ashtaka, Shibi, Yayati, Nahusha, Gaya, Manu, Puru, Raghu, Bhanu, Krishashva, Sagara and Nala.

56.11.sa: अग्नेरीशस्य सोमस्य वरुणस्य प्रजापतेः । तथा धातुर्विधातुश्च कुबेरस्य यमस्य च ॥११॥
56.11.en: There appeared also in a beautiful array the chariots of Agni, Isha, Soma, Varuna, Prajapati, Dhatri, Vidhatri, Kubera, Yama, Alambusha, Ugrasena and others and of the Gandharva Tumvuru.

56.12.sa: अलम्बुषोग्रसेनानां गन्धर्वस्य च तुम्बुरोः । यथामानं यथोद्देशं विमानानि चकाशिरे ॥१२॥
56.12.en: There appeared also in a beautiful array the chariots of Agni, Isha, Soma, Varuna, Prajapati, Dhatri, Vidhatri, Kubera, Yama, Alambusha, Ugrasena and others and of the Gandharva Tumvuru.

56.13.sa: सर्वदेवनिकायाश्च सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः । अर्जुनस्य कुरूणां च द्रष्टुं युद्धमुपागताः ॥१३॥

56.14.sa: दिव्यानां सर्वमाल्यानां गन्धः पुण्योऽथ सर्वशः। प्रससार वसन्ताग्रे वनानामिव भारत ॥१४॥
56.14.en: The holy fragrance of the celestial garlands spread all over like the odour of the blossoming trees in the beginning of the spring.

56.15.sa: तत्र रत्नानि देवानां समदृश्यन्त तिष्ठताम् । आतपत्राणि वासांसि स्रजश्च व्यजनानि च ॥१५॥

56.16.sa: उपाशाम्यद्रजो भौमं सर्वं व्याप्तं मरीचिभिः । दिव्यगन्धानुपादाय वायुर्योधानसेवत ॥१६॥
56.16.en: The dust of the earth was removed and every where was permeated by the lustre. And carrying the divine odour the wind gratified the warriors.

56.17.en: The sky appeared as if ablaze and beautiful, being decked with already arrived and coming cars lighted with various gems and of diverse make, led by the leading celestials. Encircled by the deities, and wearing garland of lotuses and lillies, the mighty holder of thunder appeared exceedingly beautiful on his car. And although he looked continually at his son he was not satiated therewith.

56.18.sa: विमानैर्विविधैश्चित्रैरुपानीतैः सुरोत्तमैः । वज्रभृच्छुशुभे तत्र विमानस्थैः सुरैर्वृतः ॥१८॥
56.18.en: The sky appeared as if ablaze and beautiful, being decked with already arrived and coming cars lighted with various gems and of diverse make, led by the leading celestials. Encircled by the deities, and wearing garland of lotuses and lillies, the mighty holder of thunder appeared exceedingly beautiful on his car. And although he looked continually at his son he was not satiated therewith.

56.19.en: The sky appeared as if ablaze and beautiful, being decked with already arrived and coming cars lighted with various gems and of diverse make, led by the leading celestials. Encircled by the deities, and wearing garland of lotuses and lillies, the mighty holder of thunder appeared exceedingly beautiful on his car. And although he looked continually at his son he was not satiated therewith.

57.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । दृष्ट्वा व्यूढान्यनीकानि कुरूणां कुरुनन्दन । तत्र वैरादिमामन्त्र्य पार्थो वचनमब्रवीत् ॥१॥
57.1.en: Vaishampayana said Seeing the Kuru army arranged in order of battle, the son of Pandu, Partha, addressing Virata's son said :

57.2.sa: जाम्बूनदमयी वेदी ध्वजे यस्य प्रदृश्यते । तस्य दक्षिणतो याहि कृपः शारद्वतो यतः ॥२॥
57.2.en: Do you go where Kripa, the son of Sharadvata is, by the southern side of the car the flag of which has an emblem of a golden altar.

57.3.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । धनञ्जयवचः श्रुत्वा वैराटिस्त्वरितस्ततः । हयान् रजतसंकाशान् हेमभाण्डानचोदयत् ॥३॥
57.3.en: Hearing the words of Arjuna, Virata's son, without loss of time, urged his silver white steeds decked in golden armour.

57.4.sa: आनुपूर्व्यात्तु तत् सर्वमास्थाय जवमुत्तमम् । प्राहिणोच्चन्द्रसंकाशान् कुपितानिव तान् हयान् ॥४॥
57.4.en: Making them one by one proceed by swifter course, he urged those those horses resembling the moon as if they were angry.

57.5.sa: स गत्वा कुरुसेनायाः समीपं हयकोविदः । पुनरावर्तयामास तान् हयान् वातरंहसः ॥५॥
57.5.en: Well-versed in the management of horses, Uttara, having neared the Kuru army, turned back his horses, fleet as the wind.

57.6.sa: प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य मण्डलं सव्यमेव च । कुरून् संमोहयामास मत्स्यो यानेन तत्त्ववित् ॥६॥
57.6.en: A skillful charioteer as he was the Matsya Prince, sometimes wheeling about, sometimes proceeding in circles and again turning to the left, bewildered the Kurus.

57.7.sa: कृपस्य रथमास्थाय वैराटिरकुतोभयः । प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य तस्थौ तस्याग्रतो बली ॥७॥
57.7.en: Going round, the powerful and fearless son of Virata, approached Kripa's car and stood before him.

57.8.sa: ततोऽर्जुनः शङ्खवरं देवदत्तं महारवम् । प्रदध्मौ बलमास्थाय नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः ॥८॥
57.8.en: Then Arjuna with force blew that great conch Devadatta emitting a great sound and announced his name.

57.9.sa: तस्य शब्दो महानासीद्धम्यमानस्य जिष्णुना । तथा वीर्यवता संख्ये पर्वतस्येव दीर्यतः ॥९॥
57.9.en: Blown on the battle-field by the powerful Vishnu the sound of that conch appeared like that of the clapping of a mountain.

57.10.sa: पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे शङ्खं कुरवः सहसैनिकाः । अर्जुनेन तथा घ्मातः शतधा यन्न दीर्यते ॥१०॥
57.10.en: Seeing that the conch was not broken into a hundred pieces when blown by Arjuna, the Kuru warriors spoke highly of it.

57.11.sa: दिवमावृत्य शब्दस्तु निवृत्तः शुश्रुवे पुनः । सृष्टो मघवता वज्रः प्रपतन्निव पर्वते ॥११॥
57.11.en: Having reached the very sky that sound came back and was heard again like that of thunderbolt when hurled by Indra against a mountain.

57.12.sa: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरो बलवीर्यसमन्वितः । अर्जुनं प्रति संरब्धः कृपः परमदुर्जयः । अमृष्यमाणस्तं शब्दं कृपः शारद्वतस्तदा ॥१२॥
57.12.en: Unable to bear that sound and desirous of fighting that heroic, powerful and undaunted car-warrior, Sharadvata's son Kripa of great strength and prowess, enraged with Arjuna, took up the conch born in a great ocean and blew it with great force.

57.13.sa: अर्जुनं प्रति संरब्धो युद्धार्थी स महारथः । महोदधिजमादाय दध्मौ वेगेन वीर्यवान् ॥१३॥
57.13.en: Unable to bear that sound and desirous of fighting that heroic, powerful and undaunted car-warrior, Sharadvata's son Kripa of great strength and prowess, enraged with Arjuna, took up the conch born in a great ocean and blew it with great force.

57.14.sa: स तु शब्देन लोकांस्त्रीनावृत्य रथिनां वरः । धनुरादाय सुमहज्ज्याशब्दमकरोत् तदा ॥१४॥
57.14.en: Covering the three worlds with the sound thereof and taking up the huge bow he twanged it.

57.15.sa: तौ रथौ सूर्यसंकाशौ योत्स्यमानौ महाबलौ । शारदाविव जीमूतौ व्यरोचेतां व्यवस्थितौ ॥१५॥
57.15.en: While those two highly powerful carwarriors, resembling the sun, fought with each other they appeared like two autumnal clouds.

57.16.sa: ततः शारद्वतस्तूर्णं पार्थं दशभिराशुगैः । विव्याध परवीरघ्नं निशितैर्मर्मभेदिभिः ॥१६॥
57.16.en: Then Sharadvata's son speedily wounded Partha, the slayer of hostile heroes with ten swift coursing sharpened arrows capable of piercing into the very vitals.

57.17.sa: पार्थोऽपि विश्रुतं लोके गाण्डीवं परमायुधम् । विकृष्य चिक्षेप बहुन् नाराचान् मर्मभेदिनः ॥१७॥
57.17.en: And drawing his huge bow Gandiva wellknown in the world Partha too discharged many Narachas capable of piercing into the very vitals.

57.18.sa: तानप्राप्तान् शितैर्बाणैर्नाराचान् रक्तभोजनान् । कृपश्चिच्छेद पार्थस्य शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥१८॥
57.18.en: Then with sharpened arrows "Kripa sundered into hundreds and thousands of pieces those blood-drinking shafts before they could reach (him).

57.19.sa: ततः पार्थस्तु संक्रुद्धश्चित्रान् मार्गान् प्रदर्शयन् । दिशः संछादयन् बाणैः प्रदिशश्च महारथः । एकच्छायमिवाकाशमकरोत् सर्वतः प्रभुः ॥१९॥
57.19.en: Thereupon displaying various movements in anger, the great car-warrior Partha covered all sides with a downpour of arrows.

57.20.sa: प्राच्छाद‌मेयात्मा पार्थः शरशतैः कृपम् । स शरैरर्दितः कुद्धः शितैरग्निशिखोपमैः ॥२०॥
57.20.en: Covering the entire sky with his arrows, that powerful warrior of exceeding energy, the son of Pritha assailed Kripa with hundreds of shafts.

57.21.sa: तूर्णं दशसहस्त्रेण पार्थमप्रतिमौजसम् । अर्दयित्वा महात्मानं ननर्द समरे कृपः ॥२१॥
57.21.en: Afflicted with those sharpened shafts resembling flame of fire and worked up with anger, Kripa, assailing soon the high-souled Partha of incomparable energy with ten thousand shafts, sent out a war cry in battle. Then the heroic Arjuna taking up his bow speedily bored through the four horses of his enemy with four dreadful straight and gold winged arrows shot from the Gandiva. Then pierced by sharpened arrows resembling flames of fire those horses all on a sudden sprang up and Kripa fell off from his place. Then seeing Gautama dislodged the son of Kunti.

57.22.sa: ततः कनकपर्वाग्रैर्वीरः सन्नतपर्वभिः । त्वरन् गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैरर्जुनस्तस्य वाजिनः ॥२२॥
57.22.en: Afflicted with those sharpened shafts resembling flame of fire and worked up with anger, Kripa, assailing soon the high-souled Partha of incomparable energy with ten thousand shafts, sent out a war cry in battle. Then the heroic Arjuna taking up his bow speedily bored through the four horses of his enemy with four dreadful straight and gold winged arrows shot from the Gandiva. Then pierced by sharpened arrows resembling flames of fire those horses all on a sudden sprang up and Kripa fell off from his place. Then seeing Gautama dislodged the son of Kunti.

57.23.sa: चतुर्भिश्चतुरस्तीक्ष्णैरविध्यत् परमेषुभिः । ते हया निशितैर्बाणैर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पन्नगैः । उत्पेतुः सहसा सर्वे कृपः स्थानादथाच्यवत् ॥२३॥
57.23.en: Afflicted with those sharpened shafts resembling flame of fire and worked up with anger, Kripa, assailing soon the high-souled Partha of incomparable energy with ten thousand shafts, sent out a war cry in battle. Then the heroic Arjuna taking up his bow speedily bored through the four horses of his enemy with four dreadful straight and gold winged arrows shot from the Gandiva. Then pierced by sharpened arrows resembling flames of fire those horses all on a sudden sprang up and Kripa fell off from his place. Then seeing Gautama dislodged the son of Kunti.

57.24.sa: च्युतं तु गौतमं स्थानात् समीक्ष्य कुरुनन्दनः । नाविध्यत् परवीरघ्नो रक्षमाणोऽस्य गौरवम् ॥२४॥
57.24.en: Afflicted with those sharpened shafts resembling flame of fire and worked up with anger, Kripa, assailing soon the high-souled Partha of incomparable energy with ten thousand shafts, sent out a war cry in battle. Then the heroic Arjuna taking up his bow speedily bored through the four horses of his enemy with four dreadful straight and gold winged arrows shot from the Gandiva. Then pierced by sharpened arrows resembling flames of fire those horses all on a sudden sprang up and Kripa fell off from his place. Then seeing Gautama dislodged the son of Kunti.

57.25.sa: स तु लब्ध्वा पुनः स्थानं गौतमः सव्यसाचिनम् । विव्याध दशभिर्बाणैस्त्वरितः कङ्कपत्रिभिः ॥२५॥
57.25.en: The slayer of hostile heroes, did not wound him for keeping his prestige. Again regaining his position Gautama speedily pierced Savyasachin with ten sharpened and Kanka feathered arrows. Then with one sharpened arrow Partha cut off his bow and gloves. Then he cut off Kripa's coat of mail with sharp arrows capable of piercing to the very vitals but he did not wound him. Then divested of the coat of mail his body appeared.

57.26.sa: ततः पार्थो धनुस्तस्य भल्लेन निशितेन ह । चिच्छेदैकेन भूयश्च हस्तावापमथाहरत् ॥२६॥
57.26.en: The slayer of hostile heroes, did not wound him for keeping his prestige. Again regaining his position Gautama speedily pierced Savyasachin with ten sharpened and Kanka feathered arrows. Then with one sharpened arrow Partha cut off his bow and gloves. Then he cut off Kripa's coat of mail with sharp arrows capable of piercing to the very vitals but he did not wound him. Then divested of the coat of mail his body appeared.

57.27.sa: अथास्य कवचं बाणैर्निशितैर्मर्मभेदिभिः । व्यधमन्न च पार्थोऽस्य शरीरमवपीडयत् ॥२७॥
57.27.en: The slayer of hostile heroes, did not wound him for keeping his prestige. Again regaining his position Gautama speedily pierced Savyasachin with ten sharpened and Kanka feathered arrows. Then with one sharpened arrow Partha cut off his bow and gloves. Then he cut off Kripa's coat of mail with sharp arrows capable of piercing to the very vitals but he did not wound him. Then divested of the coat of mail his body appeared.

57.28.sa: तस्य निर्मुच्यमानस्य कवचात् काय आबभौ । समये मुच्यमानस्य सर्पस्येव तनुर्यथा ॥२८॥

57.29.sa: छिन्ने धनुषि पार्थेन सोऽन्यदादाय कार्मुकम् । चकार गौतमः सज्यं तद‌द्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥२९॥

57.30.sa: स तदप्यस्य कौन्तेयश्चिच्छेद नतपर्वणा । एवमन्यानि चापानि बहूनि कृतहस्तवत् ॥३०॥

57.31.sa: शारद्वतस्य चिच्छेद पाण्डवः परवीरहा । स छिन्नधनुरादाय रथशक्तिं प्रतापवान् ॥३१॥
57.31.en: In this way that slayer of hostile heroes, the son of Pandu, cut off other bows as soon as they were taken up, one after the other, by the son of Sharadvata.

57.32.sa: प्राहिणोत् पाण्डुपुत्राय प्रदीप्तामशनीमिव । तामर्जुनस्तदाऽऽयान्तीं शक्तिं हेमविभूषिताम् ॥३२॥
57.32.en: Having all his bows thus sundered that highly powerful hero took up a javelin from his car resembling a lightning and hurled it at the son of Pandu.

57.33.sa: वियद्गतां महोल्काभां चिच्छेद दशभिः शरैः । साऽपतद्दशधा छिन्ना भूमौ पार्थेन धीमता ॥३३॥
57.33.en: While that golden javelin came coursing through the sky, burning like a huge fire-brand Arjuna cut it off with ten arrows.

57.34.sa: युगपच्चैव भल्लैस्तु ततः सज्यधनुः कृपः । तमाशु निशितैः पार्थं बिभेद दशभिः शरैः ॥३४॥
