57.34.en: As soon as that fell on the ground sundered into a hundred pieces by the intelligent Partha, Kripa took up another ready bow.

57.35.sa: ततः पार्थो महातेजा विशिखानग्नितेजसः । चिक्षेप समरे क्रुद्धस्त्रयोदश शिलाशितान् ॥३५॥
57.35.en: And immediately struck Partha with ten sharp arrows. Then the highly energetic Partha, worked up with rage, discharged thirteen sharp and fiery arrow3; with one he cut off the yoke, with four the four horses and with the sixth he cut off the head of the charioteer with three, the great car-warrior, pierced in battle, the three bamboo poles, and with two his two wheels.

57.36.sa: अथास्य युगमेकेन चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान् । षष्ठेन च शिरः कायाच्छरेण रथसारथेः ॥३६॥
57.36.en: And immediately struck Partha with ten sharp arrows. Then the highly energetic Partha, worked up with rage, discharged thirteen sharp and fiery arrow3; with one he cut off the yoke, with four the four horses and with the sixth he cut off the head of the charioteer with three, the great car-warrior, pierced in battle, the three bamboo poles, and with two his two wheels.

57.37.sa: त्रिभिस्त्रिवेणुं समरे द्वाभ्यामक्षं महारथः । द्वादशेन तु भल्लेन चकर्तास्य ध्वजं तदा ॥३७॥
57.37.en: And immediately struck Partha with ten sharp arrows. Then the highly energetic Partha, worked up with rage, discharged thirteen sharp and fiery arrow3; with one he cut off the yoke, with four the four horses and with the sixth he cut off the head of the charioteer with three, the great car-warrior, pierced in battle, the three bamboo poles, and with two his two wheels.

57.38.sa: ततो वज्रनिकाशेन फाल्गुनः प्रहसन्निव । त्रयोदशेनेन्द्रसमः कृपं वक्षस्यविध्यत ॥३८॥
57.38.en: With the twelfth arrow he cut off his most excellent standard, and with the thirteenth resembling the thunder-bolt, Phalguni the equal of Indra, as if smiling, struck Kripa on the breast. Then with his bow cut off, dislodged from his car, his horses and charioteer slain, leaping down and taking up a mace, he soon hurled it at Arjuna. That shining and greatly polished mace hurled by him, came back baffled by Arjuna's shafts. Then to rescue the revengeful son of Sharadvata, all the soldiers covered Partha in battle on all sides with a downpour of shafts. Then turning the horses to the left and making the circle called Yamaka, Virata's son withstood all those warriors. Then taking Kripa with them, who had been dislodged from his car, all those leading warriors led him away from Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti. f

57.39.sa: स छिन्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः । गदापाणिरवप्लुत्य तूर्णं चिक्षेप तां गदाम् ॥३९॥

57.40.sa: सा च मुक्ता गदा गुर्वी कृपेण सुपरिष्कृता । अर्जुनेन शरैर्नुन्ना प्रतिमार्गमथागमत् ॥४०॥
57.40.en: With the twelfth arrow he cut off his most excellent standard, and with the thirteenth resembling the thunder-bolt, Phalguni the equal of Indra, as if smiling, struck Kripa on the breast. Then with his bow cut off, dislodged from his car, his horses and charioteer slain, leaping down and taking up a mace, he soon hurled it at Arjuna. That shining and greatly polished mace hurled by him, came back baffled by Arjuna's shafts. Then to rescue the revengeful son of Sharadvata, all the soldiers covered Partha in battle on all sides with a downpour of shafts. Then turning the horses to the left and making the circle called Yamaka, Virata's son withstood all those warriors. Then taking Kripa with them, who had been dislodged from his car, all those leading warriors led him away from Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti. f

57.41.sa: तं तु योधाः परीप्सन्तः शारद्वतममर्षणम् । सर्वतः समरे पार्थं शरवर्षैरवाकिरन् ॥४१॥

57.42.sa: ततो विराटस्य सुतो सव्यमावृत्य वाजिनः । यमकं मण्डलं कृत्वा तान् योधान् प्रत्यवारयत् ॥४२॥
57.42.en: With the twelfth arrow he cut off his most excellent standard, and with the thirteenth resembling the thunder-bolt, Phalguni the equal of Indra, as if smiling, struck Kripa on the breast. Then with his bow cut off, dislodged from his car, his horses and charioteer slain, leaping down and taking up a mace, he soon hurled it at Arjuna. That shining and greatly polished mace hurled by him, came back baffled by Arjuna's shafts. Then to rescue the revengeful son of Sharadvata, all the soldiers covered Partha in battle on all sides with a downpour of shafts. Then turning the horses to the left and making the circle called Yamaka, Virata's son withstood all those warriors. Then taking Kripa with them, who had been dislodged from his car, all those leading warriors led him away from Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti. f

57.43.sa: ततः कृपमुपादाय विरथं ते नरर्षभाः । अपजह्रुर्महावेगाः कुन्तीपुत्राद्धनञ्जयात् ॥४३॥
57.43.en: With the twelfth arrow he cut off his most excellent standard, and with the thirteenth resembling the thunder-bolt, Phalguni the equal of Indra, as if smiling, struck Kripa on the breast. Then with his bow cut off, dislodged from his car, his horses and charioteer slain, leaping down and taking up a mace, he soon hurled it at Arjuna. That shining and greatly polished mace hurled by him, came back baffled by Arjuna's shafts. Then to rescue the revengeful son of Sharadvata, all the soldiers covered Partha in battle on all sides with a downpour of shafts. Then turning the horses to the left and making the circle called Yamaka, Virata's son withstood all those warriors. Then taking Kripa with them, who had been dislodged from his car, all those leading warriors led him away from Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti. f

58.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । कृपेऽपनीते द्रोणस्तु प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः । अभ्यद्रवदनाधृष्यः शोणाश्वः श्वेतवाहनम् ॥१॥
58.1.en: Vaishampayana said After Kripa had been taken away, the irrepressible Drona, having red horses, taking up his bow to which an arrow had already been set, rushed towards Arjuna of white horses.

58.2.sa: स तु रुक्मरथं दृष्ट्वा गुरुमायान्तमन्तिकात् । अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठ उत्तरं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥२॥
58.2.en: Seeing near him the preceptor moving on in hi golden chariot, Arjuna the foremost of victors, addressed Uttara saying

58.3.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । यत्रैषा काञ्चनी वेदी ध्वजे यस्य प्रकाशते । उछ्रिता प्रवरे दण्डे पताकाभिरलङ्कृता । अत्र मां वह भद्रं ते द्रोणानीकाय सारथे ॥३॥
58.3.en: May you fare well, O charioteer; take m before Drona's army, on whose high standard appears the emblem of a golden altar and around which flags are streaming, whose car is drawn by red, big, highly beautiful, trained, pleasant-looking and quiet horses of the colour of coral and having copper-coloured faces.

58.4.sa: अश्वाः शोणाः प्रकाशन्ते बृहन्तश्चारुवाहिनः । स्निग्धविद्रुमसंकाशास्ताम्रास्याः प्रियदर्शनाः । युक्ता रथवरे यस्य सर्वशिक्षाविशारदाः ॥४॥

58.5.sa: दीर्घबाहुर्महातेजा बलरूपसमन्वितः । सर्वलोकेषु विक्रान्तो भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान् ॥५॥
58.5.en: Of large arms, great energy, endued with beauty and strength, the powerful son of Bharadvaja is known in all the worlds for his prowess.

58.6.sa: बुद्ध्या तुल्यो ह्युशनसा बृहस्पतिसमो नये । वेदास्तथैव चत्वारो ब्रह्मचर्यं तथैव च ॥६॥
58.6.en: In intelligence he is like Shukra, and in the knowledge of moral laws like Brihaspati. He is equally well-read in the four Vedas, and follows the Brahmacharya mode of life.

58.7.sa: ससंहाराणि सर्वाणि दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि मारिष । धनुर्वेदश्च कार्त्स्न्येन यस्मिन्नित्यं प्रतिष्ठितः ॥७॥
58.7.en: All the celestials weapons with the means of their withdrawal, and the entire science of archery always reside in him.

58.8.sa: क्षमा दमश्च सत्यं च आनृशंस्यमथार्जवम् । एते चान्ये च बहवो यस्मिन्नित्यं द्विजे गुणाः ॥८॥
58.8.en: Forgiveness, self-control, truthfulness, disinclination to injury and straight forwardness these and various other accomplishments always live in that twice-born one.

58.9.sa: तेनाहं योद्धुमिच्छामि महाभागेन संयुगे । तस्मात् तं प्रापयाचार्यं क्षिप्रमुत्तर वाहय ॥९॥

58.10.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अर्जुनेनैवमुक्तस्तु वैराटिर्हेमभूषणान् । चोदयामास तानश्वान् भारद्वाजरथं प्रति ॥१०॥
58.10.en: Thus accosted by Arjuna, Virata's son urged the horses adorned with gold towards the car of Bharadvaja's son.

58.11.sa: तमापतन्तं वेगेन पाण्डवं रथिनां वरम् । द्रोणः प्रत्युद्ययौ पार्थं मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम् ॥११॥
58.11.en: Drona rushed with great force towards Partha, the son of Pandu, the foremost of carwarriors, who was advancing like a mad elephant rushing at another such.

58.12.sa: ततः प्राध्मापयच्छङ्खं भेरीशतनिनादिनम् । प्रचुक्षुभे बलं सर्वमुद्धूत इव सागरः ॥१२॥
58.12.en: Drona then blew his conch, the sound of which resembled that of a hundred trumpets. And the whole army was agitated thereat like the ocean.

58.13.sa: अथ शोणान् सदश्वांस्तान् हंसवर्णैर्मनोजवैः । मिश्रितान् समरे दृष्ट्वा व्यस्मयन्त रणे नराः ॥१३॥
58.13.en: Beholding his excellent red horses mixing with those (of Arjuna) white as swans and fleet as the mind in the encounter, all people were filled with surprise.

58.14.sa: तौ रथौ वीरसंपन्नौ दृष्ट्वा सङ्ग्राममूर्धनि । आचार्यशिष्यावजितौ कृतविद्यौ मनस्विनौ ॥१४॥
58.14.en: Beholding those car-warriors, in the field of battle, the preceptor and disciple, Drona and Partha, both endued with prowess, irrepressible, learned, high-minded and greatly powerful, engaged with each other, the huge army of the Bharatas continually trembled (in fear).

58.15.sa: समाश्लिष्टौ तदाऽन्योन्यं द्रोणपार्थौ महाबलौ । दृष्ट्वा प्राकम्पत मुहुर्भरतानां महद्बलम् ॥१५॥
58.15.en: Beholding those car-warriors, in the field of battle, the preceptor and disciple, Drona and Partha, both endued with prowess, irrepressible, learned, high-minded and greatly powerful, engaged with each other, the huge army of the Bharatas continually trembled (in fear).

58.16.sa: हर्षयुक्तस्ततः पार्थः प्रहसन्निव वीर्यवान् । रथं रथेन द्रोणस्य समासाद्य महारथः ॥१६॥
58.16.en: Reaching Drona's car by his own, the mighty car-warrior and highly energetic Partha was filled with joy, and smiled.

58.17.sa: अभिवाद्य महाबाहुः सामपूर्वमिदं वचः । उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा कौन्तेयः परवीरहा ॥१७॥
58.17.en: Saluting him, the mighty-armed son of Kunti, the slayer of hostile heroes, said in sweet and becoming words.

58.18.sa: उषिताः स्मो वने वासं प्रतिकर्म चिकीर्षवः । कोपं नार्हसि नः कर्तुं सदा समरदुर्जय ॥१८॥
58.18.en: Having spent out the term of our exile in the woods, we wish to take revenge. O you irrepressible in battle, it does not behove you to be always angry.

58.19.sa: अहं तु प्रहृते पूर्वं प्रहरिष्यामि तेऽनघ । इति मे वर्तते बुद्धिस्तद्भवान् कर्तुमर्हति ॥१९॥

58.20.sa: ततोऽस्मै प्राहिणोद्द्रोणः शरानधिकावंशतिम् । अप्राप्तांश्चैव तान् पार्थश्चिच्छेद कृतहस्तवत् ॥२०॥
58.20.en: Thus addressed, Drona discharged at him more than twenty shafts. But the light-handed Partha severed them all before they could fall down on him.

58.21.sa: ततः शरसहस्त्रेण रथं पार्थस्य वीर्यवान् । अवाकिरत् ततो द्रोणः शीघ्रमस्त्रं विदर्शयन् ॥२१॥
58.21.en: Displaying his weapons the energetic Drona soon covered Partha's chariot on all sides with thousands of arrows.

58.22.sa: हयांश्च रजतप्रख्यान् कङ्कपत्रैः शिलाशितैः । अवाकिरदमेयात्मा पार्थं संकोपयन्निव ॥२२॥
58.22.en: As if to work up Partha with anger, that one of incomparable energy covered his horses of silvery hue with sharpened and Kankafeathered arrows.

58.23.sa: एवं प्रववृते युद्धं भारद्वाजकिरीटिनोः । समं विमुञ्चतोः संख्ये विशिखान् दीप्ततेजसः ॥२३॥

58.24.sa: तावुभौ ख्यातकर्माणावुभौ वायुसमौ जवे । उभौ दिव्यास्त्रविदुषावुभावुत्तमतेजसौ । क्षिपन्तौ शरजालानि मोहयामासतुर्नृपान् ॥२४॥

58.25.sa: व्यस्मयन्त ततो योधा ये तत्रासन्समागताः । शरान्विसृजतोस्तूर्णं साधु साध्वित्यपूजयन् ॥२५॥
58.25.en: When they spread a net-work of arrows, they bewildered the kings. And all the warriors, that were present there, were filled with wonder.

58.26.sa: द्रोणं हि समरे कोऽन्यो योद्धुमर्हति फाल्गुनात् । रौद्रः क्षत्रियधर्मोऽयं गुरुणा यदयुध्यत । इत्यब्रुवञ्जनास्तत्र सङ्ग्रामशिरसि स्थिताः ॥२६॥
58.26.en: (They all) admired Drona who quickly shot arrows, exclaiming “Well done! well done! Who else can fight with Drona in battle except Phalguni (Arjuna)?

58.27.sa: वीरौ तावभिसंरब्धौ संनिकृष्टौ महाभुजौ । छादयेतां शरव्रातैरन्योन्यमपराजितौ ॥२७॥
58.27.en: Worked up with anger those two longarmed heroes, confronting each other, and each capable of vanquishing the other, covered each other with arrows.

58.28.sa: विस्फार्य सुमहच्चापं हेमपृष्ठं दुरासदम् । भारद्वाजोऽथ संक्रुद्धः फाल्गुनं प्रत्यविध्यत ॥२८॥
58.28.en: Then inflated with anger, the son of Bharadvaja, drawing his huge bow plated with gold and hard to be severed, struck Phalguni.

58.29.sa: स सायकमयैर्जालैरर्जुनस्य रथं प्रति । भानुमद्भिः शिलाधौतैर्भानोराच्छादयत् प्रभाम् ॥२९॥
58.29.en: Then shooting at Arjuna's car a goodly number of sharp arrows, bright as the sun, he covered the rays of the sun.

58.30.sa: पार्थं च सुमहाबाहुर्महावेगैर्महारथः । विव्याध निशितैर्बाणैर्मेधो वृष्ट्येव पर्वतम् ॥३०॥
58.30.en: That mighty car-warrior of large arms wounded Partha with sharpened arrows, as the clouds discharge showers on a mountain.

58.31.sa: तथैव दिव्यं गाण्डीवं धनुरादाय पाण्डवः । शत्रुघ्नं वेगवान् हृष्टो भारसाधनमुत्तमम् ॥३१॥
58.31.en: Taking up the best of bows, the celestials Gandiva, capable of destroying enemies and carrying a heavy weight, the son of Pandu delightedly.

58.32.sa: विससर्ज शरांश्चित्रान् सुवर्णविकृतान् बहून् । नाशयन् शरवर्षाणि भारद्वाजस्य वीर्यवान् । तूर्णं चापविनिर्मुक्तैस्तद‌द्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥३२॥
58.32.en: Shot a number of variegated golden arrows; and that energetic (hero) baffled the downpour of shafts made by Bharadvaja's son.

58.33.sa: स रथेन चरन् पार्थः प्रेक्षणीयो धनञ्जयः । युगपद्दिक्षु सर्वासु सर्वतोऽस्त्राण्यदर्शयत् ॥३३॥
58.33.en: And speedily discharged arrows from the bow that appeared as wonderful. Moving about in his car, Dhananjaya the son of Pritha, worthy of being looked at.

58.34.sa: एकच्छायमिवाकाशं बाणैश्चक्रे समन्ततः । नादृश्यत तदा द्रोणो नीहारेणेव संवृतः ॥३४॥

58.35.sa: तस्याभवत् तदा रूपं संवृतस्य शरौत्तमैः । जाज्वल्यमानस्य तदा पर्वतस्येव सर्वतः ॥३५॥
58.35.en: Drona was not visible (like the sun) enshrouded mist. Thereupon covered on all sides with excellent arrows, he appeared.

58.36.sa: दृष्ट्वा तु पार्थस्य रणे शरैः स्वरथमावृतम् । स विस्फार्य धनुः श्रेष्ठं मेघस्तनितनिःस्वनम् ॥३६॥
58.36.en: Like a burning mountain. Beholding his own chariot enveloped in the battle by the shafts of Partha.

58.37.sa: अग्निचक्रोपमं घोरं व्यकर्षत् परमायुधम् । व्यशातयच्छरांस्तांस्तु द्रोणः समितिशोभनः ॥३७॥
58.37.en: He, drawing his excellent bow making a sound like that of clouds, took up a huge weapon like a wheel of fire.

58.38.en: Then Drona, ornament of an assembly, discharged sharpened arrows. Then arose a sound like that of bamboo's when set on fire.

58.39.sa: जाम्बूनदमयैः पुङ्खैश्चित्रचापविनिर्गतैः । प्राच्छादयद‌मेयात्मा दिशः सूर्यस्य च प्रभाम् ॥३९॥
58.39.en: That of immeasurable energy enveloped all the quarters and the lustre of the sun with gold-winged arrows discharged from a variegated bow. one

58.40.sa: ततः कनकपुङ्खानां शराणां नतपर्वणाम् । वियच्चाराणां वियति दृश्यन्ते बहवो व्रजाः ॥४०॥
58.40.en: Those arrows, with depressed knots and golden wings, when they passed through the sky, looked like so many birds.

58.41.sa: द्रोणस्य पुङ्खसक्ताश्च प्रभवन्तः शरासनात् । एको दीर्घ इवादृश्यदाकाशे संहतः शरः ॥४१॥

58.42.sa: एवं तौ स्वर्णविकृतान् विमुञ्चन्तौ महाशरान् । आकाशं संवृतं वीरावुल्काभिरिव चक्रतुः ॥४२॥
58.42.en: Those heroes, then shooting their golden arrows, enveloped, as it were the welkin with a downpour of fire-brands.

58.43.sa: शरास्तयोस्तु विबभुः कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः । पङ्क्त्यः शरदि स्वस्थानां हंसानां चरतामिव ॥४३॥
58.43.en: Decked with the feathers of Kanka birds, these arrows looked like a number of cranes wandering in the autumnal sky.

58.44.sa: युद्धं समभवत् तत्र सुसंरब्धं महात्मनोः । द्रोणपाण्डवयोर्घोरं वृत्रवासवयोरिव ॥४४॥
58.44.en: Then there ensued a highly terrific encounter between the high-souled Drona and Arjuna like that between Vritra and Vasava.

58.45.sa: तौ गजाविव चासाद्य विषाणाग्रैः परस्परम् । शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैरन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः ॥४५॥

58.46.sa: तौ व्यवाहरतां युद्धे संरब्धौ रणशोभिनौ । उदीरयन्तौ समरे दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि भागशः ॥४६॥
58.46.en: Those two angry heroes, ornamenting the battle-field, fighting according to the practice, showed many celestials weapons in due order.

58.47.sa: अथ त्वाचार्यमुख्येन शरान् सृष्टान् शिलाशितान् । न्यवारयच्छितैर्बाणैरर्जुनो जयतां वरः ॥४७॥
58.47.en: one Arjuna, the foremost of victors, warded off, with sharp arrows, the sharpened arrows shot by the foremost of preceptors.

58.48.en: Showing many weapons to the spectators, that of dreadful prowess speedily enveloped the sky with many arrows.

58.49.sa: जिघांसन्तं नरव्याघ्रमर्जुनं तिग्मतेजसम् । आचार्यमुख्यः समरे द्रोणः शस्त्रभृतां वरः । अर्जुनेन सहाक्रीडच्छरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥४९॥
58.49.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.50.sa: दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि वर्षन्तं तस्मिन् वै तुमुले रणे । अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य फाल्गुनं समयोधयत् ॥५०॥
58.50.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. 58.52.sa: ऐन्द्रं वायव्यमाग्नेयमस्त्रमस्त्रेण पाण्डवः । द्रोणेन मुक्तमात्रं तु ग्रसति स्म पुनः पुनः ॥५२॥
58.52.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.53.sa: एवं शूरौ महेष्वासौ विसृजन्तौ शितान् शरान् । एकच्छायं चक्रतुस्तावाकाशं शरवृष्टिभिः ॥५३॥

58.54.sa: तत्रार्जुनेन मुक्तानां पततां वै शरीरिषु । पर्वतेष्विव वज्राणां शराणां श्रूयते स्वनः ॥५४॥
58.54.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.55.sa: ततो नागा रथाश्चैव वाजिनश्च विशांपते । शोणिताक्ता व्यदृश्यन्त पुष्पिता इव किंशुकाः ॥५५॥
58.55.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.56.sa: बाहुभिश्च सकेयूरैर्विचित्रैश्च महारथैः । सुवर्णचित्रैः कवचैर्ध्वजैश्च विनिपातितैः ॥५६॥
58.56.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.57.sa: योधैश्च निहतैस्तत्र पार्थबाणप्रपीडितैः । बलमासीत् समुद्भ्रान्तं द्रोणार्जुनसमागमे ॥५७॥

58.58.sa: विधुन्वानौ तु तौ तत्र धनुषी भारसाधने । आच्छादयेतामन्योन्यं ततक्षतुरथेषुभिः ॥५८॥
58.58.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.59.sa: तयोः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं भरतर्षभ । द्रोणकौन्तेययोस्तत्र बलिवासवयोरिव ॥५९॥
58.59.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.60.sa: अथ पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः । व्यदारयेतामन्योन्यं प्राणद्यूते प्रवर्तिते ॥६०॥
58.60.en: (Beholding) Arjuna, the foremost of men, of fierce energy, discharging celestials weapons in that great battle and killing (soldiers) the foremost of preceptors and warriors Drona, played with Arjuna with arrows of depressed knots. And warding off his weapons with his, Bharadvaja's son fought with Arjuna. Then there ensued an encounter between those two foremost of men, worked up with anger and striking each other, like that between the celestials and demons. Arjuna repeatedly warded off with his own, the weapons Aindra, Vayavya and Agneya discharged by Drona. Shooting sharp arrows, those two great heroes converted the sky, with a shade. Coming down on the bodies of the enemy's heroes, the shafts, discharged by Arjuna, made a sound like that of thunderbolt striking against a mountain. Then, o king, the elephants, cars and horses, covered with blood, looked like Kinsuka trees crested with flowers. And in that encounter between Drona and Partha, the field being filled with arms adorned with variegated bangles, mighty car-warriors' golden coats of mail, banners struck down, and warriors slain and assailed by Partha's shafts, the army were terrified. And moving their bows capable of bearing stain, they covered each other with shafts. O foremost of Bharatas, there took place a great encounter between Drona and Arjuna like that between Bali and Vasava. Then with arrows of depressed knots shot from the bows fully drawn, they struck each other even at the risk of their lives. There was heard a voice in the sky speaking highly of Drona.

58.61.sa: अथान्तरिक्षे नादोऽभूद्द्रोणं तत्र प्रशंसताम् । दुष्करं कृतवान्द्रोणो यदर्जुनमयोधयत् ॥६१॥

58.62.sa: प्रमाथिनं महावीर्यं दृढमुष्टिं दुरासदम् । जेतारं देवदैत्यानां सर्वेषां च महारथम् ॥६२॥
58.62.en: Drona has performed a difficult feat for he fights with Arjuna, of great energy, firmhanded, irrepressible and an afflicter of foes.

58.63.sa: अविभ्रमं च शिक्षां च लाघवं दूरपातिताम् । पार्थस्य समरे दृष्ट्वा द्रोणस्याभूच्च विस्मयः ॥६३॥
58.63.en: The conqueror of the celestials and Daityas and of all mighty car-warriors. Beholding in battle Partha's certain aim, training, lightness of hand and the range (of his arrows), Drona was stricken greatly with wonder. Then taking up with his hands the celestials bow Gandiva, the energetic Partha, O foremost of Bharatas, drew it. Beholding the downpour of his shafts coming down like a swarm of locusts, they, all filled with wonder, exclaimed “Well done! well done!" Even the very air could not penetrate into the space intervening between his arrows.

58.64.sa: अथ गाण्डीवमुद्यम्य दिव्यं धनुरमर्षणः । विचकर्ष रणे पार्थो बाहुभ्यां भरतर्षभ ॥६४॥

58.65.sa: तस्य बाणमयं वर्षं शलभानामिवायतिम् । दृष्ट्वा ते विस्मिताः सर्वे साधु साध्वित्यपूजयन् ॥६५॥
58.65.en: The conqueror of the celestials and Daityas and of all mighty car-warriors. Beholding in battle Partha's certain aim, training, lightness of hand and the range (of his arrows), Drona was stricken greatly with wonder. Then taking up with his hands the celestials bow Gandiva, the energetic Partha, O foremost of Bharatas, drew it. Beholding the downpour of his shafts coming down like a swarm of locusts, they, all filled with wonder, exclaimed “Well done! well done!" Even the very air could not penetrate into the space intervening between his arrows.

58.66.sa: न च बाणान्तरे वायुरस्य शक्नोति सर्पितुम् । अनिशं संदधानस्य शरानुत्सृजतस्तथा ॥६६॥
58.66.en: The conqueror of the celestials and Daityas and of all mighty car-warriors. Beholding in battle Partha's certain aim, training, lightness of hand and the range (of his arrows), Drona was stricken greatly with wonder. Then taking up with his hands the celestials bow Gandiva, the energetic Partha, O foremost of Bharatas, drew it. Beholding the downpour of his shafts coming down like a swarm of locusts, they, all filled with wonder, exclaimed “Well done! well done!" Even the very air could not penetrate into the space intervening between his arrows.

58.67.en: The on-lookers could not mark any cessation between Partha's taking up arrows and shooting them.

58.68.sa: तथा शीघ्रास्त्रयुद्धे तु वर्तमानेः सुदारुणे । शीघ्रं शीघ्रतरं पार्थः शरानन्यानुदीरयत् ॥६८॥
58.68.en: In that dreadful battle of quickly discharged weapons Partha, speedily and more speedily, shot arrows.

58.69.sa: ततः शतसहस्त्राणि शराणां नतपर्वणाम् । युगपत् प्रापतंस्तत्र द्रोणस्य रथमन्तिकात् ॥६९॥
58.69.en: Then simultaneously hundreds and thousands of arrows with depressed knots came down upon the car of Drona.

58.70.sa: कीर्यमाणे तदा द्रोणे शरैर्गाण्डीवधन्वना । हाहाकारो महानासीत् सैन्यानां भरतर्षभ ॥७०॥
58.70.en: O foremost of Bharatas, beholding Drona entirely enveloped with shafts shot by the holder of the Gandiva bow, the army set a mighty lamentation.

58.71.sa: पाण्डवस्य तु शीघ्रास्त्रं मघवा प्रत्यपूजयत् । गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव ये च तत्र समागताः ॥७१॥

58.72.sa: ततो वृन्देन महता रथानां रथयूथपः । आचार्यपुत्रः सहसा पाण्डवं पर्यवारयत् ॥७२॥
58.72.en: Then encircled by a vast array of cars, the mighty car-warrior, the son of the preceptor obstructed Partha.

58.73.sa: अश्वत्थामा तु तत् कर्म हृदयेन महात्मनः । पूजयामास पार्थस्य कोपं चास्याकरोद्भृशम् ॥७३॥
58.73.en: Though greatly enraged with him, Ashvathama praised in his mind that deed of the high-souled Arjuna.

58.74.sa: स मन्युवशमापन्नः पार्थमभ्यद्रवद्रणे । किरञ्छरसहस्त्राणि पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान् ॥७४॥
58.74.en: Then possessed by wrath, he encountered Partha in battle and discharged at him a downpour of arrows like clouds discharging their watery contents.

58.75.sa: स तु लब्ध्वाऽन्तरं तूर्णमपायाज्जवनैर्हयैः । छिन्नवर्मध्वजः शूरो निकृत्तः परमेषुभिः ॥७५॥
58.75.en: Then turning his horses towards Drona's son, Partha offered Drona an opportunity to retreat.

59.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततो द्रौणिर्महाराज प्रययावर्जुनं रणे । तं पार्थः प्रतिजग्राह वायुवेगमिवोद्धतम् । शरजालेन महता वर्षमाणमिवाम्बुदम् ॥१॥
59.1.en: Vaishampayana said Then, Drona's son, O king, encountered Arjuna in battle. Partha then faced him, moving like the wind.

59.2.sa: तयोर्देवासुरसमः संनिपातो महानभूत् । किरतोः शरजालानि वृत्रवासवयोरिव ॥२॥

59.3.sa: न स्म सूर्यस्तदा भाति न च वाति समीरणः । शरजालावृते व्योम्नि च्छायाभूते समन्ततः ॥३॥

59.4.en: The sky was enveloped with shafts and there was a shade all around. When the two combatants fought with each other, there was a mighty cracking sound.

59.5.sa: हयानस्यार्जुनः सर्वान् कृतवानल्पजीवितान् । ते राजन्न प्रजानन्त दिशं काञ्चन मोहिताः ॥५॥
59.5.en: Like that of bamboo's when on fire. O conqueror of enemies' cities, greatly assailed by Arjuna, his horses.

59.6.sa: ततो द्रौणिर्महार्वार्यः पार्थस्य विचरिष्यतः । विवरं सूक्ष्ममालोक्य ज्यां चिच्छेद क्षुरेण ह । तदस्यापूजयन् देवाः कर्म दृष्ट्वाऽतिमानुषम् ॥६॥

59.7.sa: द्रोणो भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्चैव महारथाः । साधु साध्विति भाषन्तोऽपूजयन् कर्म तस्य तत् ॥७॥
59.7.en: Exclaiming "Well-done Well-done" Drona, Bhishma, Karna, and the mighty carwarrior Kripa too, applauded his deed.

59.8.sa: ततो द्रौणिर्धनुः श्रेष्ठमपकृष्य रथर्षभम् । पुनरेवाहनत् पार्थं हृदये कङ्कपत्रिभिः ॥८॥
59.8.en: Then drawing his that best of bows, the son of Drona again wounded Partha, the foremost of car-warriors, on the breast with Kanka-feathered shafts.

59.9.sa: ततः पार्थो महाबाहुः प्रहस्य स्वनवत् तदा । योजयामास नवया मौर्व्या गाण्डीवमोजसा ॥९॥

59.10.sa: ततोऽर्धचन्द्रमावृत्य तेन पार्थः समागमत् । वारणेनेव मत्तेन मत्तो वारणयूथपः ॥१०॥
59.10.en: Then drawing his bow to the shape of a crescent, Partha proceeded as an infuriated leader of an elephant herd when met by another.

59.11.sa: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं पृथिव्यामेकवीरयोः । रणमध्ये द्वयोरेवं सुमहल्लोमहर्षणम् ॥११॥
59.11.en: Then there took place a great hair-stirring encounter between those two heroes peerless on earth.

59.12.sa: तौ वीरौ ददृशुः सर्वे कुरवो विस्मयान्विताः । युध्यमानौ महावीर्यौ यूथपाविव संगतौ ॥१२॥
59.12.en: The Kurus, all filled with wonder, saw those two highly powerful heroes like two elephant chiefs.

59.14.sa: अक्षय्याविषुधी दिव्यौ पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः । तेन पार्थो रणे शूरस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः ॥१४॥
59.14.en: And because the high-souled son of Pandu, Partha, has a pair of inexhaustible celestials quivers, he remained in battle unmoved like a mountain.

59.15.sa: अश्वत्थाम्नः पुनर्बाणाः क्षिप्रमभ्यस्यतो रणे । जग्मुः परिक्षयं तूर्णमभूत् तेनाधिकोऽर्जुनः ॥१५॥

59.16.sa: ततः कर्णो महाचापं विकृष्याभ्यधिकं तथा । अवाक्षिपत् ततः शब्दो हाहाकारो महानभूत् ॥१६॥
59.16.en: Then drawing to its full his huge bow, Karna twanged it, and thee arose exclamations of Alas!"

59.17.sa: ततश्चक्षुर्दधे पार्थो यत्र विस्फार्यते धनुः । ददर्श तत्र राधेयं तस्य कोपो व्यवर्धत ॥१७॥
59.17.en: Then Partha looked forward to where from came the twang of the bow and saw the son of Radha, at which his anger was excited.

59.18.sa: स रोषवशमापन्नः कर्णमेव जिघांसया । तमैक्षत विवृत्ताभ्यां नेत्राभ्यां कुरुपुङ्गवः ॥१८॥
59.18.en: Desirous of slaying Karna and possessed by anger, that foremost of Kurus looked towards him with expanded eyes.

59.19.sa: तथा तु विमुखे पार्थे द्रोणपुत्रस्य सायकात् । त्वरिताः पुरुषा राजन्नुपाजह्रुः सहस्रशः ॥१९॥
59.19.en: Then Partha going away from the son of Drona, his men, o king, shot thousands of arrows at him (Partha).

59.20.sa: उत्सृज्य च महावाहुर्द्रोणपुत्रं धनञ्जयः । अभिदुद्राव सहसा कर्णमेव सपत्नजित् ॥२०॥
59.20.en: Leaving behind the son of Drona, the mighty-armed Dhananjaya, the conqueror of enemies, rushed towards Karna.

59.21.sa: तमभिद्रुत्य कौन्तेयः क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः । कामयन् द्वैरथं तेन युद्धं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥२१॥
59.21.en: Approaching him and desiring a duel, the son of Kunti, having his eyes reddened with anger, said.

60.1.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । कर्ण यत् ते सभामध्ये बहु वाचा विकत्थितम् । न मे युधि समोऽस्तीति तदिदं समुपस्थितम् ॥१॥
60.1.en: Arjuna said O Karna, this is the time for you to make good the boastful words you gave vent to in the midst of assembly, 'there is none equal to me in fight.'

60.2.sa: सोऽद्य कर्ण मया सार्धं व्यवहृत्य महामृधे । ज्ञास्यस्यबलमात्मानं न चान्यानवमन्यसे ॥२॥
60.2.en: Fighting with me today in the encounter, O Karna, you will know your strength and will never disregard others.

60.3.sa: अवोचः परुषा वाचो धर्ममृत्सृज्य केवलम् । इदं तु दुष्करं मन्ये यदिदं ते चिकीर्षितम् ॥३॥
60.3.en: Disregarding piety, you had given vent to many harsh words. But I consider what you wish to do today as difficult.

60.4.sa: यत् त्वया कथितं पूर्वं मामनासाद्य किंचन । तदद्य कुरु राधेय कुरुमध्ये मया सह ॥४॥

60.5.sa: यत्सभायां स पाञ्चालीं क्लिश्यमानां दुरात्मभिः । दृष्टवानसि तस्याद्य फलमाप्नुहि केवलम् ॥५॥
60.5.en: Do you reap now the fruit of your suffering the Panchala princess to-be distressed by the wicked-souled one in the court.

60.6.sa: धर्मपाशनिबद्धेन यन्मया मर्षितं पुरा । तस्य राधेय कोपस्य विजयं पश्य मे मृधे ॥६॥

60.7.sa: वने द्वादश वर्षाणि यानि सोढानि दुर्मते । तस्याद्य प्रतिकोपस्य फलं प्राप्नुहि संप्रति ॥७॥
60.7.en: O wicked one, we have undergone many miseries in the forest for twelve years. Do you now reap the fruit of our vengeance today

60.8.sa: एहि कर्ण मया सार्धं प्रतियुध्यस्व सङ्गरे । प्रेक्षकाः कुरवः सर्वे भवन्तु तव सैनिकाः ॥८॥
60.8.en: Do you fight with me, O Karna, in the battle. Let the Kurus and your soldiers witness it.

60.9.sa: कर्ण उवाच । ब्रवीषि वाचा यत् पार्थ कर्मणा तत् समाचर । अतिशेते हि ते वाक्यं कर्मैतत् प्रथितं भुवि ॥९॥
60.9.en: Karna said Do you carry out your words into action, O Partha. That your words exceed your deeds is known in the world.

60.10.sa: यत् त्वया मर्षितं पूर्वं तदशक्तेन मर्षितम् । इतो गृह्णीमहे पार्थ तव दृष्ट्वा पराक्रमम् ॥१०॥
60.10.en: What you deed suffer formerly was in consequence of your inability. We can admit today by seeing your prowess, O Partha.

60.11.sa: धर्मपाशनिबद्धेन यत् त्वया मर्षितं पुरा । तथैव बद्धमात्मानमबद्धमिव मन्यसे ॥११॥
60.11.en: If you had suffered the miseries by having been bound by the noose or morality, you are equally bound so even now though you consider yourself free.

60.12.sa: यदि तावद्वने वासो यथोक्तश्चरितस्त्वया । तत्त्वं धर्मार्थवित्क्लिष्टः स मया योद्धुमिच्छसि ॥१२॥
60.12.en: If you had passed your exile in the same way as you said, and being distressed (for practising austerities) why do you conversant with Dharma and Artha as you are, wish to fight with me?

60.13.sa: यदि शक्रः स्वयं पार्थ युध्यते तव कारणात् । तथाऽपि न व्यथा काचिन्मम स्याद्विक्रमिष्यतः ॥१३॥
60.13.en: If Shakra himself, O Partha, fight on your behalf, still, there will be no obstruction to my displaying my prowess.

60.14.sa: अयं कौन्तेय कामस्ते न चिरात् समुपस्थितः । योत्स्यसे हि मया सार्धमद्य द्रक्ष्यसि मे बलम् ॥१४॥
60.14.en: Your wish O son of Kunti, is about to be fulfilled. You will fight with me today and see my prowess.

60.15.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । इदानीमेव तावत्त्वमपयातो रणान्मम । तेन जीवसि राधेय निहतस्त्वनुजस्तव ॥१५॥
60.15.en: Arjuna said Up to now you had always fled from the battle while fighting with me. For this, you are still alive; but your younger brother has been slain, O son of Radha.

60.16.sa: भ्रातरं घातयित्वा कस्त्यक्त्वा रणशिरश्च कः । त्वदन्यः कः पुमान् सत्सु ब्रूयादेवं व्यवस्थितः ॥१६॥
60.16.en: Having seen his younger brother slain, what other man except you, would retreat from the battle-field, and then boast as you do in the midst of good men?

60.17.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । इति कर्णं ब्रुवन्नेव बीभत्सुरपराजितः । अभ्ययाद्विसृजन् बाणान् कायावरणभेदिनः ॥१७॥
60.17.en: Vaishampayana said Having thus spoken to Karna, unconquerable Bibhatsu, encountered him, discharging arrows capable of piercing the coats of mail.

60.18.sa: प्रतिजग्राह तं कर्णः प्रीयमाणो महारथः । महता शरवर्षेण वर्षमाणमिवाम्बुदम् ॥१८॥
60.18.en: The mighty car-warrior Karna delightedly received it with a heavy downpour of arrows like a shower of clouds.

60.19.sa: उत्पेतुः शरजालानि घोररूपाणि सर्वशः । अविध्यदश्वान् बाह्वोश्च हस्तावापं पृथक् पृथक् ॥१९॥
60.19.en: That dreadful network of arrows covered, on all sides, piercing severally, the horses, arms and gloves (of the hero).

60.20.sa: सोऽमृष्यमाणः कर्णस्य निषङ्गस्यावलम्बनम् । चिच्छेद निशिताग्रेण शरेण नतपर्वणा ॥२०॥
60.20.en: Unable to bear the attack of Karna, Arjuna cut off the string of his quiver with a keenedged and straight arrow.

60.21.sa: उपासङ्गादुपादाय कर्णो बाणानथापरान् । विव्याध पाण्डवं हस्ते तस्य मुष्टिरशीर्यत ॥२१॥

60.22.sa: ततः पार्थो महाबाहुः कर्णस्य धनुरच्छिनत् । स शक्तिं प्राहिणोत् तस्मै तां पार्थो व्यधमच्छरैः ॥२२॥
60.22.en: Then the large-armed Arjuna cut off Karnas bow into pieces. He then struck (Arjuna) with a Shakti, but Partha cut it off with his arrows.

60.23.sa: ततोऽनुपेतुर्बहवो राधेयस्य पदानुगाः । तांश्च गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैः प्राहिणोद्यमसादनम् ॥२३॥
60.23.en: Then the heroes who followed Karna all attacked Arjunat who killed them with arrows shot from his Gandiva bow.

60.24.sa: ततोऽस्याश्वान् शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बीभत्सुर्भारसाधनैः। आकर्णमुक्तैरभ्यघ्नंस्ते हताः प्रापतन् भुवि ॥२४॥
60.24.en: Then Bibhatsu killed his horses with sharpened arrows shot from his bow drawn to the ears, and they all fell down slain on earth.

60.25.sa: अथापरेण बाणेन ज्वलितेन महौजसा । विव्याध कर्णं कौन्तेयस्तीक्ष्णेनोरसि वीर्यवान् ॥२५॥
60.25.en: Then taking up another strong, sharp, and powerful arrow, the powerful son of Kunti struck Karna with it on his breast.

60.26.sa: तस्य भित्त्वा तनुत्राणं कायमभ्यगमच्छरः । ततः स तमसाऽऽविष्टो न स्म किंचित्प्रजज्ञिवान् ॥२६॥
60.26.en: Boring through his coat of mail, that arrow penetrated into his body and he was deprived of the power of perception and consciousness.

60.27.sa: स गाढवेदनो हित्वा रणं प्रायादुदङ्मुखः । ततोऽर्जुन उद‌क्रोशदुत्तरश्च महारथः ॥२७॥
60.27.en: Experiencing a great pain and leaving the battle-field, he fled towards the north. Then Arjuna and the mighty car-warrior Uttara began to scoff him.

61.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततो वैकर्तनं जित्वा पार्थो वैराटिमब्रवीत् । एतन्मां प्रापयानीकं यत्र तालो हिरण्मयः ॥१॥
61.1.en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon having vanquished Vaikartanas son (Karna), Arjuna said to Virata's son (Uttara). "Take me to that army where is seen the emblem of golden palmyra.

61.2.sa: अत्र शान्तनवो भीष्मो रथेऽस्माकं पितामहः। क्वाङ्क्षमाणो मया युद्धं तिष्ठत्यमरदर्शनः ॥२॥
61.2.en: There our grand-father, Bhishma the son of Shantanu looking like an immortal, wait on his car, desirous of an encounter with me.

61.3.sa: अथ सैन्यं महद्दृष्ट्वा रथनागहयाकुलम् । अब्रवीदुत्तरः पार्थमपविद्धः शरैर्भृशम् ॥३॥
61.3.en: Then beholding the huge army consisting of cars, elephants and iorses, and being wounded greatly with arrows Uttara said to Partha.

61.4.sa: नाहं शक्ष्यामि वीरेह नियन्तुं ते हयोत्तमान् । विषीदन्ति मम प्राणा मनो विह्वलतीव मे ॥४॥
61.4.en: "O hero, I am incapable of restraining here your excellent horses. My vital breaths are being exhausted and my mind is bewildered.

61.5.sa: अस्त्राणामिव दिव्यानां प्रभावः संप्रयुज्यताम् । त्वया च कुरुभिश्चैव द्रवन्तीव दिशो दश ॥५॥
61.5.en: The ten quarters appear as if melting away on account of the effulgence of the celestials weapon used by you as well as by the Kurus.

61.6.sa: गन्धेन मूर्छितश्चाहं वसारुधिरमेदसाम् । द्वैधीभूतं मनो मेऽद्य तव चैव प्रपश्यतः ॥६॥
61.6.en: I am beside myself with the smell of flesh, blood and fat. Beholding your feat, my mind has been divided in twain.

61.7.sa: अदृष्टपूर्वः शूराणां मया संख्ये समागमः । गदापातेन महता शङ्खानां निःस्वनेन च ॥७॥
61.7.en: I had never seen before in battle such an assemblage of heroes. By the great sound of the clashing of maces, the blare of conchs

61.8.sa: सिंहनादैश्च शूराणां गजानां बृंहितैस्तथा । गाण्डीवशब्देन भृशमशनिप्रतिमेन च । श्रुतिः स्मृतिश्च मे वीर प्रनष्टा मूढचेतसः ॥८॥
61.8.en: By the war-cries of the heroes, the roars of elephants, by the twang of the Gandiva resembling the sound of lightning.

61.9.sa: अलातचक्रप्रतिमं मण्डलं सततं त्वया । व्याक्षिप्यमाणं समरे गाण्डीवं च प्रकर्षता । दृष्टिः प्रचलिता वीर हृदयं दीर्यतीव मे ॥९॥
61.9.en: I have been so stupified, O hero, that I have been deprived of the power hearing and recollecting. Beholding you making, a circle in battle while drawing your Gandiva bow my vision is growing dilated, O hero, and my heart is rending asunder.

61.10.sa: वपुश्चोग्रं तव रणे क्रुद्धस्येव पिनाकिनः । व्यायच्छतस्तव भुजं दृष्ट्वा भीर्मे भवत्यपि ॥१०॥
61.10.en: Beholding your dreadful figure in battle resembling that of the holder of Pinaka when worked up with anger and as well as the terrible arrows discharged by you, I am filled with fear.

61.11.sa: नाददानं न संधानं न मुञ्चन्तं शरोत्तमान् । त्वामहं संप्रपश्यामि पश्यन्नपि न चेतनः ॥११॥
61.11.en: I am at a loss to find out when you take up your fine arrows, set them on your bowstring and shoot them. Deprived of my consciousness, I do not see you, although before my eyes.

61.12.sa: अवसीदन्ति मे प्राणा भूरियं चलतीव च । न च प्रतोदं रश्मींश्च संयन्तुं शक्तिरस्ति मे ॥१२॥
61.12.en: My vitality is sinking and the earth seems moving before me. I have no power to hold the reins of these horses.

61.13.sa: अर्जुन उवाच । मा भैषीः स्तम्भयात्मानं त्वयाऽपि नरपुङ्गव । अत्यद्भुतानि कर्माणि कृतानि रणमूर्धनि ॥१३॥
61.13.en: Arjuna said Do not fear; cheer yourself up. You too, O foremost of men, performed many wonderful deeds in the battle-field.

61.14.sa: राजपुत्रोऽसि भद्रं ते कुले मत्स्यस्य विश्रुते । जातस्त्वं शत्रुदमने नावसीदितुमर्हसि ॥१४॥
61.14.en: May you fare well. You are a prince born, in the well-known race of Matsya, for vanquishing your enemies. You should not therefore be dispirited.

61.15.sa: धृतिं कृत्वा सुविपुलां राजपुत्र रथे मम । युध्यमानस्य समरे हयान् संयच्छ शत्रुहन् ॥१५॥
61.15.en: Stationed on my car, call up your great energy, O prince. Restrain my horses in battle, O slayer of enemies.

61.16.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्वैराटिं नरसत्तमः । अर्जुनो रथिनां श्रेष्ठ उत्तरं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥१६॥
61.16.en: Vaishampayana said Having thus addressed the son of Virata, the foremost of men Arjuna the best of carwarriors again said to Uttara.

61.17.sa: सेनाग्रमाशु भीष्मस्य प्रापयस्वैतदेव माम् । आच्छेत्स्याम्यहमेतस्य धनुर्ज्यामपि चाहवे ॥१७॥
61.17.en: Take me again before Bhishma's army. I shall cut off his bowstring in battle.

61.18.sa: अस्यन्तं दिव्यमस्त्रं मां चित्रमद्य निशामय । शतह्रदामिवायान्तीं स्तनयित्नोरिवाम्बरे ॥१८॥
61.18.en: You will see today the divine weapons, aglow with beauty, shot by me, flashing like lightning in the midst of clouds in the sky.

61.19.sa: सुवर्णपृष्ठं गाण्डीवं द्रक्ष्यन्ति कुरवो मम । दक्षिणेनाथ वामेन कतरेण स्विदस्यति ॥१९॥
61.19.en: The Kurus shall see my Gandiva with back made of gold. The enemies assembled together shall discuss by saying "By which hand of his, right or left, does he discharge arrows." I shall make a terrible river to flow today towards the other world, with blood for its water, the cars for the eddies and the elephants for the sharks. I shall, with arrows of depressed knots, cut off the Kuru forest having hands feet, heads, backs and arms for the branches of the trees. And vanquishing alone the Kuru army with a bow in hand, there will be a hundred roads to me as to fire in the forest. Struck by me, you will see, the army whirling only like a wheel.

61.20.sa: इति मां सङ्गताः सर्वे तर्कयिष्यन्ति शत्रवः । शोणितोदां रथावर्तां नागनक्रां दुरत्ययाम् । नदीं प्रस्कन्दयिष्यामि परलोकप्रवाहिनीम् ॥२०॥
61.20.en: The Kurus shall see my Gandiva with back made of gold. The enemies assembled together shall discuss by saying "By which hand of his, right or left, does he discharge arrows." I shall make a terrible river to flow today towards the other world, with blood for its water, the cars for the eddies and the elephants for the sharks. I shall, with arrows of depressed knots, cut off the Kuru forest having hands feet, heads, backs and arms for the branches of the trees. And vanquishing alone the Kuru army with a bow in hand, there will be a hundred roads to me as to fire in the forest. Struck by me, you will see, the army whirling only like a wheel.

61.21.sa: पाणिपादशिरःपृष्ठबाहुशाखानिरन्तरम् । वनं कुरूणां छेत्स्यामि शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥२१॥
61.21.en: The Kurus shall see my Gandiva with back made of gold. The enemies assembled together shall discuss by saying "By which hand of his, right or left, does he discharge arrows." I shall make a terrible river to flow today towards the other world, with blood for its water, the cars for the eddies and the elephants for the sharks. I shall, with arrows of depressed knots, cut off the Kuru forest having hands feet, heads, backs and arms for the branches of the trees. And vanquishing alone the Kuru army with a bow in hand, there will be a hundred roads to me as to fire in the forest. Struck by me, you will see, the army whirling only like a wheel.

61.22.sa: जयतः कौरवीं सेनामेकस्य मम धन्विनः । शतं मार्गा भविष्यन्ति पावकस्येव कानने ॥२२॥
61.22.en: The Kurus shall see my Gandiva with back made of gold. The enemies assembled together shall discuss by saying "By which hand of his, right or left, does he discharge arrows." I shall make a terrible river to flow today towards the other world, with blood for its water, the cars for the eddies and the elephants for the sharks. I shall, with arrows of depressed knots, cut off the Kuru forest having hands feet, heads, backs and arms for the branches of the trees. And vanquishing alone the Kuru army with a bow in hand, there will be a hundred roads to me as to fire in the forest. Struck by me, you will see, the army whirling only like a wheel.

61.23.sa: मया चक्रमिवाविद्धं सैन्यं द्रक्ष्यसि केवलम् । इष्वस्त्रे शिक्षितं चित्रमहं दर्शयिताऽस्मि ते ॥२३॥
61.23.en: The Kurus shall see my Gandiva with back made of gold. The enemies assembled together shall discuss by saying "By which hand of his, right or left, does he discharge arrows." I shall make a terrible river to flow today towards the other world, with blood for its water, the cars for the eddies and the elephants for the sharks. I shall, with arrows of depressed knots, cut off the Kuru forest having hands feet, heads, backs and arms for the branches of the trees. And vanquishing alone the Kuru army with a bow in hand, there will be a hundred roads to me as to fire in the forest. Struck by me, you will see, the army whirling only like a wheel.

61.24.sa: असंभ्रान्तो रथे तिष्ठ समेषु विषमेषु च । दिवमावृत्य तिष्ठन्तं गिरिं भिन्द्यां स्म पत्रिभिः ॥२४॥

61.25.sa: अहमिन्द्रस्य वचनात् सङ्ग्रामेऽभ्यहनं पुरा । पौलोमान् कालखञ्जांश्च सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥२५॥
61.25.en: Formerly at Indra's command I killed hundreds and thousands of Paulomas and Kalakhajs in battle. I have obtained the firmness of grasp from Indra and successful aim from Brahma.

61.26.sa: अहमिन्द्राद्दृढां मुष्टिं ब्रह्मणः कृतहस्तताम् । प्रगाढे तुमुलं चित्रमिति विद्धि प्रजापतेः ॥२६॥
61.26.en: Formerly at Indra's command I killed hundreds and thousands of Paulomas and Kalakhajs in battle. I have obtained the firmness of grasp from Indra and successful aim from Brahma.

61.27.sa: अहं पारे समुद्रस्य हिरण्यपुरवासिनाम् । जित्वा षष्टिं सहस्त्राणि रथिनामुग्रधन्विनाम् ॥२७॥
61.27.en: I have learnt from Prajapati the diverse kinds of fierce warfare. On the other side of the ocean, I defeated sixty thousand car-warriors all dreadful archers living in Hiranyapura. Behold me, today striking down the vast number of Kurus like a high wind scattering a heap of cotton. By the power of my arrows I shall set fire to the Kuru forest having standards for the trees, the infantry for the shrubs and the car-warriors for the beasts of prey. Like the holder of thunder routing the demons alone shall I today with my straight arrows strike down from the nests of their cars the Kurus fighting to the best of their power in battle.

61.28.sa: शीर्यमाणानि कूलानि प्रवृद्धेनेव वारिणा । मया कुरूणां वृन्दानि पात्यमानानि पश्य वै ॥२८॥
61.28.en: I have learnt from Prajapati the diverse kinds of fierce warfare. On the other side of the ocean, I defeated sixty thousand car-warriors all dreadful archers living in Hiranyapura. Behold me, today striking down the vast number of Kurus like a high wind scattering a heap of cotton. By the power of my arrows I shall set fire to the Kuru forest having standards for the trees, the infantry for the shrubs and the car-warriors for the beasts of prey. Like the holder of thunder routing the demons alone shall I today with my straight arrows strike down from the nests of their cars the Kurus fighting to the best of their power in battle.

61.30.sa: तानहं रथनीडेभ्यः शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः । यत्तान् सर्वानतिबलान् योत्स्यमानानवस्थितान् । एकः संकालयिष्यामि वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान् ॥३०॥
61.30.en: I have learnt from Prajapati the diverse kinds of fierce warfare. On the other side of the ocean, I defeated sixty thousand car-warriors all dreadful archers living in Hiranyapura. Behold me, today striking down the vast number of Kurus like a high wind scattering a heap of cotton. By the power of my arrows I shall set fire to the Kuru forest having standards for the trees, the infantry for the shrubs and the car-warriors for the beasts of prey. Like the holder of thunder routing the demons alone shall I today with my straight arrows strike down from the nests of their cars the Kurus fighting to the best of their power in battle.

61.31.sa: रौद्रं रुद्रादहं ह्यस्त्रं वारुणं वरुणादपि । अस्त्रमाग्नेयमग्नेश्च वायव्यं मातरिश्वनः । वज्रादीनि तथाऽस्त्राणि शक्रादहमवाप्तवान् ॥३१॥

61.32.sa: धार्तराष्ट्रवनं घोरं नरसिंहाभिरक्षितम् । अहमुत्पाटयिष्यामि वैराटे व्येतु ते भयम् ॥३२॥

61.33.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवमाश्वासितस्तेन वैराटिः सव्यसाचिना । व्यवागाहद्रथानीकं भीमं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् ॥३३॥
61.33.en: Thus consoled by Savyasachin the son of Virata entered into that dreadful array of cars protected by Bhishma.

61.34.sa: तमायान्तं महाबाहुं जिगीषन्तं रणे कुरून् । अभ्यवारयदव्यग्रः क्रूरकर्माऽऽपगासुतः ॥३४॥
61.34.en: The patient Bhishma (the son of river) withstood the mighty armed Arjuna advancing with a view to vanquish the Kurus in battle.

61.35.sa: तस्य जिष्णुरुपावृत्य ध्वजं मूलादपातयत् । विकृष्य कलधौताग्रैः स विद्धः प्रापतद्भुवि ॥३५॥
61.35.en: Then approaching him and drawing out a sharp arrow, Vishnu cut off with it the root of his banner. Struck down it fell on the ground.

61.36.sa: तं चित्रमाल्याभरणाः कृतविद्या मनस्विनः । आगच्छन् भीमधन्वानं चत्वारश्च महाबलाः ॥३६॥
61.36.en: At this the four powerful heroes Dushasana, Vikarana, Dussaha and Vivinshati, skilled in the use of weapons, gifted with great energy and adorned with beautiful garlands and ornaments, approaching, withstood that dreadful bowman Bibhatsu.

61.37.sa: दुःशासनो विकर्णश्च दुःसहोऽथ विविंशतिः । आगत्य भीमधन्वानं बीभत्सुं पर्यवारयन् ॥३७॥
61.37.en: At this the four powerful heroes Dushasana, Vikarana, Dussaha and Vivinshati, skilled in the use of weapons, gifted with great energy and adorned with beautiful garlands and ornaments, approaching, withstood that dreadful bowman Bibhatsu.

61.38.sa: दुःशासनस्तु भल्लेन विद्ध्वा वैराटमुत्तरम् । द्वितीयेनार्जुनं वीरः प्रत्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे ॥३८॥
61.38.en: Having pierced Virata's son Uttara with a dart, the heroic Dushasana struck Arjuna on the breast with a second one.

61.39.sa: तस्य जिष्णुरुपावृत्य पृथुधारेण कार्मुकम् । चकर्त गार्ध्रपत्रेण जातरूपपरिष्कृतम् ॥३९॥

61.40.sa: अथैनं पञ्चभिः पश्चात् प्रत्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे । सोऽपयातो रणं हित्वा पार्थबाणप्रपीडितः ॥४०॥
61.40.en: He then wounded him on his breast with five arrows. Assailed by the arrows of Partha, he left the battle-field.

61.41.sa: तं विकर्णः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गृध्रपत्रैरजिह्मगैः । विव्याध परवीरघ्नमर्जुनं धृतराष्ट्रजः ॥४१॥
61.41.en: Then with sharp and straight arrows having the wings of vultures, Dhritarashtra's son Vikarana sounded Arjuna, the slayer of hostile heroes.

61.42.sa: ततस्तमपि कौन्तेयः शरेणानतपर्वणा । ललाटेऽभ्यहनत् तूर्णं स विद्धः प्रापतद्रथात् ॥४२॥
61.42.en: Immediately also the son of Kunti wounded him on his forehead with straight arrows. Thus wounded, he fell down from his chariot.

61.43.sa: ततः पार्थमभिद्रुत्य दुःसहः स विविंशतिः । अवाकिरच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैः परीप्सुर्भ्रातरं रणे ॥४३॥
61.43.en: With a view to rescue his brother in battle, Dussaha, accompanied by Vivinshati, approached Partha and covered him with sharp arrows.

61.44.sa: तावुभौ गार्ध्रपत्राभ्यां निशिताभ्यां धनञ्जयः। विद्ध्वा युगपदव्यग्रस्तयोर्वाहानसूदयत् ॥४४॥
61.44.en: Not the least excited Dhananjaya simultaneously struck both of them with a pair of sharp arrows and destroyed the horses of the both.

61.45.sa: तौ हताश्वौ विभिन्नाङ्गौ धृतराष्ट्रात्मजावुभौ । अभिपत्य रथैरन्यैरपनीतौ पदानुगैः ॥४५॥
61.45.en: Having their horses slain and persons wounded, both the sons of Dhritarashtra were taken away by their followers who came there with other chariots.

61.46.sa: सर्वा दिशश्चाभ्यपतद्बिभत्सुरपराजितः । किरीटमाली कौन्तेयो लब्धलक्षो महाबलः ॥४६॥
61.46.en: Bibhatsu, never defeated in battle-the highly powerful son of Kunti, adorned with a diadem and having sure aim, covered all the quarters with his arrows.

62.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । अथ सङ्गम्य सर्वे ते कौरवाणां महारथाः । अर्जुनं सहिता यत्ताः प्रत्ययुध्यन्त भारत ॥१॥
62.1.en: Vaishampayana said O descendant of Bharata, then united together all the mighty car-warriors of the Kuru army began to strike Arjuna collectively.

62.2.sa: स सायकमयैर्जालैः सर्वतस्तान् महारथान् । प्राच्छाद्यदमेयात्मा नीहारेणेव पर्वतान् ॥२॥
62.2.en: That one of incomparable energy covered, on all sides, all those mighty car-warriors with a net-work of arrows as the mountains are covered with dews.

62.3.sa: नदद्भिश्च महानागैर्ह्रेषमाणैश्च वाजिभिः । भेरीशङ्खनिनादैश्च स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥३॥
62.3.en: The huge elephants roaring, the horses neighing and the bugles and conchs being sounded, there arose a great tumult.

62.4.sa: नराश्वकायान्निर्भिद्य लौहानि कवचानि च । पार्थस्य शरजालानि विनिष्पतुः सहस्रशः ॥४॥
62.4.en: Piercing the bodies of elephants and horses as also the iron coats of mail, the arrows of Partha dropped down in thousands.

62.5.sa: त्वरमाणः शरानस्यन्पाण्डवः प्रबभौ रणे । मध्यन्दिनगतोऽर्चिष्मान् शरदीव दिवाकरः ॥५॥
62.5.en: Shooting speedily his arrows, the son of Pandu looked in battle like the blazing mid-day sun of the autumn.

62.6.sa: उपप्लवन्ति वित्रस्ता रथेभ्यो रथिनस्तथा । सादिनश्चाश्वपृष्ठेभ्यो भूमौ चैव पदातयः ॥६॥
62.6.en: Possessed by fear, the car-warriors began to leap down from their cars, the horse-men from horse-back, and the infantry to fly away.

62.7.sa: शरैः संच्छिद्यमानानां कवचानां महात्मनाम् । ताम्रराजतलौहानां प्रादुरासीन्महास्वनः ॥७॥
62.7.en: There arose a great sound when the arrows of the high-souled Arjuna pierced the copper, silver and iron made coats of mail.

62.8.sa: छन्नमायोधनं सर्वं शरीरैर्गतचेतसाम् । गजाश्वसादिनां तत्र शितबाणात्तजीवितैः ॥८॥
62.8.en: The field was soon filled with the corpses of the warriors mounted on elephants and horses, killed by sharpened arrows.

62.9.sa: रथोपस्थामिपतितैरास्तृता मानवैर्मही । प्रनृत्यतीव सङ्ग्रामे चापहस्तो धनञ्जयः ॥९॥
62.9.en: The earth was covered with dead bodies of men fallen down from the chariots where they were. Dhananjaya as if danced in the battlefield with bow in his hand.

62.10.sa: श्रुत्वा गाण्डीवनिर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः । त्रस्तानि सर्वसैन्यानि व्यपागच्छन्महाहवात् ॥१०॥
62.10.en: Hearing the twang of Gandiva like the rumble of thunder and being possessed by fear, all the soldiers fled away from the battle-field.

62.11.sa: कुण्डलोष्णीषधारीणि जातरूपस्त्रजस्तथा । पतितानि स्म दृश्यन्ते शिरांसि रणमूर्धनि ॥११॥
62.11.en: 1 There were seen, fallen in the battle-field, heads having earrings and helmets and golden necklaces.

62.12.sa: विशिखोन्मथितैर्गात्रैर्बाहुभिश्च सकार्मुकैः । सहस्ताभरणैश्चान्यैः प्रच्छन्ना भाति मेदिनी ॥१२॥

62.13.en: O best of the Bharata race, on account of the heads cut off by sharpened arrows, falling continually on the ground, it appeared that a shower of stones fell from the sky.

62.14.sa: दर्शयित्वा तथाऽऽत्मानं रौद्रं रुद्रपराक्रमः । अवरुद्धोऽचरत्पार्थो वर्षाणि त्रिदशानि च । क्रोधाग्निमुत्सृजन् वीरो धार्तराष्ट्रेषु पाण्डवः ॥१४॥
62.14.en: Displaying his own fierce prowess, Partha of dreadful prowess ranged in the battle-field pouring his celestials weapons.

62.15.sa: तस्य तद्दहतः सैन्यं दृष्ट्वा चैव पराक्रमम् । सर्वे शान्तिपरा योधा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पश्यतः॥१५॥
62.15.en: The dreadful son of Pandu discharging his fire of anger at the sons of Dhritarashtra and beholding his dreadful prowess burning down the army.

62.16.sa: वित्रासयित्वा तत्सैन्यं द्रावयित्वा महारथान् । अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठः पर्यवर्तत भारत ॥१६॥

62.17.sa: प्रावर्तयन्नदीं घोरां शोणितोदां तरङ्गिणीम् । अस्थिशैवालसम्बाधां युगान्ते कालनिर्मिताम् ॥१७॥
62.17.en: Arjuna, the foremost of victors, ranged in the battle-field. He made a river of mighty currents having blood for the water to flow,

62.18.en: Having coats of mail and turbans floating on the surface, the elephants standing for islands. The marrow, fat and blood constituted the greatly terrific currents.

62.19.en: It was dreadful and highly terrific, resounding with the yells of ferocious beasts. It was filled with sharpened weapons forming its crocodiles, and was frequented by cannibals.

62.20.en: Strings of pearls formed its ripples and diverse other ornaments the bubbles. The arrows were the eddies, the elephants were the crocodiles, and it was incapable of being got over.

62.21.sa: शरसङ्घमहावर्तां नागनक्रां दुरत्ययाम् । महारथमहाद्वीपां शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिःस्वनाम् । चकार च तदा पार्थो नदीं दुस्तरशोणिताम् ॥२१॥
62.21.en: The mighty car-warriors were the islands and it was filled with the sound of bugles and conchs. Thus Partha made a river of blood which it was so hard to cross.

62.22.sa: आददानस्य हि शरान् सन्धाय च विमुञ्चतः । विकर्षतश्च गाण्डीवं न कश्चिद्ददृशे जनः ॥२२॥
62.22.en: People could not make out when Partha took up arrows, when he drew the Gandiva bow and discharged them.

63.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततो दुर्योधनः कर्णो दुःशासनविविंशती । द्रोणश्च सह पुत्रेण कृपश्चापि महारथः ॥१॥
63.1.en: Vaishampayana said Then Duryodhana, Karna, Dushasana, Vivinshati, the mighty car-warrior Kripa, Drona, with his son, holding out their strong and powerful bows, rushed with anger towards Dhananjaya with a view to kill him.

63.2.sa: पुनर्ययुश्च संरब्धा धनञ्जयजिघांसवः । विस्फारयन्तश्चापानि बलवन्ति दृढानि च ॥२॥
63.2.en: Vaishampayana said Then Duryodhana, Karna, Dushasana, Vivinshati, the mighty car-warrior Kripa, Drona, with his son, holding out their strong and powerful bows, rushed with anger towards Dhananjaya with a view to kill him.

63.3.en: O great king, then on his car effulgent like the rays of the sun, the standard of which was struck down, Arjuna, having the emblem of a monkey on his car, encountered them.

63.4.sa: ततः कृपश्च कर्णश्च द्रोणश्च रथिनां वरः । तं महास्त्रैर्महावीर्यं परिवार्य धनञ्जयम् ॥४॥
63.4.en: Then covering Dhananjaya with highly powerful weapons, Kripa, Karna, Drona, the foremost of car-warriors, showered a downpour of shafts, like clouds, on him, and struck him.

63.5.sa: शरौघान्सम्यगस्यन्तो जीमूता इव वार्षिकाः । ववर्षुः शरवर्षाणि पातयन्तो धनञ्जयम् ॥५॥
63.5.en: Then covering Dhananjaya with highly powerful weapons, Kripa, Karna, Drona, the foremost of car-warriors, showered a downpour of shafts, like clouds, on him, and struck him.

63.6.sa: इषुभिर्बहुभिस्तूर्णं समरे लोमवाहिभिः । अदूरात् पर्यवस्थाप्य पूरयामासुरादृताः ॥६॥
63.6.en: Waiting at a distance they speedily covered him in battle with numberless arrows crowned with feathers.

63.7.sa: तथा तैरवकीर्णस्य दिव्यैरस्त्रै समन्ततः । न तस्य द्व्यङ्गुलमपि विवृतं सम्प्रदृश्यते ॥७॥
63.7.en: He being thus covered with celestials weapons, not even a space measuring two fingers was seen on him.

63.8.sa: ततः प्रहस्य बीभत्सुर्दिव्यमैन्द्रं महारथः । अस्त्रमादित्यसङ्काशं गाण्डीवे समयोजयत् ॥८॥
63.8.en: Then smiling, the mighty car-warrior Bibhatsu set the Aindra weapon, effulgent like the sun, on his Gandiva bow.

63.9.sa: शररश्मिरिवादित्यः प्रतस्थे समरे बली । किरीटमाली कौन्तेयः सर्वान्प्राच्छादयत्कुरून् ॥९॥
63.9.en: Like the sun covering (the earth) with rays, the powerful son of Kunti, decked with a diadem, remained in the battle-field covering all with arrows.

63.10.sa: यथा बलाहके विद्युत्पावको वा शिलोच्चये । तथा गाण्डीवमभवदिन्द्रायुधमिवानतम् ॥१०॥
63.10.en: As lightning in the clouds, as fire in the rock, so the Gandiva shone like the rain-bow.

63.11.sa: यथा वर्षति पर्जन्ये विद्युद्विभ्राजतेः दिवि । द्योतयन्ती दिशः सर्वाः पृथिवीं च समन्ततः ॥११॥
63.11.en: Gandiva bow had covered all the ten directions in number, by shooting volley of arrows as the lightening glows in sky while raining and it illumines all directions including the earth from all sides. O Barata! all soldiers including elephant riders and car riders were loosing their conscious.

63.12.sa: तथा दश दिशः सर्वाः पतद्गाण्डीवमावृणोत् । नागाश्च रथिनः सर्वे मुमुहुस्तत्र भारत ॥१२॥
63.12.en: Gandiva bow had covered all the ten directions in number, by shooting volley of arrows as the lightening glows in sky while raining and it illumines all directions including the earth from all sides. O Barata! all soldiers including elephant riders and car riders were loosing their conscious.

63.13.sa: सर्वे शान्तिपरा योधाः स्वचित्तानि न लेभिरे । सङ्ग्रामे विमुखाः सर्वे योधास्ते हतचेतसः ॥१३॥
63.13.en: They all were stunned (inert and dumb) with no conscious at all. All soldiers discouraged to carry on fight and showed their back to the battle-field.

63.14.sa: एवं सर्वाणि सैन्यानि भग्नानि भरतर्षभ । व्यद्रवन्त दिशः सर्वा निराशानि स्वजीविते ॥१४॥
63.14.en: O the best in Bharata dynasty, ) Janamejaya! thus the war-craft/strategy of the whole army shattered. The soldiers began departing under sheer despair wherever they found the way to escape and defend their life.

64.1.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो भरतानां पितामहः । वध्यमानेषु योधेषु धनञ्जयमुपाद्रवत् ॥१॥
64.1.en: Vaishampayana said The warriors being thus slain, Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, the grandfather of Bharatas, rushed at Dhananjaya,

64.2.sa: प्रगृह्य कार्मुकश्रेष्ठं जातरूपपरिष्कृतम् । शरानादाय तीक्ष्णाग्रान् मर्मभेदान् प्रमाथिनः ॥२॥
64.2.en: Taking up the best of bows made of burnished gold, and sharp arrows capable of piercing to the very vitals.

64.3.sa: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण ध्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि । शुशुभे स नरव्याघ्रो गिरिः सूर्योदये यथा ॥३॥
64.3.en: And on account of a white umbrella being held over his head, that foremost of men shone like a hill at sun-rise.

64.4.sa: प्रध्माय शङ्खं गाङ्गेयो धार्तराष्ट्रान्प्रहर्षयन् । प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य बीभत्सुं समवारयत् ॥४॥

64.5.sa: तमुदीक्ष्य समायान्तं कौन्तेयः परवीरहा । प्रत्यगृह्णात्प्रहृष्टात्मा धाराधरमिवाचलः ॥५॥
64.5.en: Seeing him approach, that slayer of hostile heroes, the son of Kunti received him gladly like a hill receiving a cloud.

64.6.sa: ततो भीष्मः शरानष्टौ ध्वजे पार्थस्य वीर्यवान् । समार्पयन्महावेगान् श्वसमानानिवोरगान् ॥६॥
64.6.en: Then the greatly energetic Bhishma discharged eight quick arrows, sighing like serpents, at Partha's flag.

64.7.sa: ते ध्वजं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य समासाद्य पतत्रिणः । ज्वलन्तं कपिमाजघ्नुर्ध्वजाग्रनिलयांश्च तान् ॥७॥
64.7.en: Reaching the flag-staff of the son of Pandu, those winged arrows struck the blowing monkey and other creatures stationed on the flag-staff.

64.8.sa: ततो भल्लेन महता पृथुधारेण पाण्डवाः । छत्रं चिच्छेद भीष्मस्य तू तदपतद्भुवि ॥८॥
64.8.en: Then with a huge and sharp dart, the son of Pandu quickly cut off Bhishma's umbrella and it fell down on the ground.

64.9.sa: ध्वजं चैवास्य कौन्तेयः शरैरभ्यहनद्भृशम् । शीघ्रकृद्रथवाहांश्च तथोभौ पार्ष्णिसारथी ॥९॥
64.9.en: The son of Kunti, with arrows, struck his flag-staff, his two horses and her driver that protected his flanks.

64.10.sa: अमृष्यमाणस्तद्भीष्मो जानन्नपि स पाण्डवम् । दिव्येनास्त्रेण महता धनञ्जयमवाकिरत् ॥१०॥
64.10.en: Unable to bear this, Bhishma though he knew Arjuna's prowess covered Dhananjaya, the son of Pandu with celestials weapons.

64.11.sa: तथैव पाण्डवो भीष्मे दिव्यमस्त्रमुदीरयन् । प्रत्यगृह्णादमेयात्मा महामेघमिवाचलः ॥११॥
64.11.en: Then discharging a celestials weapon at Bhishma, Pandava, of incomparable energy, received him like a hill receiving a huge mass of cloud.

64.12.sa: तयोस्तद्भवद्युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम् । भीष्मेण सह पार्थेन बलिवासवयोरिव ॥१२॥

64.13.sa: प्रैक्षन्त कुरवः सर्वे योधाश्च सहसैनिकाः । भल्लैर्भल्लाः समागम्य भीष्मपाण्डवयोर्युधि । अन्तरिक्षे व्यराजन्त खद्योताः प्रावृषीव हि ॥१३॥

64.14.sa: अग्निचक्रमिवाविद्धं सव्यदक्षिणमस्यतः । गाण्डीवमभवद्राजन् पार्थस्य सृजतः शरान् ॥१४॥
64.14.en: The Kuru warriors, with their soldiers witnessed that encounter between Bhishma and Partha attacking each other with darts. Partha shooting arrows with both the hands, the Gandiva bow looked like a continuous circle of fire. The son of Kunti enveloped Bhishma with hundreds of sharp arrows like a cloud covering the mountain with rain. Bhishma with his own arrows counteracted that shower of arrows like banks resisting the surging deep, and covered Arjuna with shafts. Those shafts, sundered into a thousand pieces, fell on Arjuna's car. Then arose a downpour of gold-winged shafts going through the sky like a swarm of locusts. He then pierced Bhishma with hundred sharpened shafts.

64.15.sa: ततः संछादयामास भीष्मं शरशतैः शितैः । पर्वतं वारिधाराभिश्छादयन्निव तोयदः ॥१५॥
64.15.en: The Kuru warriors, with their soldiers witnessed that encounter between Bhishma and Partha attacking each other with darts. Partha shooting arrows with both the hands, the Gandiva bow looked like a continuous circle of fire. The son of Kunti enveloped Bhishma with hundreds of sharp arrows like a cloud covering the mountain with rain. Bhishma with his own arrows counteracted that shower of arrows like banks resisting the surging deep, and covered Arjuna with shafts. Those shafts, sundered into a thousand pieces, fell on Arjuna's car. Then arose a downpour of gold-winged shafts going through the sky like a swarm of locusts. He then pierced Bhishma with hundred sharpened shafts.

64.16.sa: तां स वेलामिवोद्भूतां शरवृष्टिं समुत्थिताम् । व्यधमत्सायकैर्भीष्मः पाण्डवं समवारयत् ॥१६॥
64.16.en: The Kuru warriors, with their soldiers witnessed that encounter between Bhishma and Partha attacking each other with darts. Partha shooting arrows with both the hands, the Gandiva bow looked like a continuous circle of fire. The son of Kunti enveloped Bhishma with hundreds of sharp arrows like a cloud covering the mountain with rain. Bhishma with his own arrows counteracted that shower of arrows like banks resisting the surging deep, and covered Arjuna with shafts. Those shafts, sundered into a thousand pieces, fell on Arjuna's car. Then arose a downpour of gold-winged shafts going through the sky like a swarm of locusts. He then pierced Bhishma with hundred sharpened shafts.

64.17.sa: ततस्तानि निकृत्तानि शरजालानि भागशः । समरे च व्यशीर्यन्त फाल्गुनस्य रथं प्रति ॥१७॥
64.17.en: The Kuru warriors, with their soldiers witnessed that encounter between Bhishma and Partha attacking each other with darts. Partha shooting arrows with both the hands, the Gandiva bow looked like a continuous circle of fire. The son of Kunti enveloped Bhishma with hundreds of sharp arrows like a cloud covering the mountain with rain. Bhishma with his own arrows counteracted that shower of arrows like banks resisting the surging deep, and covered Arjuna with shafts. Those shafts, sundered into a thousand pieces, fell on Arjuna's car. Then arose a downpour of gold-winged shafts going through the sky like a swarm of locusts. He then pierced Bhishma with hundred sharpened shafts.

64.18.sa: ततः कनकपुङ्खानां शरवृष्टिं समुत्थिताम् । पाण्डवस्य रथात्तूर्णं शलभानामिवायतिम् । व्यधमत्तां पुनस्तस्य भीष्मः शरशतैः शितैः ॥१८॥

64.19.sa: ततस्ते कुरवः सर्वे साधु साध्विति चाब्रुवन् । दुष्करं कृतवान् भीष्मो यदर्जुनमयोधयत् ॥१९॥
64.19.en: All Kauravas at that moment thanked Bhishma by saying-"Hurrah! Bhishma has showed this rare valour as to wage battle against Arjuna. a

64.20.sa: बलवांस्तरुणो दक्षः क्षिप्रकारी धनञ्जयः । कोऽन्यः समर्थः पार्थस्य वेगं धारयितुं रणे ॥२०॥

64.21.en: Arjuna is mighty, young, efficient and quick in shooting arrows. Hence, who otherwise than Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, Srikrishna, the son of Devaki or Drona, the son of Bharadvaja, mighty and great preceptor (Acharya), can face Partha in battle.

64.22.sa: अस्त्रैरस्राणि संवार्य क्रीडन्तौ भरतर्षभौ । चक्षूंषि सर्वभूतानां मोहयन्तौ महाबलौ ॥२२॥
64.22.en: Both the mighty warriors, crown to the Bharata's dynasty were detouring or splitting the weapons shot by each other as if it was a play not war for them and the spectators were dazed to see it.

64.23.sa: प्राजापत्यं तथैवैन्द्रमाग्नेयं रौद्रदारुणम् । कौबेरं वारुणं चैव याम्यं वायव्यमेव च । प्रयुञ्जानौ महात्मानौ समरे तौ विचेरतुः ॥२३॥
64.23.en: Both of the great warriors were thus engaged in battle-field by shooting the weapons Prajapatya, Aiendra, Agneya, Raudra, Kaubera, Varuna, Yama and Vayavya.

64.24.sa: विस्मितान्यथ भूतानि तौ दृष्ट्वा संयुगे तदा । साधु पार्थ महाबाहो साधु भीष्मेति चाब्रुवन् ॥२४॥
64.24.en: All spectators to that battle could not resist them saying frequently, Ogreat warrior Partha! we thank you. O great warrior Bhishma! We thank you (viz. we appreciate your war-craft and expertise).

64.25.sa: नायं युक्तो मनुष्येषु योऽयं संदृश्यते महान् । महास्त्राणां संप्रयोगः समरे भीष्मपार्थयोः ॥२५॥
64.25.en: The great use of specific divine arms and weapons as it is being seen in the battle of Bhishma and Partha, impossible to anywhere and amid other warriors.

64.26.sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवं सर्वास्त्रविदुषोरस्त्रयुद्धमवर्तत । अस्त्रयुद्धे तु निर्वृत्ते शरयुद्धमवर्तत ॥२६॥
64.26.en: see O Janamejaya! a battle with divine arms between Bhishma and Arjuna both experts kept on incessant for a certain time. A battle with arrows then started.

64.27.sa: अथ जिष्णुरुपावृत्य क्षुरधारेण कार्मुकम् । चकर्त भीष्मस्य तदा जातरूपपरिष्कृतम् ॥२७॥
64.27.en: The victorious Arjuna then marched closer to Bhishma and cut in pieces the gold studded bow of him by shooting an arrow having sword like blade.

64.28.sa: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण भीष्मोऽन्यत्कार्मुकं रणे । समादाय महाबाहुः सज्यं चक्रे महारथः । शरांश्च सुबहून् क्रुद्धो मुमोचाशु धनञ्जये ॥२८॥
64.28.en: The great warrior Bhishma with his huge arms picked-up just at an eye-wink another bow, tied it with string and shot a volley of arrows at Arjuna in sheer anger.

64.29.sa: अर्जुनोऽपि शरांस्तीक्ष्णान्भीष्माय निशितान्बहून् । चिक्षेप सुमहातेजास्तथा भीष्मश्च पाण्डवे ॥२९॥
64.29.en: Arjuna, the great valorous also shot several acute arrows at Bhishma and Bhishma in reaction also shot numerous arrows at Arjuna.

64.30.sa: तयोर्दिव्यास्त्रविदुषोरस्यतोर्निशितान् शरान् । न विशेषस्तदा राजन् लक्ष्यते स्म महात्मनोः ॥३०॥

64.31.sa: अथावृणोद्दश दिशः शरैरतिरथस्तदा । किरीटमाली कौन्तेयः शूरः शान्तनवस्तथा ॥३१॥
64.31.en: Arjuna, the son of Kunti holding a crown on head and Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, both were Atirathi warrior. They had covered the directions, ten in number with the arrows shot at each other.

64.32.sa: अतीवं पाण्डवो भीष्मं भीष्मश्चावि पाण्डवम् । बभूव तस्मिन्सङ्ग्रामे राजंल्लोके तद‌द्भुतम् ॥३२॥
64.32.en: o king Janamejaya! it was really a phenomenon to see of this world that at one time Arjuna, the son of Pandu was seen overlapping Bhishma while Bhishma overlapping Arjuna on the other moment.

64.33.sa: पाण्डवेन हताः शूरा भीष्मस्य रथरक्षिणः । शेरते स्म तदा राजन् कौन्तेयस्याभितो रथम् ॥३३॥

64.34.sa: ततो गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्ता निरमित्रं चिकीर्षवः । आगच्छन्पुङ्खसंश्लिष्टाः श्वेतवाहनपत्रिणः ॥३४॥

64.35.sa: निष्पतन्तो रथात्तस्य धौता हैरण्यवाससः । आकाशे समदृश्यन्त हंसानामिव पङ्क्तयः ॥३५॥

64.36.sa: तस्य तद्दिव्यमस्त्रं हि विगाढं चित्रमस्यतः । प्रेक्षन्ते स्मान्तरिक्षस्थाः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः॥३६॥
64.36.en: Arjuna was shooting divine arms capable to pierce the heart in an excellent manner and Indra etc. all gods were watching his war-craft from the sky where they had come and stood to see this phenomenal battle,

64.37.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतो गन्धर्वश्चित्रमद्भुतम् । शशंस देवराजाय चित्रसेनः प्रतापवान् ॥३७॥
64.37.en: The chivalrous Gandharva Chitrasena was impressed highly with Arjuna and he said Indra, the king of gods in appreciation of his excellent and phenomenal war-craft.

64.38.en: O sovereign king! see that forwarding swiftly and compact with each other on release from Arjuna's bow. This arrows strategy of Arjuna is really excellent and splendid as he is expert in using divine arms.

64.39.sa: नेदं मनुष्याः संदध्युर्नहीदं तेषु विद्यते । पौराणानां महास्त्राणां विचित्रोऽयं समागमः ॥३९॥
64.39.en: As this arm is not with other people, they cannot use this divine arm for battle. An excellent conglomeration of the powerful arms has been made only in this battle here.

64.40.sa: आददानस्य हि शरान् संघाय च विमुञ्चतः । विकर्षतश्च गाण्डीवं नान्तरं समदृश्यत ॥४०॥
64.40.en: Nobody could measure the difference of time between the acts of picking up arrows from holster, putting on bow, shooting and giving tension to the bow.

64.41.sa: मध्यन्दिनगतं सूर्यं प्रतपन्तमिवाम्बरे । नाशक्नुवन्त सैन्यानि पाण्डवं प्रति वीक्षितुम् ॥४१॥
64.41.en: The soldiers on part of Kauravas have lost courage even to see straight way at valorous son of Pandu as nobody can gaze at the sun glowing in sky with acute rays in the noon. Similarly, nobody can dare to look straight at Bhishma, the son of Ganga.

64.42.sa: तथैव भीष्मं गाङ्गेयं द्रष्टुं नोत्सहते जनः ॥४२॥
64.42.en: The soldiers on part of Kauravas have lost courage even to see straight way at valorous son of Pandu as nobody can gaze at the sun glowing in sky with acute rays in the noon. Similarly, nobody can dare to look straight at Bhishma, the son of Ganga.

64.43.sa: उभौ विश्रुतकर्माणावुभौ तीव्रपराक्रमौ । उभौ सदृशकर्माणावुभौ युधि सुदुर्जयौ ॥४३॥
64.43.en: Both warriors are famous for their excellent deeds through the world. Both are aggressively valorous. Both equally chivalours and tough to defeat in the battle.
